Title: Absolutely divine French bistro
Review: We had seen some very good reviews on here but, our experience at this wonderful bistro last night exceeded all of them! Contemporary interior, great ambience and an amazingly warm welcome all evening from Ikram and Diana. The food was simple, very French and exquisite. Generous too. Very reasonable prices. We were then shown very proudly around the rest of the restaurant, upstairs, by Ikram, and it’s huge! We have a home in France, so know what to expect. This trumped many French restaurants we have been to. Thoroughly recommend.Show less

Author: rlow168Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: First time here for dinner
Review: First time here for dinner but the place is almost full to cater for resevations. No choice but to sit at the couch area which is not comfortable to have a proper meal.Decided to go for their homemade foie gras (RM88++). Taste not bad although i expect the portion is a bit more. Love the caramelized onions (free flow)Served toast bread n butter but without providing a butter knife.Staff is courteous n occassionally ask me how is the food n clear the plates when finished.Show less

Author: astra
Title: Great French food
Review: We arrived without a reservation but we were quickly given a table. The food was delicious and the service excellent. Loved the desserts.

Author: GL O
Title: Dinner with mom
Review: Excellent service. All-round good dining experience. Good place when one feels like a Nicoise Salad or a French onion soup, among a big menu of French favourites.

Author: Tour167331
Title: lunch break
Review: the bistro is nearby my office. when it opened i was curious to try it out. one day i dropped by for lunch and enjoyed a lovely lunch. good staff, good food and good ambience. thank you

Author: colinlaney
Title: great food, great service
Review: We had great service from Diana and the food was great. Great little oasis of French cuisine in the middle of Penang.

Author: V7991AYjonathanw
Title: Highly recommended
Review: Fantastic ! This offers top quality French food at a very reasonable price . The service is immaculate and it has a great atmosphere .

Author: landlordtom
Title: Great place
Review: Had lunch with a couple of friends the food and service were top notch. The best French Onion soup I have ever had.  Will definitely visit again.

Author: 220jok
Title: Amazing!
Review: This place is the place we take all of our guests. The food is to die for, the staff are friendly & always at your service. I highly recommend this place for any occasion.

Author: Roubaix23Singapore, Singapore
Title: Beyond Excellent!
Review: Food and service quality beyond what we have expected. It was a impromptu visit on Sunday evening but the Manager managed to squeeze out a table for us without reservation.The duck breast and ribeye were one of the best we have tasted. The pictures I have posted will tell a thousand words.I will definitely visit Two Frenchies again in Dec but will also make my reservation in advance to avoid any disappointment.Show less

Author: Stephen BHarrogate, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic starter and main and desert!!
Review: First night in Penang and it was my wife’s birthday so wanted to get somewhere special and we certainly found it. Great service, great food. Loved the sharing platter for the starter and chicken main to share. Only reason not scored a 5 as unfortunately the steak was a bit tough, despite being hung for 30 days. But don’t let that put you off this is a great restaurant. Show less

Author: RisingSoon019
Title: One Of The Best Meal In Penang.,
Review: Delecious food!!  I have been there with my friend for dinner, that was one of the best meal  i have had in penang. We had the roasted chicken which i like most.Service was very nice and friendly.

Author: CharlotteNormandieKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great French food
Review: The staff was very kind and efficient.We went 2 times there. First time for the dinner and second one for lunch. The food was very good and the same taste like in france. We were just disapointed because we didn't see the owners but we thought the chef was occupied in kitchen. But we are french so we like to see who is behind the foodShow less

Author: scottkind1877
Title: No 1 in Georgetown
Review: Wow! Tried it not only once but twice! Some of the best food I have had. Cassoulet was fantastic. Service was very very good.

Author: AnnKindDoha
Title: Lovely place
Review: This place is lovely! Very comfortable and staff are so helpful. We arrived without a booking and they squeezed us into the bar area without any problems. Food is very tasty and traditionally French.

Author: Tay08
Title: A fairly good french restaurant cafe
Review: Good food, coffee and good service.  It is run by a Frenchman and Chinese wife. Pretty authentic food and good atmosphere.

Author: DAZZAW
Title: Great food and service
Review: The food was fantastic and the service we were given by Ikram was exceptional. Our party of 4 would highly recommend you try Two Frenchies when in Penang

Author: kathete15
Title: Good Vibes
Review: We came across this place by coincidence and loved it. The owners, the food and the employees were just great! Go there if you have the chance...

Author: gabrieny
Title: Worth a visit
Review: nice food , nice ambience , good services , a place that worth a visit . sure i will come back again .

Author: Andy SEdinburgh, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent Food - Over Enthusiastic Staff
Review: We had an excellent meal here with friends. Top quality ingredients and cooked to perfection. It was obvious that the chef was French as there is certainly enough garlic to keep the vampires at bay.Our only criticism was the over enthusiastic staff who seemed to be a bit over the top considering the type of establishment.We will be back though as it is certainly a place worth a visit in Georgetown.Show less

Author: Margot N
Title: I wish I could give 6 stars
Review: I went here with my family two days in a row. We felt homesick so we wanted to have some European food. We were welcomed with a lot of enthusiasm by the lovely staff and took place. What we ate and drank there was beyond expectations! We all enjoyed the fresh meals and my mum even asked for the recipe, which rarely happens since she is a very good chef herself. The restaurant is very cosy and beautifully decorated. I could not give one negative point, it was just splendid. And most importantly we had the best waiter in the world. He was very thoughtful and sympathetic. If I would live in the area, I would go there every week. I would love to give more than 5 stars.Show less

Author: nooshandGoofyAvalon Beach, Australia
Title: Fabulous French
Review: WowWe have just been to the Two Frenchies for a beautiful birthday celebration Ikram and Fatin were fantastic in looking after us and making our family feel welcome and specialThe food was delicious!Not only did we enjoy the meal and hospitality but we could sense that others around us felt the same.Serving sizes were generous. Thank you Ikram for making our daughters birthday on Bastille Day so special We will be back Show less

Author: James B
Title: Fast and delicious refreshing lunch
Review: Visited and we had Onion Soup, Boeuf Bourguignon, Honey glazed Duck with Balsamic, and Salade Nicoise.Truly authentic and delicious. Not too big portions so we could try different things. Oh and not to firget the refreshing Lime Juice and 1664 Kronenbourg Blanc made topped off our sunny Penang day.Starred in my Google so I remember to come back and try the other menu dishes.Thanks Two Frenchies for the great service and food!Show less

Author: RossR908Thames, New Zealand
Title: A must to dine at in Penang
Review: We had dinner here and loved the atmosphere the efficient and friendly staff and of course the divine food. The escargot were perfect. My wife had the honey glazed duck breast and I had the creamy salmon with Market fish and we both loved our meals. I had the apple tart which while tasty could have had the pastry cooked a couple of minutes more. My wife had the vanilla cream with Berry coulis and loved it. Highly recommended for sureShow less

Author: CaffeinatedCapybaraElcho Island, Australia
Title: Elegant French Inspired Cafe
Review: We ate breakfast at Two Frenchies. The Pancakes and Croque Monsieur were delicious. The coffee, a flat white and a latte were carefully prepared and an excellent standard. The building is a beautiful light filled indoor courtyard space with tasteful furnishings. The coffee mug, plate, serviette and menu all had the Two Frenchies logo printed on them. The attention to detail was appreciated. The staff did their utmost to make our dining experience an enjoyable one and were very attentive. I would definitely dine here again. The toilets were also very clean and tidy.Show less

Author: Lancelot25St. Asaph, United Kingdom
Title: Comfort food
Review: We visited for breakfast and for dinner during our trip and both meals were delicious and super comforting. We've been travelling Thailand and Malaysia for 6 weeks +, so this was such a nice break from rice and noodles! The desserts are absolutely to die for and my boyfriend said his burger was the best he's had on our trip! "Proper beef" as he calls it! The staff are all so friendly and attentive aswell. And you get unlimited free filtered water which is something we haven't experienced much. Can't fault it! Show less

Author: bus11traveller
Title: Bon Bon Bon!
Review: Highly recommend if you fancy something non-local, have a relaxing breakfast or easy lunch. Great value for money for the quality. We will be back again for sure. Must have is their tarte tatin!

Author: manlyfanCanberra, Australia
Title: Excellent traditional French Bistrot.
Review: Located in a tastefully renovated Bishop Street shophouse, Two Frenchies offers a range of traditional French dishes for a light lunch or a more substantial meal. On this occasion we were here for dinner and started with Onion soup and Escargots followed by Steak Frites and Boeuf Bourguignon. All were beautifully prepared in authentic style and served in the friendly manner of a good French Bistrot. We were also pleased to be able to find a very palatable Bordeaux Red on the wine list for MYR200, which is good value for Malaysia or Singapore. We finished an excellent meal with Creme Brulee and Lemon Heaven (Syllabub to the English) and coffee.We would highly recommend Two Frenchies for the food, service and value for money.Show less

Author: Dream1095
Title: A lovely dining experience
Review: The staff was attentive & on point and the food was excellent. I would recommend to friends. We had a great celebration dinner for our 18th anniversary.

Author: Foodie480BSingapore River, Singapore
Title: Unanimous Best!
Review: I try not to go overboard in my review but this is one time I am going to break my own rule. We went in a group of 12 and had the upstairs room for our gathering. We had food cooked to perfection - semi buffet appetizers of quiche Lorraine, Croques Monsieurs, Bulgur and Ratatouille- all bite-size; French onion soup that left me wanting more; choice of mains from Beef Bourguignon, Lamb, Roast Duck breast to Salmon; and dessert to die for. Yum and yum. The price is pretty reasonable for what you get - food, service and ambience par excellence. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to have a memorable dinner event without breaking the bank.Show less

Author: adandang
Title: The best restaurant in Georgetown
Review: Wow what a great night! Fabulous food and  impeccable service from the Two Frenchies team. Totally deserving of the number one spot for best restaurant on the Island. Wish we could stay longer and visit again. High praise for this restaurant indeed. Loved it!

Author: RenukaKL
Title: Lovely!
Review: A delightful cafe on Bishop Street - very tasty food in a pleasant and cool environment. Good value for money and excellent service.

Author: Annachuah
Title: Drooling in my sleep
Review: The food here is always in my dreams as i always think of the delicious food that they provide me with, this leaves me drooling for more each time and every visit.

Author: Cabana1973Dubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: Christmas Eve 2018
Review: Booked my table through facebook after looking at a few options for Christmas Eve. The Two Frenchies menu was spot of for what I wanted to eat. Surrounded by simple, modern decor and families enjoying their dinner we had a lovely time. The food (my confit de canard and truffle mash) was excellent. The service was sharp and the food came out hot and on time! We had a lovely evening and if we are ever to return to George Town I would go back.Show less

Author: Kaylethean
Title: Great food i love em
Review: Second time here n still loving this place! Can always ask them to recommend if u have no idea what to grab, its always good! Cozy place n super helpful n friendly staffs, authentic taste too! They serve wines at reasonable price too, definitely worth few visits ! <3Show less

Author: scottishpubspy
Title: Excellent Restaurant with friendly staff
Review: Had dinner in the restaurant last week. While the menu is relatively small the dishes are very good and well prepared. Very typical authentic French bistrot menu. The cassoulet and Beef Bourginon were exceptionally good. I had a pea and ham soup starter, also. The Apple Tartin is also not to be missed. We drank the house pour wines which were good and unusually for Penang of reasonable value. If you are in Penang and you like good food, I personally would recommend you do not miss the Two Frenchies. Show less

Author: catherinemac24Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious French cuisine
Review: I had very luckily won a voucher to the Two Frenchies and had a great experience. The staff made us feel so welcome and the decor is clean and classic. The duck was beautifully cooked and full of flavour. We stayed for hours chatting and never felt like we were an inconvenience. Would definitely consider returning. Show less

Author: KMS888Singapore, Republic of Singapore
Title: Good Food, Good Service, Good value.
Review: Had dinner at this restaurant. Food was excellent and a good example of basic French brasserie type food. Service was very good and friendly. House wines were enjoyable and of very good value. We loved the Casoulet and the beef bourginon. The apple cake was also very good. If you are in Penang and you want a very good relaxed meal this is the place for you. We will be going back again.Show less

Author: asellaliBatam, Indonesia
Title: Best food and service
Review: We never final better French restaurant in AsiaWe went for a lunch even the advice of trip advisor was good we can say this place is more than perfectThe food was tasty very good qualityThe staff especially Ikram and Dan were so professional and kind we feel at homeThey advise us the food which was halal and they adao the sauce to usWhat can be better than a nice food with a nice and a staff who pay attention to usWe lost our phone and they really support usWe had the chance too to meet the owner and his wife. And now we understand how this place can so good Show less

Author: 341anniep
Title: Great food, cozy environment, Awesome service!
Review: We went there for dinner. As we were not really “french dining experts”, we then asked for recommendations. The staff was very patient and helpful to recommend and help us to decide. When the food arrived, it was great. We started with onion soup (love the cheesy burnt on top of the soup. Was sceptical to taste but turned up awesome!), had cheese platter for sharing (good mix of cheese, meat, pickles and dip), followed by Confit de Canard (again was sceptical a bit, but turned up to be pleasantly smooth meat without overwhelming “duck” smell. And the masked potato was really nice). We also ordered Pasta a la Normande - my daughter loves it! We had creme brûlée for dessert - awesome! The place also serve good variety of wine, cocktail and mocktail. A pleasantly designed and decorated place which gave us the coziness and comforts to enjoy our meal. Highly recommend!Show less

Author: racheich
Title: Excellent meal and service
Review: 5 of us had dinner there. The service was fantastic, food was lovely. Wide variety of food and drinks was great. Highly recommend.

Author: Patrick SSatun, Thailand
Title: Perfect afternoon in a little European timelapse!
Review: We were drenching in sweat and desperately looking for a cool nice place to have a drink. And voilà! A little bubble of Europe. For sure we travel to be out of our beaten path!! But sometimes it’s great to be reminded about our origin!! A nice glass of Provence rosé was the holy grail at the time :)And no we are not French :D We are just Canadians that knows how to appreciate a warm welcome when it happens! Thanks to Ikram and his wonderful smile we felt at home and well taken care of! Food was great but welcoming was even better :)A nice place that I would always go back to if I was living here in Penang!Just Go!!Show less

Author: SunMoonShineOxfordshire, United Kingdom
Title: A gem in Penang
Review: After the char kway teow, penang laksa etc, we would like some good continental food. Fortunately for us the manager at the E&O recommended this place. Lovely interior, cosy and great service staff. Food was excellent too. Onion soup, beef and Valrhona chocolate cake. Brought our own wines and always happy to pay corkage. Restaurant can consider making same standard charge between champagne and wine corkage, We paid a higher price for our cava compared to the re wine.Show less

Author: Maksim B
Title: Tasty piece of France in Malaysia
Review: Super-tasty food, cozy interior, friendly stuff. We really rested in this place after all day walking. Strongly recommend!

Author: AL8890
Title: Our Go To place!
Review: Definitely our Go To place for great food, great service and great ambiance. Never had a bad experience there and give it the highest recommendation.

Author: travel275
Title: Great!
Review: Came for lunch one day then went back for dinner the next. Great food, the duck confit so tender and duck ravioli delicious!  Desserts were also good. Nice music with air conditioning made it a lovely atmosphere!

Author: Sophie M
Title: Well worth a visit
Review: We came here as we had read good reviews and we weren’t disappointed. If you fancy a change from local cuisine as we did this is a great choice, the boeuf bourguignon was delicious as was the chocolate mousse. Really friendly and attentive service too.

Author: Ally E
Title: Good food & nice ambience
Review: Been there a few times & still loving the food served. Great place for family/friends gathering. Friendly staff too!

Author: MGF88
Title: What a find!
Review: This was French cooking that would satisfy diners almost anywhere!  My truffle mashed potatoes were to die for!  And the service was perfect.

Author: xieminee
Title: Definitely coming back. Lovely place!
Review: I came here after reading good reviews on Google and TripAdvisor. Arrived at 6.30pm on a Friday evening and was lucky to get the last free table! We felt instantly at home. Greeted by a short hair lady who manned the cashier, very warm and pleasant. I ordered the duck confit (very good reviews!) and my boyfriend got the striploin. We also ordered the French onion soup and escargot. Love the soup and bread (came in a little metal tray, very cute touch) and boyfriend loves his escargot. True enough, duck confit is delicious. The duck skin is paper thin crisp and meat falls off without much effort. Mash potatoes is lovely. We enjoyed our meal very much and will be definitely come back. Keep it up!Show less

Author: 176christopherh
Title: A typical Normandy Bistrot
Review: We like this restaurant and were well received by one of ‘The Frenchies’. The food offering is really classic Normandy style and kept to a limited but delicious set of dishes he’s to choose from! There. Is a relatively limited wine list but it’s well priced by Malaysian standards! It’s very popular so book early! My French Onion Soup and Boef Bourgogne was delicious!Show less

Author: daisycake23Nottingham, United Kingdom
Title: Great French Food in Penang
Review: Excellent Menu Great Wine Choices Brilliant Service We arrived quite late in the evening without a reservation however the restaurant was very helpful and still managed to fit us in for a delicious meal Highly recommend the sharing plate and snails to start and the moules were excellent my husband opted for the duck and it was a pleasant evening in beautiful surrounding Waiting staff were very attentive we will be backShow less

Author: nadia lTunis, Tunisia
Title: Eating non Asian in an Asian country is the decision you will never regret
Review: I visited two Frenchies restaurant with my husband and some other family members for a lunch. Let me tell you that We do love Asian food and the French family of my husband was curious to try a French restaurant in Malaysia and particularly in penang. We were amazed by the chilled and relaxed atmosphere and mostly the charming welcome. The restaurant decoration is very nice with amazing details decoration. We tried several plates listing here, escargots, moules frites, bœuf bourguignon, steak, tarte au pommes,.. and many other plates from the amazing selection of food. All the food was great, tasty, feels and smells like home made. I felt myself in a Trip, we were all happy and I was delighted to see my husband happy about the food. It made us in a very good mood, like the good holidays type of mood.I tried other restaurants in Penang, what I loved about my visit is that the service is professional and efficient and this French restaurant in food feels Malaysia in the spirit because of the charm, the team and the atmosphere I would recommend this restaurant to the lovers of food, trips (as you feel yourself in a trip while eating, good humour and joy lovers Huge thanks for the Two Frenchies team, I would say your team is a squad of competent members Show less

Author: jasmineganSingapore, Singapore
Title: Christmas lunch gone missing
Review: My friend and i came for lunch. When we walked in about 12:30pm, most tables under reservation are empty. We were given a table on 2nd floor. Our starters came about 12:55pm. Then the nightmare begun... we waited for an hour plus and chased for our mains as i had to go to the airport later. 1st staff inform us that they have to serve the 12 pax of reservation before us because someone forgotten our orders and they will do it now. But we arrive and order before them??? After a few mins of waiting , we asked the 2nd staff and he said they overcook our lamb and have to cook a new one. Our lamb was supposed to be well done.Two different staffs gave different excuses for the delay.After about 1 hour 45 mins without our mains...1 main finally arrive but the lamb still missing. How can one enjoy your meal seeing your friend without her order?As i need to head to airport i went downstairs to cancel the lamb and asked for the bill. They serve the lamb instead. Much too late. I don't even have time to enjoy my Bouillabaisse. Only managed a few mouthful as i lost my appetite.Thank goodness we ordered starters. Else we will be starving. Our plan to have a nice Christmas lunch was spoiled.To be fair, the food is nice. The service even on busy day is horribly. We was not angry or being rude but the staffs should be honest. We felt we were being taken for a ride because we are patient? Nice?Show less

Author: PCzns
Title: Enjoyable meal
Review: We celebrated our 33rd anniversary at the restaurant and found the the food was very good and the service excellent.

Author: Ekkamai
Title: Yes!
Review:
This is nice - really, really NICE.
Fantastic service, lovely ambiance and highly recommendable food. 
Will be back for sure!

Author: travelwithpam
Title: Fantastic!
Review: While visiting Georgetown, Penang our tour guide recommended this place for dinner.   Atmosphere is wonderful and I love anything French. Do not miss this restaurant. Friendly staff as well

Author: puffaenquiriesNorwich, United Kingdom
Title: Up and Coming
Review: Recommended this restaurant on my first night back to Penang. What a nice clean place with great food and staff. First class place, not too expensive and will return.This is definitely worth a visit if you are looking for a meal in an up and coming area of Georgetown.Show less

Author: stuffmattersLondon, United Kingdom

Author: Christine FPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Very promising
Review: Two Frenchies have only been opened for a little over 4 months and already this new bistrot has - deservedly - earned excellent reviews. Our visit last night was a very pleasant experience. It is located in one of Chinatown traditional shophouses, its interior occupying a long and narrow space which has been tastefully renovated. Pristine whitewashed walls, sober furniture, with minimalist ornaments, mirrors to give it more width and non obtrusive lighting which could be slightly toned down. The menu is short and features resolutely traditional French specialties: salade niçoise, onion soup, platters of "charcuterie" and cheese, snails, quiche for starters and Boeuf Bourguignon, Confit de Canard and Blanquette de Saumon as main courses. Our confit, served on a generous bed of creamy potato purée was cooked to perfection: crispy outside and mouth wateringly tender inside. Servings are actually so generous that we had no room left for a dessert. The service is diligent and friendly, the wine list is short with selections from the Southern Hemisphere and France. It includes a very decent house wine in carafes of 50cl (an excellent idea) priced at RM50. Prices are reasonable considering the quality of the food. Bravo!!!Show less

Title: Good meals & ambience
Review: Turned up just before 7pm on a Saturday with no reservation but was warmly welcomed at the door by a nice young man named Ikram. While apologetic that it was a full house he offered a table in the function room upstairs or the bar - which is really for drinking. Took us up but it was rather lonely with just us and a karaoke setso we chose the bar. We had thought that since the restaurant was just a few months old it would be off the radar - wrong!! So do book ahead especially on weekends. The bar turned out to be a nice spot but if you are not tall or tend to slouch you might find it hard to eat due to the height of the bar. It can also be a tad narrow for serving if you want to fussy about table service. The food did not take too long and we had beers including the red & sweet Monaco that’s great for ladies. When the food arrived it was hot.The French Onion soup came off the grill so don’t plunge in! The cheese was nicely melted and went well with the soup. My personal preference is for more onions & richer flavour. This was more gentle on the palate but pleasant nonetheless.For mains we had very good confit du carnard & Beef bourguignon. Both came with very delicious mash - super smooth & creamy The duck confit had slightly crisp skin but was so tender, the knife stayed un-used!! The beef was very tender too. Both were very flavourful and made for a delicious meal. Washed off by an interesting drink called Monaco which was beer flavoured with Grenadine and a blonde beer the meal was a complete success. Sitting at the bar was another plus. We got to chat a little with bar-tender in training, Richmond, who made the evening pass even more pleasantly and the extra attention of staff who came to check on us, with even the manager Diana coming to apologise!! for having us sit at the bar.Great service, pleasant atmosphere & wonderful food. Will be back & maybe to sit at the bar (if it’s not otherwise occupied )Show less

Author: Adrian_on_TAPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A sensationally divine 6-course dinner at Salsas Penang
Review: One thing you will notice in the scrumptious delights served as Salsas Penang is that the dishes have outstanding quality, mainly due to the freshest ingredients used and David Kaw, the man who knows how to prepare them beautifully. I gave David a budget and he worked out an impressive 6-course menu. We started the evening with a refreshing salad. Crunchy rocket and romaine lettuce leaves, Japanese cucumber and radish slices, roma tomatoes and raisins were tossed with a balsamic vinaigrette. The salad was topped with some toasted almond slices. The sweet and juicy tomatoes balanced the flavours of the salad well. Next was a trio of seafood offerings – a plump buttered oyster, char-grilled octopus slices with a capsicum salsa and a breaded homemade fish cake. The large Japanese oyster was deshelled and buttered gently, preserving its soft, rich creamy content. Topped with black caviar, this was a combination made in heaven. How you might ask, did David tenderise the octopus? Well, it was at least a 3-hour job for David before he smoked it with hickory chips, then grilling it in a flash over strong flames. So much tender loving care had been given in preparing this delicious offering. On the platter was also a homemade golden fish cake topped with aioli and a dill sprig. The seafood platter was indeed a sublime mix of flavours, textures and aromas that only a well-trained chef can put together. The seafood parade continued with a showstopper dish – a grilled giant river prawn from Thailand. David grilled it with lemon butter and some herbs. The firm, white flesh of the freshwater prawn had a delicate sweet flavour, close to that of a lobster. The real treasure was within the head – the orangey yellow blob of butter-looking cream was what eating the prawn was all about! The rich, umami flavour was out of this world. The fourth course was a generous portion of seared halibut, topping some cauliflower gratin and drizzled over with dill oil. Its lean white and flaky flesh had a subtly sweet taste (of crab or clam). David cooked it perfectly – the skin was crispy and the succulent flesh melted in every mouthful. Simply scrumptious!Next to arrive at the table was a serving of warm, comforting mushroom soup, drizzled with truffle oil. It was lighter, velvety smooth and aromatic. Using only porcini mushrooms, the colour of the soup was a lovely shade of apricot orange. By the sixth and final course, most of us were stuffed to the gills. Having said that, I somehow mysteriously managed to tug in a combo of lamb rack and chicken roulade with a creamy spinach conchiglioni on the side. The tender lamb rack was flavoured with rosemary while the chicken roulade was stuffed with a tarragon herb mix. It was a potpourri of scents that really brought to light David's sensitivity to preparing fine cuisine. The vibrant pub vibe and eclectic decor of Salsas are welcoming. The service was excellent and my friends and I could let our hair down, enjoying a rambunctious evening of merrymaking and cheer. On TripAdvisor, Salsas ranked No. 2 out of 935 restaurants in Penang (on 6 February 2022). Incidentally, Treffpunkt that ranked No. 1 on TripAdvisor out of 935 restaurants in Penang was also owned by David. Due to the pandemic situation, David decided to close Treffpunkt and focus his attention on Salsas. I would highly recommend Salsas to anyone who appreciates good food. If you want to try something else beside tapas and pub grub from the standard menu, give David a budget and you might be in for a surprising treat.Show less

Author: Nordeukmelbourne
Title: affordable delicious set lunches
Review: This air conditioned restaurant attached to the Hotel Continental is conveniently situated at 5 Penang Rd. At street level and on the corner, it offers interesting glimpses of passing people and traffic.The range of set lunches offers excellent value. For ringgit 16.50++, we had the choice of soup or salad. The latter was fresh and varied, then came a generous serve of grilled chicken with mushroom sauce, with fresh, tasty vegetables and finally a freshly baked coconut sponge and ice cream. Plus a large glass of iced peach tea. This was so refreshing we ordered another two each. With a small bottle of Carlsberg, the total bill for two was 68.44 ringgit.The service was prompt, friendly and efficient.Show less

Author: Steve31PenangPenang

The choices were not that spectacular, with steak (with the ever present disgusting Malaysia black pepper sauce, chicken thighs or one dish with chicken breast, pasta and some interesting appetizers. Two of us had the baked chicken breast with mozzarella cheese and we both found it to be sort of bland. One friend had pasta with salmon which was very good. Another had the pate, which was average. The service was good , but the atmosphere was very noisy for a high class restaurant. It appears that they get a lot of business from the hotel guests and tourists. I wouldn't waste my time going there again.Show less

Title: Pleasant place for an inexpensive personal steam boat
Review: I am an American who has spent extensive time in Penang over the last 15 years so I am familiar with many restaurants and and hawker stands all over the island.I decided to try Cheang Kee with a friend because we both like the George Town area and I saw that Cheang Kee was one of the very few places with a five bubble rating and a reasonable number of reviews.We were not dissappointed. The selections were simple but met our desires and expectations perfectly. The waiter was friendly and checked back to see that we were OK. He gave us good advice on how to make our selection.The building is simple, but the ambience is pleasant.I plan to go back from time to time and certainly encourage anyone who likes steam boat in a pleasant ambience to find a time to try it.I wouldn't consider this to be a romantic restaurant, but I think many of the other diners might since I noticed many people dressed up more than normal for Penang, as if on a date.The restaurant has both steam boat and barbeque, but it is primarily steam boat so I did not list it as a barbeque restaurant in the check boxes.The cuisine choices from Trip Advisor do not inclue either Steam Boat or Hot Pot. I think the web site editors need to get out more often.Show less

Author: TokyoMuncherMarbella, Spain
Title: Steer Away...Steer Clear Away
Review: Food was unseasoned, unsophisticated and, if not bland. then simply flavourless. The broccoli soup was abysmal - think, tasteless and so full of culinary mistakes. The main meat course was initial described as strip loin, but turned out to be a sous vide loin of lamb...that was tough, chewy and lacked any depth of flavour. The glazes used throughout were watery thin and lacked any depth. It was as if there was no quality control, no tasting, no attention to detail in the kitchen. The serving was flustered - on two occasions wines were not poured with the new plates being served, cutlery was forgotten and when asked for wine to be replenished (on one occasion) we were told that we would have new wine served for the next course! What????Two major faux pas I cannot help but mention: (1) At a degustation menu one expects to have a new set of cutlery served with new plate servings. Orinea appears to simply keep your cutlery and takes the plates away. A word of advice - this is not a buffet! (2) At such a 'fine ding' experience (which it is NOT) diners should not expect to see boxes stored under the stairs in the dining room (see picture)! Oh...and let's not even talk about the state of the restrooms...certainly no better than many hawker stall food courses dotted around the town - this is not a fine dining restaurant...but it has prices to match...this was by far the most expensive dinner we had at over USD 320 per couple (and we stayed and dined at the Eastern & Oriental!).Show less

Author: NLinTKOPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A restaurant with two faces
Review: I took my wife to Orinea for her Birthday dinner. We selected the five course menu (RM188/person). My wife asked the foie gras Appetizer to be replaced with something else, for which an extra RM18 was charged. I was surprised that the restaurant would charge this, but did not comment as I didn't want to ruin the atmosphere.We enjoyed the Amuse-bouche and Starter as each had its own taste and presentation. I had Angus sirloin for Entrée, which was very tasty. My wife had the red snapper and found it rather tasteless, especially compared to the previous courses. We both found the Dessert (mango based) the least of the courses. It was too sugary sweet and did not match the refinement of the other courses.This restaurant presents itself as being in the "haute cuisine" category: meaning many courses but each course consists of a small amount. Nevertheless was the total amount sufficient for us: we did not leave hungry. The pace at which the courses were served was fine: not too fast or too slow.There were a few things which I liked less about the experience:(*) The interior decoration. The restaurant looks very sterile. The floor has dark tiles. All walls are black and are without decoration. The tables and chairs are black with metal legs. The lights remain dimmed at night except for a strong blue ceiling light, giving the impression that you are in a night club. This is not my preferred setting for a nice dinner.(*) I had made a reservation online and the reservation mentioned that I would "get a RM20 voucher for After Hours x 2". I expected this to be useful for having coffee after finishing dinner, as that was not included in the selected menu. However, upon entering the restaurant the waiter told me that this voucher would be given to me after I had paid and would only be valid on a next visit to the restaurant. In my eyes is this a blatant sign of misleading marketing as it is nowhere mentioned that the voucher could not be used on the same visit. After having left the restaurant I noticed that the waiter did not give me the vouchers.(*) In between courses were we regularly pushed by the waiter to write a positive review on social media (e.g. Facebook, Tripadvisor). This happened at least three times, even though we did not have mobile phones on the table. He even promised "something special" if we would show him our online message during the dinner. I don't know whether this is restaurant policy, or that only our waiter did this. I think that this is very inappropriate for a restaurant in this category. The waiter made very sure that we know and remember his name: he pointed multiple times at his badge saying his name is Akie.All in all is it clear to me that Orinea has a very good kitchen, but I have some hesitations towards the restaurant. In this category of the market, and at this price range, do I have higher expectations of a restaurant, its pricing policies and its staff.Show less

Author: FlyDineWineSydney, Australia
Title: Not fine dining
Review: Overall: this was a disappointing and pretty dismal dining experience and feel the restaurant is quite deceitful in its overall web presence. Would advise any future guests and travellers to avoid!What we ordered: 358 RM 9 course 'surprise' chefs tasting menu + non alcoholic drinks pairingService: Overall the servers were nice, but not very professional. They understood very little about the food they were serving. The server we had, omitted certain items on our plate and when probed further about them would only be able to tell whether they are edible or not (not whether they were part of the taste of the dish). So overall, very rehearsed and robotic service... didn't feel natural, was definitely not happy about the automatic 10% service charge on the meal!Food: Overall the food quality was poor and not worth the money. The flavours were boring and we had some flavours repeat over a few courses, which u don't expect when offered a chefs supposed 'surprise' tasting menu. The food was hardly fit for fine dining with very rudimentary presentation, on one course we had to half deshell a prawn, which is not expected when fine dining.Drink: the drinks which were paired with didn't really match the flavours in our food. They all tasted the same with a lot of them tasting of varied fruits mixed through sprite. They were also not introduced in detail by our server..Portion size: The portions were also very tight...my girlfriend wasn't even full after 9 courses. Some courses were embarrassingly small.Ambience & setting: The view off the external balcony is a slight redeeming feature of this venue. But there is overall a lack of attention to detail by the staff in the dining atmosphere. We heard utensils being washed behind the open bar, the reception mobile going off often & loudly. The bathroom was also unfit for a fine dining venue in terms of decor and the soap dispenser hadn't even been filled. The background music in the dining room was a loop of Christmas carols quite noisy, noticeable and maddening.Show less

Author: theBunBunKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: OMG!! If you have ANY standard at all, please go elsewhere!!
Review: A lovely building and setting! What a shame that such a fantastic place is occupied by a bunch of amateurs!! By far the worst meal in Penang for the price that you pay!I have never taken the time to write such a criticizing review as I think taste can be very subjective, so no need to be too judgemental. I have decided to write this after "cool down period" of a few days. I really do not wish my fellow travellers to waste their time, money, and calories at this place while in Penang!!Lovely room that we sat in. Started to be served by a young Asian waitstaff who claimed to have worked there for 5 months already. The menu seemed interesting enough and wine list had good choices.I noted placemats on the table... not only I rarely see placemats at fine-enough dining establishments, the ones that FM chose were similar to those that one could find at an IKxA outlet!The bread basket was simple; breads were warmish but very doubtful that they were freshly baked. That would be fine if we were at a "family-style chain restaurant".Amuse-bouche consisted of the "chicken texture" and "fish and chips". Based on the photos that I saw, these two offerings are either extremely popular that the chef wished to keep presenting, OR... the chef was simply uncreative and take the easier route. The chicken things were overly salty gizzards and the fish and chip with ikura on top, the ingredients simply did not complement each other.Ordered a la carte, the pumpkin soup with a piece of scallop... why a piece of scallop was beyond me because it didn't really match the soup... tasted acceptable but by NO means anything special. If I imagined hard enough, I could actually taste pumpkin. Soft shell crab was also acceptable... fried, just like one that you get at a mediocre Japanese restaurant. Rack of lamb and duck confit were again okay. The side garnishings for the two dishes were identical!! The chef... I mean the cook... zero creativity?I was going to get oysters but they ran out. Oh, they also did not have espresso nor machiato, because the coffee machine was broken.Another highlight of the evening was the Asian waitstaff. I had trouble understanding his English. He was careless and unobservant. Bread plates were missing; when asked, he only returned with one for my wife, had to ask again for mine. When describing the dishes, we were simplistically told what we were having. Ordered a bottle of red, and this young waiter... perhaps an optimist... poured enough wine to ensure the glass was way more than half-full! He did not keep our sparkling water cold till I asked, and later, he did not even remember we had a bottle of sparkling water! Despite all these, he was attentive though!Show less

Author: stuffmattersLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Disappointing.
Review: Any restaurant that calls itself fine dining is clearly going to be at the top end of its market price wise. The challenge therefore is for the restaurant to deliver on the promise through great food, service & ambiance. Unfortunately Farquhar fails to do so. The restaurant comprises several rooms over several floors which whilst it may be excellent for small groups or parties certainly does not help ambiance particularly when it’s quiet / empty. In our case we were the only occupied table in our room which had a capacity of 2/3 tables so the ambiance was funereal. The menu was interesting but portions although beautifully presented were seriously nouvelle cuisine / small with the Goulash soup being approx 5/6 spoonfuls and the mash accompanying the main course being 1 inch diameter.Service was however very attentiveThe experience was disappointing but given the generally positive reviews on the site it is clearly meeting the expectations of many guests if not mine. Show less

The restaurant has several rooms and groups were discreetly spaced to provide a private environment. Service was attentive but unobtrusive, which also enhanced the experience.We ordered the Black Angus Tenderloin and Australian Lamb Rack for mains and were served excellent bread and an amuse-bouche while we waited. Main courses were both delicious and perfectly prepared. There was an extensive wine list to complement the food. We followed up with desserts that were very tasty and artistically presented and coffee.The overall cost was high but similar to other fine dining restaurants in the region. We would happily recommend Farquhar Mansion and will return.Show less

Author: PaimanPai
Title: Afternoon High Tea. The Way It is Supposed to Be
Review: My idea of high tea is a somewhat lavish, but comfortable affair, in an old colonial setting, being served an assortment of savory and sweet bites along with a high quality tea. Farquhar Mansion delivered on all counts. When first entering the premises, we were struck by the posh late 1800-like ambience, from the linen covered colonial tables, comfortable chairs, and gold rimmed porcelain service settings. During this visit, my dining partner and I dined alone in the quiet and comfortable space, with only the background music of mellow jazz, followed by classical piano. The perfect choice when one wants to concentrate on the food and carry on a quiet conversation. The small bites were served on a three tier setting and consisted of ten offerings, plus a crisp waffle served on the side. The Bottom part of the second ties consisted of savory items, with mini pastries filling the rest of the two tiers. Every item looked like a small work of pastry art with flavors to match. The service was attentive and excellent, with the wait staff knowing when to refill our tea, and then leave us to resume our conversation.Show less

Author: kesharooPJ
Title: Fine dining in Penang
Review: It was not easy to secure a booking at Farquhar which was a surprise. We wanted to have dinner on Friday evening but was informed that it was full and Saturday as well. Later on we were informed that there was a private function on Friday but they could allocate us a table on Saturday which we accepted. We were also informed of a dress code whereby slippers and shorts weren't allowed.We arrived promptly at the appointed time and parking inside the restaurant compound was available at no extra charge. We were ushered to our table quickly and were given the menus. I would describe the food at leaning towards French with an emphasis on presentation and sauces. They certainly took care of the details and our comfort, the air-cond was quickly turned down when the saw my wife feeling cold. The wine list is the most impressive I have seen in Penang but leaning heavily towards Bordeaux with no Burgundies in sight. We requested for a bottle of the pinot noir from New Zealand which was exceedingly quaffable.We had starters and meats as our main courses, my wife had the lamb and I had the tenderloin, all done to perfection. To start there were 2 sets of amuse bouche and in between courses, sorbet to clean our palate.Service was great although a tad formal, my guess is that they wish to keep it all very tight with no room for errors. I would have preferred a more relaxed service.The final bill was equal to fine dining restaurants everywhere and I would say that the quality of the food justifies the prices. However I would hesitate to return, after all there are many more restaurants to visit in Penang and fine dining such as that offered by Farquhar is also available elsewhere.Show less

There were 3 small things that let down an otherwise top class dining experience (1) The food menu and the wine list both offer house wines by the glass but at vastly different prices! Like RM 25 and RM 40 for what was the same grape and I suspect the same wine. Of course the cheaper version was "unavailable" (2) this is a fine dining restaurant that serves no cocktails! Not even a gin and tonic. (3) we tried the chefs tasting menu which was awesome except for the onion consommé which had no seasoning or flavour. But everything else was great including the service from a team of super-cute waiting staff who were locals and therefore understood you even if they spoke with strong Chinese accents and a little too quickly for my ancient western ears to decipher. Although the restaurant has many reviews on TA where the reviewer is a first-timer it probably deserves its top spot anyway. If you go easy on the wine the prices are reasonable. Don't miss the tour of the private lounge & dining rooms upstairs. (Members only).Show less

Author: iisechewMalaysia
Title: Superb Wood-fire pizza
Review: The Loft Pizzeria & Bar @ Love LaneThe smell of actual wood-fire searing authentic Italian Pizzas; that's what we were welcomed with the moment we stepped in The Loft. Beautifully picturesque, this location makes for the perfect date or grand occasion, with amazing authentic Italian dishes. You won't miss out the gigantic wood-fire oven at the center of the pizza-making station; it truly is a grand sight to behold. Farouk, the head chef of the pizza bar, has an actual 16 years' experience of creating pizzas from scratch. From the very pizza dough he kneads to the wood-fire oven, the pizzas here are, without surprise, the biggest sellers.We thoroughly enjoyed the Al-Funghi Pizza, which was truly a delight to the tongue, especially with the wood-fire fragrance. It was baked to perfection. If you want to be adventurous, give the Agnello Pizza a go; marinated lamb chunks which make it seemingly a fusion of Briyani and Italian Pizza make for a unique favourite. The garlic bread with cheese was impressive; toasted in the wood-fire oven, it really gave what seemed to be a simple dish a classy experience. If I were to return, I'd definitely repeat having the Cheese and Spinach Patties.. They were simply rich, juicy and delicious.The Loft serves deliveries for those who interested; GrabFood is limited in its menu for The Loft, so I'd recommend to give the restaurant a call for the entire menu to be Whatsapped to you, at 017-586 5755.Show less

Author: thomasyasudaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Unforgettable poor experience - never believe complementary reviews
Review: I recommend readers NOT to believe positive reviews. My wife and I dined The Loft a day before "doraemon3636" visited. Her review is fully agreeable, our experience was something similar. We were misled by reviews and restaurant raking listed on tripadvisor. The restaurant owner must take disappointed diners' review seriously, and shall take immediate action to improve, significant improvement is needed on service staff (unprofessional staff shall be removed) and food quality (nothing impressive, everything was below the average).Show less

Author: doraemon3636
Title: 本当に酷い店です。クリスマスが台無し！
Review:
12月24日クリスマスイブに主人と2人で事前に予約して行きました。予約したにも関わらず、ドアが椅子にあたるんですけど？という席。クリスマスだから混んでるし仕方ないか。と諦め着席。サラダ、ステーキ、ボロネーゼパスタ、ワインをボトルで注文しました。サラダは間違ったオーダーが届き、勿体ないからOKと言いました。万が一、会計時にそのままのオーダーだったら指摘しよう、と思っていましたら、その後4回もミスオーダーがありました（頼んでもいない物がどんどん届く）。
またパスタは、やわやわ茹で過ぎ、麺が水っぽいという、何ともお粗末なものでした。
会計時、気をつけてレシートをチェックしなければと思っておりましたが、案の定、間違ったオーダーが２つ載っており、サラダも間違っていました。間違いを指摘し、請求を直している間に、また5回目の頼んでもいない注文を持って来たので、流石にキレました…
謝りもしない店員、本当に酷い店です。何度も海外旅行をしておりますが、こんなに酷いレストランは初めてです。クリスマスが台無しです。何故、こんなに評価が高いのかわかりません。絶対に評価に騙されないでください！

It is a terrible restaurant full of mistakes and does not apologize.  Don't be fooled by the evaluation!

Title: Sunday Lunch at The Loft
Review: One of my favorite places in Penang, Malaysia is The Loft on Love Lane. They are open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. There is also live music on Friday and Saturday nights. For the main course we had baked canneloni with ricotta and spinach and a made to order thin crust pizza. I highly recommend The Loft on Love Lane. You will not be disappointed. Show less

Author: chasingrainsSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average Food, Awkward Seating
Review: We visited The Loft after a quick search on tripadvisor. I had high hopes given the huge wood fire pizza oven at the centre of the restaurant. The pizza was strictly okay, the base could be a lot better. Our pasta was excessively buttery. The tiramisu, however, was quite perfect. I have to add in a word about the seating because, could one really enjoy eating anything half-hung from a high sofa with no foot rest? They need to improve this ASAP. The live band was just warming up while we finished desserts so I won’t comment on it. If you’re at an Italian restaurant in Penang, you’re either giving yourself a break from all the Laksa & Kway Teo or, like me, you just absolutely love anything Italian irrespective of geolocation. Perhaps, this is meant for neither. Sadly- I’d say, skip this one. Show less

Review: Today we arrived in Georgetown. A great city with good atmosphere. Through TripAdvisor we noted this Italian restaurant on the love lane. Especially the kitchen personnel did really manage to give us an Italian experience with their good food for a good price. We ordered an vegetarian pizza and a nice pasta which we asked to share as a starter/main so we could really enjoy our bottle of wine. This was not a problem. Overall a really good experience and we will definitely come back some time. We have only one advice for the personnel. During our dining experience three different individuals requested us to write a review on TripAdvisor. One of them even provided us the WiFi password at the table during our main course so we could write the review immediately. In the end we think this was all with good intentions but it does question the credibility of all the good service. Show less

Author: Mr_rossduncanAdelaide, Australia
Title: Sleek and modern but disappointing pizza
Review: We always try and make Friday night pizza night, no matter where we are in the world.Somtimes it's easy to track down a good spot, sometimes not.Much of Asia is difficult, the toppings are off, the cheese is wrong or the dough hasn't proved.When we walked past The Loft in Love lane one mid-week evening we did a secret little happy dance, it looked the goods.Modern and thoughtful design and the promise of wood-fired pizza, we vowed to return for Friday night pizza night.The interior of this slick new build is great, they've spent a lot of time and money getting the look and feel of a contemporary modern trattoria and it mostly works.I say mostly because the one glaring fail on design is the huge and unwelcome television set screwed to the back wall, nobody, and I do mean nobody, paying any attention to it. Why they would ruin the feel with a dreary soccer match playing above everybodys head is a mystery.There's also the threat that later in the evenings a DJ will climb into a high perched booth and ruin the atmosphere even more with some overloud tunes.To the food and service.The staff are great, all friendly and knowledgeable, busy looking after the crowd but keeping an eye on the tables as well, good stuff.The food, well, the salad was nice, a green leaf salad with apple and parmesan cheese, nicely seasoned was a hit.The pizza. Not a hit.Sad and flat it resembled something you would order from Pizza Hut, it really wasn't good.The dough had no chew to it, burnt around the edges, but not in that good slighly charred classic Italian pizza way, this was just dry and burnt, but what was really unforgivable was the use of those horrible black seeded and sliced olives, the ones that look like small car tires, they should be banned from public, they're fake olives, they have not been cured properly, they are soaked in a chemical bath first to make them go black. Most canned black olives are soaked in lye first, have a read what lye chemical is and you will not want to eat those round black balls of hell again. Horrible.Show less

Title: Flavourful Laksa in the heart of Georgetown
Review: From speaking to locals and other tourists, you will either really love the flavours of the laksa here, or you will just think it is so so. [Maybe it depends on how much laksa you have ever eaten!!] Therefore I recommend that you just go and try it out for yourself! We tried all three laksas (Nyonya, Asam and mixed). We ordered spring rolls one day, and fried bananas the other. We also ordered some extra crackers too. At RM1, this was a bargain. Most of the prices are really reasonable actually. A bowl of laksa won't even set you back RM10. That's like 2 euros!! On the two occasions we went, there were only a few people in the restaurant, but this was due to the RMCO making most places quiet. Therefore the atmosphere wasn't completely great but we didn't mind. On the second occasion, the lad working there wanted us to sit up in the cafe, but there is no window there and the place was empty, so we asked to go back downstairs and sit near the window. I feel that especially at a time like this, it's important to support the restaurants in Georgetown. The lack of tourists right now is making things dire. Laksalicious really relies on the great rating at Tripadvisor (much deserved), and I definitely think it is what will help boost their business. So please go and support if you are ever in the area!Show less

Title: Streetfood With Air-Conditioning

Author: Kamil S

Review: After quite a few disappointments in Penang, I was thrilled that we stopped here for a lunch. The portions were generous (we could not finish). I had a vegetarian Laksa which was very good with a lot of greens. I wish there was more vegetables but it remains the best Laksa I had in Southeast Asia !The Pea flower sago was amazing, what a beautiful desert!And food was very decently priced, 9,90 for a Laksa is a great price considering the fact that it is not a street food stall but an actual restaurant.The waitress was very friendly and knowledgeable which made the experience even more pleasant.If you are a foodie and happens to be in Penang, you must visit this place!Show less

Author: SFOYYZ_EricToronto
Title: Delicious!

Author: MoPekoeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent restaurant, excellent service, excellent laksa
Review: I visited this shop for the first time in June 2019. I was born-&-bred in Penang, so I know Penang food very well, even though I have lived & worked in Singapore since the 1980’s. The food in this restaurant is excellent. Tasty, Penang-authentic, pleasing to the eye, well-rendered, fresh ingredients. The restaurant is walk-in casual, pleasant, clean, cool, well-organized, a great place, whether to chill with family & friends, or simply to eat-&-run. It is very popular with locals & travellers. I saw a constant stream of travellers with roller baggage bags in tow, either just arrived in Penang, or checking-out, tucking in, & plenty of locals. And this wasn’t even mealtime! I took the laksas, both the assam (sour) & lemak (also known as nyonya-style or often called Siamese or Siam Laksa too), both were excellent! Note that the Lemak-style is unique to Penang, & even in Penang, only very limited stalls sell this variety, whereas the ‘assam’ variety is the quintessential Penang laksa, commonly available. The Penang Lemak Laksa has some resemblance to the Singapore Katong Laksa, but they are not the same, I just can’t describe the difference. The hands-on dynamic buzzing proprietress of the shop, is a wonderful good-looking young lady, who is pleasant, engaging, interactive, responsive. You can see that she takes great pride in her food offerings, the service, the restaurant, the biz. This restaurant is conveniently located at quaint Lorong Hutton (Hutton Lane), just slightly off the main downtown street of Jalan Penang, within a very short strolling distance. I can’t wait to return to Laksalicious in my next Penang trip, particularly for the Lemak/Nyonya/Siamese Laksa which is my fav laksa variety. Kudos to the shop proprietress/manager for running an excellent outlet, in the midst of downtown Georgetown!Show less

Author: ClarkzulSingapore, Singapore
Title: Laksa without the heat
Review: This place serves the 2 kinds of Laksa.... The Laksa Penang and also Laksa Lemak. Difference, Laksa Penang is the sourish soupy one whilst Laksa Lemak is the creamy one. If you're unsure on which one to choose, they are nice enough to let you have a tasting portion of both the gravies, so you can decide after tasting.Personally for my tastebuds, the Laksa Penang was not bad. You may want to skip the springrolls that is to dip into the gravy. There're tastier springrolls out there. The chicken spring roll (named in the menu), is just Ngoh Hiang. But i highly recommended the Chempedak Springrolls!! There're other dessert springrolls which you may want to try!Try out the Coffeelicious (coffee with Gula Melaka)! Show less

Author: YogaBoy123

Review: I loved the local laksa here. I went twice and the family who runs the place is great. I highly recommend.

Author: ArgamemnonWellington, New Zealand

Author: Zurich_HZurich, Switzerland

Everything was delicious and amazing value for money. The ‘ginger tea’ served cold is also definitely recommended! Show less

Author: herbertsmith241065Melbourne, Australia
Title: Oh my gosh!! Where have you been all my life
Review: My first 5 star. I don’t give it but at the same time I don’t want to sound critical. Here is space you would want more. It’s very reasonably priced. Here is where we ate our A1 Nyonya assam laksa and d9 mango sagolicious at 2pm. Needed to check this place for my own after raving reviews to make us for real. Today is public holiday and expected long queue but it was not. So it was amazingly relaxing, quite and cooling. The place is still busy half full (48 seats in total) but not crowded. (Well it got crowded when we finished.) Just cannot describe to you about taste. Just to say that I had been disappointed with many Assam and so it turned me off. But if there is one Assam you must have in life, this is it. The taste was mild not overpowering not salty or sour and the balance of mint lemon fish spices was perfect. I have never had a perfect dish. But now finally in this life, I have found perfection. It was not great. It was Supreme. Got a chance to talk to Christine ooi the owner for 7 mins even though she was busy serving others. It’s very hard to find quality cheap food around. Everyone claims to be the one and only the famous this and that. Every one has the same ingredients more or less. Well not so: freshly made ingredients and real efforts are put into the mix are the big difference. Christine does not take short cuts. She thinks about this. She wanted to make a statement m, a difference. Laksa is meant to be spicy but you can’t eat spicy food in hot and sweaty humid shop and she knows it. You Just won’t enjoy it as much. Her humility is also what makes this place pleasant. She just let her customers do the talking. I will miss this place, I will dream about it for many moons to come. I am coming back. Please come to Melbourne! I will be waiting.Show less

Author: 341anniep

Author: lydias666London, United Kingdom
Title: Lighter, delicious and full of flavour
Review: My partner and I walked about 45 to reach this place so we were hungry by the time we arrived. I usually don’t finish a laksa as they are a little heavy. With this vegetarian laksa, I ate the entire meal and got a dessert. Maybe it was the walk too but it was a little les a heavy than I am used to which made it absolutely perfect. I would recommend this to westerners. It’s a great price, great flavours and the extremely helpful host made it worth the walk in the heat. Show less

Author: Teamkarma

Author: ChittenBrisbane QLD
Title: Lament for the Lost Laksa
Review: I have been consuming laksa since I first discovered them at the old Malaya Restaurant in Sydney Australia in 1970. After almost 50 years of travel thru Asia in the time since, those first experiences continue to set the benchmark. Perhaps it is the quality of ingredients available in Australia, or perhaps it is an older guy's fond but inaccurate memory. Whatever is the case, this restaurant that purports to specialise in laksa does a terrible disservice to one of the great Asian dishes.While in Penang I tried laksa at three different establishments, one upmarket, the other like this one. They all disappointed. Tinned tuna added to coconut milk with a bland mix of spices does not a laksa make!Thus my lament.If anyone can guide me to laksa heaven please let me know. It will have been a long long wait. And yes, I do know there are two distinctly different types of laksa etc etc.Show less

Author: KopiMochaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Love the cracker
Review: Uniquely Penang. The laksa soup base is thick, and if you are not an asam lover, you can try their coconut laksa. Or better still, they offer a combination of both asam and coconut laksa in a bowl. Surprisingly the soup is not spicy hot or too sour but after a few minutes, I start to perspire from within. They will offer you some prawn paste to add to the soup. The prawn paste does not have any strong unpleasant smell and you can add a few drop to a spoonful of soup to taste the difference. It actually reduce the spiciness and add flavour to the soup. And I love the cracker dipped into the laksa soup. Definitely worth a detour!Show less

Author: Wolf D K

Author: D N
Title: Best laksa, very clean, good price
Review: One of our famous Malaise restaurant in Penang, Malaysia, well known for the laksa. The lady owner is very fluent in English, and very kind. She greeted us, explained the menu , recommended the dishes that we should try in order to compare with other places. The price was very reasonable compare to the quality and quantity of the food. There is AC, the restaurant is very clean.I had laksa at few other restaurants, but I had to admit that her laksa was super, the soup was thick, the noodle was chewy, the flavor and taste were just right.We were curious about the blue rice. She went out of her way describing how it was prepared, from the extraction of the color from the flower to cooking the rice. She even demonstrated to us how to extract the blue color from the flower. My wife shared with her another plant, the magenta leave, which also gives a similar color as the flower that she used but requires much less labor and can be preserved in the freezer for a longer period.Her desserts were also excellent. It may not fit for Americans, since they were not sweet enough.Her restaurant closed at 8 pm , but we were there until 8:30 pm, she treated us like family even we just met for the first time. She picked the flower seeds for my to try plant it at home.Highly recommended this restaurant if you are in Penang.Show less

Author: happydevo55Portland, Oregon
Title: We went for the laksa, but a bit dissappointed
Review: We went for the Laksa after reading reviews saying it was not spicy here. My wife wanted to try it, but unfortunately it was spicy and so she could not eat it. The service was outstanding and the person serving us apologized and explained that Laksa is ALWAYS a bit spicy by its nature and asked if we would like to order something else for my wife. I had the blue rice chicken curry which was pretty good, but I have certainly had better chicken curry rice. My wife ordered a sesame chicken which was only ok, but certainly not good and lacked any sesame flavor. I tried the Laksa that my wife could not eat, but did not care much for the noodles as they reminded me of soba noodles - big thick things, and the broth was quite fishy tasting. I am a fan of Laksa, but this was one of my least favorites I have had. We also had spring rolls which were OK, but a bit on the greasy side. Lastly we had a curry puff which was the best part of the meal by far. The restaurant is cute and clean, and the prices are fair, but we were not impressed with the food, so not likely to come back.Show less

Author: jcktsaoe

Author: r_gnr2003Los Angeles, California
Title: Delicious food in a quiet setting

Author: Albertmah77Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia
Title: Leisure
Review: Was looking for something light and decided to try the super famous penang laksa. Heard about this place but never tried it before. Was pleasantly surprised to say the laksa is up there among the best in Penang; I've lived here 15 years before. And the hidden gem is the cempedak roll. Never had one before and I admit I bought more after tasting it. It is very good. The cendol taste yummy, the gula melaka taste is strong, very authentic. A must try for any serious foodie. Highly recommended. Will come again. Show less

Author: Davobro
Title: Very friendly, good food
Review: We were very happy with our dinner at this restaurant. In particular the hostess was very gracious, answering all of our questions about the dishes. We can recommend eating here.

Author: simonhughes0705Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not Too Bad
Review: Was keen to try some good Assam laksa while in Penang for the first time and this place was highly recommended. Environment pleasant (very clean) and attentive staff. Laksa was quite good but room for improvement to be top class.Worth a visit especially if you prefer the aircon and dont want a really rustic experience.Show less

Author: lisawT9835SY
Title: Nice food
Review: Very nice food. The owner is a young lady. Very kind and introduced us great food. Clean and new place. Recommend to people who visit Penang.

Author: gheeyinz
Title: Great laksa
Review: clean environment and good laksa with umami crispy cracker. I love the music selection here it's jazzy. Got aircon to beat the heat while eating laksa.

Author: timmiulderUtrecht, The Netherlands
Title: Very good Laksha
Review: This place serves some seriously delicious Laksa Nyonya! The restaurant is very clean, and the interior is nicely decorated. Very kind host, she even provided a small meal (blue rice, egg and soup) for my son at no cost, amazing! I will definitely will visit Again, very much recommended!Show less

Author: Adventurer824206
Title: Fresh & delicious 😋
Review: The best meal I’ve had in Penang so far! Fresh, delicious, great service, clean, welcoming. The mango sago-Lucius was delightful 😋

Author: 394jesd
Title: Tasty soup
Review: My boyfriend and I loved our Laksa’s. The lady who ran the restaurant was so kind and chatty- she informed us what desserts to try and spoke to us about the different types of Laksa. Very good value for money too.

Author: Discover821916
Title: Superb! Delicious food, Probably best in the town.
Review: The restaurant laksa is the signature of the restaurant and the city. Future visitor should try laksa with crunchy prawn crackers. Of course ended with a sweet n melt in mouth sago desert. Will definitely dine in again if visit Penang.

Author: BarryM845
Title: Fantastic food and lovely staff
Review: I ordered something that I wouldn’t usually have and absolutely loved it. The only thing nicer than the food was the lady that runs it, so friendly and helpful. Worth going a little out of your way to eat here.

Author: Charles TPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A refreshing change from the traditional and common Penang Laksa
Review: Although Penang laksa is an indigenous and popular delicacy, I personally don't care for fishy bits swimming in my tamarind mixed broth. Give me the real maccoy laksa, which, for me, is Nonya Laksa.This unassuming eatery offers both options, so I happily ordered what I like and miss in Penang - Nonya Laksa. After all, Penang is a supposedly an enclave of the Peranakans, so why are there so few places which offers Nonya Laksa like this joint?Thankfully, the Nonya Laksa here met my expectation. The taste was good although the broth could have tasted even better had it been served piping hot. Price point was a tad higher than I anticipated. But, then again, the owner has to cover retail space rental cost in town which ain't cheap.I would give this place a rating of 6.5-7 out of 10 for excellent. Give it a try.Show less

Author: laura_ret91
Title: Very fresh- But not our taste
Review: We went there for an early dinner. Via google maps it was very easy to find. As starters we ordered spring rolls and mango rolls. We were at the beginning the only customers-after we ordered a family joined. Unfortunately our starters got then mixed up with the ones of the family but as our laksa came, we didnt need the starters anyway. Still disappointed that it wasnt nötiges singe there were so little guests. The ingredients were fresh, it was our first laksa and tasted ok. Everybody was very nice. The dessert was very good Show less

Author: RandomGuy23Phnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: Limited choise for non-fish eaters
Review: I'm allergic to fish and seafood, so the only laksa I could eat was the vegetarian one. If only a non-fish version, but with meat, were available. My wife loved her one, and mine was good, but I was craving meat. I know it wouldn't be authentic without the fish that is added, but I would have preferred that option. Nice restaurant, though, and the owner spoke excellect English.Show less

Author: YY C

Review: Wonderful food and comfortable place. Assam laksa, laksa lemak - beautifully blended with 'lai fun'. Perfect for slurping up! Perfect Fried cempedak roll  , home made treasure roll, nyonya sago gula malacca,  etc

My husband ordered the nasi lamek and he loved that. Was really nice. We also got the sesame oil chicken and noodles for our little one which went down well as well. Author: R879XYmatthewc
Title: The best

Author: youwh
Title: Better than i expected!
Review: Was not expecting much since each have different taste on food, but the laksa does lives up its shop name and rank in the list!

Author: 292vishnuk
Title: Excellent!!!
Review: Definitely one of the best laksa I have ever had! Homely environment with awesome food...worth the try!

Author: Princess-Sharonz

Lady boss is friendly and honest.
