Service was good and but a word of warning - this is a pricey place by Malaysian standards. If you are on Euros, USD, AUD or SGD then its fine. Go on treat yourself. I seldom sing such high praise after a first visit.Show less

Author: ByxbeeLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent meal
Review: Probably one of the most expensive restaurants in Penang, but given the quality of the food and service, very reasonably priced by US/European standards. It was RM370 for 4 courses for two people, plus 2 glasses of wine.Its a 4 course menu but you get to make your own choices from each section - appetite, main course, vegetable and dessert. They can accommodate vegetarians.Everything we had was delicious, flavorful, and amply sized portions. The service was very good, and the ambiance was nice. It was quiet enough to easily have a conversation, but the live pianist made for a nice environment.Definitely book ahead.Show less

Author: grahamc628
Title: Excellent place for a special meal
Review: Although somewhat expensive by local standards we had a memorable meal at this beautiful restaurant. My wife has dietary issues and the staff were extremely helpful accomodating her needs.

Author: Dan B
Title: Our favorite restaurant in Malaysia
Review: There is a good reason why this is the top rated restaurant in Penang! While I could go on about the fantastic food, service, and ambiance, suffice it to say that we broke our self-imposed travel rule and went back to the same restaurant the next night. The staff greeted us like old friends, remembered our drink preferences, suggested alternative dishes we might want to try. You really do want to eat here!Show less

Author: ajr493Orpington, United Kingdom
Title: Great meal, still a must visit restaurant
Review: I have to confess the heavy rain and the taxi journey conspired to put me in a bad mood before we even entered the restaurant. Then the waiter insisted I order not only my starter and main course but also dessert because "things are running out" - at 20:00 on a Saturday night! I was not thrilled. The food however restored my equilibrium. Bhan xheo and a version of crispy rolls made me feel less homicidal. Then mains of chicken Kapitan and Crispy pork belly with spicy salad and vegetables made everything ok. If I had to be picky, the chicken Kapitan wasn't as good as I've had locally - probably because they used chicken breast rather than thighs and (maybe) the chicken wasn't cooked in the curry sauce. But otherwise, I love Kebaya and the food. Show less

Author: edmunkie
Title: Great treats from Seven Terraces
Review: You haven't been to Penang if you haven't tried dining at Kebaya Restaurant at Seven Terraces. Service is impeccable and food is awesome. You will feel so pampered through the whole experience from the start at the entrance right till they usher you to your seats. Otak otak is a must have and we felt the grilled snapper was grilled to perfection. Soft and supple! Really gotta give props to Benjamin and his fantastic crew in providing us with this unforgettable experience. This is only my first day in Penang and they certainly set the tone right!Great work and i will definitely visit this place again when i am back! They definitely deserve the No.1 spot not only in Georgetown but Penang as well.Show less

Author: LakeanahuacAberdeen, United Kingdom
Title: A Pleasant Evening
Review: My wife and I enjoyed our dinner at Kebaya. The ambiance of the restaurant was amazing.The service from Ming and the rest of the staff was very attentive and friendly. The piano music provided by Jerome was a highlight of the evening. The food was good, especially the Tamarind Beef. The rest of the dishes were ok.Overall a wonderful night.Thank you Show less

Author: marcderbHong Kong, China
Title: Fantastic dining opportunity in Penang
Review: Lovely to come back to our favourite restaurant in Penang. Jackie our host was most welcoming and we had a fabulous dinner... The beef dish is absolutely fantastic as is the spicy prawn curry. The setting is very quaint and makes for a very relaxing evening with superb ambience. We will be back again on our next trip to Penang in December.Show less

Author: WorldTicos
Title: Gracious dining in Georgetown
Review: Did we just travel back 8,771 miles to eat once again at Kebaya? Yup! Had we been thinking about the Tang Yuen dessert all this time......you bet!, and don't even get me started on the Kebaya Tamarind Beef!Dining at Kebaya is to experience Nyonya cuisine with a modern twist as imagined by the creative kitchen in this Peranakan dreamworld.The moment you enter the door, you are greeted by Jackie and the warm sounds of the pianist playing classical music. The mood continues with a room lit by candlelight and period furniture from another more gracious era. Timing of the meal is elegant and not rushed, but one of a thougtful explanation of every dish. While attentive with water/rice, service is never intrusive. A well curated wine selection complimented the complex flavors of the Kebaya Tamarind Beef and the Thai Soft Shell Crabs.Not wanting the evening to be over, we retire to the Baba Bar where we fully expect Bogart & Bacall to be enjoying a nitecap. Dreams being what they are, we will settle for one of Podi's soothing Lemongrass Tea's before retiring back into the night and planning our return to visit Kebaya.Show less

Author: FrilchritschMelbourne, Australia
Title: Our culinary highlight
Review: With the temptation to run around George Town sampling as much as we could, we hadn't realised that the best food and service was right here at Kebaya. We had a degustation menu and all tried something different. Meals were prepared for one but it's a place where food envy gets you and we couldn't help but share everything. Delicious.Show less

Author: beatricel330Kuantan, Malaysia
Title: Great ambience!
Review: The ambience here is really superb! With all the classy furniture, and settings, flawless. Food are great but is a bit too salty for me. Staffs are friendly. They will constantly approach you to offer you extra rice and water. The best thing I have encountered is the staff Ming did an extra mile to provide customer service! He brought me around the hotel and show me. Really amazed with the hotel, is really well maintained. No defect can be spotted! Show less

Author: livingdolldisasteraustralia
Title: Beautiful setting with great service and ok food
Review: Went to kebaya for dinner based on the reviews here and was a little disappointed, i will start off with the good. The interior was really elegant and the staff were efficient, attentive and spoke good English. For appetizers we had the otak otak and miang kham of salmon roe which were both very tasty, for our main course we had the soft shell crab salad and the lamb shank, the soft shell crab was fantastic, but the salad that went with it and the lamb shanks were a little on the sweet side. For the greens we had the sautéed greens which were too salty and drenched in sauce and the wing bean Kerala which was really sweet. Dessert was pana cotta and chocolate fondant, the pana cotta had good flavour, but it was rather firm and had a grainy texture, the chocolate fondant had a very interesting bright yellow liquid centre which tasted strange with the chocolate cake. I had high expectations since it's number one on TripAdvisor so I was a bit disappointed and thought it was a bit of a hit and miss. I don't regret eating there, but I would definitely not eat there again.Show less

Author: Burnt77
Title: Excellent restaurant, great experience!
Review: We were there with a group of 8. The setting is very nice in an old traditional Chinese mansion. The food was fantastic! Great variety and also some innovative variations of dishes that you know. Highly recommended and worth the price.

Author: aprilm179Hong Kong, China
Title: Nice cuisine, Nice Lady Manager
Review: I booked for 8pm 2 weeks in advance and no need to wait for a table. The restaurant with is cosy and elegant, with live pianist playing relaxing music. Only 4-course-menu is served but you can choose options for each appetizer, main, vegetable and dessert. My husband and i choose different of those so that we can try 8 dishes. The food is so delicious. Actually it is a Nyonya and European-Thai mixed fusion cuisine. All servers were polite and spoke fluent English. The lady manager who wore a traditional Nyonya dress is quite charming in the restaurant. She talked to me in English and Cantonese, made us a warm hospitality. The Prawn in coconut and lemongrass sauce, tempura veggie and Tong Yuen is highly recommended.Show less

Author: burryNewcastle, Australia
Title: Lovely evening
Review: We came to this restaurant based on the suggestion of expat friends of ours who live in Penang and know good food. My hubby and I thoroughly enjoyed our lovely meal after many previous evenings eating street food. Everything was beautifully prepared and very tasty. My only surprise was that the yummy tempura vegetables did not come with a dipping sauce, but we made do with the other sauces that accompanied other elements of the main. The pandan panacotta at dessert was my favourite part, as well as the view up in the inside of the terraces as I walked to and from the bathroom. I didn't think it was too expensive for the quality. It was a fairly short stroll from our hotel at the E&O. Thanks for a lovely evening.Show less

Author: Olivier G
Title: Expensive restaurant
Review: It's a really beautiful place inside the 7th terrace hotel, but it's a really expensive restaurant for the meal. Fix menu at 120RM, no other choice. The food is good but not enough for the price... The starter are really small, more amuse-bouche than starter! The staff is correct but not as friendly as the other restaurants in town. And you can't come after 8:00pm...You can find better for cheaper in this beautiful city of Penang...Show less

Author: anav493Singapore, Singapore
Title: Amazing setting but disappointing service
Review: Food and atmosphere could not get better. Although we were quite disappointed with the staff. What you expect from such a good restaurant is some sort of guidance through the menu. We did not get any advice or recommendation from the waiters or the owner. The feeling was more of a money making business than of a culinary experience... Show less

Author: Bobby EK.Lumpur
Title: Up market fine dining!
Review: Located just behind the Chinese Assenbly Hall or Kuan In Temple near Little India, this place is really tuck away. Also known as Seven Terraces which houses I think 18 rooms (aprox. RM700 per night includes breakfast & afternoon tea). They served a set menu only opens for dinner (RM127.20 nett per person with minimum 2 and reservation is a must on weekends). Listed under UNESCO World Heritage Building as well, the interior is well decorated with English and Chinese mother of pearl furniture which includes opium beds! Not to be missed!!!Show less

Author: alejandroa291Punta Arenas, Chile
Title: Marvelous food !
Review: The place is just a dream. Very fifties. Great porcelain dinnerware set. Excelente music. The staff is very friendly but they are not as well trained as suppose to be for a number 1 restaurant at trip advisor. The food is just amazing. Well served and excellent cost benefit for someone used too pay high prices in São Paulo's restaurants. I do recommend. Show less

Author: Nick C
Title: Worthy #1 in Georgetown
Review:
Superb ambiance in an impressive setting

Menu doesn't do the good justice as it was fab - never quite have such great fish and lamb!

Staff v attentive and friendly. Jackie went the extra mile

Author: MarykarFrance
Title: The best in Penang
Review: We booked a table at this beautiful restaurant because we were a bit tired of the simple street food and wanted to eat finer cuisine with good wine. We based our choice on the TripAdvisor rating and it didn't lie. It is really number one in Georgestown. Gorgeous venue, nice interior, delicious food. Would love to come back. Show less

Author: JPSWashington_DCWashington, DC
Title: Stuffy service and average food
Review: The Kebaya is located in a beautifully renovated historic heritage house. While the interior is lovely, the service in the restaurant is somewhat stuffy and I think the appeal of the restaurant is that it is a fixed price menu, that some tourists appreciate more for its price and quantity of food, than for its quality. The starters and entrees were average (we had the much touted lamb and prawn curry), but the desserts were very good. All in all, the restaurant for dinner is overrated.Show less

Author: sandypink1Melbourne, Australia
Title: Deserving of number 1
Review: We went there to dinner as per trip advisor recommendations! It was excellent! A choice of 2 plates each from entree/main and dessert! With a pre dinner drink each and a bottle of wine total price rm 448! Amazing price for such an excellent meal! The staff were very attentive and the ambiance was great! Surrounded by antique furniture and a lovely pianist on the grand piano we couldn't have wanted for anything! We had too much food though as not used to eating so much but just couldn't resist not finishing the meal! Excellent value for money and well worth a visit! Show less

Author: 793jil
Title: Perfect restaurant
Review: Oh it is like having dinner in a museum. The building itself is gorgeous and the interior is splendid. The taste of the course menu is out of this world.

Author: PatfromPerthPerth, Australia
Title: Special Night Out
Review: If you want a special night here - here is the place. Beautifully restored building and excellent service. And the food was magnificent. Every dish every course. Treat yourself to old charm dining in Penang. The highlight of our visit. Got lots of brownie points from the ladies. Show less

Author: cheryloas
Title: Amazing food and deco
Review: The nyonya meal was flavorful and rich with taste. The rice has a sticky feeling but it's amazingly delicious. The environment was superb. There was a live piano performance when dining.

Author: jjbali
Title: delightful experience
Review:
Through email I booked a table for a friend's birthday celebration, response was quick, detailed and clear.
the room is truly wonderful, elegantly designed. Service is very attentive whilst quality of food is exceptional.
This is a place not to be missed whilst visiting Penang.

Author: robbos644Perth
Title: Our perfect celebration
Review: The ambience is from another time. The relaxing welcome and attentive staff put you at ease from the start. Then comes the meal. Our helpful waiter guided us through the options with attentiveness to our likes etc. The meal was of top quality and we savoured all the traditional spices and fragrances. The manageress was welcoming and surprised us with a delicious sweet treat for our anniversary. Thank you we will be back one day and highly recommend.Show less

Author: macsymMcGregor, South Africa
Title: Captivating Keybaya
Review: Loved everything about this restaurant - the ambience, the decor, the pianist, all the waiters and last but certainly not least, the food. Being able to go shoeless was also a joy! It was so enjoyable that we had dinner there every night during our 3 night stay at The Seven Terraces. The menu offers plenty of choice and everything sampled was delicious although I particularly enjoyed the Otak Otak (red snapper cooked with garlic and turmeric in a pastry case) and served with the most delicious sauce and also the Prawn Geng, the flavour of which was absolutely spot on. Wines are somewhat more limited and like most places in Asia relatively expensive. The lovely Aruna makes a fabulous mojito. Prices may be higher than the average in George Town but it is excellent value. Highly recommended!Show less

Author: TRR99
Title: Birthday meal
Review: Had my 50th birthday meal here whilst on holiday. The restaurant staff were warm and friendly and made use very welcome and the surroundings were spectacular. The food here was superb and the choice fantastic. We chose meals and shared them so we could all experience the variety. The snapper, tamarind beef and Hong bak lamb were stand out dishes and desserts were also very good. Wine was expensive - starting price RM145 but was good. Would definitely visit again. Show less

Author: Tash_SplashMelbourne, Australia
Title: Penang elegance
Review: Kebaya was a lovely change away from the hustle and bustle of the street food markets. Service was great and we weren't fussed over. The building, decorations and ambience were perfect as was the pianist playing in the background. The food was unassuming with delicious flavours and the wine list was ok. I would highly recommend this restaurant for those looking for a nice change to street food.Show less

Author: the_gh0striderBerlin, Germany
Title: ...amazing...
Review: I am usually not easy to impress but for the Kebaya restaurant I have to say "Life is great if you visit". I have lived for a long time in Penang and never found a restaurant like this which gives a modern interpretation of Peranakan Cuisine. Exciting!Great Selection of well-executed drinks, fantastic attentive service, a chic amabiance all well combined with amazing food! If I have to critize one thing - then only the fact that you have to choose a menu which is for me fine but was almost too much for my wife.Anyway, lets talk about the food and with the only small criticism that I have. The Kebaya Ban Xeo needs improvements - This Vietnamese Dish was done in a style that is far from the original and was rather tasting flat. The seafood pancake as it is was not reflected well.... but this disappears behing a great version of Otak-Otak, a super well spiced and prepared Chicken Kapitan or the Tamarind Beef...the side dishes such as Kerabu and Sambal Goreng are just "burner" ( and they are spicy). However, the nail of the night were surely the dessert... The Pandan Creme Brulee - world class and Tang Yuen... well, my tongue is still dancing Tango if I think about the food.All in all - the is be far the most interesting Penang reflecting restaurant I have been to. Guys, keep moving - you are great!Food Factor: 5***** (plus) Drink Factor: 5*****Value Factor: 5*****Ambiance Factor: 5***** Soul Factor: 5***** (plus)Visit Factor: a MUST try before you DIE!!!!!Show less

Author: Jonism85
Title: good local cuisine with a modern touch
Review: excellent service and food.as the patron of the hotel, we have the option of ordering ala carte. this is much better than ordering full set meals for all 4 of us as the portion would turned out huge. the entree: otak otak was exceptionally food. special mention to the snapper in the main section and dessert was no less than ordinary. highly recommended for those who desire to try a peranakan cuisine in a comfortable environment with excellent service.Show less

Author: Gongboy53Woolooware, Australia
Title: Exceptional
Review: Firstly thanks to the Maitre ' d for getting me in on a busy Saturday night with no booking. This is the best meal that I have had in Malaysia. I lived everything about this place.The food was amazing. The service exceptional. The ambiance great.It deserves the accolades. Show less

Author: night1809
Title: Extraordinary
Review: This is a remarkable restaurant with a very interesting menu. A must visit if you are a fan of peranakan food and culture

Author: moooxVienna, Austria
Title: trés chic and amazing food
Review: We had a great time there and dropped in without a reservation. The food was quite a surprise (sous vide cooked meat and all). The location is amazing anyway and the staff is superfriendly. I would say it is a must see for everyone who is not on a budget and passes through Georgetown.Show less

Author: TracyORyanBrisbane, Australia
Title: Assembly line
Review: This was my second visit and again I felt like I was on an assembly line. The set courses arrived far too quickly to be freshly prepared and we were done and out within an hour. It may have been our order but nothing was especially interesting or tasty. However I'm not sure how much the restaurant has decided this is all ok as a significant number of diners turned up in shorts and thongs as if it was a cafe rather than a smart restaurant.Show less

Author: KRafteryLimerick, Ireland
Title: Great food in classic setting
Review: Ate dinner hear. It was a Set menu-3 courses for reasonable fee. Was a pretty plush setting with piano playing in background. Some western options on the menu given a n Asian twist. I had the lamb which was fantastic. Highly recommended. Only negatives were the very expensive price of the wine and the fact that a number of the wine options were not available. Show less

Author: Meeghan ZMumbai, India
Title: Superb Setting for Delicious Local Flavors
Review: The perception that Kebaya is expensive is the greatest illusion about this restaurant. For the price, the quality and quantity of their set meal goes above and beyond. The good thing about this perception is that it attracts a very well-dressed crowd for dinner. We greatly enjoyed the food and will return on our next trip to Penang.Show less

Author: mariecassandra
Title: Great service, yummy food, highly recommended
Review: It's not the best Peranakan/Nyonya food that I have tasted, but it comes close. What you get here is a packaged experience - the service, the ambiance, the nice authentic decor. I would recommend this to tourists visiting Penang. Call to book a table first!

Author: vincentc816Singapore, Singapore
Title: A modern rendition of traditional Chinese Nyonya dishes
Review: Situated in the Seven Terraces hotel in Penang, Kebaya is truly a place not to be missed if you happen to visit Penang. The dining room is beautiful, the service fantastic and as for the food, we had an excellent meal and by far the best dining experience of our entire stay. There were 4 of us including our 2 children and we ordered dishes from the menu including one appetiser, one main, one green and one desserts for 3 persons (12 dishes in total, which we shared). All the dishes were excellent and some highlights were the Chao Tom (minced prawn grilled on a skewer), the Miang Kham of Salmon Roe, the organic roast pork and Gula Melaka Mousse. We had a great evening and would recommend this restaurant anytime.Show less

Author: PDT1809
Title: A highlight of our visit
Review: Kebaya is a magnificent restaurant offering delicious Malaysian food. It is In the Seven Terraces Hotel (also wonderful) and feels like you are dining in the home of a wealthy Georgetown businessman in the 19th century. This is a must do in Georgetown.

Author: Simon W
Title: Delicious - on a different level from everywhere else
Review: Peranakan cooking taken to another level. Kebaya is like a top London restaurant but in the heart of old Georgetown. I could happily have eaten there every night of my stay. Totally delicious food in an amazing (and quite camp) setting. Fun staff and a relaxed atmosphere. The best!Show less

Author: Timbo9
Title: First Class
Review: We were recommended to the Kebaya restaurant and we weren't disappointed.   Amazing food, almost too much, but everything about it was great.   Would highly recommend as a top notch dining destination to mix in to the great many options in Penang

Author: RicP950London, United Kingdom
Title: Truly elegant
Review: Kebaya truly deserves its number one spot. The food is divine and very elegantly presented. The staff are friendly and helpful. Great piano player. We loved it. As you walk along the street you could easily miss Kabaya. The traditional terrace house front look like any other in Penang, if a little smarter. Behind is the voluminous Kebaya, restaurant if the Seven Terraces hotel (because seven of the traditional Terraces have been knocked through - get it?)The food formula is delightfully simple: fixed price, choose one starter, one main, one veg, one desert (rice is included). You can add extra dishes if you wish, but you probably won't need to as portions are generous. We had crispy prawns and an interesting Asian take on mini tacos: delicious. For mains some wonderful belly pork accompanied by a flavoursome prawn curry in a Thai-style coconut milk sauce. The tempura veg were delicious. Expensive by Penang standards, but very good value. We will definitely return. Show less

Author: cprsjo
Title: Delish authentic Peranakan dinner
Review: I'm glad I made a reservation a week before coming here. This beautiful Peranakan house serves delicious authentic 4-course Peranakan dinner set at 2 timing: 6pm and 8pm. I had amazing otak-otak, prawn geng, sambal goreng, and pandan creme brulee. Highly recommended!

Author: constantinm2015Bucharest, Romania
Title: I expected more from the best restaurant in Penang
Review: We live for 3 months in Penang, we've tried already a few good places and we heard of course about the best rated here. Reading a few reviews, we have decided to try a dinner in Kebaya. 4 courses fixed price of $40 per person, without any other choice, normally. Maybe someone needs just a drink and an appetizer, maybe I just joined my family after another dinner and I'm not into another one.. Anyway the supervisor was kind and made an exception for us, because he considered we want to make a fuss from this, not my intention though. All these because they are opened 4 hrs/ day and they have to cover their costs, so every adult seated has to take the 'menu'. Beside this unpleasant situation, food was good, not exceptional though. I've tried duck, not much better than at Goodall. Pork was soft and tasted good. Delicious desert. Bottom line, a place to try, but you'll never see me another time here. Enjoy!Show less

Author: JoL510Sydney, Australia
Title: Best meal in Malaysia
Review: This was easily the best meal we had in our two week trip around Malaysia. The restaurant is beautiful and the service is great. We arrived and ordered both the house speciality cocktails - one of which is made with nutmeg juice which was really interesting. To start we had the otak otak to start and the betel leaves both of which were delicious but the betel leaves were one of the most special dishes we had ever tried. For main we had the lamb (a must have) and the duck with beans and tempura veggies on the side. For dessert we ordered the pandan crime brûlée and the rice dumplings. These were both so good it was hard to pick a favourite but the rice dumplings probably won by a whisker. Nice wine list too. All up it cost two of us around MYR500 (with two cocktails and a bottle of wine). Expensive for Malaysia but cheap for fine dining! Show less

Author: Philippo ASydney, Australia
Title: One of the Best meals I have eaten ion the last 30 years.
Review: The Kebaya restaurant is part of a new, boutique hotel , Sevan Terraces, located on the North end of Georgetown. Easy walking to Love Lane and both Little India and China Town. Restauant serves classic Indonesian and Straits Chinese Nyonya dishes but with a modern twist...the result is sublime. It is a fixed price , 4 course menu. Each of the 4 course have numerous offerings so that all palates are catered for. Excellent value for money considering the quality of the food and variety. It is extremely popular so booking is essential. Many people were turned away while we ate. Simply a must do...and one we will defiantely visit on our next trip to Penang.Show less

Author: movingsin
Title: Probably the best meal I have ever had in a restaurant
Review: Oh my goodness, this food. Sure, the atmosphere, amazingly sweet waiters, beautiful decor and lounge piano music, too. But my goodness, this food. My visit to Kebaya has gone down in my restaurant book as one of my top three, if not number one, meals I have ever had. This is a set 4-course menu of Nyonya (Penang Straits Chinese) style food, but with a twist - each dish surprises your tongue with more flavour than you thought it could handle and leaves you so satisfied, so unbelievable content and happy, that all you can do is regret you didn't book in for a second, or third, or fourth evening to try every single dish.Show less

Author: finch496Barcelona, Spain
Title: Wonderful dinner.
Review: We stopped by one evening to make a booking for the following night - which was happily taken, despite our ragged appearance after a full day exploring George Town. The next evening - dressed and smelling more appropriately - we were treated to a great dining experience.We were very impressed with the menu and thoroughly recommend the slow cooked beef, and we were extremely impressed with the drinks menu. It offered several price ranges and was very well put together and would keep most people very happy. The cocktails were impressive and I'm happy to say that my negroni was one of the best I've had anywhere in Asia.The only complaint - and this is minor - is that we felt service was a bit rushed at our 8pm sitting, but it was a matter of a few minutes here and there - understandable on a Sunday night! Staff were friendly and attentive and service was close to impeccable. We were impressed some time later when we returned to George Town and stayed at Seven Terraces when two waiters at breakfast remembered us from nearly two weeks prior when we dined at Kebaya.Kebaya is thoroughly recommended for an excellent meal and gorgeous surrounds - it is truly deserving of being regarded as one of, if not the, best restaurants in George Town.Show less

Author: Orator11Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious food and pleasant ambience
Review: We were moving from Cheong Fatt Tze to the 7 Terraces, so wanted to check out the hotel. When we saw Kebaya, we decided to have dinner there as it was high-end and different from the usual char kway teow and assam laksa.The food did not disappoint. We especially loved the starter of joo he (squid) crispy popiah, eaten on a lettuce leave with chilli, basil and mint leaves. It was heavenly. The other starter reminded me if a deconstructed pie ti, and looked like a taco. It was also very good.For our mains, we had five-tiered pork in rendang sauce (one of the specials of the night), and beef sou vide for 72 hours in tamarind. Both portions were generous and both were cooked well and went great with the fluffy white rice. The rendang, particularly, was rich and tasty. On hind sight, though, perhaps we should have gone with a slightly different main course such as duck or snapper as both meat courses were slightly the same in terms of texture, consistency and taste.For greens, we had vegetable tempura - excellent - and sambal goreng, which was a stir fried mixture of long beans, snow peas and sliced baby corn.Dessert was a little of a let down though. The gula melaka was a tad too sweet while the chempedak (jackfruit) pudding, which I expected to be stronger, was very bland.The rose wine we ordered was a tad young and slightly vinegary I felt, but my wife said it was okay. The platewear was exquisite, and set off the food well.Service was okay. The two male staff who served us were very attentive and helped to enhance the dinner experince but the other staff just milled around. We asked one of them for sambal belachan but it never arrived even after 15 minutes. When we asked our male Malay server, we got it in a minute.We had the 4 course dinner and the meal, including drinks, was slightly north of M$300. Overall, it was a great meal.Show less

Author: fionayeoh
Title: Delicious local food...
Review: Food that really can represent Penang....excellent service... Great heritage house... The food is great for me but a little bit too spicy for my children... Good experience for us as even we live in Penang but never notice about this excellent restaurant... Love it...

Author: WkT22
Title: Romantic and exquisite place for dining
Review: This place is welly recommended by a lot of connoisseur and experience food lover. They converted the old houses into this very unique restaurant where they decorated the whole places with real antiques which is totally impressive. Apart from the setup of course the meal their provide is top notch and yummy. Please don't forget the tasty desert as well.Show less

Author: CNMItravels
Title: Serene and beautiful
Review: We'd just like to add our praise for the delicate combination of flavours, that made for an outstanding dinner, in the most beautiful of settings. A very memorable venue.

Author: Neil MSouth Queensferry, United Kingdom
Title: High end fushion cuisine
Review: It was a lovely dining experience set in sumptuous surroundings. It is very fine dining and I’m not sure if you can gentrify predominately Chinese/Asian food and present it in a nouvelle cuisine way, and still hold true to the original. That is just my viewpoint. This however does not detract from a quality, tasty and lovely meal set in a fantastic dining room with a lovely courtyard beyond. An expensive meal in Penang terms, but worth the cost for the overall experience. Show less

Author: koidivemalaysia
Title: Excellent Ambience nyonya/baba restaurant
Review: Being a baba and from penang. I grew up surrounded by all things baba/nyonya heritage. Kudos to the owner ( christopher) on the layout of the restaurant. It is stunningly beautiful and the ambience is just right. The food as quoted is a fusion of indo/ peranakan nyonya dish.. If you are looking for the old traditional type of nyonya cooking don't expect here. Go somewhere else. However, I find it refreshing with this fusion cooking. I strongly recommend the kerabu, duck, otak otak, pie tee, lamb, chiap chai(green veg) and especially the roast pork. All the dessert is great.. Price is reasonable.I find KEBAYA DININGROOM especially on the ambience is just great! Show less

Author: mattandamy2015Fleet, United Kingdom
Title: Stunning design
Review: This restaurant is set within the hotel. A stunning decadent dining room with food to match! A fixed price menu you choose from each course... It really was impeccable. I had lemongrass prawns, tempura vegetables, prawn curry and a passion fruit and coconut panacotta. One of the best and most memorable meals I've ever had out. Reasonably priced in uk standards worth every penny! A must do for exquisite Nyoyan cuisineShow less

Author: Mpk1970
Title: Superb food
Review: We went to dinner here with a large group and so were fortunate enough to experience a wide range of the dishes.  Each was very good, but highlights included the betel leaf entree, the prawn curry main and the pineapple dessert.

Author: Susan S
Title: Good food, nice atmosphere, stellar staff
Review: Delicious food in a relaxed atmosphere.  The staff is attentive without hovering.  The perfect "real restaurant" alternative to the wonderful street food of Penang.

Author: SeacroftKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Klassy Kebaya
Review: They have an unusual but extremely successful ordering policy at this fine restaurant in the Seven Terraces boutique hotel. Each diner orders a starter, main course, vegetable and dessert. So with three of us eating we had three of each.And the servings are most generous. So we had quite a feast. And a feast of waonderful food. The starters of pai tee, ban xeo and otak-otak were wonderful introductions to the main courses of Thai soft shell crab, delicate roast pork Chinese style and a prawn geng curry which was spicy and cream with six or more large prawns. The tempura vegetables were my favourite. Desserts were all tempting but we loved the chocolate fondants with an unusual lime filling. This is a wonderful dining experience and we could have returned two or three times during our stay in lovely Penang.Show less

Author: cristen12
Title: Great dinner
Review: Went for my wife's birthday. Had a great time. Beautiful place with rich history. Had the for course meal. The New Zealand beef is amazing.

Author: Julie ZDubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: The best restaurant we have been to in a long, long time!
Review: Elaine and I visited Kebaya tonight, what a fantastic evening! Amazing food, fabulous ambience and outstanding service. Thank you to Dinesh, Jackie and chef Zac. So good we have booked to go again on Tuesday in our own designed kebaya's!! A true gem in Georgetown, number one restaurant and deserves to be.Show less

Author: zeljkon534Sydney, Australia
Title: Fantastic meal and exceptional service!
Review: The food is excellent! The meal is a 4 course set menu but with about 4-6 choices for each course. The flavours in each course were fantastic.We had a family dinner here with our two young kids and the staff were very helpful with suggestions that might best suit the kids. Dining room is beautiful and complemented by some live piano music. It was an all around fantastic meal and overall experience.Show less

Author: Nicholas BNottingham, United Kingdom
Title: Amazing meal
Review: Went here for my partner's 30th birthday celebration whilst we were in Penang.It is a 4 course menu but there is lots of choice. I cannot remember exactly what I had but each course was absolutely amazing and not too expensive either.Highly recommended - will definitely return when we are next in Penang.Show less

Author: Sudesh77Hong Kong, China
Title: Didn't live up to the hype
Review: Heard much about this restaurant, especially since it was rated #1 on TripAdvisor. Being Malaysians ourselves, we took our friends from HK to the restaurant to savour 'supposedly' one of the best Nyonya cuisines in Penang.Probably it was our timing that we visited the restaurant, as they had a big group from Hong Kong who had booked up the place for a day (the day after our dinner night). We tried ordering all their famous dishes, which included the lamb. Low and behold, we were told it was not available that evening because there was not enough lamb as it has been reserved for the next day. Fine, then we asked for the otak otak, and had the same response.Didn't end there, the waiter came back to us after that saying that some dishes we ordered was not available as they finished the raw ingredients. Seriously? This is supposed to be a fancy (and pricey) restaurant, and you can actually finish your raw ingredients? Same went for the desserts.On the plus side, whatever we ordered did taste good, and the ambiance was unique as you feel that you have been transported back to the the 70s heydays. The staff were ok, and were apologetic to us, but it makes the restaurant look bad. Just because they had a big booking, doesn't mean they wouldn't have planned for enough?Would I go again? No. I think there are better places to eat on the island. It's Penang, the best in the world.Show less

Author: Ty DSydney, Australia
Title: Amazing gorgeous place.
Review: How romantic. Piano player and heritage restaurant. Amazing welcome from a cool lady and awesome service from every staff member. The pork was lovely the duck was even better. Big servings. Not cheap but worth every cent. Highly recommended for the special night and special person. I just loved it. Show less

Author: PassionatehawkerMelbourne, Australia
Title: 2nd visit in 3 years
Review: This is our second visit to Kebaya - even better second time. Service is wonderful, the room is beautiful and the food is delicious. This is really fine dining and not to be done on the cheap. That said the quality of the food, service etc is remarkable value by Australian standards. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: danigreMelbourne, Australia
Title: An experience not to be missed
Review: The building is gorgeous. The service was attentive. The food was amazing. Even when a dish was delivered that I was then worried about not liking....it was fantastic! Don;t eat lunch as it is a lot of food and is a set three course with individual dish choices and is a lot of food. i seriously considered going back. There is a lot of cheaper food in penang but the whole experience was worth it an certinaly a lot cheaper than the same experience at home. I was also worried about being a solo traveller here but it was certainly not a problem and i was made to feel very comfortable.Show less

Author: Tita W
Title: So much food but so yummy
Review: Must do reservation (it's usually full) and must go with very hungry tummy. The portions are huge and since you can't order less (3 dishes + rice + dessert for every pax) you might end up eating too much. Saying all that the foods are really tasty. I would describe it as original local food freshen up with interesting choice of western ingredients yet still not running away from the authentic taste. The ambience is also good though can be a bit too noisy if you have family with kids around. Anyway I will definitely recommend this place if you enjoy your food and want some "upscale" restaurant experience :-) Show less

Author: Intrepidation
Title: More style than substance
Review: Overall ambience is incredible with beautiful architecture inspired by local nyonya dwellings. Service is attentive and polite. Our starters Meng Kiam & Chohnthom were original and delightfully unique . However the main course dishes left a lot to be desired . The Chicken Kapitan was way too spicy , had a flat taste and was flavorless. The Beef in tamarind sauce was too salty, killing off the subtlety of the spices.Again you get the impression the dishes were prepared by an enthusiastic but inexperienced chef. The deserts were pretty much average , pale imitations of the original versions. If you have an Asian palate, weaned on rich and delicious Nyonya cuisine, you will be sorely disappointed as it lacks the underlying flavor, flair and subtlety. Also the price charged is many times that of authentic Nyonya fare. However if you are unfamiliar with the nuances of wondrous Nyonya food, you might well leave Kebaya inspired and amazed. Show less

Author: Fritz19Singapore, Singapore
Title: Exquisite!
Review: This has got to be some of the best tasting Asian food I've had in a while. Flavours are bold without being overwhelming. Portion sizes are decent and great for sharing and good excellent value for money (although may be considered pricey for Penang standards. I thought it was well worth it and by far the best meal we had in Penang. Also try My Nyonya Favourites for home cooked Peranakan food, which is dirt cheap and fantastic.Show less

Author: Rod S
Title: OMG
Review: There is a reason this restaurant is No 1 in Georgetown, don't bypass it! Fantastic food, service and setting.

Author: OliviaodeleSingapore, Singapore
Title: very good nonya food
Review: fine dine setting that doesnt look very child friendly, the food serving were little but its very high quality, and expensive but we felt its worth it, difficult to find by taxi as there are no sign, look for the hotel instead, nonya food dont have much selection for kids so better bring your own, must order the beef and roasted pork, i hope to be back soon for the best nonya food i ever had Show less

Author: donk28Singapore, Singapore
Title: Can't be bettet
Review: I did some research about this restaurant before our visit to Penang .I gathered that the food was good and the service depend on your luck.We walked from Kimberly rd to the restaurant located at Steward Rd in a hot late afternoon. When we reached there around 515pm we realised that dinner starts at 6pm. We asked the staff if we could go in to wait and after seeing us 3 adults 1 young child standing and one sleeping in my arms and visibly tired and hot he let us in. What's more he let us rest on a sofa so that I can rest my sleeping child. While we wait a staff by the name of Dinesh asked if we want any drink and did we make any reservation. We did not and he told us it was fully booked. We were really disappointed and told him that we had walked a distance to reached here. In the end he arranged a table for us with a baby child without us asking. He also went thru the menu and recommended the dishes to us considering we had 2 young children.I must admit the review is spot on on the food . They were really delicious and appealing . For the service we received, I don't think it was pure luck but genuine customer service . Dinesh even came out of the restaurant to return our change after we boarded the taxi . Overall, I give them 3 thumbs up - excellent service, attentiveness and food.Show less

Author: LittleStar2016Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Excellent service with impeccable food
Review: An excellent indochina and nyonya-styled restaurant nestled in the heart of Penang that should not be missed!Highly recommend having 'Tang Yuan' - glutinous ‘onde one’ rice balls stuffed with coconut simmered in Melaka palm sugar and served with a warm coconut broth - as a dessert to end the exquisite dining experience at Kebaya.Show less

Author: James DGreater Melbourne, Australia
Title: A special place to finish off a wonderful holiday
Review: Georgetown is a wonderful place.....and so is Batu Ferringhi where we stayed at the Shangri La. So for our last night in Penang we went to Seven Terraces which has the Kebaya restaurant.....WOW fantastic food and a beautiful place ! If you visit Georgetown GO TO KEBAYA !! you won't be disappointed.Show less

Author: lulubilu
Title: Not up to the hype!
Review: We were looking forward to be blown away by something new but it was very average peranakan food -the dishes were mediocre-nothing innovative at all! The desserts were also disappointing - not as sophisticated as we expected. Not somewhere we would recommend anyone except to view the beautiful courtyard on the way to the loo!Show less

Author: Suzanne DWellington, New Zealand
Title: The highlight of our trip to Penang
Review: Firstly, Kebaya is beautiful - set in restored 19th century buildings with beautiful furnishings, and meals are served from traditional patterned Peranakan ceramics. Dress up a bit and you might feel like you're back in a bygone age of elegance.Dinner is set menu / 3 course degustation: for each course, you get to choose from a range of dishes (including green sides for the main course) and they are presented so the whole table can share. The dishes are strongly influenced by traditional Peranakan cooking but they are not museum pieces; the food is executed with modern style. At RM120 per head plus drinks, it is not cheap by local standards but I have never eaten food this good at anywhere near this price in the West.We got good guidance from Benjamin as to what I could and couldn't eat due to dietary restrictions - I took his recommendation for a starter with reluctance but it turned out to be one of my favourite dishes of the evening (miang kham: salmon roe, coconut, shrimp, lime and nuts wrapped up in fresh betel leaves - light, fresh and flavoursome). My partner described his starter of pork man tou as 'like a traditional pork steamed bun, but really really good'.For the mains we had the lor ark confit duck in local spices, which was the highlight of the meal. in short - best duck *ever*. Crispy skin, juicy meat, fantastic sauce, mmmmmm. We also had the tamarind beef, a piece of slow-cooked shoulder - this seemed a bit unremarkable at first bite compared to the duck but the subtle sweet flavour of the glaze and the amazing sous vide texture really grew on us as we worked our way through it. The sides were interesting too: the greens were exquisite and while the wing bean salad was not what we were expecting (Benjamin warned we might find it a bit spicy for our tastes) it was very flavoursome and a good counterpoint to the richness of the meat and rice.My partner really enjoyed the gula melaka mousse and sponge dessert, with its caramel flavours, and I enjoyed the striking-looking tang yuen - you would need to be a fan of glutinous rice dumplings to enjoy these, and luckily I am.Service is attentive without being overpowering, and advice was freely given when asked for. The wine list provided a good range of by the glass choices. Try the nutmeg juice-based Georgetown Cooler cocktail while you're deciding what to eat, it's certainly an authentic and distinctive local flavour.Show less

Author: wolfraidersBoston, Massachusetts
Title: amazing food, albeit a little pricy
Review: food was fantastic. Slight twist to your typical Peranakan food. quality was exceptional. some of the dishes were average but on the whole it was excellent. service was also very pleasant and attentive. Would definitely come back again. price wise it is one of the more expensive places in malaysia but it was definitely worth while.Show less

Author: rewib
Title: Five star food and ambience
Review: Authentic peranakan food served in fabulous surroundings. From the moment you enter, you are greeted by friendly staff smartly attired, live grand piano music and an interior that is truly tasteful. The four course menu designed for sharing is a great way to enable small groups can sample a range of the deliciously authentic and flavoursome food. The menu is adequately descriptive down to the level of spiciness. Well priced for the quality and ambience - I will be sending people here and coming back myself!Show less

Author: Samagal2000
Title: Very nice place good cuiaine
Review:
Service was very good. The first course was not exceptional. The rest was excellent. On evening a set menu of 4 courses was served.
Unfortunately not all deserts where available at the end of the meal.

Author: ThrillingMeLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Must Visit for a Cocktail... or two
Review: The Bababar or the Baba Bar (been described differently by different people in Penang) is tucked away at one far end of the Kebya restaurant which is in itself attached to the beautiful Seven Villas complex. Everything here is just beautiful in terms of attention to detail, a demonstrated high care factor, and an almost slavish attachment to its colonial past. We dropped into the bar in between lunch and dinner service and had the bar almost entirely to ourselves as staff reset the room, and yet the cocktail barman and duty manager ensured we were very well care for. Normally I'm a bit dismissive about the term mixologist to describe a cocktail barman - but this fellow was incredible. Within the context of Penang and local competition - this is not a cheap bar experience by any stretch of the imagination but well worthwhile. Next visit we'll need to actually book in for dinner!Show less

Author: robinb607Manila, Philippines
Title: " Do you have a reservation? "
Review: We arrived reasonably early at 1900 hours to be met with "Do you have a reservation?". My experience of this question is that if a table can be found a memorable evening will follow. So it proved.The room itself is a treat to the eye, a beautiful conversion within a renovated Chinese courtyard mansion. Dinner was a treat, beautifully served by staff who made the time to stop and chat. What was ultra impressive was that my companion asked for a seasoning that was not available in the kitchen-the waiter took the trouble to exit the building to a nearby shop to met her request. Talk of the extra mile! The pianist expertly played medleys of well known opera arias and Chopin. Magic!This was our last night in Georgetown, Penang. An unforgettable evening to round off our six day stay.Show less

Author: damiens1960
Title: Sophisticated Fine Dining in Penang
Review: Believe me it's not easy to find 5 star dining in Penang, despite the vast number of restaurants that say they are. But this is the real thing.Kebaya is sublime. The decor, the service, the wine choices, the food. To boot, it is within the Seven Terraces Hotel, a unique boutique hotel hidden in the depths of George Town. Do yourself a favour, find someone is enjoys fine food, fine wine and good taste and head here ☺Show less

Author: JenniferITGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Outstanding experience
Review: The setting is stunning, the food is delicious and Benjamin and his staff went out of their way to make our dining experience special. It was a busy night with some large bookings but their service and assistance was second to none. Would highly recommend Kebaya restaurant.Show less

Author: MY58Singapore
Title: Prime dining experience
Review: We had dinner there recently and enjoyed it very much. Beautiful, elegant ambience, good service, and creative, delicious fusion Peranakan-Indo Chinese cuisine. Kebaya is the restaurant of Seven Terraces, a beautiful boutique hotel housed in seven adjoining restored Peranakan shophouses. They have two fixed dinner sittings (6pm and 8pm). Reservations are necessary if you don't want to risk disappointment as they are often quite full. Kebaya is a definite must do if you are looking for a memorable dinner experience in Penang. The dining room is large and elegant with live piano music and beautifully restored Peranakan features. The food we had was creative and delicious, and portions fairly generous. For RM120+ per person, we had a 4 course dinner (appetiser, main course, greens, dessert), and got to choose from a list of options for each course. We had grilled chicken kapitan and tamarind beef for mains, and tang yuen (glutinous rice balls in coconut broth) and Gula Melaka mousse for dessert. All very good, and creatively conceived and presented. A great dining experience.Show less

Author: Rebecca MBanbury, United Kingdom
Title: Lovely settings, well presented and good food but the service is lacking..
Review: We were told this was THE restaurant of Georgetown and has good reviews, we went with another couple from our hotel E and O who also recommended it. Having booked ahead we were not greeted, in fact there seemed to be some confusion by the staff. Eventually we were shown to our table. There are two sittings, 6-8 and 8-11we chose the latter. The interior is similar to the adjoining hotel full of antiques and curios. There is a set four course meal at 120 RM or separate plus wine. There then began confusion over the choice of wine, at first we were told there wasn't enough of the wine for four glasses....only two ....??? Then after our friend's protracted insistance there magically appeared a full bottle of the same wine....?obviously a ploy....and only sorted because we asked for the manager( who never appeared to talk to us) anyway, on with the rest of the evening, the menu looked good, our friends took a long time in deciding what to eat as they have health problems then after taking our order the waiter said that their choice was not on the menu...!!!! Why not tell us this when he gave us the menues?? Three of the sets were not available ! Not a good start to our introduction to this place. We found it difficult to talk at a normal pitch as the piano player was far too loud.That being said when the food finally arrived it was well presented and good, starters were a little over crispy ie dry but well what the hell, we knew it wasn't going to be perfect. Mains were adequate in size and the lamb, prawns and duck were good, nothing to rave about tho( we are foodies so taste is important). We hadnt chosen desserts and when the eaiter brought us the menues he told us we had to hurry up because they would be closing soon......!!!!!! How rude is that??? We chose to ignore his comments and he went off to pull on his inhaler.... puddings were fine, chocolate cake oozing a lovely orangey centre, jellies in coconut cream and young coconut shavings were yummy. Then to top it all, our friends are not so mobile, the front entrance was locked and we had to wait for our taxi at the back of the restaurant, our friends found it difficult to walk through gated doors and steps. The setting is lovely, the sweets were delicious but the rest of the experience was not up to standard I'm afraid to say. This is our second time to Penang and the third we will not be returning here. There are many restaurants to choose from in Georgetown so we won't be stuck for where to go.The reason I have not rated this visit highly is because we were led to believe this was numerous uno but this was not the case. I would suggest that the staff receive extra training in patron relations and be more friendly and not so uptight, unscrew those wound up screws and realise who they are.Show less

Author: GPORDOCMelbourne, Australia
Title: The place to eat if you dont mind the price
Review: The meals are terrific with a mix of oriental styles the waiter staff while lovely people did not seem to have a clue you could wait forever for just a menu or a glass of water two items that should come automatically and quickly. The Bar is the place to drink as the staff in this area are exemplary. Food is all the other reviews have mentioned.Show less

Author: LaVoyageuse777Everywhere.
Title: Beautiful venue, excellent food, nice service. A great value!
Review: We had dinner there and had a great experience. The venue is just stunning, traditional but chic. It's perfect for a special occasion it a romantic date. There was a lot of options for food. The formula is pick one appetizer, one main, one dish of vegetables, and one dessert for RM120+, which is great value. It's a creative spin on traditional dishes and everything tastes wonderful and the portions were generous. A small detail: despite the staff being friendly, they need to be more attentive. We needed rice and beverages and couldn't get anyone's attention. We will definitely be back on our next trips to Penang!Show less

Author: DongNLos Angeles, California
Title: Should skip
Review: My girlfriend and I visited kebaya based on tripadvisors reviews. You guys wronged us! The food was uneventful; however, the decor was memorable. For a four course meal per one person, it's around $120 rm. I can definitely say I have had better. I can honestly say that I actually enjoyed local/stall food compared to kebaya. The restaurant was full of tourists. Take that how you want it but I would definitely recommend that you would skip kebaya, save your money and spend it at gurney drive where your money will go a lot farther. Show less

Author: QiqiChowPenang, Malaysia
Title: Great place and food!
Review: Had a very awesome dinner with my friends at Kebaya. Appetisers were great especially miang kham and pork mantao. Main courses were nice too, best was the hong bak lamb! Greens are a bit disappointing, but still ok. Desserts were good. Personally I love the tang yuan, blue tang yuen looks nice and tasted good.. Staff were friendly but it would be better if they are able recommend and explain to diners on selections of dishes..Show less

Author: MOBrien1907Port Douglas, Australia
Title: Best Fine Dining In Georgetown
Review: While on a recent trip to Penang we stayed at the beautiful Muntri Grove Hotel and dined at Kebaya, located just up the street at one of its sister hotels, Seven Terraces.The food was outstanding, the wait staff were attentive without being obtrusive.Without a doubt an extremely memorial dining experience.Show less

Author: David524524Sydney, Australia
Title: Superb creative Peranakan Cuisine
Review: Really superb cuisine at the restaurant within the Seven Terraces boutique hotel. Modern takes on Peranakan cuisine in really elegant surrounds. Pretty much all of the entrees are highlights, but also great was the duck salad, the snapper in curry paste, and the veggie sides. The service is friendly, knowledgable and very helpful whilst the bar serves very, very good cocktails. If there was one area that I would suggest improvement, it would be with the wine list, especially those by the glass. Though common practise is to serve red wines at room temperature, that probably doesn't take into account the SE Asian climate and in Penang they could be chilled a bit as they were a bit on the warm side here.All in all, a fabulous experience, and if you're in Georgetown you really shouldn't miss Kebaya!Show less

Author: Dzr1208Singapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent food and atmosphere
Review: We ended our Penang trip in this restaurant full of Peranakan heritage. The food was remarkable and waiters are beyond attentive. All the dishes were cooked and flavored to the best... One of the best dining experience I had so far. The four course set is priced at RM120 per head and alcohol is served. Absolutely recommended! Show less

Author: 421michelletTiong Bahru, Singapore
Title: A dining experience to remember
Review: It's an experience dining here at Kebaya at the Seven Terraces Boutique Hotel. It's set menu but with plenty of choices. The food is fusion Malaysian, quite strong taste and flavorful on the sweeter side in my opinion. Loved the colonial style decor everything is so picturesque and as if you went back in time! The staff were lovely and attentive and we never had to flag down to ask for something as the minute you look up they will be right at your side. If you're in Georgetown you should definitely come here, make sure to make advance reservations as they tend to be fully booked. Show less

Author: WTBAALondon, United Kingdom
Title: Classy
Review: A great place for a special meal. The food is excellent but nothing outstanding. One feels they could be a bit more creative. Opt for a set menu which is reasonably priced but also comes with a lot of interesting food. We had exchanged emails with them about our reservation but when we arrived we did not have a reservation, and in were staying on the lovely boutique hotel where it is localed Luckily a table was available. Service impeccable.Show less

Author: frydayukHigh Wycombe, United Kingdom
Title: Beautiful flavours and venue
Review: We loved our 3 course tasting experience at kebaya. We were staying at their sister hotel and just managed to get a table that evening. I would suggest booking in advance if you want to eat here! The food was exquisite and the presentation was very pleasing to the eye. The traditional, colonial decor was stunning and the staff were very attentive. Every dish had a wow factor and the cocktails were tasty too. My only criticism was that the place slightly lacked atmosphere, even with someone playing the grand piano in the background. Maybe it was lighting?? Anyhow still an arming experience made even better by 50% off food due to staying at their sister hotel!!!Show less

Author: Naomi J
Title: Flawless meal
Review: The food, the service, the live piano music, the building. It all made a perfect evening. Highly recommend this place. Was very happy to be somewhere serving decent wine too.

Author: 45SatisfiedKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Fine Dining at its Best
Review: The Kebaya restaurant is located on the ground floor of the Seven Terraces Hotel. In my opinion this is the best dining venue in Georgetown. It has seating for 50 people and is open for dinner only. Advance booking is essential as many non hotel guests dine here. The food is exquisitely different and you are able to choose three or four courses. The menu is diverse, making ones choices very difficult. Our party of six, chose different dishes and shared. The service is exceptional. As it was my birthday, I was allowed to bring in a bottle of wine, sans corkage. A complimentary cake, and the usual singing by staff were accepted with gratitude.Show less

Author: AzzalyIsmailPenang, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya cuisine in a cultured ambience....
Review: Staff dressed in Peranakan threads are softly spoken and magically appear and disappear as needed. Hand picked antique tiles and furniture add the finishing touches to beautifully restored Anglo Chinese architecture. Kebaya Restaurant should be part of your Penang experience, whether fortunate enough to stay at Seven Terraces or not.Show less

Author: D1524EOmarkbSydney, Australia
Title: Above the bar in regards to flavour
Review: I understand why this is rated so high it has a class that is from another time and the food is top of the tree we shared our dishes between 4 so we all tried a lot and it was full of flavour. Well done Benjamin and staff for making us feel welcomeShow less

Author: bal00mnaBangkok, Thailand
Title: Fantastic dinner in Penang
Review: My boyfriend and I was looking for memorable dinner in Penang then we found out 1st restaurant in this site. The foods were superb!!! I can't explain how delicious of panna cotta. It's great combination ever. Also the staffs are so nice and professional. Thanks you for made my night.Show less

Author: queenlinzJakarta, Indonesia
Title: An Exquisite Restaurant.
Review: I found this exquisite restaurant from Tripadvisor, saying that it's number one in Penang.Indeed it is. The Peranakan food is delicious with lovely presentation, the setting is old colonial style, the background music is just right.. a grand piano playing soft music with perfect volume.Service is also good and attentive, and that adds more value to Kebaya.We paid about $120 for a set menu + a bottle of wine. Not cheap but definitely not overwhelming for the experience.At the back of the restaurant, they have a lovely boutique hotel with the same setting called Seven Terraces.We may try that if we visit Penang in the future. Show less

Author: JulieLimSYSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious
Review: Set dinners are served every night and the menu is fixed. Reservations are a must and the dress code is smart casual.Each person chooses one item each from the list of appetisers, main dishes, vegetable dishes, and dessert. For the appetisers, my husband and I chose the shredded chicken in crispy wrappings, and the chicken wrapped in sugarcane. For the mains, we took the 'lor ak' or braised duck, and crab curry done in Thai style. The menu says prawn curry but they substituted the prawn for crab that night. For the vegetable dishes, we chose the vegetable tempura, and vegetables in sambal. For dessert, we decided on the daily special of the deconstructured coconut ice cream, yam fritters, jelly and banana chips.The food was really good and the servings were more than adequate. By the time it came to dessert, I was so full that I could not finish it. The ambience is lovely with live piano playing in the background. A must try if you feel like having a pleasant and intimate dining experience in a peranakan setting. Show less

Author: Wendell DNew York City, New York
Title: Wonderful set menu. Leave room for desert.
Review: Fine dining and service in a truly elegant restoration. The dishes from the set menus are Peranakan with a French touch. There are two seatings, and you should reserve well ahead of time. We loved our meal. But had we realized we were going to have so many dishes with large portions, we would have left a little on our plates in order to avoid feeling so full towards the end of the meal. Definitely a case where less is more!Show less

Author: 68faithnMakati, Philippines
Title: A Bit Underwhelming
Review: Kebaya is Seven Terraces boutique Hotel’s fine dining restaurant. It is open daily but only for dinner at 6pm-10pm. Set in a dramatically opulent oriental setting using blue ceramic dinnerware. I expected the food to be equally superb.There were 8 of us in the group and since most tables are good for 2-4, we were led to one of the big round tables located at one end of the room. Although it is pleasantly cool in the middle of the room where the piano is, I believe we were further away from the airconditioning so was not cool enough where we were. There is a ceiling fan for our table set on high but still it wasn’t comfortably cool enough. Plus we couldn’t light the centerpiece candle because of the fan.Kebaya encourages people to share so they serve the food in a Chinese Lauriat way meaning all food is placed at the center of the table regardless of who ordered what. I imagine this is not a problem with smaller intimate tables but ours was a big round table and there was no lazy susan provided so it was a bit difficult to ask and/or hand over food to one another. For RM 100, you are to choose your own set meal. One starter, one entrée, one vegetable and a dessert. There are 7 kinds of starters, 8 kinds of entrees, 4 kinds of vegetables and 5 kinds of dessert to choose from. Since there were 8 of us, all different orders, we were all able to taste most of what is on the menu. Unfortunately, not all of what is on the menu is good. Although not lacking in presentation some were average, even lacking. Miang Kham of salmon roe serve on betel nut leaf is very pretty but dry when you take a bite of it without the salmon roe. The good ones though were really tasty such as Chao Tom (minced prawn) for appetizer, very tender and tasty Hong Bak Lamb (cooked to perfection for 48hrs) , Lor Ark (duck) and Prawn Geng (prawn in curry sauce which was not too spicy and seasoned just right). Crispy Nyonya Tempura (vegetables cooked tempura style) is good. For dessert, order Chocolate Fondant. The panna cotta is too sweet and heavy which should normally be light and not too sweet. Although the wait staff was very attentive and friendly, it took the food forever to arrive. We waited 15 minutes or so after we were finished with our starters. We spent more than 20 minutes talking, some of us went outside to the hotel and restrooms, some smoked outside and came back, talked more after we finished with the main course. We waited so long that we asked for the bill. Were it not for the wait staff who gently reminded us that there is still dessert, we would have forgotten about it.Show less

Author: 2RightyPerth, Australia
Title: Excellent not to be missed
Review: The entrees and deserts were perfect. It is a 4 course meal so each of us had different meals which we taste compared. The food was really brilliant and there were no duds. Service was fine dining, efficient and prompt. The restaurant is also one of the most elegant and beautiful you will find. Don't miss if in Penang.Show less

Author: TravelingOYEsterNew York City
Title: Delicious and Friendly
Review: We went here on a whim. So happy we did as the food was spectacular.The flavors of each dish were unique and the food itself was creative. After 10 days in Malaysia, this was a lovely treat. It is $30 usd for the 4 course meal. Considering the wonderful service and the atmosphere, this was just what we wanted our last evening in Malaysia. Kudos to Benjamin - his smile alone was worth the trip!Make reservations! We lucked out as there was 1 table left and it was late when we showed up without a reservation. Glad we took the chance and it worked out! I woke up thinking about my red snapper pastry and pork belly. Show less

Author: YLKwanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Meticulous Service
Review: The waiters are likely to be foreign labourers, just like any other restaurant in Klang Valley except they are so well trained that I hardly experience any where else. I asked for washrooms, instead of just pointing the directions to me, the waiter actually walked me to the washroom. The appetisers and the desserts are better than the greens. The main course is similar to some other Nyonya restaurants patronised before. The service is fast because the meals come in sets. It was an unforgettable dining experience. Show less

Author: FancyFree007Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: upscale twist on NYONYA food
Review: Beautiful colonial cum Peranakan style restaurant with great service. Only set courses can be ordered which got 9 of us a bit worried as we aren't big eaters. But the waiter was great.. Allowed us to order 7 sets for 9 pp which worked out well. Could try all the dishes on the menu and were stuffed by the end of the evening. Dessert was also great.. A bit of east and west. Took photo of the external area which is part of a boutique hotel, can't recall the name. Had a wonderful time. Show less

Author: Quest27545
Title: Dinner at Kebaya, Seven Terraces
Review: Restaurant Manager, Benjamin was very courteous and accommodating. He consented to our choice of courses that deviated somewhat from the norm. Food was excellent and of unique flavours found nowhere else in Georgetown. Great piano music in the background. Benjamin personally gave us a short tour of the courtyard of the boutique hotel before we left the restaurant. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: TagItTravelMelbourne, Australia
Title: Birthday dinner in Georgetown
Review: The 4 course Set menu had enough choices to keep all happy except for we were disappointed in one dish the Organic Pork Belly was already sold out and our booking was at 7pm. Our recommendations are: Entree try the Chao Tom entree was really delicious with lots of flavour could have just kept eating these all night. Also try the Kebaya Ban Xeo - chicken. For mains would order again the Kebaya Tamarind Beef, Grilled Chicken Tapikan, note this has chilli but is delicious as was the duck dish too. For desert the chocolate fondant sounded nice but 2 of the 3 ordered at our table had a passion fruit sauce in the centre that wasn't mentioned on the menu - not ideal when you don't like passion fruit. Overall a very nice meal within a beautiful old style building with quick and friendly service. An option for only three courses ( ie skip desert) would also work well. I would recommend Kebaya consider upgrading the fan circuits and AC to allow them to be used separately as was very hot when we were there and was comfortable enough with the fan on until the adjacent table didn't want it on, so made it difficult for waiter to manage guests requests. ( Penang actually closed schools the next day due to the heat) Show less

Author: CLEE1988Singapore, Singapore
Title: Finally worthwhile dinning experience in PENANG
Review: The food was good, was not satisfied with just 2 items. 1)sambal goreng, had no sambal. not spicy enough 2) the passionfruit panna cotta was too firm for my liking! when i shook it, it does not have the jiggle!!Hmmm where should i begin with the GOOD STUFF.1) oh the pork bun!! the bun was like WOOW, this handmade bun was soft and tasty.2) the wing bean salad! thats my favorite dish its spicy and refreshing and crunchy, damnnn yummy.3)lor ak (duck) its sweetness is from the fruits, its really different from any of the lor ak i have tried but the skin was crispy the meat was tender!! im hungry writing this review.4) Tamarind beef, ok maybe i have 2 favorites. This has to be the other one! not sure why they gave us a knife when this dish is fork tender, like just poke it and u sees it falling apart. so this dish melts in ur mouth and the flavor it has, makes me want to go back for more.5) The gula melaka moose!!, wahhhh i was so happy when they elevate a plain local ingredient like gula melaka (brown sugar) this dessert tinkled my tastebuds.So its a must go if you are willing to spend! just RM150 per pax.Show less

Author: CavalinoRampante
Title: Exotic
Review:
Kebaya is the fine dining restaurant at the Seven Terraces Hotel. It serves both a four-course menu and a la carte.  
The service is delightful and gracious, and the food is a delicious fusion of Malay and Western cuisines.  Highly recommended.

Author: jncy
Title: Peranakan food
Review: The only special about here is the ambience. The food I consider as normal where I can every where in Penang. And the charges was high. If you are foreign people, this is a good place to start.

Author: LaoK66Hong Kong, China
Title: Best restaurant in Penang
Review: Frankly, I booked Kebaya because I want to take a look at the Seven Terraces Hotel, and had no expectation of the food. Boy was I surprised. The food was fantastic. Probably the best nyonya style cuisine in Penang. Although each person have to order a four course set dinner, the whole table can share. It's great for family dinner as the table are full of dishes and we were busy passing them around while enjoying the food.Service was friendly and professional. The setting of eating in a traditional row house with nicely done retro decor was another form of enjoyment. Finally, big thanks to the Benjamin, the manger, who gave us a quick intro of the concept of Seven Terraces which made us appreciate the work the owner had put in to restore this beautiful place. I am from Penang and I was impressed. So if you have tried all the yummy hawker food in Penang and want to have a well cook local meal in a classic setting, think about Kebaya.Show less

Author: Mike OPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Deserves it's reputation
Review: Dined for the first time at Kebaya but hopefully it won't be the last. We had very good cocktails in the Bababar before eating. The staff were all very professional, helpful and cheery which helped to create a very nice atmosphere. The building - shophouses converted into a period style mansion - was a very pleasant place to spend the evening. The food was delicious and the quantity more than adequate. Very good value.All in all an excellent experience.Show less

Author: mrshrysmShanghai, China
Title: Don't understand this
Review: Excitedly wanted to try out this so-called fusion fine dining peranakan/nyonya restaurant. Wanted so badly to like it. And I did. Kind of. But I won't come back. Here's why. I felt like its more of good home cooked food served in a pretty setting. Not too much creativity in the dishes. Nothing special about the presentation nor the taste. It was all quite delicious. But nothing that made me go 'woahhhhhhh! Love it!'. Yes, it was in a beautiful setting. Yes, everything was executed perfectly. But it lacked that special ooomph. That special something something. Show less

Author: 320lionelyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Can't handle the real Peranakan food? Try Kebaya...
Review: Located within Seven Terraces Hotel, this restaurant aims to introduce Peranakan (Straits Settlement) food to the uninitiated. What we locals would term as fusion Peranakan because it is prepared in the most un-local way. The flavors are very close to the real thing but the presentation isn't. Very impressive indeed. My only gripe with this place is the mosquitos in the restaurant...so, whilst we dine, so do the mosquitos. P/s...sorry if the pictures are blur. Didn't realize they were until a few days laterShow less

Author: Jembo2002Sydney, Australia
Title: Delicious!
Review: Kebaya offers a four course meal that showcases the local cuisine, while taking it to the next level.For each course you have several choices so there are real benefits if you're a larger group who are happy to share.There are two sittings which always seemed to be well patronised so bookings are recommended.Show less

Author: sumoodyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Amazing dinner experience
Review: Kebaya is inside 7 Terrace Boutique hotel and it's at the end of a small lane called Love Lane ( google map can be a bit misleading). Once we found the place and entered, we were transported to the old days by the decor and the ambiance of the place. There is a small bar at the left end with old timber counter top, a pianist playing yesteryear's classic and the staffs are very attentive and well trained. The food was amazing. Linda is an amazing hostess. Tips for foreigners, ask the waiter which local dish is spicy and ask the kitchen to cut down on the small chili.. it can be amazingly spicy!Show less

Author: Joe MSingapore, Singapore
Title: Fantastic food and faultless service.
Review: A number of friends had recommended this restaurant to me and so I was compelled to try it for myself. As soon as we arrived Benjamin and the other staff were attentive and helpful. Benjamin went through the menu and helped us decide on our choices and everything we had was delicious. A very memorable meal in a beautiful setting. I would highly recommend. Show less

Author: 587markdMelbourne, Australia
Title: Birthday Dinner
