Review: Came for my daughters birthday emailed a booking unfortunately they did not reply rang to confirm they said they where fully booked. When we explained they fitted us in. When we got to the restaurant we got the table by the kitchen and different chairs very uncomfortable.We asked for the fan to be turned on as all others in the restaurant where. Then the table beside us asked for it off this is where it became unpleasant as there was no control.We asked to move so did the other party eventually they moved.The waiter did offer to make good for the disruption unfortunately it put a downer on the evening as the other party where very upset.The food was good and excellently presented a lot of food when you have all the courses.The building is exceptional and worth a look would have been nice to be at a better table. I agree with some other reviews that it is 3 courses including the sides with mains. Two would be enough for most people not an option.They did give some free drinks and the service was good but the other incidents caused me to mark it down.Show less

Author: susantiuSingapore, Singapore
Title: Unusual degustation setting for Malaysian dishes in a beautiful shophouse.
Review: While on a weekend trip to Penang, we reserved a table here because of what I read on Tripadvisor. We had just come down from Dinner in the Sky before this but needed to bring my mum and daughter for dinner after. My daughter was also celebrating her birthday and I had earlier called the restaurant and spoke to Shahrul who was absolutely helpful and obliging in accommodating us. Degustation in a Malaysian-style dinner with a Peranakan/Nonya slant is unusual but it is cleverly compromised with shared plates. Very smart! Food wise, it tries to refine familiar Malaysian dishes and achieves this with a fair degree of success. The dishes were tasty, but definitely not any more tantalising than other restaurants serving similar cuisine, but because of its famous setting, prices are justifiably higher. For those comparing it to hawker food (esp. the prices), one just can't draw a parallel. It is akin to comparing apples with oranges; not fair simply because dining is also about the surroundings, service, setting, ambience etc. The appetizer Chao Tom, main dish Tamarind Beef and the desserts were particularly memorable. It is definitely a recommended visit for tourists, esp. those who have had quite a bit of street food already, due to its restored old shophouse setting which is architecturally attractive and historically interesting. Thank you to Benjamin and Shahrul who came to chat with us about the restaurant - they were most friendly and attentive. Just an amusing observation about the "lady with the white hair" - I note that she has had quite a number of mention here in the reviews as a haughty and rather rude person. Well, she was pottering around back and forth without giving our table any attention and not a nary of a glance from her, that is until she had to come to the table along with other waitstaff to sing Happy Birthday to my daughter. Only then did I notice a hint of a smile!Show less

Author: Sharon Z
Title: A Plus
Review: All of the food was absolutely amazing. It was a pleasant experience and we still talk about the curry.

Author: LanceBradwell_11
Title: Excellent Treat
Review: Took family of 11 for wife's 40th Birthday - Her Mum is in a wheelchair and the restaurant sent out staff to help carry her up the couple of steps outside. Ambience and staff were excellent. Food tasty and over plentiful

Author: Shwu Ling L
Title: Overated food and bad experience
Review: We went there in a group of 4,since it's a must for everyone to have a four courses set, we managed to try most of the dishes.The atmosphere is classy and clean however, i think the food is overated.I had a very unpleasent experience that night and i think i would never go back or recommend this restaurant to any of my friend. We found the chicken was not fully cooked as the meat cannot be teared off and it looked a little reddish inner. My intention was just to let the chef know and not to change the dish or whatsoever but the white haired lady took the plate to kitchen and then came out again talked to me in a very bad tone to let us know that how much time they comsumed to prepare the food and how long they had cooked it and it's how impossible that the chicken is not fully cooked and etc, till a week later i can still remember her arrogant face. I was really offended by what she said,i doesn't mind to pay for a uncooked pricey meal but not talking to me in a way that she did. The staffs there are good and polite except the white haired lady.Show less

Author: chryavenJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Peranakan cuisine at it's best!
Review: What a wonderful experience Kebaya Restaurant is for all the senses!Located at the UNESCO heritage site boutique hotel Seven Terraces, this restaurant is amazing!The decor is authentic without being overwhelming and kitsch, and the food is really beautiful. A fusion of Peranakan cuisine with Western cooking techniques and presentation, we chose their Set Menu and tried any dishes.One of our favorites was the Pork Bun appetizer dish, a perfect blend of succulent tasty pulled pork with pickles on a steamed bun.I would definitely come back to this restaurant. A perfect fusion of Ambience, Good Food and Great service! Show less

Author: Andreward
Title: Fabulous food
Review: The food here is something special and the experience was made all the better by the staff - Ben, the maitre d' was wonderful, welcoming and helpful. This is quite justifiably the number one restaurant in George Town.

Author: sischka
Title: very good choice
Review: A very good choice, when you look at the choices, the quality and the ambiente. Prices were good and overall it was a very pleasant experience.

Author: W3616OTchristianb
Title: What's there not to love?!
Review: The setting of course is stunning; beautiful old shophouses lovingly and skilfully restored, a smattering of antique pottery, slightly wobbly marble tables, attentive staff, good cocktails and a simple menu. Just choose starter, mains, veg and dessert for RM120 a head. It could be a bit boring if you were trying to eat alone, but for 2-4 people, it's perfect. You share everything and get to taste a good variety. My only problem was that so many of the starters were fried. The otak otak, which is a light, coconutty seafood custard is encased in puff pastry, the ju hoo char, a flavourful stewed vegetable dish in deep fried in a casing - does it make the dishes better? Don't get me wrong, nothing was bad or overly oily, I just didn't think that these particular "twists" added anything to the original. The mains on the other hand are excellently varied. A well sauced prawn curry, a relatively drier chicken kapitan and a simple, spiced, soy stewed beef together with three vegetable dishes made a great and plentiful selection. Should you eat here? Most definitely. But tread carefully when partaking of the wine list. Nothing is particularly expensive, but the selection is not particularly thrilling either. Show less

Author: 304spPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Amazing premises!
Review: The food is good but not amazing .... However the atmosphere, service and surroundings are just incredible. I am not keen on the fact that they have introduced sitting ties rather than simply booking a table ... But ... Sometimes I just want to show visitors to Penang a beautiful heritage building in a lovely atmosphere so the food is not the most important thing. Having said that .. .The prawn curry is totally amazing and the one dish I would definitely say is a must try.Show less

Author: Tydus_cKuching, Malaysia
Title: The taste of Penang
Review: This restaurant is part of the Seven Terraces boutique hotel. The cuisine at Kebaya captures the character of Penang. Like this heritage city with its cosmopolitan buzz, it pays homage to traditional flavours while using trendy/ French techniques.The set dinner is RM 120 per person for a 4-course meal. Family style dining where you can share the dishes. Dinner seatings are at 6 pm or 8 pm. Do book in advance.I enjoyed the duck confit, the curry snapper, and kerabu. I found some of the other dishes just ok, but that could be a matter of personal taste. The décor is lovely and there is a talented pianist to set the mood.Overall, a memorable meal.Show less

Author: Jo_AnneE98Traralgon
Title: Great food fantastic service beautiful surrounding
Review: Kebaya was recommended to us by another hotel guest who assured us we would not be disappointed.and how right they were !! The food was amazing and a great introduction to local cuisine.The service was great with the staff being very friendly and informative.The restaurant itself is beautiful.Show less

Author: RchewieLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Outstanding meal. A definite MUST if you are in Penang
Review: My family of six adults had dinner here at 8pm on a Saturday and were completely blown away by Kebaya. The service was wonderful and attentive, the setting was impeccable and the live piano music was the cherry on top. The food. Oh my word the food. When you make the reservation you are told that it is a four course meal at RM120 per head, which is just such incredible value for money for the quality of food served. That meal includes a starter, main, side dish and dessert. You have various options for each course but because there were six of us, we were lucky enough to sample pretty much the whole menu by ordering one of everything. (We are so grateful to the waiter for recommending that we do this!). Absolutely everything was just exquisite. It was one of those meals where everyone was silent and the only words spoken for a while was 'this is so good', 'this is even better', 'you have to try that' and everyone passing dishes up and down the table. I'm obsessed with pandan and my favourite dessert is creme brûlée and they served a pandan creme brûlée which was just heaven on a plate. The Maitre D was also lovely- she patiently answered all our questions about Baba Nyonya culture!Just wonderful- if you're in Penang you must visit for incredible Nyonya cuisine.Show less

Author: B9222YLamandam
Title: Dinner
Review: Excellent, fine dinning. Food amazing and great service. We had a 3 course meal and wine $120 dollars, excellent. Definitely go again.

Author: Marc_from_ChinaBeijing, China
Title: Charming place, good food
Review: We stayed in the hotel and made a reservation here for dinner. You have to choose between 6-8pm and 8-10pm seating, which is a little weird for a restaurant of that class, so we chose 8 as it's always possible to come earlier if a table is free before time.The place is nicely decorated and there is a live piano music which is also a lovely touch. Most of the dishes were good, although I'd not call them excellent. There is no 'a la carte', you have to order among a 3 course menu at 120 ringgit per person (which claims to be 4 course but the 4th one is just the main's side).Show less

Author: Abi V
Title: Nice, so luxury!
Review: Everything is good. Decoration and foods. Nothing more! Staff were so polite and trained. It was a memorable night for us. Thank again!

Author: Nadeen ALondon, United Kingdom
Title: Simply stunning!
Review: This restaurant is simply outstanding. The interior design is stunning. We were shown pictures of the before and after renovation works, simply amazing. The food is absolutely delicious. We practically wiped out every plate offered to us.The service is spot on. We had 3-4 waiters hovering discreetly over us. Cannot be faulted.Would highly recommend.Show less

Author: lihshyy
Title: Excellent
Review:
Excellent food, excellent environment, excellent service.
No ala carte. Only serve course dining.
Very generous serving portion.

Author: plaintruthinessFort Lauderdale, Florida
Title: Romantic and classy Nyonya dining
Review: Kebaya is part of the fabulously rebuilt Anglo-Chinese Peranakan inspired Seven Terraces boutique hotel. The before and after photos are unbelievable. The dining room is probably one of the nicest and most beautiful you'll encounter in Penang.Strait ambiance abounds. A pianist played on a baby grand during dinner. The Nyonya dinner was prix fixe with enough variety for 3 of us to share. Try the Pai Tee (crispy top hats of prawns with julienned vegetables and sweet chili coriander sauce) appetizers. The Hong Bak Lamb entree was marinated for 48 hours and so moist and delicious. Prawn Geng in curry of tumeric and lemongrass exploded with spices. Dessert selection was eclectic ranging from Pana cotta to Tang Yuen to Chocolate Fondant.The food, the service and especially the decor and ambiance make this restaurant a must stop.Show less

Author: Y_Y000Phuket, Thailand
Title: A-am-zing!!!
Review: It was amazingly delicious! I'm not a huge fan of spicy Asian food, so I was a bit apprehensive about the restaurant. But it was so tempting to visit tripadvisor's no1 in Penang! Make sure you're really hungry going to Kebaya, because you'll be offered a 4 course dinner. Starters, main dishes and side dishes were full of flavor. And great service and live piano music enhanced our night even more. Highly recommend!Show less

Author: LangladeMontboyer
Title: Wonderful!
Review: Fantastic food, great service and ambiance. Very definitely worth a visit. One of the few restaurants we had had to make a return visit to! Advisable to book in advance.

Author: misstravelbug-ukUK
Title: Asian fusion, excellent selection
Review: We stayed in the hotel and made a reservation here for a large group that includes friends from the local area. This is a beautiful choice with a menu that is different, including touches of Vietnamese and Thai. It is a set menu where you can choose from a number of items. The more people in the group, the more choice you get to share, so we were able to sample 7 mains and 4 entrees and all the desserts. The price is very reasonable by western standards, though obviously compared to the local choices, this is considered a lovely high-end treat. Live piano music was also a lovely touch. Most of the dishes were excellent, some were very good. The desserts were delicious. The 4 course menu is 120 ringgit per person from memory.Show less

Author: Tomsue2015Manchester, United Kingdom
Title: Classy Food
Review: We were pleased to eat at Kebaya on a recent visit to George Town as it showed how good food in Penang can be in the right hands. A delicious meal with interesting choices for each course. Pick the 8-10 slot if you can and turn up early for a drink at the bar.Show less

Author: B3atric3Greater Manchester, United Kingdom
Title: Elegant Chinese
Review: Welcome was somewhat unfriendly, however it made up for this in the food. Unfortunately the tables are turned so don't go for a long romantic dinner. It's either 6.30 pm or 8.0 pm. It somehow doesn't relate to its very smart image. We were late as couldn't get a cab so our meal was a tad hurried. Take heed and be there on time as the food warrants it.Show less

Author: sailorboy4real
Title: OUTSTANDING!!!!!!!
Review: The meal here was superb, the service was outstanding, the location and ambiance are unique, the menu was asian-fusion (my interpretation) and prepared with skill.

Author: Travel3717
Title: Authentic Fusion
Review: The food at Kebaya features well known and unusual South East Asian dishes packed with flavour.   David Thomson's influence on the menu is obvious.

Author: Fiona MMelbourne, Australia
Title: Magnificent mansion, great food
Review: Kebaya restaurant is in the Seven Terraces hotel complex, a magnificently renovated mansion. It has a nice bar where we had bubbles before dinner, and then it is a 4 course menu, you can choose from a selection for each of the 4 courses. Be warned, they only do sittings 6-8pm and 8-10pm. I forgot this and we rocked up at 7pm, whoops. But the manager Ben couldn't have been nicer. Fabulous food, lovely ambience.Show less

Author: mychngPenang
Title: Venue Better Than Food
Review: They serve peranakan cuisine but perhaps more suited for non-locals. My personal preference is that there should be more "belacan" but I found that the taste was not present or maybe there is very little "belacan" used. I do however, like the curry with prawns. The venue is very "peranakan" style and very classy. They have very polite staff. Now if only there's an option for a-la carte. (If i'm not mistaken, that option is only available for guests staying in the hotel. (Seven Terraces). Parking might be a bit difficult.Show less

Author: Christine FPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Disappointing
Review: Admittedly, my last (and third) visit was a while ago. The first one was shortly after it opened. The second and third time we were invited by friends. This is an atmospheric restaurant inside a renovated row of traditional shophouses converted into a boutique hotel in the middle of the Heritage area of Georgetown. The decoration is respectful of the original features but the overall feeling is rather cold and unwelcoming, perhaps because the lighting is quite unforgiving. I do like spotlights but not when they shine into my eyes while eating (it happened in my first visit). Chairs are wooden and quite uncomfortable discouraging after dinner lingering; service is adequate. The food is mostly local (with an emphasis on Nyonya dishes) but I was not impressed with the result: not bad and some of it even good but generally overpriced. A good place for first time travellers to the cultural heritage of Penang to get acquainted with its environment but somehow not quite authentic and a little staged, with an eye to the tourist trade. Most of all it is expensive for what you get.Show less

Author: GuenmaiLos Angeles
Title: Delicious!
Review: I've eaten at a lot of restaurants throughout S.E. Asia since the 1990s as that's where I vacation regularly and have loved Nyonya food for well over a decade. This restaurant was absolutely wonderful. I was in S.E. Asia for 6 weeks straight and ate at a lot of restaurants. My best friend was with me for 12 of those days and commented that our meal at Kebaya was her #1 meal.The food was really tasty and I loved the otak otak as I'm a big otak otak fan and have had many different styles of it. But, we both really enjoyed it. Aside for the food being delicious, the staff was absolutely wonderful. They were so nice and attentive. But, then again, I've found folks in Georgetown to be lovely. It was my second trip to Georgetown in two years and I've already booked for my 2016/2017 trip back to S.E. Asia and will be really looking forward to another meal at the Kebaya restaurant.Show less

Author: TamutoscanaDeddington, United Kingdom
Title: Very fine Peranakan Cuisine
Review: The Kebaya Restaurant is part of the Seven Terraces hotel on a small back lane in the old heritage part of Georgetown. The building’s interior is decorated in a charming, artistic, old Peranakan style, with the tables sufficiently widely spaced to offer a degree of privacy. There is a set menu of four courses (appetizer, meat/fish, vegetable, dessert) with two sittings for dinner at 6pm and 8pm. The range of dishes is imaginative and varied, but not too extensive, which is reassuring because it suggests the food is freshly cooked, which definitely seems the case. There are also special dishes of the day.The food was sufficiently exciting and special that we came back for a second evening to try a quite new range of tastes. All the dishes were prepared with thought and care, each having a different delicate and complex taste, which is what you expect of first class Nyonya cuisine. The service was excellent – quietly attentive and helpful. It would be fun to return and work our way through the remaining choices. If you are a gourmet, then it would be regrettable to stay in Penang and not eat here at least once.Show less

Author: Vincent PHong Kong, China
Title: One momentary lapse of service created a lasting bad taste
Review: During each vacation, we would always schedule a outing to a fine dining restaurant or at least one of the best restaurants in the respective city. Kebaya was one such restaurant. As with every fine restaurant, we received the most exceptional service each time. However this was not the case at Kebaya. Shortly after arrival, we were asked for our reservation and then seated down. After one of the waiters explained the menu and how it worked, all I can say is a white haired lady stormed over with the most menacing look and interrogated us about whether we had a reservation. That look and those words somehow sent chills down our spines. After timidly replying that we had, she checked with her staff to verify our claim. This really left a bad taste in our mouth for the rest of the dinner. I haven't given them a terrible rating because honestly the rest of the waiters and waitresses were very nice and hospitable. And the surroundings and food was actually quite good. But I hope we don't experience another situation like this in another fine restaurant again.Show less

Author: kj51ordCardiff, United Kingdom
Title: Great meal at Kebaya
Review: We visited for our 25th Wedding anniversary meal, and very glad we did.The meal was terrific, well cooked, and served by pleasant, hard working, attentive staff in lovely surroundings. This is probably some of the best fine dining that Georgetown has to offer and for fine dining, the price was reasonable too.Jackie also made sure that we receive a special dish on hearing of our celebration; a lovely desert. Thanks to the team in the kitchen and to Jackie for ordering it. All in all, A great experience. Book to go here and take your time to fully appreciate all that this little gem has to offer.Show less

Author: Lee O
Title: Fine dining as good as anywhere
Review: Amazing food and very reasonably priced for the quality. 120 each for a 4 course set menu. We booked in again for another night as soon as we had eaten. Great place for a romantic meal.

Author: cutiedoggy13Hong Kong
Title: Very Nice Ambience But Food Average
Review: Managed to book this top ranking restaurant in Penang just 2 hours before dinner which was quite lucky. It might also be because we ate at 6 p.m. when nobody was there yet. For tourists taking a free ride on the CAT free shuttle bus serving Georgetown area, get off at station 16. Just walk back half of the street and turn right into the very first lane on the right. You could see a small blue print on the wall directing you into The Seven Terrance Hotel. Just a 3 minutes walk from the bus station.There was a lady Maitre D who greeted us and led us to the table. The restaurant had a very nice setting and the whole environment and decor of the hotel was very beautiful. Many furniture dated back at least to 70-100 years. Although my mom and myself weren't a big eater, we already prepared for the 4-course set meals as diners were not allowed to order a la carte. Luckily the portion wasn't too big and we managed to finish it. It turned out the appetizers of Pai Tee and Chao Tom were the most delicious. We had beef and lamb as main course but the fusion tastes didn't quite suit us. The Sambal Gorong and Tempura vegetable as ok. As for the dessert, a bit disappointed with the Creme Brulee but the Chocolate Fondant was ok. Guests were being provided a small pot of water for cleaning hands after the appetizer. When I checked whether they provided a dry towel, the waiter replied just use the table napkin for drying. Later when the Maitre D checked whether everything was ok, I gave her the suggestion that they should provide guests a dry towel instead of using the napkin. She courteously admitted having overlooked that point and thanked us for the advice. The hotel reception was kind enough to call a taxi for us as the area was very quiet and dark.Overall it was a nice dinner given the ambience, good service but average food.Show less

Author: Andromeda W
Title: Excellent food
Review: Delicious Nyonya food in a beautiful restaurant with wonderful soft live music...Christmas carols as we visited just before Christmas, attentive staff.

Author: BobcockGreenford, United Kingdom
Title: As good as it's reputation.
Review: Chose this restaurant based on it's number one restaurant here and was not disappointed. We arrived without a reservation and a request to spend some time in the bar area before eating. Accommodated with a smile.The waiters were informative and on the ball throughout the whole meal. We ordered from the four sections and shared. For starter we had the Chao Tom and the Otak Otak. Both were excellent. For the main course we had the Hong Bak Lamb and the Kebaya Tamarind Beef. The lamb was very good but the beef was out of this world. I'm not a huge orderer of anything steak wise as I tend to always be disappointed but this piece of beef didn't disappoint. It was tender and flavoursome and the first time I'd had red meat with tamarind (Usually we have it with prawns). Possibly the best piece of beef I've ever experienced. We also had the wing bean salad which was also very good providing a difference in texture to the meat and greens.Desserts were good, the creme broule and the Panna cotta,Throoughly recommend this restaurant, certainly deserving of it's rating.Show less

Author: N285NJlindad
Title: Amazing restaurant!
Review: On December 31, 2015, we went to Kebaya restaurant for dinner. We like to dine outside but unfortunately that is not possible at Kebaya so that’s why we didn’t eat there that night.A few days later we decided to try Kebaya anyway. We had not made a reservation and the restaurant was actually fully booked but Jackie (the very friendly host) remembered us from New Year’s Eve and managed to clear a table for us, which we really appreciated.The restaurant is located in the heart of the World Heritage site in Georgetown. The building is beautifully restored and the restaurant looks amazing. It is furnished very tastefully and with great care. The kitchen serves Peranakan food with a modern twist. Absolutely worth mentioning is the wonderful tableware!We ate Kebaya Ban Xeo, Otak Otak, Kebaya Tamarind Beef, Prawn Geng Pandan, Sambal Goreng, Nyonya Crispy Tempura and for dessert Créme Brulee and Tang Yuen. All the dishes tasted absolutely delicious but the big surprise was the super tender, deliciously spiced beef!The waiters are fast, skillful and very friendly and Jackie has everything well under control and tries her best to make everybody comfortable by having a brief chat at each table. Being a host is in her blood since she does her job with passion and knowledge.The whole experience of eating at Kebaya suited us so well that we reserved a table for the next evening when we left the restaurant. When we came back the next day Jackie greeted us by our surname, very thoughtful! This time we ate Pork Man Tou, Chiao Tom, Grilled Snapper, Hong Ball Lamb, the same vegetable dishes as the day before and for dessert Gula Melaka Mousse and Pana Cotta. And since my husband has become a huge fan of the beef dish, we ordered that too. Again the food was delicious. Of course, you go to a restaurant for the food but the ambiance, the friendly service and the atmosphere certainly contribute to a successful evening.A week later we decided to have a farewell/end of our holiday dinner at Kebaya again and so it was that we took a seat again on January 13 in this beautiful restaurant. This time I ate the Thai Soft Shell Crab Salad and my husband could not resist his favorite, the Kebaya Tamarind Beef. The salad was a bit spicy but not overwhelming and the crab was absolutely amazing! Although all the other dishes we tasted here were all delicious, the crab salad and the beef were our favorites. It is such a pity that there is no restaurant in the neighborhood of our home where we can eat these dishes. Now we have to wait until we go back to Penang! Jackie and staff, thank you very much for your great care, we are impressed!Martin & LindaShow less

Author: charlotte l
Title: Amazing place with awesome food
Review: If you only choose one restaurant in Penang make sure to choose this one. It is one of the best I've been to in Malaysia.

Author: Kathy WPerth, Australia
Title: Beautiful food and atmosphere
Review: Three of us enjoyed a meal here on our first night in Penang. Our neighbour had recommended the restaurant. We were lucky enough to get a booking without booking days ahead. The food was fresh, tasty and well presented. I would have liked a little time between courses. Other than that it was a great dining experience.Show less

Author: sharonm81Melbourne, Australia
Title: Beautiful food and atmosphere
Review: We got a booking at the last minute no problems for six people. The entree was outstanding and we shared main dishes. Service and atmosphere were excellent. We enjoyed the duck confit and snapper very much. Desserts were very tasty and well presented. It was lovely food and a very enjoyable evening.Show less

Author: chefmenkePhoenix, Arizona
Title: One of our finest meals in Asia
Review: As a chef I am always inquisitive about what is on the menu, but it was the ambience and service that made our evening special. From the live piano playing in the background to the French Colonial architecture and fabulous food, Kaybaya lived up to its reputation. The Sous Vide Lamb shank cooked for 36 hours was one of the star performers for the evening as were the shrimp skewered on sugar cane. Service was attentive and no details were missed. An incredible value as the same multi coarse meal would have been 5 times more expensive in NYC. If I had any issue it might have been the otherwise excellent red wine was served a bit to warm. This incredible restored space makes Kabaya my top food stop in Georgetown!Show less

Author: UKcriticLancashire, England
Title: Very close to perfection
Review: My 2nd review of Kebaya about a year after my first. As before, the setting and food is hard to beat and oozes care and quality.Only negative was that we were told that we couldn't have coffee after our meal because the machine had broken!! Hard to understand why a restaurant wouldn't have a back for that.Still well worth 5 stars though.Show less

Author: MandM5960Lancaster, United Kingdom
Title: Dinner with Friends
Review: This must be one of if not the best restaurant on the Island. Serving Nonya cuisine a mix of Chinese, Malay and Indian, the choice whilst limited is cooked to perfection. Whilst the choice as I say is limited there is enough to cover everyone. I would recommend this as a must eat at restaurant. Whilst here take a minute before desert to see the hotel guest areas.Show less

Author: HP8_11Sydney
Title: Visited twice
Review: We were staying at the gorgeous Seven Terraces hotel in which this restaurant is located, so couldn't pass the restaurant up, and liked it enough to return on our last night. House guests are also able to order a la carte, rather than fixed priced 4 courses, so we had a combination of 4 courses for one of us, and 2 for the other and shared everything both times. This did seem to confuse the kitchen with only one entree appearing on both occasions, until requested, but it was a small issue. The food is modern, fusion, rather than traditional and we enjoyed it, particularly the soft shell crab salad and the sticky rice sort of dessert ( forgotten it's name). Wine is expensive, as usual for Malaysia. The interior is lovely and I'd go for the place as much as the food.Show less

Author: Ronald_jelleThe Hague, The Netherlands
Title: A nice dinner in a nice (Chinese?) setting
Review: My wife and I decided to give the restaurant a try and we were happy we did.The setting is nice with what I would guess to be old chinese decorations (carved wooden screens of which some parts are gold plates, porcelain and furniture).The card indeed wasn't that big, but for us there was more than enough to choose from. The choices are: one of atleast five starters, one of atleast five main dishes, one of atleast four green dishes and one of atleast four desserts... They have pork (which i dont eat), beef, fish.. so something for most of us.For me it was the best meal during the first ten days of this malaysian holiday and for MYR 120 per person we were very satisfied.I can recommend this Asian fusion kitchen.Show less

Author: glutenfree4lifeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Fine dining atmosphere, average food
Review: The seven terraces hotel in which this restaurant is located is a nice quaint hotel and the restaurant is very nicely decorated. The service is also good. If you have not tried many Asian foods before then it's definitely worth it. However if you live in Asia and know Asian food well (Malaysian, Thai, Singaporean) then the food itself is nothing great. They only have set menu and 2 seatings to chose from: 6 to 8pm and 8pm to 10pm. We took the early seating. The starters were just average. The desserts were the best part of the meal we felt. We also visited 'my own cafe' (didn't care much for the Asam laksa, loved the coconut ice cream served in the coconut shell); 'jawi house' ( loved the biryani, lamb-okra dish was just ok, desserts were good).Show less

Author: PompeyPenangPrincessPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Occasional indulgence
Review: Visit Kebaya for the overall experience rather than delicious and reasonably priced food and you won't be disappointed. None of the dishes here can't be found elsewhere in tastier and cheaper versions but you will struggle to find a more impressive venue, especially if you look around the whole building. Best to go as a 4 or more pax group to sample all the dishes. The service is excellent and pacing just right. Coconut milk is a predominant feature of baba nyonya cooking so avoid the prawn curry and coconut desserts if it is not to your liking. The fish in curry sauce is delicious but a small portion (can't recall if it is snapper, grouper or sea bass). All the veggie dishes are delicious but all portions are quite small. The restaurant can be a little noisy when full but otherwise a special treat, but definitely not a regular eatery-the menu doesn't seem to have changed since they opened although they do put on one or two specials.Show less

Author: cfloyd48Vancouver, Canada
Title: New Years Eve Excellent - with some reservations
Review: The peranakan ambience and service are excellent. The food got mostly good reviews from our group - the duck and snapper were full of flavour, the lamb was a disappointment. For the appetizers the otak otak was good,so too the pork buns. All the desserts we had were excellent. There is no doubt that in Penang there is equally good or better nyonya cuisine available for far less money. I would still recommend this restaurant for a memorable experience, but for me the one time is enough.Show less

Author: SydBJ
Title: Lovely treat
Review:
Dinner for two. Lovely service. Tasty food. Good portions. Was pretty quiet for the evening so it was a relatively subdued atmosphere. 

good value experience. I'd recommend it.

Author: harrynsamVancouver, Canada
Title: Disappointing meal
Review: The restaurant was in a beautifully and sympathetically restored period building and the maitre d' kindly escorted us to see the common areas of the Seven Terraces Hotel when we expressed an interest in the building. The dining room was lovely.Having read previous Tripadvisor reviews, we were prepared for the 4 course menu. For appetizers, we had the pai tee (the deep fried prawn was shrivelled and tough) and the maung kham (delicious), each of which were 3 mouthfuls of food.For mains, we had the roast pork and the special of the day, a scallop sashimi salad. The roast pork was delicious except there were only 5 small slices. The salad was interestingly delicious with at least 10 ingredients that I could identify.The tempura vegetables came in a thick, crisp, hard batter with no resemblance to Japanese tempura. The sprinkled belachan powder was a non event.The cher char was just a small heap of stir fried mixed local greens with nothing to distinguish it.The pandan creme brûlée although too sweet was deliciously smooth for the 5 teaspoons that we got out of the teacup it was served in.The cheesecake of the day was 2 spoonfuls of fluff with 1 spoon of ice-cream.We felt that the 4 courses were at best appetizer sized.Perhaps Kebaya is trying to emulate some Michelin starred restaurants who serve precious little tastings.With so many excellent reviews, our expectations might have been too high. However, the food served did not include expensive or exotic ingredients or require elaborate cooking techniques and there was no reason for the food quantities to be so small.Show less

Author: adriancckJurien Bay, Australia
Title: 1st Jan 2016 dinner
Review: The restaurant atmosphere has a good ambience and lighting in restaurant is adequate. There was accompanying pianist on the day we had dinner.Service was excellent ,however it was not clear of the menu how the charges per head include starters ,main course and dessert including coffee and starter drink are included. The food was a bit pricey for the food on what we ordered.The dishes we order was Otak Otak,spring roll of some kind, (crispy moo hoo char) with prawn , confit duck(Lok ark) veggie (Kerang) and sambal goreng n 2 dessert .Overall taste of all the food is not to local palette and the dishes we order had a sweet after taste on all the dishes.Show less

Author: jksCNXChiang Mai, Thailand
Title: Nonya Cuisine at its best
Review: This is a wonderful, romantic restaurant located in Old George Town. The food was excellent and the staff were very gracious and accommodating. recommend you make a reservation, they are quite popular. Show less

Author: Sissy1B
Title: Delightful and historic
Review: We stayed at Seven Terraces and enjoyed breakfast in Kebeya each morning. The food was always delicious served by very warm and welcoming staff.  We had dinner one evening and it was superb! Host Jacqui was very hospitable and again service was impeccable.

Author: MissSaucyRichmond, United Kingdom
Title: Good food, worth a visit
Review: We'd heard good things about Kebaya (almost everyone will tell you to go) and we were not disappointed. The food is as explained on numerous other reviews - you pick a starter, main, greens and dessert for a set menu price (100 MR). We had the salmon roe and chicken on wafers to start (the chicken was especially delicious), and the beef, lamb and fish for the main - we ordered an extra main. The lamb was to die for and I highly recommend trying it. There was also a decent wine selection. I was suggested a nice sweet riesling that perfectly complemented the flavours of the food. The only reasons I didn't give this a five star rating is that while the food is excellent there are places nearly as good for substantially cheaper and on the night we went (Sunday) it was only half full so perhaps lacked some atmosphere. Having said that, in our experience Penang doesn't have a lot of high quality, medium priced options (i.e. not quite fine dining but more expensive that many of the local options) so this was in certainly worth trying if you are looking for a restaurant in that category. Show less

Author: jonytt
Title: Sumptuous experience!
Review: Was with family to celebrate mum and dad's anniverversary . The food was above average in taste as well as price but not particularly memorable but nevertheless it was a nice experience of a sumptuous setting.

Author: Allison_WongSWKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: I Wish My Stomach Was Well Enough To Properly Taste All The Food...
Review: Since we were staying at the Seven Terraces, we made a dinner reservation the last night when we were there. Although I was still not feeling well from the whole food poisoning ordeal (not the fault of Seven Terraces or Kebaya), I still put up a brave face and tried to enjoy the dinner.The dinner menu was simple, RM120++ per person for 4 courses of nyonya cuisine to choose from Appetizer, Main Course, Greens and Dessert. I couldn't really taste most of the food, only the Pandan Creme Brulee that really stood out and I finished it all. It was so good that I still crave for it sometimes even when I'm back in KL! The Otak Otak re-imagined was like pastry, although I still love the original version better. So for appetizer, the Crispy Joo Hoo Char Roll tasted better. Also, I think we ordered too much creamy main course, like the Prawn Geng and Grilled Snapper which were all drenched in creamy sauces which my weak stomach didn't quite enjoy. However, my better half loved every single dishes and raved that it was the dinner he had in a long time. Well, I'm glad that one of us had really enjoyed the dinner. I should return one day and hopefully I could really taste every single dish properly.Show less

Author: Jonathan RSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent Peranakan food, just don't bother with the cocktails
Review: Lovely setting and food to match. The shophouses have been wonderfully converted into a large, spacious and authentic-feeling dining room. We ordered the four-course menu and ended the meal very, very full. All the dishes were top quality but the tamarind beef was a standout.I'm only knocking off a point because of the poor quality of the cocktails. The bar appeared to be well-stocked and the menu listed a range of classic cocktails, so I mistakenly assumed they knew what they were doing. Ordered a Manhattan and received a watered-down mess filled with crushed ice. Sent it back, and while they were apologetic and helpful, the replacement I received was hardly any better. Eventually I gave up and had a glass of wine.Still, this is just a small point, and it didn't spoil an otherwise exceptional meal.Show less

Author: nmpstorm98
Title: Nice fusion on Penang classics
Review: A bit high end but worth the effort. Helpful staff which were able to prepare dishes of menu for children. Worth a try

Author: margaretleesy
Title: Cool peranakan experience
Review: Though pricey at rm120 per pax, it's money well spent for the delicious food and unique dining experience. The place is beautiful.

Author: Kirs T
Title: Birthday surprise
Review:
It's a scrumptious dinner I ever had in Penang.. The combination of nyonya & western is perfectly done .
I will definitely return for kebaya each every time I visit Penang

Author: Kent WSeattle, Washington
Title: Excellent!
Review: This isn't a typical restaurant. For a fixed price of RM120 (US$30) you get one choice of an appetizer, main dish, vegetable, and dessert. But you should try it because the food is delicious. I enjoyed it so much I returned again two nights later. All 8 dishes I tried were excellent. Highly recommend!Show less

Author: 548darrenwDorking, United Kingdom
Title: Very nice
Review: Recently visited Kebaya for an evening meal with family. Restaurant is in what appears to be a nice boutique hotel just away from little India. They offer a 4 course set menu for 120 Rm + tax. With wine it averages out between £30-40pp. Yes it's very expensive for the area, but you get what you pay for - I.e. A very nice meal. Chicken kapitan and 72hr slow cooked beef curry were both very tasty. Be warned however, although advertised as a 4 course meal (starter, man, vegetable, dessert) in reality it's a 4 dish (3 course) meal. Show less

Author: Alex M
Title: Delicious!
Review: Definitely worth it. Delicious, great sized portions, wonderful service in a clean and open space. I would eat here again and recommend others to go here.

Author: celinewongyinli_Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Perfect authentic Peranakan experience!
Review: Couldn't have asked for anything better. Particularly appreciated the decor and the guy playing classic Chinese songs on the piano. The food is really good and especially the dessert. We ordered the Pandan Creme Brulee and the Passion Fruit Panna Cotta and they were exquisite. Show less

Author: Kate_GzSingapore, Singapore
Title: Amazing place and experience
Review: Kebaya is a very beautiful restaurant, they did a great job in the renovation as it is elegant but still retains the flavour of its origins.Definitely try this restaurant if you want an experience of elevated local food with great staff, live piano music and amazing environment. They offer a 4 course menu that might seem expensive if compared to local restaurants but I think it was a good deal for a great experience.Show less

Author: Austin JSingapore, Singapore
Title: As expected of #1 on Tripadvisor!
Review: Plenty of reviews here for the tripadvisor community to go on with. My two cents worth is that the Miang Kham (u'll find out what is is!), otak-otak, chicken Kapitan and Hong Bak Lamb were truly outstanding dishes. Don't forget to lick the otak-otak sauce!As for desserts, the table agreed that the creme brûlée was not only great, it was a cut above most creme brûlées. Plenty of food for Rm120++ per person, enough for two I reckon.Do have a walk around the hotel too (Seven Terraces), it's beautifully maintained/restored.Show less

Author: Olle AStockholm, Sweden
Title: Excellent food in a delightful environment
Review: We had high expectations since Kebaya is rated the best restaurant in Georg Town. The dining room is spacious and very comfortable. The staff was very attentive and friendly. Drinks were served at once. We had a innovative betel leaf/betel nut starter topped with Norwegian salmon roe. The other starter was red snapper baked in a pastry served with a tasty sauce. One of the mains was smoked pork belly and the other a lamb shank. Both came with vegetables, one of them tempura. The desserts were delicious, particularly the very crispy creme brule. Everything was excellent. A nice surprise was a discount that was given because we accepted to dine at an early seating (you could either come at 6 pm or 8 pm). I think this is a very good idea that more restaurant should adopt when they do not offer customer to come at any time.Show less

Author: ajr493Orpington, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent local cuisine at reasonable prices
Review: Based on the Trip Advisor reviews we booked a table here for last night. Let me just say that all the pictures on TA are completely accurate, it really is this beautiful and elegant.The menu is called a set menu, but basically you choose any starter, any main, any vegetable side and any dessert for MYR120 plus 6% (service or tax I'm not sure which). You can also order additional dishes for a small charge. Rice is free of charge and dispensed by a man with an enormous tureen. Although you order for yourself the food is served up to the table so that you can share.We had the salmon roe and red snapper starters. The salmon roe is served on a betel nut leaf with various ingredients piled up, you roll up the leaf and eat it all. In some of the pictures in the magazines it is shown as lots of separate ingredients that you put together yourself. The red snapper comes in a small puff pastry shell with a spicy creamy dipping sauce. Both were unusual and very tasty.For main course we had the prawn curry and the chicken Kapitan together with stir fried greens and tempura vegetables (and rice of course). The prawn curry was exceptional, tasty and creamy with lots of prawns. The chicken Kapitan was a little too sweet for my tastes - it may be that I am used to the less authentic version served in local restaurants. Both vegetables were also lovely.After a 15 minute break we felt able to eat dessert, although I no longer felt that I could manage mango sticky rice which as the day's special. Instead we had chocolate dessert and passion fruit panna cotta. They were very different but both wonderful.We thoroughly enjoyed our meal here, all of the staff from the elegant maitre d' to the waiters were knowledgeable and very helpful.Although there is no dress policy the restaurant is so elegant that it makes you want to dress up, I doubt that you could outshine the maitre d' however who was wearing a beautiful embroidered green traditional outfit when we visited. Highly recommended for special occasions.Show less

Author: CK2012_12Singapore, Singapore
Title: Well restored interior
Review: The place is well restored to its original "form" a place to visit if u want to have a look how the people in Penang Stay in long ago. As for the food, it have some fusion added, it is not really Nonya food having said that food and service are ok. The place is not easy to Find, but tell the taxi driver you are going to Kebaya House or 7 terence they know the place, if possible get the same taxi driver to come pick you after ur dinner. The restaurant booked a taxi for us but we wait almost half an hour to arrived. Dessert was not too tasty but the beef rendang is a must have.Show less

Author: Jon E
Title: Amazing
Review:
5 star service. Beautiful decor & the 4 course set menu was perfect.
Get the creme bulee as your dessert! 
Would love to visit again next time in Penang

Author: TWhyteLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Amazing setting!
Review: The restaurant is set in a converted set of shop fronts - hence the name "seven terraces". Our welcome was warm and the staff were all cheerful and helpful. The food was amazing - fabulous flavours and some new spice combinations to us. A fixed price menu and very reasonable wine list made for a thoroughly enjoyable evening Show less

Author: NotcreativeenoughHong Kong, China
Title: Nostalgia Restaurant
Review: It offers surprise at the back of an old alley behind a Chinese folk religion temple. Google map would take you up to 30m off the exact location. So beware when it says you arrived at your destiny. Go further forward until you see something of interest. The restaurant is a rebuilt on a heap of ruins. Ask the manager and she will show you albums of the then and now of the building. You can even book a room and stay inside the hotel attached to the restaurant. It's quite cosy and tranquil. Like a traditional Chinese inn in ancient China. All our foods were recommended by the friendly waitress. Good service and excellent food quality. Reasonable price for the quality that you can get. A must go in Penang.Show less

Author: Jman293Milwaukee
Title: Teriffic venue, interesting taste of old Penang
Review: I came here with some business colleagues for a dinner. We arrived early and were among the first people to get there. The restaurant had not opened yet, so we had a drink in the bar while waiting for our table. We enjoyed the beautiful bar and dining room. The staff was friendly and accommodating, and we were soon seated for dinner. We ordered the set multi-course menu, which was really wonderful.Since one of our party lives in the area and has been to Kebaya many times, we got a special tour of the hotel area after dinner. It's usually closed to non-residents, so we felt we had gotten some really special treatment.We noticed a problem with the bill after returning to the US, which the restaurant was able to resolve remotely and refund the overcharge directly to my credit card. This was really outstanding customer service, and I definitely appreciate the assistance in rectifying this error.Definitely I'd go back on my next visit to Penang! You should try it too!Show less

Author: b0bnw8London, United Kingdom
Title: Unpretentious fusion cuisine
Review: It is difficult to imagine that vision cuisine can be as unpretentious and as simple as it is in this restaurant.Taking inspiration from traditional Asian cuisine, Kebaya shows its impeccable knowledge of French cooking skills and brings local flavour to a different level.Situated in renovated buildings (seven of them) in the Georgetown city centre, Kebaya is a hotel restaurant, making most of the unique location."Fixe" menu is nothing but an opportunity to enjoy in the offer as much as possible, and while it is not that cheap for Malaysia (though at ca. 20 GBP per head it is dirty cheap for foreigners) it is also very good value for money.If you are lucky enough to be part of a group of four or five or more, you can easily enjoy most of the menu and share the dishes.Service is impecable, and extremely professional. Food delivered at pace that allows guests to enjoy it, and all your requests are catered for at fast speed.A great experience, in addition to a wonderful meal, this is a restaurant we would like to come back to soon.Show less

Author: Richard TBangkok, Thailand
Title: Quite the "Adventure in Cuisine"
Review: Inside the beautiful Seven Terraces boutique hotel a gem of a dining experience. Wonderful selection of complimentary dishes served in a nice 4 course set . You can choose your appetizer, main, greens and dessert . Portions just nice to share together with your guests.Small but good wine selection to compliment the meal.Highly recommended!!!EnjoyShow less

Author: Alex_85_11Melbourne, Australia
Title: Fantastic!!
Review: My partner and I had an absolutely fantastic meal here! Everything was absolutely delicious and cooked to perfection.The service was very attentive but not obtrusive, and the decor was very sophisticated and elegant.We loved every bite, the portions are very generous and you will leave feeling very satisfied, the real winner for us was the desserts!Great value for money. The entire meal including a martini came to RM 330 approx $110. Highly recommend!!Show less

Author: LocaDomBarcelona, Spain
Title: Fantastic dinner
Review: We wanted to try the 1rst restaurant in town and we were very surprised by the quality of the meals and the quality of the service.The menu is composed in 4 steps: starters, main course and greens and the dessert.I recommend the crab salad it is so incredible! But very spicy....The creme brûlée-for French people like us- was a very good surprise!!!The menu is very expensive for the town but the place,the service, and all the meals, until the mojitos were fantastic.Show less

Author: Dennis MPort Aransas, Texas
Title: Most likely best in Georgetown
Review: We met two other couples for dinner, menu is limited but diverse enough for anyone's taste. Wine list is good, and the portions poured were well above average. The restaurant is very authenticity retro, and has a feel of old works charm, which flows well with the Seven Terrace Hotel which it is part of. The staff is very attentive and professional. If you wish to impress your date, or have a great dining experience in Georgetown, Kebaya is then a must.Show less

Author: Macfarlaine
Title: Excellent Ambience + Food
Review:
Excellent Ambience and food at dinner time...but the night's dinner experience was not cheap.

Richard

Author: Vince B
Title: Beautiful food, great ambience, terrific staff
Review: We just loved everything about our night here. Try the 72hr cooked beef!  Great staff, very attentive, fair pricing.

Author: TCM952Santa Rosa, California
Title: Great ambience, excellent food, decent price
Review: This restaurant is just off the main tourist road in Georgetown. A beautiful, refurbished home, now a restaurant and guest house. We had an excellent 4 course meal for $30USD each, plus wine. Excellent shrimp curry, good lamb, great appetizers and dessert. The best meal we had in a week in Malaysia. Only small item was wine we wanted that was on list, not in stock. But the substitute was excellent. A sure stop in Penang.Show less

Author: TNT924Melbourne, Australia
Title: Amazing food and service in a gorgeous, historical setting
Review: We've eaten a few times at the Kebaya restaurant, and we held our wedding reception there in September 2015. The food is exceptional, with great options for vegetarians and those who are gluten-free. Our favourite dishes include the prawn curry, the wingbean salad and the ever-popular pandan creme brulee! The staff are very friendly and attentive, Kebaya has a great range of drinks and the decor is stunning; many of our guests returned for a repeat visit! Our thanks to Marcus and the whole team for making our special occasion so memorable, it was the perfect place for our function.Show less

Author: Scooter-across-Asia
Title: Kebaya is up there with the best on International scale
Review: Ate here Fri 18 Sep with a group of 18 people. Was absolutely sublime. The food, the setting, and the grand piano playing in the background. A perfect end to a week of travelling. Thank you for such a high standard.

Author: TIMOTHYWETTONUK
Title: Fusions food
Review: We really enjoyed our set dinner here. It's expensive for Penang, but by international standards it's quite cheap for this quality of food. Lovely staff and beautiful setting. Highly recommended for a relaxing dinner. Very tasty fusion food. Our only slight criticism is that when we went nearly all of the meat dishes we sous vide. But, we'd still go back for sure.Show less

Author: Arne_LeuvenLeuven, Belgium
Title: Certainly not worth place #1 in Georgetown
Review: Based on the good reviews we reserved at this restaurant.After sending an email they replied we could only choose between 2 time slots:"We have 2 sessions for dinner. The first session is from 6pm - 8pm and the second session starts from 8.30pm  until 9.30pm onwards."As 6 was too early, we took 8:30pm, which was in my opinion too late..When we arrived 70% of the tables were empty, no idea why the timeslot was so important if the restaurant was only booked for 30%..Regarding the food, because I dont like rice and the menu said this was included for all dishes, i asked whether it was possible to get noodles or something else as an alternative.The answer we got: no, not possible.If you want to be a quality restaurant, you need to think out of the box and be able to provide alternatives. Almost all other restaurants in Malaysia we visited had no problem with providing noodles or naan, most of the time we even could choose the type of noodles.One of the dishes we has was the lamb, it was nice but not really warm, which was disappointing.Service is really good, we did not need to wait, maybe also because there were as many waiters as guests during our visit :)Overall experience was really disappointing based on the created expectations of tripadvisor. We have had better experience with simple streetfood in Penang which was only 5% of the price we paid in Kebaya.Show less

Author: Galer67
Title: Beautiful location, amazing food
Review: The atmosphere is divine, the service is excellent, the food was amongst the best I have eaten and the wine selection, brilliant!

Author: RickandTatianaWangaratta, Australia
Title: Excellent food in a wonderful spot
Review: We dined here as part of a gourmet food tour and had a great meal.The setting is superb, in a renovated set of terraces that are beautifully respired at no expense, and the ambience really does add to you enjoyment of the experience.Food is Malaysian/fusion and the dishes just kept coming - range of chicken, duck, fish, prawn dishes etc, each with its unique flavour. Excellent desserts and wines at very good prices for Malaysia.Definitely worth a try!Show less

Author: immanlynSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent service and food
Review: Had dinner there twice during a 3 days stay. Very attentive service and accommodating. I love the staff. Very observant and with initiative. I have a son who's on the autism spectrum n being a fussy eater, he enjoyed his dinner. We managed to have a nice slow dinner. Our second dinner was ruined by a large group of rowdy dinners . It's no fault of the staff thou. Price is definitely on the high side , but every cent is well spent . Love the fusion peranakan food and spices . But the deserts are way too sweet . That chocolate cake with the ice cream is fantastic thou . Cos it's got a sour filling inside . Will love to visit againShow less

Author: Andy WMelbourne, Australia
Title: Delightful experience
Review: This is an excellent Nonya fusion restaurant. Good service and delightful surroundings. We enjoyed the 4-course fixed price meal and shared each other's dishes - all of which were extremely well prepared and beautifully presented. Recommend booking. This is considered best restaurant in Penang, so popular.Show less

Author: Angelo1975Nijmegen, The Netherlands
Title: Excellent food, very nice atmosphere
Review: This restaurant is part of the Seven terraces hotel. This in Baba Nyonya style decorated restaurant has a very cosy atmosphere.The food is truly excellent. Predominately Baba Nyonya style dishes. Staff is very attentive and friendly. Make a reservation to be safe, or just try your luck (as we did). You won't be disappointed!Show less

Author: PhilipCarolOxford, United Kingdom
Title: Good service and great food
Review: The best (and most expensive) meal we had in Malaysia. Set price menu at 120 ringgits with starter, main and side, and dessert. Stunningly good cooking, modern twist on Peranakan classics. Dinesh, our waiter, was lovely and helpful. Gorgeous setting in converted shophouses. Pitch perfect dining, strongly recommend.Show less

Author: AlistitleBangkok, Thailand
Title: Upper class Malay food
Review: We were there for a dinner. It was a good experience, food looked great and beautiful, the taste was good but not so impress.A dinner set cost RM120 exclude beverage.There are 4 dishes, appertizer, main dish, vegetable, serve with rice and dessert.It worth to pay for experience, but if you hungry or need something local -go another place.Show less

Author: huanyinchanMalaysia
Title: Pretty Place but Average Food
Review: I have been thinking to visit Kebaya since last year when I noticed it has been ranked as top restaurant among all others fantastic restaurants in Georgetown. I called to the restaurant in the afternoon and fortunately they have got table for us. We were the earliest guests in the evening. Kebaya is attached to Seven Terraces- a boutique hotel. I can see the parking spaces and quite limited in front of the restaurant. However I have been told that there are few more parking lots at the frontage of Seven Terraces. The interior is nicely done with antiques being display around the premise. There is a bar at the left, a grand piano right at the center and the dining area is on the right. The distance between tables is far enough to ensure privacy. However, the food didn’t really impress us that much. For rm120 per head, we can choose 1 dish each from the starter, 1 main dish each from the main and 1 dish each from the green as well as an item from the dessert section. Personally I love the Miang Kam with salmon roe a lot. The Meat Bao tasted not too bad but the taste of the Assam Fish-the day special not really to our liking. Both of the dessert was quite disappointed to be honest.The service was quite attentive but definitely not up to fine dining level. However, I do not treat the dining experience at Kebaya as fine dine but rather a cultural dine experience at a pretty heritage building.Show less

Author: porkkkchop
Title: Greeat service
Review: We would like to commend Dinesh, our wait staff, who made great recommendations and was always checking on us and other guest throughout the mail. My family and I loves his smile and attitude. Thanks for making our night, Dinesh. :)

Author: sebhoffTrier, Germany
Title: Excellent (upmarket) food, mostly visited by tourists.
Review: This was an interesting experience! My wife loved it, while I had some minor (but still somewhat nagging) doubts about it. Penang has wonderful food - and some of it both wonderful and cheap. This restaurant certainly isn't on the cheap side, but the interior and the general ambiance of the place (looking into the courtyard of the Seven Terraces) - besides the food itself, of course - justify the price. Food was excellent and in part surprising (for example the Miang Kham with Norwegian salmon roe). Even though I don't usually like desserts, I must say the durian crème brûlée was divine. We had some good fruit juices and a decent glass of white wine, too.Service was fine, but I did feel that they could have waited a little longer between the starter and the mains, which arrived almost as soon the empty starter plates had been removed.For me, the whole experience felt somewhat out of place, and I can't really say why. Perhaps it had to do with the fact that virtually everybody in the restaurant seemed to be a tourist. My (Malaysian) wife didn't think this was an issue at all - so I'll follow her evaluation and rate it as five stars...Show less

Author: sophiangSydney, Australia
Title: Baba Nyonya Fusion
Review: Set in the lovely 7 terraces hotel restored in full peranakan baba Nyonya style, this restaurant is set on the street front with a long beautiful open air courtyard separating the rooms and hotel quarters.It's fine dining Nyonya and though not cheap in Penang standards, I would say it's not expensive for such a superb standard of restaurant. Everything is visually pleasing and thumbs up to the interior design.Service was excellent and food pleasing. If I am to write in true honesty of a Penangite then I would say the food is more geared for foreigners and having Nyonya food as one of my favorite cuisines, it's not authentic but then hey it's meant to be fusion. Highly recommended to all as it's still very yummy and my partner thought it was sensational.Show less

Author: SandyCaroline
Title: Deserves its reputation
Review: A delicious meal in very pleasant surroundings. We enjoyed the fixed 4 course menu but others might  prefer more flexibility. Professional  service.

Author: Veggie-Reenie
Title: Beautiful food
Review: Delicious Malaysian food set traditional surrounds. Every course was perfect with amazing flavours and fresh food. Highly recommended. Possibly the best restaurant we went to Malaysia!

Author: BornVivantSingapore
Title: Mod-Peranakan executed with precision
Review: The Seven Terraces is probably the fanciest hotel in Georgetown, and Kebaya is its centrepiece. A beautiful space filled with some of the owner's collection of antiques, dinner is served on Peranakan porcelain. Food is Asian inspired, mainly Peranakan with some twists and some flavours inspired by Thai, Viet and other Southeast Asian cuisines. Dinner is a very reasonable RM 120 for 3 courses plus a veg. For our dinner of 5 we chose to try almost all the appetisers and all the desserts. Standouts for appetisers were the ban xeo, the otak-otak (for those who know this, a very unexpected deconstruction, basically a chicken pie with otak gravy) and the pie tee (fairly trad except for the deep fried prawn). For mains, the Thai style prawn curry was amazing if you like rich coconut- based curries. The tenderloin was perfectly tender. For veg, the kacang bottle was the standout. This trad Peranakan green veg was enlivened by pink pomegranate seeds and the acidity of pomelo added another layer of complexity. Desserts were all good, my favourite being the ondeh-ondeh floating in coconut milk. A must try when in GT.Show less

Author: KandJ52628
Title: The best restaurant experience
Review: Left this restaurant to our last night as a special night out. Coming from a 'foodie' place like Melbourne our standards are high and Kebaya met the admirably. Don't leave this one off your must do list

Author: Angela20140210
Title: Best in Penang
Review: The best restaurant in Penang. Great food, great ambience with live music. Amazing service. You should not miss the set dinner and I am sure you will be too full with great taste.

Author: SarnasotaSingapore
Title: MISS IT, MISS OUT, IS RIGHT!
Review: OMG… What an amazing meal, atmosphere and evening I had. After the Concierge at my hotel had called to find out that the restaurant was sold out for the three days I was in Penang, I emailed the website and got a call back from the gracious and charming General Manager, Ewan Taylor. There was a cancellation and he could happily seat me at 7. I was so excited! Having read the reviews here on TRIPADVISOR, and seeing the photos, I could not miss out dining in this exquisite, very special place. Dining solo, I entered the beautiful doors of KEBAYA and was greeted by Jackie, hostess extraordinaire, dressed in a beautiful Peranakan outfit. "You must be Sita…" nodding yes, I was escorted to my corner table. I sat for a few moments absorbing the atmosphere, the music and spectacular carved and gilded woodwork around me. Then i ordered…Appetizer was Miang Kham of Salmon Roe… a hundred bursts of flavors all bite sized and wrapped in a betel nut. Yum Yum… Main course was Grilled Salmon marinated with spice paste and baked wrapped in a banana leaf… so delicate in texture and deep in flavor. To complement this, I had a bit of rice and seasonal greens with a bit of a kick. Simple but sublime.  Dessert was… drumroll... Gula Melaka Mousse. Pure heaven. What can I say, it was the best meal I had in Penang. Not saying that there isn't other great food, but the combination of your first impression…walking into this beautiful space and being greeted by Jackie and then the ambience, service and food. Everything was a 100... I can't wait to go back to Penang and KEBAYA.Show less

Author: simmoGoldCoast
Title: Well deserving of its mantle of best restaurant in Penang.
Review:
Fantastic food, service, drinks selection.
You MUST try this restaurant.
Drop in for a beer or a Gin and Tonic on a hot day, or any day for that matter, you will be wonderfully surprised.

Author: JohnL104
Title: Superb
Review: A restaurant of the highest standard. Delicious, inventive food. Service that is welcoming, knowledgeable and attentive without being intrusive. A unique environment, dining among collectibles. Superb!

Author: sallyA_md
Title: Unique flavors in a romantic setting!
Review: We enjoyed everything we ordered! The service is impeccable. I loved the design and ambience of the place. I would be interested to stay at their boutique hotel if I visit Penang again.

Author: NomadicBoys
Title: Great food in a very grand setting
Review:
We came here for desserts and loved it. It has a very grand, beautifully decorated setting with grand piano music in background.

We tried the pandan creme brulee and panna cotta - highly recommend the pandan creme brulee - delicious!

Author: 16GinnyTPortsmouth, United Kingdom
Title: Superb food
Review: From the moment we stepped inside we loved this restaurant. While we sat at the bar before going to our table one of the waiters showed us a couple of folders outlining the renovations. It really enhanced our appreciation of the building, the owners are truly innovative. This was the best meal we had during our 7 night trip to Penang. Loved it. We had 2 different curries and shared them. Starters superb and the mango panna cotta perfect to finish. After our meal we were invited to look round the hotel, we can't wait to return and intend staying here next time.Show less

Author: BeeOutsideSydney, Australia
Title: Restoration terraces and food wonderful at Kebaya
Review: Magnificently restored buildings in the heart of Georgetown( 7 terraces). The ambience and the food was superb but you have to book as it is understandably very popular. Quite expensive by Malaysian standards but if the price of the food contributes to the maintenance and restoration of such historic buildings I don't mind! Show less

Author: Allan C
Title: Excellent Meal and Service
Review:
The Chinese styled foods were very good although the Vietnamese inspired dishes were lacking.
Staff were pleasant and attended at a reasonable rate. We were not rushed or pestered.
Dining room is quite ornate.

Author: Katinka Jussie B
Title: great service, amazing food!
Review: We went without booking beforehand, but even though the restaurant was full when we got there, they managed to smoothly make us a table and make everything ready so we got our food as soon as we sat down. The food was amazing, many different flavours and dishes that all tasted really good. Recommended!Show less

Author: momo11BrisbaneBrisbane, Australia
Title: Highlight of penang
Review: Our meal here was a highlight in an area that is know for its fantastic food (since of the best in the world in my opinion). The food was nothing short of amazing. The chicken curry kapitan was a real highlight. The building is lovely as well and the staff are lovely. Number 1 for a reason!!!Show less

Author: Edward K
Title: Stylish restaurant
Review: Inside the Seven Terraces hotel. The restaurant matches the hotel in style. Serves local style fusion food. Expect more local favor in the dishes. Generous portion. Moderate pricing but near the high end when benchmarked against the local restaurants.Show less

Author: weboflifeDelhi
Title: Certainly worth dining at Kebaya.
Review: Clean and delightful interpretation of Nonya food. Kebaya is ideal for a romantic dinner or a dinner for new conversations and reconnecting.

Author: red b
Title: Great local (but high end) fare!
Review:
Beautiful atmosphere, gorgeous decor, fantastic food, delicious cocktails and fabulous service.
Highly recommended

Author: Andrea L
Title: Superb!
Review: We had saved Kebaya for a special occasion and it was worth waiting for. We celebrated my husband’s birthday there last week. I could go on and on about our dinner but the other reviewers have said it all: it was simply wonderful.

Author: TomG493Leeds
Title: Superb
Review: We stayed at Seven Terraces with our children aged 3 and 5 in April 2014 (TA won't let me select further back than Aug 14). We had an early family dinner for 6 and the staff were great with the children and provided food tailored for them. The food was superb with every dish absolutely hitting the spot. The soft shell crab was a highlight as was the ambience with live piano music.Show less

Author: broughbadgerDunbar, United Kingdom
Title: Great decor, outstanding meal
Review: Booked dinner here based on reviews and as we were staying at hotel. Dinner is. 4 course set meal, there is a huge choice so you will find lots you will like. Portions are huge and we were advised only to book 3 mains, it was enough for 4 of us. Food is Nonya with additional western food, all with a modern twist and all delicious. Great service as well, would highly recommendShow less

Author: milo_k2014
Title: Maybe best dinner in life
Review: This restaurant will provide you really gourmet experience. There is a fixed menu, we tried three 4-course menus and they were all absolutely amazing. Environment is quite and looks really fancy. Price is really high when you compare to local average but this is really something. Reservation recommended - we've got last table.Show less

Author: RocketMelbourneMelbourne
Title: Fine dining in Penang
Review: We weren't staying at Seven Terraces but had booked the restaurant on the reviews of others. We weren't disappointed as the set price menu turned out to be really good with a small choice with regards to entrees, mains and desserts.What we had was delicious and we struggled to finish our meals.The wine list was okay with the cost being what you would expect in this part of the world. The only down side really was the location as the lane where the restaurant is located is a bit out of the way and badly lit especially when leaving later at night.Show less

Author: kelllipsCanberra, Australia
Title: Lovely experience and great dinner
Review: Glad we decided on kebaya for our swanky dinner. With so much good street food we needed it to be special and it was. The starters were ok but the main was excellent. The special duck red curry was so tasty and the duck so very tender. Dessert was A treat - the special of a durian creme brûlée - could have been so wrong but was just right. The service was particularly attentive but not over the top. I guess it is technically the quiet season so no trouble getting a reservation. The price is high for Penang but hardly a stretch compared to any capital city in Australia if you like good food it is worth it. Show less

Author: DerekCYCHong Kong, China
Title: Best Nyonya in Georgetown
Review: Staying in Seven Terraces Hotel was the highlight of our trip in Penang. Dining in Kebaya is the jewel. The Nyonya food there was modified, in a nice way. The heritage provided a wonderful old style ambiences that was memorable. I recommend to come early to walk around and enjoy the building and the gift shop in there. Absolutely beautiful Show less

Author: PookiecatKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Truly special
Review: It is the second time I've celebrated my birthday at Kebaya, and for me, there is nowhere else in Penang I would rather go. The food is delicious, the setting is really special and it just makes for a perfect experience.There seems to be quite a debate raging on Trip Advisor about the food, but whether it is fusion or not, Peranakan or not, Nyonya or not, authentic or not (etc.), for me, all the dishes are very flavourful and bring a unique set of tastes to the dinner plate. I would suggest going with an open mind, not stressing about the origins of the food and really enjoying the whole experience which the staff will do their utmost to help you enjoy.Show less

Author: Richard Y
Title: Well worth the premium pricing!
Review: The food was excellent as was the ambience. While the theme was peranakan nonya, the food was a little bit of fusion cuisine and quite refined. Well worth the premium pricing!

Author: sorboman1Sydney, Australia
Title: This is foodie heaven
Review: Having stayed at the boys place in Sri Lanka we decided to eat here on this trip due to their proven attention to detail. We were not disappointed as the place had been beautifully restored and was a great venue for their take on refined Penang food. Wines quite reasonable compared to some others.Show less

Author: AlmakrakenKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not overrated, just a simple place for two...or more
Review: I'm sure a lot of people have enjoyed their experience in Kebaya and written a lot of nice things about it...but I'm just gonna say this: This restaurant is really amazing. I wanted to say F$%king amazing but they wont let me.I had a great company, great food, great place and great live piano music!Show less

Author: khoo-boo-eng
Title: A Must
Review: If you are talking about highend Nyonya dishes both authentic and fusion, then this is the place. Serving and hospitality Excellent. The deco - truly Penang. Just very near to Muntri Mews.

Author: michelleh263Melbourne, Australia
Title: An affordable indulgence
Review: This restaurant is set inside the Seven Terraces Boutique Hotel. With the same attention to detail and understated elegance!The menu price includes four courses with plenty of choices from and Eurasian inspired fusion. So step back from the street stalls and surrounding cafes to experience the excellence that is Kebaya. You will not be disappointed.Show less

Author: dhcfMontreal, Canada
Title: Perfect!
Review: It was a perfect evening. We started with a drink at bababar before dinner at Kebaya. The food was fantastic and service was almost perfect (our waiter forgot to bring us our wine), beautiful setting, great atmosphere. Good for a romantic evening as well as a celebration.Show less

Author: JudiHC
Title: Perfection
Review: Beautiful dining space true to its heritage.  And so is the food.  Ate there three times and suspect I tasted everything on the menu and it's all very very good.  Small and appropriate wine list which has some nice choices.

Author: kirstieyatesLondon
Title: Beautiful venue and food
Review: Given its high rating on TA, we felt compelled to visit, but hadn't realized it's a 4 course set dinner!
