Due to the english pound being so strong, this made the restaurant amazing value for money.We actually stayed at the hotel thats connected (The Seven Terraces), and these two establishments are without doubt some of the best places we have ever visited. A great experience, cant recommend this highly enough!Show less

Author: Karen150161
Title: Elegant dining experience
Review: Excellent service,  set menu for 100RG  for four courses with plenty of options for each course .  The food was divine and very  good value. It was one of our favourite dining experiences in Penang.

Author: Otwal_Helsinki, Finland
Title: Dine here.
Review: The set menu (RM 100) might sound expensive, but it's well worth the money.You get to choose four dishes from the wide selection. We took in total eight different dishes and all of them were great. But even better, if possible, was the service and the place itself. The staff made us feel extremely welcome and important and there was a skillful pianist playing live music.They also have a good selection of reasonably priced wines. Go here.Show less

Author: ScottLoarPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Beautifully Southeast Asian Premises
Review: Many, many restaurants lay claim to the title "nonya" which has become a euphemism for good Malaysian food in the peranakan style, but that society no longer exists (peranakan is strictly defined as the merchant class society comprising Straits Chinese males who married Muslim Malay women, resulting in a distinctive, syncretic culture that flourished in the last half of the 19th and very early 20th centuries; today the term "peranakan" has been loosely but incorrectly appropriated to include Straits Chinese) as only relics such as a few restored homes, some jewelry and antiques, seppia-coloured photographs, and the idea of "nonya" cooking remain. So said, the Kebaya restaurant and the larger premises of Seven Terraces are a syncretic mix of traditional peranakan style - including shelves and shelves of antiques - and Western taste.First the premises. Beautiful. The Seven Terraces lobby, just beyond the restaurant if entering from Lebuh Stewart, is done in fine taste, the best I've seen in Southeast Asia, and amplified in the Kebaya restaurant. This restaurant is well worth a visit if only to tour the premises, but the food does reach the high limits of that euphemism "nonya", and as its namesake the food is a synthesis of tradition with innovation. I hosted a Chinese couple to dinner, fourth-generation in Penang, and they were impressed by the surroundings as well as the taste.Note that this restaurant by Penang standards (and Penangites are infamous for cheap eats) is expensive, each set costing 100++MR per person (about US$40 each), but well worth the expense. This place is best for dinner with business associates, a date, or even a good meal by oneself, civilized to the max. If you're a visitor this is the one place in Penang to which you must go and enjoy the food and surroundings. If you have little or no experience of Malay and Straits Chinese food follow the recommendations of the maitre d'.Show less

Author: Arthur_MarthaBrisbane
Title: good even for local tourists
Review: A Ringgit 100 menu allows you to select a starter, mains, veg and dessert. I think it is very good value because the food is well prepared, service is excellent and the decor ... superb. Many locals will not pay for this, but if you are looking for a special evening, it's hard to beat. The duck (lor ark) was delicious, as were the entrees and desserts.Show less

Author: 492traveller1974Toowoomba, Australia
Title: Total class
Review: With such great reviews it was a no brainer to eat here and it did not disappoint. Seven Terraces is an extraordinary building and we felt so fortunate to see this hotel and dine in such a lovely restaurant. The food was incredible, particularly the prawn curry and the beans with the sambal goreng sauce. We had a gorgeous mousse for dessert also that my husband ordered. I honestly do not know if the flavours were correct as the curries were quite mild and if they are tailored to the western palate but I found the food so elegant and the best that we had on our 2 week stay in Malaysia. I would go back to Penang just to eat here and it was difficult not to go again while we were in Penang for a few more days.Show less

Author: Mon59Kuala Lumpur
Title: Nice place for entertaining
Review: The food here seems to have been tailored to the western palate with mild flavours so if one is looking for 100% authentic peranakan food, you will not find it here. However, for what it is, the food is tasty and the ambience and service is faultless. A must-visit hotel for its beautiful ambience and decor. Steeped in tradition.Show less

Author: Suet_YuHong Kong, China
Title: very good service, nice atmosphere and food
Review: We had a family trip and visited Kebaya for dinner. The communication before hand was very smooth and easy. When we arrived, the decoration and the ambience of the restaurant was great. All the staff are very welcoming and attentive to details. Jackie and waiter who served our table were very good. They gave good advice to us. The food was good. After the meal, Marcus (the hotel manager) took our whole group to tour around the hotel. He is very passionate. We enjoyed the night there and really like the ambience and service of this restaurant.Show less

Author: Joe MManchester, New Hampshire
Title: Amazing food with allot of class
Review: Amazing. That word just about sums up our visit to Kebaya. This place was a bit of a change from our normal pace of checking out local food stalls and local eateries. It was nice to have a air conditioned sit down where we could enjoy fine wine, drink and a fine dining twist on local delicacies.Show less

Author: roshanm188Hong Kong, China
Title: Great date nite with my wife
Review: Restaurant is gorgeousMarcus the manager and Jackie the hostess are wonderfulTheir team including bartender post and waiter Dilip are top notchTheir is a large menu with many options of APs mains side and desertsBar is super kool and the fresh juices are magnificentPiano player is a huge plus and makes the ambience ever more electic and chiqueFood is deliciousAnd great value for moneyWe will come backShow less

Author: MelbourneJanineMelbourne, Australia
Title: Lovely dinner for my birthday
Review: I'm glad I booked this restaurant before leaving home, as it is very popular. For 100 ringgit we had a four course meal, with at least a couple of choices for each course. The waitress was very helpful in helping us choose and we were very happy with everything we ate. Especially good was the vegetable tempura and the pandan flavoured creme caramel dessert. We had a good bottle of Chilean white wine. A great experience.Show less

Author: 37SteveD37London, United Kingdom
Title: Truly superb
Review: I've had many a fantastic eating out experience around the world but the 2 meals experienced recently here are up there with the best. The whole experience was spot on: excellent service - friendly, professional but never overbearing; a beautiful dining room and the food was magnificent. I won't single out any dish as everything sampled was delicious. Though there are only 5-6 options for each of starters, mains and desserts, plus 4 side vegetable options, and we largely ate different things across the 2 visits, there were still things on the menu I wish I'd been able to try. The wine list is decent and competitively priced and they mix a mean cocktail - special mention for the Georgetown Cooler. The fact that this tremendous experience with 4 courses, plus a cocktail and a bottle of wine came to only about £40 a head is all the more amazing. If I could dispense 6 stars I would. Show less

Author: narni4Perth, Australia
Title: Perfect for a celebration Dinner
Review: The restaurant is very opulent with magnificent furniture throughout and is part of the Seven Terraces Boutique Hotel.It features classic Straits and Indo-Chinese cuisine.The four course Menu has choices to satisfy most.The best dish of our selection was Lor Ark- a Duck Confit absolutely delicious.We celebrated our 50th Wedding Anniversary and for RM360 including wines and flowers was good value .Show less

Author: Frequenttraveller076Japan
Title: Very fine, uniquely elegant dining experience
Review: By any international standards Kebaya stands out as a memorable establishment. The long, exceptionally elegant dining-room decorated with high personalized style, prepares one for an excellent meal. I dined there twice with only one dish out of eight slightly disappointing. I am surprised to read among recent reviews a harsh view of the sous-vide pork belly. Mine was superb. (The lamb, in a heavy sauce, somewhat less so.) Kebaya can be recommended without reservation as holding its own with the best Asian restaurants of the world.Show less

Author: Mumbai2Johannesburg, South Africa
Title: Beautiful experience
Review: Went to this restaurant with family who lives in Malaysia. . We waited for family in the bar area as this would be a nice place to absorb the ambience of the restaurant before dinner. Seating was for 3 and we requested 1 more chair. Jenny the maître dee suggested we have our pre dinner drinks at our table.Not a good suggestion: as we got to our table the waiting staff was rather quick to take our meal order. The waiting staff was pleasant but the whole dinning experience became a little rushed. When eating at a venue like this one would think that the dinning experience would be slower. The meal was mediocre as I think I had better in Penang.the venue actually overshadowed the actual meal.Show less

Author: libero7London
Title: Best restaurant in Malaysia
Review: Knew it would be good, didn't realise it would be that good. Weren't quite sure what to expect when we pulled up in front of the Seven Terraces hotel but were quickly swept through the incredible public areas through to the restaurant. The style is truly beautiful, the serene ambience and zen furnishings almost felt a bit like being in a riad in the middle of Marrakech.Service was very friendly and efficient, we had a drink in the bar and were then shown to our table when our food was ready. Menu is really interesting and packed full of Malaysian specialities done in a modern way. The food was outstanding - red snapper was my pick of the dishes but all of our party raved about their meals. Creme brulees also delicious. Price was very reasonable considering the quality, 100 ringgit for 4 courses which is a steal for an awesome meal in a restaurant bursting with atmosphere.Show less

Author: DaveEgglestoneMawson Lakes, Australia
Title: Wow.
Review: I would have to say having eaten lots of asian food that this would rate as the best ever. The silky sauce for the prawns was magnificent as was the snapper in yellow curry sauce. The wingbean salad with pomegranate was very tasty and a good amount of heat. Don't expect the drinks to be cheap especially the wine but it is asia after all. Overall a lovely experience shared with friends in a great spot. PS share some wine with the somellier/waiter. They certainly appreciated it and the smiles in response were worth it!Show less

Author: WillyWahPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: You wont regret to dine here
Review: yeah, i know many of the locals told me that this restaurant is not cheap and expensive. But I keen to try by myself bfore making any judgement, me and my other two blogger fren were there on April, we have nothing to complain about it, nice food, nice environment it is worth to pay for the food.I have tasted quite alot of nyonya food in town, but what make me happy was the dishes here was delicious and surprising. Chef is creative and innovative to infuse french method to the local nyonya food, I love it. I will back again definitely.Show less

Author: karenr132Baltimore, Maryland
Title: An unforgettable dining experience
Review: I only eat at my hotel's restaurant if it's almost midnight, there's blizzard outside and the snack machine is broken. I stayed at the Seven Terraces for two nights and on the first night I ate at a local street market (good and cheap!) but when I came back to the hotel I walked through Kebaya and the aromas made my mouth water. I thought if I was going to try a restaurant attached to a hotel, this one would be it.Well, this was one of the best meals I ever had! I had prawns in a curry sauce, sambal goreng and to top it off, the jack fruit creme brulee. I asked for more rice because I was not going to let one drop of the luscious gravies remain on my plate. I have never left the table more satisifed!When I think of times I spend much more money on far inferior meals, the 100 ringgit cost for 4 courses was an absolute bargain!!Show less

Author: 885maddiehSydney, Australia
Title: Amazing!
Review: This is easily one of the best meals I have ever had! Everything we had was out of this world, the depth of flavour and beautiful cooking of everything makes it a great experience. It's about 100RM++ for four courses, well worth every cent! The otak otak entree was amazing! The main course duck was also sensational! The idea here is to order different things and share around the table which we did. So you get the option to try lots of different things. And i can assure you that everything was sensational! The service is great, all the staff were attentive. The restaurant itself is stunning! From the second you walk in you are overwhelmed by the beauty of the building. There is a live pianist playing which just adds to the experience. I highly recommend a visit!Show less

Author: Bruce T
Title: Your Tastebuds Will Sing!
Review: One of THE GREAT meals of all time, outstanding ambience, service and food, words do not and cannot describe how happy your tastebuds will be nor the sheer all round excellence of this sublime experience.

Author: Richard MHong Kong, China
Title: Beautiful surroundings and beautiful food
Review: We came as tourists and loved it. The setting is gorgeous and the food is wonderfully presented on lovely porcelain. For a four course meal (RM116) you can't go wrong. I could understand why some might not consider the food totally authentic but for foreign tourists wanting a modern take on traditional cuisine in a lovely room, it hits the spot. We had our share of street food and beach food and wanted a grown up venue to relax after a long day. We loved it and would recommend to friends.Show less

Author: btbmShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Suitable for Tourists
Review: The taste of the food is more suitable for western palate - though the angle beans kerabu, the thai salad and tong yuen are worth a mention.Saving grace - Dilip our waiter - very good service and put us all at ease. Alice is not too bad too.Not happy that Marcus told my guest that he can't take photo with the flash on as it "disturbs" the other diners. Look we were placed at the very end of the dining hall away from all other guests - why were we put there because apparently there were 10 of us and we can only be placed at that very end near the bar. I hardly thinks your guests can be disturb by the flash bulb when we are so far way from everyone and what more the flash was pointing to the ceilings. Should have informed me earlier so I can warn my guests instead of embarrassing me in the situation.I realised I am paying more for the ambience rather than the food but that is also spoilt!Show less

Author: ZLKingSingapore
Title: Handmade and beautifully Fused
Review: " A new approach to Classic Straits and Indochinese Cuisine " That's what is on the menu of the Kebaya Restaurant at 7 Terraces, but what an understatement, for dinner that night was simply sublime. The wing bean salad, miang kham and crispy joo hoo were fabulous morsels packed with flavor.The lor ark was a revelation, a reinterpretation of braised duck with orange and plum segments. The catfish was fried with batter and smothered with a home made compote, a veritable explosion for our taste buds.Would I come again...? Yesssss!!Show less

Author: Becky UGreater London, United Kingdom
Title: Absolutely Stunning
Review: I have eaten here 3 times and every single time I have been it has been faultless. Everything about it is just incredible- the staff, the service, the atmosphere and the building just work perfectly. I don't think I really want to say much as I do not want to spoil the experience for you but all I can say is you would be missing out on one of the best meals in Georgetown. MENU/ PRICE: There is a set menu and you pick one dish from each course, but you can order extras if you like. It costs RM100 per set of food which for the quality of food is a bargain! Portion sizes for main are very good and the desserts are incredible. DRINKS: there is a bar attached to he restaurant which is fab to go to before your meal to enjoy the atmosphere. I hope this helps. P.s the hotel it also incredible if you are looking for an unusual and authentic hotel. Beautiful! P.p.s I have rated outdoor seating as 5* by accident but there isn't any... But if they had it would be 5*!!Show less

Author: PhilN415
Title: Top notch
Review: Visited the restaurant during April. Top notch food, duck superb, no complaints. Wish I stayed in the hotel part to break up our penang holiday

Author: cheah99Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Over-rated restaurant more suited for tourists!
Review: I ate here twice and both times I find both the food to be average at best. The only food worth a mention is the glutinous rice ball dessert- this dessert has both the required texture and taste. The restaurant's take on several local dishes is average at best and probably more suited to the tourists looking for a sort of local flavour in a clean & nice setting. While the food is generally average, I've given the restaurant a 'poor' rating by virtue of the cost of eating here-There are certainly less hyped and better value restaurants in Penang.Show less

Author: Terry PPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Amazing experience in Georgetown Penang
Review: If you're looking for great food in a stylish setting with a touch of old-world romance then this is the place for you. The added bonus is that it doesn't even cost the earth!It's located in the Seven Terraces Hotel which is a beautifully refurbished terrace of shop houses in the heart of Georgetown. The food consists of a set menu of starter, main course with greens, and dessert. You have a choice of around 4-5 dishes in each course and there is usually a daily special too. Price ... RM100++ per person . A good choice of wines and cocktails so get there early to enjoy a relaxing aperitif before dinner. The service is excellent and nothing is too much trouble. Best to book on weekends. Enjoy!Show less

Author: RosserdaleMt Eliza, Australia
Title: The Jewel of Penang
Review: The restaurant is set in a beautifully restored terrace house in Georgetown. The area is a little seedy but has really rustic charm and authenticity. Chris the owner is rightfully very proud of his achievement in bringing his beloved nyonya food Into the 21st century. The dishes are beautifully presented and prepared with the freshest of ingredients. The herbs and spices create a flavour sensation with each and every dish. This was undoubtably the highlight of our trip to Penang. A must visit restaurant at ridiculously cheap pricesShow less

Author: pppinotStrathfieldsaye VIC
Title: A special place to remember
Review: Had the set nyonya style menu. The food was delicious with generous portions and served at a comfortable pace. This was by a long way our best meal for the three week holiday in Malaysia, in fact I can't recall to many better ones anywhere. Had cocktails in the bar area before our meal which added to occasion. We were also entertained by a very competent pianist. Kebaya is part of Severn Terraces both the accommodation and restaurant are class acts. If your looking for something special this the place to comeShow less

Author: kevin c
Title: Nice ambience and great food
Review: Great ambience with pianist playing in the background. The nonya food was delicious, and found the portion to be appropriate. Service was excellent.

Author: Guntsche
Title: Best environment for a dinner in Georgetown
Review: This was not my first time at this excellent restaurant. And again the mail was great and the atmosphere great. Try the lamp and follow the daily recommendations!

Author: theng820Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Rigid
Review: I have to fully agree with some reviewers on the menu part. The food selection is pretty scarce and it is strictly on a set-meal basis. That's right folks, no ala-carte order! This doesn't fit in very well with me because I do not like to be forced into ordering a 4-course meal without having the chance to order what I prefer or what my family members prefer. Waiters there were unable to address my queries well too. I am not nit-picking on the food but rather the whole dining experience. Hence, the 1-star rating.Show less

Author: Juliet CKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Kids not allowed
Review: Guess this is not a kid friendly restaurant. We had wanted to try the Kebaya restaurant, and were looking forward to it. We tried to change our dinner booking to 8pm but were told that we can't bring in kids after 8pm because they will be disruptive to guests. We won't be visiting this place and won't recommend it to families or even to stay just in case they disrupt their guests or break any precious things in there.Show less

Author: Bruce BLaunceston, Australia
Title: In top 5 best dinner ever
Review: Don't deny yourself the pleasure of dining in this restaurant if you have the good fortune to be in Penang. The venue, the ambience, the music, the friendliness and welcome were only surpassed by the quality and flavours of the meals presented and add to this an inspired range of wines, and you have the makings for a treasured dining experience.Show less

Author: Casa62Brisbane, Australia
Title: Amazing food and service; gorgeous setting
Review: We went here for dinner on New Years Day and this is the best meal we have had in a long time. We kicked off with cocktails (RM28++) and then sat down for our four course nonya meal (RM100++) with endless rice. We shared two entrees, two mains, two vegetable dishes and two desserts. I'm still dreaming about otak,otak, pork belly sous vide, braised duck with spiced plum, oranges and star anise, morning glory with garlic and the coconut balls in milk. Exquisite. Sure this is expensive for Penang but so worth it after lots of cheap curry! Not to be missed! Show less

Author: JulieDPerthPerth
Title: A must in Penang
Review: Walking down dark Stewart Lane, you enter one of the treasures of Penang. Kebaya serves a 4 course degustation menu for R100++. You can eat a lot cheaper in Penang, but for the equivalent of the local Chinese at home this is amazing value. Lots of choices for each course. Waiter suggested we both choose different items and share. We had Prawn cups, squid roll, duck curry, soft shell crab, sautéed and tempura vegetables, and mousse and crenels brûlée to finish. You can order extra courses, but quantity was more than enough. wine prices were reasonable and the service was attentive. Ambience of the restaurant was beautiful. A true find.You need to make a reservation. Arrived Penang Thursday and couldn't get reservation until Sunday.Show less

Author: MADSemaphoreMelbourne, Australia
Title: Fine Dining not to be missed
Review: Treat yourself to the experience of Fine Dining for great value at Kebaya. Generous serves of tasty dishes from a well selected and thoughtful menu. The additional warm welcome, outstanding service and beautiful live piano playing added to the delightful ambience. If you're able, enjoy some cocktails from the bar area. A thoroughly enjoyable evening and we'd recommend it to all who are visiting Georgetown.Show less

Author: TurquoisePort
Title: Great!
Review:
We ate at Kebaya following friends' recommendation and the place did not disappoint!
Beautifully decorated, very attentive service, piano player.
Delicious food and plenty of it!

Author: SherborneCelt
Title: Fantastic
Review: Having read great things about this restaurant, we had to give it a go. It totally lived up to our expectations. Beautiful food, lovely surroundings and excellent service!

Author: TheYumList
Title: Great Taste of Penang
Review: Lovely Peranakan setting and delicious food. When we visited the meals only came in a set so you had to make a minimum purchase - ie no a la carte. We enjoyed every bite.

Author: MumtoScruffyYorkshire, United Kingdom
Title: Consistently Good
Review: We ate at this restaurant on our previous visit to Penang in December and it left us wanting more. So without hesitation on our return to Penang, we headed to it and again experienced wonderful food, wine, ambiance and fantastic service. Everything about the evening was just as good as we remembered and a restaurant we will difinately be returning to. The only very minor criticism we have is that the menu hadn't changed from our previous visits and because it only has a small selection of dishes to choose from on each course we found that we ordered exactly the same ones that we had before. It was for this reason that we cancelled our reservation for a few nights later because we didn't want the same food again.Show less

Author: SophiaKAthens, Greece
Title: Fantastic restaurant, delicious food with chic ambiance
Review: A fantastic restaurant in Georgetown housed in an old colonial building. The food is outstanding, the ambiance wonderful and the service superb but discreet. Menu is fixed but there is a great variety to choose from and all dishes came beautifully presented. If you are in Georgetown don’t miss this place. Special thanks to the staff; when I called for a reservation (our last evening in Georgetown), restaurant was fully booked but managed to accommodate us.Show less

Author: hamish88scotland
Title: not as good as they say
Review: Ok it was in a wonderful setting. Nicely renovated but situated in a bit of a rundown street.The service I thought was impeccable. You order off a set menu of which you pick four items. A starter,A main,a side of vegetables and a dessert.There were six of us so we got most of the things off the limited menu.The starters were actually not bad, an interesting choice to pick from. The best of the lot I thought was the miniature pies which came with a wonderful dipping sauce. The rest were good but not great. The mains......what can I say.. Culture clash of western and Asian food? The lamb shank was tender but the flavours weren't deep.The duck in which we got a leg and a bit of breast, the breast was actually quite chewy though the leg was fine. The curry kapitan was.... Meh. S'alright.The king prawn curry was also Ok, flavours were quite good.The fish... It was a nice price of fish but we didn't like the marinade.The rest were hmmmmm.... It's Ok but nothing outstandingAlso got to add all the portions were generous in size.The price for six with a drink each came to just under 800rm.Now for western standards that's nowhere expensive just a normal night out.But for penang it's a bit toppy. Remember you can get a seafood buffet with unlimited lobster in a five star premises for around the same price.I can probably understand where the money is going as it is in a wonderfully refurbished colonial setting and I don't mind at all paying the price. The food was Ok not bad by any means and remember my taste may be different to yours and you might find it great.But personally the mains would be what I expect from a normal restaurant back in the UK.Except I wanted to try something else when I come to penang.And if you DO want to try something else that is very keenly priced there is always jawi house.....Show less

Author: Hotflop2Reading, England
Title: Interesting food and attentive service
Review: We chose to eat at Kebaya on the basis of Trip Advisor reviews and were definitely not disappointed. I would describe it as fusion food rather than traditional Nonya cuisine, but delicious and beautifully presented.Our waiter was very attentive, without being at all intrusive and assisted us with our selection.We enjoyed sharing our choice of dishes - stopped either of us getting "food envy".We thought the meal was excellent value for money.The restoration of the hotel is fantastic and, from what I could see on a trip to the loo, would be a great place to stay.We liked the ambiance so much we returned for drinks in the bar on our last night in Penang.(You could easily be put off on your walk to the hotel / restaurant, as much of the surrounding buildings are pretty run down. Dont be!!)Show less

Author: Christopher HToulouse
Title: Beautiful restaurant
Review: We discovered the Baba Nonya cuisine in Malacca,the Kebaya which is part of the Seven Terraces Hotel in a beautifuly restored shop house it offers modern Baba Nonya cuisine,The dinner was superb and lived up to the Baba Nonya tradition,in a refined & very chic atmosphere.The service was discreet and efficient,and certainly value for money.The wine was excellent,we chose a South African white which is on a par with our French wines.Realy Worth the detour if visiting the World Heritage city of Georgetown.Show less

Author: flyingbreakLeeds, United Kingdom
Title: High quality food, fantastic venue
Review: A fantastic restaurant in Georgetown. It is probably one of the most expensive you'll find, but the price, I believe, was worth it. It is a set menu every night, with 4 choices per person, of starter, main, side and desert, so with two of us, we got to taste 8 fantastic dishes. The food is beautifully presented, and the flavours were fantastic. The restaurant is in old colonial style building, which looks magnificent inside. The staff were attentive without being in the way.I can't fault anything about the restaurant, it was very impressive!Show less

Author: Fiparker7London, United Kingdom
Title: Really Amazing place
Review: We booked a tabled at this restaurant a day ahead having read the trip advisor reviews! Glad we booked, as it was busy! When we booked they seemed keen to explain the pricing, I guess it may have proved a problem in the past! In a month in Thailand and Malaysia this was the most expensive place we have eaten (I should make clear that we like the cheap and cheerful, couldn't afford this every night and and are happy to forgo plush surroundings). This meal was a treat... And what a treat it was. It is absolutely terrific and a fraction of the cost you would pay for this quality in many other cities. It's a fixed price menu 100 ringers, about 18 UK pound for starter, main which comes with rice, veg and a desert. This simplifies it too much, the choice is great, portions generous and it's a sophisticated menu. Wine was excellent and much cheaper than at our hotel! Both my partner and I thought the food was fantastic. We had a drink at the bar before dinner, there is a pianist playing throughout the evening and the decor of the restaurant is beautiful! Really seems to give a glimpse into Penang's past! I can't recommend this restaurant highly enough. Food was excellent as was the service, beautiful setting and in my view reasonably priced for the quality of the restaurant! Show less

Author: Mark8888Singapore, Singapore
Title: Wonderful food and ambience - we'll be back
Review: Went with wife, kids and in-laws and enjoyed a truly fantastic dining experience. Helpful booking by phone and they proposed to allow the young kids to eat from the adult set menu and once there the service was attentive & helpful. The menu had some unique twists and everything was nicely presented and tasted great. The dining room itself is full of wonderful antiques set in a converted shop house and this just adds to the experience.Show less

Author: marco063
Title: Verry good
Review: One of the best in Malasia. The service was one of the  best. The furniture and the ANTiqutes items in the restaurant are verry nice.

Author: John SMelbourne, Australia
Title: WOW experience
Review: The four of us recently went to Kebaya in Georgetown. The most amazing food experience we had. Outstanding food, wonderful ambiance and all with the constant tones of a magnificent piano player. The service was impeccable and the price was so low it was amazing. After Penang we visited Dubai and went to perhaps 3 of the most expensive resturant I have ever been to at well of US$400/person. However these did not compare to Kebaya. If you are in Penang, do yourself a favour and don't miss it. It is a must!Show less

Author: JobbonesAdelaide, South Australia
Title: My First Nonya Cuisine
Review: We had been recommended this restaurant for our Nonya experience by a regular to Penang. Whether it was the best Nonya, I don't know given my level of knowledge. However we both agreed that the night was amongst our best. The ambience, the food and service were all good.I had checked Tripadvisor (as always) before we booked and saw the comments on fixed price. This is a non event. In Australia you would be lucky to get a main course for this money, here it is four fantastic dishes. This is a top restaurant not a street stallShow less

Author: NiglettiMelbourne, Australia
Title: Totally Brilliant Meal & setting
Review: Not often we are completely impressed by a location & the food.The hotel is stunning. Period. If you don't get it then you miss the point.The food & service was brilliant. best we had in Malaysia so far after nearly two weeks of travel.At RM100 for 4 courses it was truly excellent value. This ain't MacDonalds, but seriously its only $33 for this meal p/p is the steal of the century.Service was just right, attentive with out being in your face.The snapper was the standout & the creme brulee one of the best, believe me we sample every creme brulee on menus around the world - not traditional, but wow!Lots of food, we were there with our two children 8 & 10, made most welcome, well done .Show less

Author: 894sarac894Bournemouth, United Kingdom
Title: Great Value
Review: We ate here on christmas day. The menu was a set menu for 100 MYR each which included a starter, a main, a veg dish and a desert. All of it was fabulous and we couldn't fault a thing, it was definitely worth the money. The service was fantastic too.Inside the restaurant is beautiful, tiled floors and wooden panelled walls, worth popping in for a cocktail / drink if you don't fancy eating here.Show less

Author: cmleicesterPhnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: Amazing food served by wonderful staff
Review: Many thanks to Dinesh and Diop for making a great night and going above and beyond to make an excellent meal in lovely surroundings outstanding. Lamb shank and roasted belly pork mains were to die for, most wines available by the glass and a R100 4 course dinner is well worth a visit. I will be dining there again.Show less

Author: V_WindmillLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic meal
Review: Food was fantastic and atmosphere in historic Seven Terraces great. Although this is expensive by local standards, compared to what I would expect to pay back in the UK for a meal of equivalent quality, I found this to be good value. Set price for 4 courses - pandan creme brûlée in particular is delicious. Cocktails also excellent (particularly after rip-off prices of Singapore Slings in larger hotels).This is a real experience - would definitely recommend.Show less

Author: assampedas
Title: Kebaya Restaurant is amazing
Review: What a wonderful dinner we had at the Kebaya Restaurant. Impeccably beautiful surroundings but more importantly, stunning dishes which attempt a Peranakan-Western fusion without losing that recognisable nonya flavour. Highly recommended for a special dinner.

Author: Wayne TBrisbane, Australia
Title: Penang's best restaurant?
Review: It has to be!! The food, the wine, the staff, the atmosphere, just everything. Even the music being played on the Grand Piano, it was all just wonderful. My wife and I enjoyed our meals so much, we returned two nights later to try more of the exciting choices on the menu. We were not disappointed, it was just great. Can't wait for our next visit to Georgetown and Kebaya Restaurant.Show less

Author: MumtoScruffyYorkshire, United Kingdom
Title: Wow Wow Wow
Review: The title says it all. the food is some of the best we have ever experienced.We visited Kebaya on our second night in Penang and had to really discipline ourselves not to rush back the following evening however, our willpower was short lived and we returned on the 4th night for our farewell meal. Each visit was a gastronomic experience for us, we had food which we had never experienced before and the fact that there is only 4 or 5 choices for each course helped us to select a balanced menu in terms of flavours and textures. If you want to pay street stall prices then this place is not for you however, if you require wonderful food served in jaw dropping surroundings by wonderful people at a reasonable price then I would suggest that you give it a try - you will not be disappointed. Without doubt we will be returning as soon as possible.Show less

Author: thebrews10Bradford, United Kingdom
Title: Christmas dinner nonya style
Review: We decided that as it was Christmas Day we should have a more upmarket Penang dining experience and Kebaya did not disappoint. They offer a set 4 course meal for 100 ringgit per head and I convinced my other half that it would be best if I chose all the courses. Ever single dish was superb though I did find myself looking at neighbouring tables and thinking that looks good, I'll try that next time. There was a bit of a mix up over our booking which had been made by the hotel and the restaurant had no record of it, however the manager sorted it and we were given a table. The decor was traditional nonya and the service excellent. All I can say is - roll on the next visit!Show less

Author: Jane TBrisbane, Australia
Title: As good as I remembered!
Review: Kebaya is not only a beautiful, stylish restaurant, but its food is the best I have eaten in Georgetown. During our 5 night stay in Georgetown, we had two meals at Kebaya. The portion sizes are perfect, the food superb and the service is excellent. Much as I loved eating in tiny restaurants and stalls in Little India and Chinatown, it was a real treat to be able to eat and drink at leisure in a such a gorgeous setting. No matter how short my next visit to Georgetown, dining at Kebaya will certainly be on my itinerary.Show less

Author: MLSun1Singapore
Title: very nice food
Review: My family and I have seen rave reviews and decided to make it a point to make a trip to Kebaya on our most recent trip to Penang. We asked for recommendation from the staff and tried some outstanding dishes and desserts ie. Chao Tom (minced chicken paste wrapped in herbs & lettuce), Grilled Snapper (otak), Gula Melaka mousse & Pandan Creme brulee. Service from staff was attentive as they taught us how to assemble and eat the chao tom so as to appreciate the taste. Well done and we certainly enjoyed the food, ambience and live music performance!Though we have enjoyed our dinner and services at the end of the day, our first impression was not too good:When we first step into restaurant without reservation, we were immediately led to the side of restaurant, shown the menu and highlighted on the pricing $100 per pax (while still standing)... Hmm, didn't seemed too welcoming and friendly on first impression. Subsequently, when other patrons arrived, they didn't get the same treatment as we did.. certainly hope treatment given is not based on appearance from your esteemed restaurant. Hope that this feedback is received constructively and helps your services as we really love your food!Show less

Author: StudleyToowoombaToowoomba
Title: Blast from the past...
Review: Enough has been said by others about how brilliant the food is at Kebaya, and it is. The wonderful restoration of these seven contiguous, heritage-listed terraces in Muntri Street by Christopher Ong is the other half of the story, and why you should not miss the opportunity of at least indulging yourself in a great dining experience at this restaurant even if you are not staying at Seven Terraces. The cuisine is presented as "Nyonya Fusion". The re-creation of a 1920s-40s ambience in Kebaya is also a kind of fusion between Art Deco and the contemporary upper class Malaysian/Chinese lifestyle of the era. Mr Ong has used a mixture of period and repro furniture and fittings, including painstakingly restored floor tiles, to re-create his own version of this fabulous period down to almost trivial details. His attention to authenticity and good taste are exemplary. The beautiful bar at Kebaya even has original stools from one the original E&O bars; apparently he snapped these up at one of their chuck-out sales when they (unwisely) decided to "move forward" into the 21st century! The whole effect is subtle but stunning, especially in the evening when the place starts to fill up with pretty glamorous looking people (my wife & I being rather daggy Australian holidaymakers were the exception the night we went there, although we tried our best - and I hasten to add that my wife looked gorgeous as usual). The food and service are flawless, and it's all a trip back into dreamland, never more so than when the piano player caresses the baby grand piano into life with a blend of Gershwin, Berlin and Kern & Co. You truly expect to see Bogie & Bacall slink out from behind one of the potted palms! I see that many people have reservations about the expense of dining at Kebaya. I have completely forgotten what we paid for one of the most memorable experiences I have had as a lifelong traveller, but I see that the price range is quoted as "A$17 - A$39". All I can say is - you cannot be serious. Do not go to Penang and miss this.Show less

Author: Ian MBath, UK
Title: An absolute delight
Review: The food is an excellent fusion of Asian and European. It's a fixed menu and every dish we tried was really enjoyable. The food and the wine are both very good value for money and the very attentive and friendly service complete a very nice evening. Very highly recommended. Show less

Author: LiniC_13Choeng Thale, Thailand
Title: Excellent restaurant
Review: Highly recommended for a special evening. Delicious food, very high quality. Excellent for a special occasion. Lovely decor and excellent service. We would have eaten here more during our trip, but there is a 4 course requirement/ set price menu (vs a la carte) and which is a bit too much food for us every night. Although the experience and quality of the cooking means that the set menu is actually very good value.Show less

Author: george b
Title: Good fusion
Review: You must try this place the atmosphere is good service so so but friendly and good food if you do not mind pay high price

Author: snuff82MelbourneAltona, Australia
Title: Great ambiance and fantastic food
Review: This restaurant is set inside a beautifully resorted traditional house which is now a boutique hotel. Though you cannot see much of the hotel because it's a private area for the guests, if you use the restrooms you have a bit of a glimpse of the rest of the complex. The four-course set menu did not fail to impress (100RM not including taxes) and the drinks menu is extensive. The staff were helpful and very attentive, without being intrusive or rushing us to choose our meals/drinks. Our waitress was also very helpful in helping us to select our dishes based on our preferences and dietary needs. My only slight grumble is that I would have preferred the entree and mains to be served at a higher temperature as they cooled off very quickly - when you're trying to savor your meal you want it to stay reasonably hot! Show less

Author: Egbert192
Title: Dining in style
Review: We had a most remarkable dinner at Kebaya, enjoying the delicious food, the beauty of the historic ambiance and the excellent service. Every aspect was perfect. We particularly loved the desserts, which were outstanding both in taste and in creativity ("where East meets West").

Author: BeachesAreBest123Columbia, Connecticut
Title: Delicious Nyonya-fusion food
Review: We had a delicious dinner here while in Penang, recently. The restaurant is in a historic house that is beautifully decorated with Peranakan antiques. The live piano music helps set the mood. The set menu had a number of interesting choices; we chose different dishes so we could share. We had Chao Tom (minced prawn, herbs and spices wrapped around a sugar cane stalk and grilled) and a Kebaya Banh Xeo dish for appetizers, both delicious. The Prawn Curry was out of this world, as were the Nyonya style desserts. We went all out and had a bottle of wine too. I can see why this restaurant is rated #1 currently in Penang. Would be happy to go back!Show less

Author: Mezzanine11
Title: Delicious!
Review: We had a fabulous dinner after choosing the restaurant from trip advisor. The decor, ambience, food, staff and value for money mean we will be recommending it to anyone who visits Penang. Make sure you have a drink at the bar first with Podi!

Author: SebastianVuHo Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Title: Fantastic dinner!!
Review: We were on holiday in Penang and I selected this restaurant after browsing Tripadvisor.I agree with the rest of the past patrons that this restaurant deserves its number one spot.The hotel (Seven Terraces) with is connected to the restaurant is outstandingly beautiful. Nice furniture and decoration. It was that the hotel was fully booked, otherwise we would have stayed here.The restaurant itself too is nice. I really like the decoration with displaying cabinets filled with nyonya style porcelain. I am jealous now.There is only the option to take the set menu of four courses, so we selected two of each and we could share. The price is very reasonable the menu.Very nice food, the appetisers with prawns were very nice, the main course with duck and its sauce, wow!!!, that was just awesome; the spices in the sauce made it taste really like Christmas. My favourite. The desserts were good too.Staff was friendly and showed us the picture book of the renovation of the hotel and restaurant.Tip: visit the antique shop too. Beautiful nyonya pieces of antiques, furniture and porcelain.Show less

Author: JeremyKnottRobertsbridge, United Kingdom
Title: Lovely food in a very relaxing setting
Review: The taxi driver struggled to find it despite actually first pulling up outside the hotel, but the bell boy hadn't heard of the restaurant! Later we discovered that it is in fact attached to the same hotel so not sure where that bell boy was from but clearly not a local!Once inside we were struck by a beautiful room with piano music playing discretely. On offer was a four course meal at a fixed 100RM price, but the vegetables counted as one course so in fact a thee course meal! Nonetheless the food was fabulous. Full of flavour and spices - a real fusion of tastes. The duck confit was lovely as was the lamb shank. But why do they not offer us hot plates to eat it on? It gets so cold so quickly. The wine list was good - we chose the Rose for a change and it went so well with the meat. Puddings were a treat. Recommend the Creme brûlée but be prepared for the green colour!PS I read some of the other TA reports and although we didn't get pestered by the waiting staff, I did get a little irritated by being hassled to order wine on arrival, hurried to order our food and then ignored when we were ready to leave! Why do so many restaurants do that?Show less

Author: LondonPlutoLondon
Title: A superb meal at a wonderfully relaxing setting
Review: A memorable meal at a wonderfully relaxing setting, Kebaya is set within Seven Terraces hotel in Georgetown. Don't let the 'hotel' tag put you off - Seven Terraces is a row of shophouses in the historic city centre, beautifully restored and brimming with antiques and Peranakan artefacts. There is a live piano music to ease your mood and a wonderfully warm welcome by the Maitre D who takes the time to talk each of the tables through the set menu. The food is fusion Asian-Peranakan-Western. It's a refined approach to the local cuisine though still packed full of flavour. I cannot wait to be back!Show less

Author: FanlaoBarcelona, Spain
Title: Excellent Fusion
Review: I can see why this restaurant is rated as the best restaurant in Penang. There are some great combinations of different flavors and they are all great. The place is also classy with a pianist playing some great tunes in the background. The hostess was also lovely who knew a lot about the food and her recommendations were spot on. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: WawachichiYangon (Rangoon), Myanmar
Title: It's alright
Review: Maybe I've been backpacking for awhile now so my standards are higher if I have pay 10x more than usual for meals.Wine - prices are decent with a small selectionCocktails - decent enough, pricing standard for the typical chi chi places Food - it's ok, not great tasting, pork was dry though everything was beautifully presented. My foreign friends seems to like it so maybe it's just me.Like the previous comments - environment is pretty uptight and we are totally locked off from the hotels, would be nice to have a look and no this is hotel and restaurant is by no means cheap for local standards, maybe for expats and 10% of the affluent crowd but not locals. It's pretty much a miss for me, so much potential and expectations yet so little returns Show less

Author: Sully0759Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
Title: Quite Good but not Great
Review: The food in Penang falls into very different categories. You can eat in a Hawker setting or a roadside restaurant and have a perfectly good meal for RM4. Or there is this experience which is fine dining in anyone's language. A minor hiccup at the start with the advice that my chosen entrée was not available because they were 'out' was a bit galling as I must have been the first patron of the night. A better explanation from one of the owners (I think) said that the prawn dish was not available as they were not happy with their quality today was totally fine. My alternative of otak otak baked in pastry was ok, but as a fusion dish it did not maintain the integrity of a delicate fish mousse. My main of organic sous vide pork was again good, but a bit overcooked. Thankfully the accompanying tempura vegetables were well presented and the Pandan leaf infused Crème Brulee for dessert was sublime.I don't know what people mean by the price of wine. A glass was AUD6-7 which is more than reasonable. You Aussies who whinge about this must be used to BYOs where you take your 6 pack of VB and box of Chateau Cardboard. Get real. For a total of about AUD40 for a meal plus wine I thought this was good value. Excellent no. The service is typically Asian in that they always aim to please. Perhaps I don't need to be asked if I enjoyed every mouthful by every staffmember every time they walk by but I can't criticise their aim to please.Show less

Author: Lionel888Melbourne, Australia
Title: Nice food with amazing ambiance
Review: My husband and son ate here tonight and the food was lovely and staff very lovely. Drinks menu pricing is on the high side but with such superb surroundings its all worth it. We enjoyed the night so much we are returning again tomorrow on our final night in Penang as it really is an experience you won't forget. I nearly forgot to mention they have live Pianist which makes the dining experience magical. Guterres FamilyShow less

Author: wagetKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: consistently perfect!
Review: been awhile before we are able to visit kebaya but very glad to know that it continues to be the perfect place ... food is consistently good, service is superb, ambiance is classy. this is really the place to go for special occasions. organic pork is a must try!Show less

Author: RoRoBrisbaneBrisbane
Title: Expensive
Review: After reading all the Tripadvisor reports maybe we were expecting too much. The food was good but we would have preferred to have had a couple of courses instead of having to have four. A set menu. The wine was expensive and the ambience a bit stark. For the price it just didn't have the right atmosphere.Show less

Author: Xexplorer
Title: Must Go !!!
Review: Good food, good service and very interesting settings. A very enjoyable dining experience. Can't leave Penang without visiting Kebaya!

Author: DudeEatSleep
Title: Great Kebaya
Review: The service is personal, pleasant and detailed. The food is fabulous. It is not as expensive as I thought after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor. It is less expensive then like restaurants in Penang and on a par with the best restaurants in its class.Show less

Author: M-wondererSingapore, Singapore
Title: Absolutely compulsory
Review: If you are in Penang because you are fascinated by the Nyonya food and culture - you have to, absolutely must, dine at Kebaya. Actually you should stay at Seven Terraces ( stunningly gorgeous boutique hotel where Kebaya is located ) but I did not manage stay there this time so I shall review that next time I am in Penang.Back in Kebaya, the food is superb - it is traditional Nyonya food with a fun twist. My parents are not into " fun twists" and they loved it.I agree with the other reviewers, for the quality of food, service and the scrumptious surroundings ( I love the doors ) the prices are very reasonable and the general vibe of the restaurant convivial.Pick up the phone and book a table.Show less

Author: kh1010
Title: superb setting
Review: very nice setting, extremely tasty food. not pure peranakan, but better and modernised. and a nice bar to conclude the evening.

Author: Leesa DJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Delicious!
Review: We had a great meal here on Monday night. The staff did not rush us to order (we wanted to have a drink first) and we didn't find them to be hovering over us like previous reviewers have mentioned. It was a really busy night so the atmosphere was lively and if we needed something we were attended to promptly. We liked that we were allowed to have a break to finish our wine before moving onto dessert, there is nothing worse than feeling rushed. We opted for the pork bun and betel leaf entree, the mains were the pork and duck and for dessert we opted for the more Asian style desserts rather than playing it safe with the brulee and panna cotta. We are glad we did, the little coconut balls were amazing and I can't remember the other dessert apart from the fact that it was delicious. Our only regret?? That we weren't staying here, we stayed at E&O and next time we will definitely stay at Seven Terraces. We are Australian but live in Malaysia and found the prices to be really reasonable even for Malaysian standards. You can easily pay RM60 just for a main course in KL. Can't wait to come back and try different dishes!Show less

Author: extrapagespassportCambridge, Massachusetts
Title: Beautiful heritage setting; modern take on classic dishes
Review: The restaurant is in a beautifully restored mansion and the focus is on traditional food with an updated treatment. It is a 4 course set menu: starter, protein + greens, dessert. Dishes are made to be shared and many can be made to order for vegetarians. For us, the stand-out dishes were the salmon roe appetizer, a very interesting blend of coconut, shrimp paste, grapefruit, cashew and roe wrapped in betel nut leaf; the prawns in a kind of coconut curry with lemongrass; the sambal greens; the passion fruit pannacotta and the pandan crème brûlée. Service is warm and professional. The set menu is 100 Ringgets; with a very nice bottle of wine from the small but well chosen list, expect to pay around $100 USD for dinner for two. It can get crowded but our hotel made us same day reservations. We were delighted with Kebaya and will definitely return when next in Penang.Show less

Author: lucyc342Beijing
Title: Beautiful setting, great food
Review: The restaurant is set in a heritage house that has been converted into a stunning boutique hotel con restaurant. The interior of the restaurant is simply beautiful with antique chinas donning the walls and glass cabines. It is probably the most romantic restaurant in Georgetown and the price is reasonable. The food portion is large and there is an extensive wine list. The food is a sort of of Nyonya Chinese and western fusion, not too spicy to cater for the foreign clientele and tasted great. Service is excellent and attentive so it is definitely somewhere worth splashing out for.Show less

Author: theodorichongkong, china.
Title: a night in heritage
Review: Georgetown is actually quite a good place to wander around, as itoffers a wide variety of items that evoke our bygone memories.Among which is a very well-preserved building group that has beenoperating as a 7-roomed heritage hotel and Kebaya is actually its restaurant. The dinner menu was Hobson's choice -- a setdinner costing MR100++ for three courses inter alia we can choose.Unfortunately our most favourite - prawn and pork - were out of order.(which is really a mystery, the menu is supposed to be daily!)Anyway, quality of food was all right and service was impeccable.Whether it is value for money is up to each individual, for ambienceand heritage I assume, is part of the bill. The management ordereda taxi upon our request but unfortunately it took about 30 minutes toarrive, despite a couple of telephone reminders. So be warned about this, it is almost impossible to hail a taxi in Georgetown atnight. On another night in Batu Ferringi, the situation was completelydifferent, the taxi came promptly and has waited for us for a coupleof minutes outside. The locals told me that all good restaurants arein Georgetown, I cannot vouch for this. Good luck.Show less

Author: fellowtraveler900Australia
Title: A 'Foodies' must in Penang
Review: Just had dinner at Kebaya restaurant at Seven Terraces, Stewart Lane, 10200 Georgetown, Penang.Food: taste was 10/10Presentation was 10/10Service was 10/10Relaxed atmosphere 10/10ambiance & elegance 10/10cleanliness 10/10coffee (for Australian latte coffee lovers) 10/10My only disappointment; this is my last night in Penang and I won't have time to investigate the surroundings more.A great and memorable way to end my first visit to Penang Island. Thank you.Show less

Author: ParisSingap
Title: Fine cuisine but a bit uptight
Review: We really enjoyed the food. All dishes have been modernised using french cooking technique. The result is amazing. We cannot say we preferred a dish over another one. All were excellent, especially the lamb. The only 2 negative points are the service which was a bit uptight and the impossibility to have drinks at the terrace as is reserved to the guests of the hotel.Show less

Author: RoseE88Melbourne
Title: Brilliant service but felt watched at all times
Review: This restaurant is situated in a spectacularly renovated heritage building. No expense has been spared on the decorating of the place.The menu consists of four dishes, an entree, a main and a vegetable dish and finally a dessert. A small selection in each one which I always find a positive as it means more care goes into each dish. The food itself was beautifully done with flavours complimenting each other. I could not find too much to fault in the food. I chose a small dessert of panacotta which was just on the too firm side but the flavours were delicious. My brother had a local delicacy which the waiter took the time to explain that it should be blue.My one big fault with the restaurant is it did feel like someone or multiple people were always intently watching you. I feel despite a high standard restaurant that the waiters should always appear relaxed and give you space while you eat.I would recommend this place for the food and scenery. It is expensive especially considering the other options around.Show less

Author: GloriaSomeHobart, Australia
Title: A very special dining experience
Review: We stayed in georgetown for four nights and although we didn't stay at Seven terraces we had made a decision to have a special evening out at Kebaya. I booked ahead but on the evening we visited the restaurant was not full. We decided to "dress up" something we had not had the opportunity to do much on our 4 week trip and although you could very comfortably walk in off the street after a day of sightseeing and not feel out of place it was nice to make a special effort and add to the whole experience. we arrived early and had a couple of drinks in the bar. the Gallefort cocktail is lovely. While we were enjoying our drinks we had the opportunity to make our selections from the menu, which was explained in detail and we were encouraged to make different choices so we could then share our selections. Once our entree was ready we were taken to our table and the tatste sensations began. The whole meal was truly superb but the standouts for us were the soft shell crab and papaya salad, the tempura vegetables and the pandan brulee. The meal portions were generous without being excessive and we managed to finish everything as we were urged to enjoy and take our time. The price of the meal represents exceptional value for money in fact our drinks bill came to more than the meal! The atmosphere is understated and elegant, the wait staff were attentive without being intrusive and we will most definately revisit as we have several more combinations of food to try!Show less

Author: 69PennyMelbourne, Australia
Title: Slice of heaven
Review: Four course dining in splendour. Kebaya is about taste: tasting different dishes, sharing and marvelling at intricate cooking. It is not fussy in the slightest. We dined with two teenagers who tucked into everything with gusto. Their only disappointment was that there was no ice cream - soon dispelled with stunning creme brulee and panacotta Asian style. Do try it.Show less

Author: AdrianCheahPenang, Malaysia
Title: The opulent Kebaya – inventive pan-Asian haute cuisine
Review: Kebaya restaurant elevate Nyonya cuisine a notch and introduces haute cuisine that has never been served before in Penang. The menu of classic pan-Asian and Straits Chinese Nyonya dishes use French cooking techniques and innovative produce to deliver surprising new twists on an already fascinating cuisine. The effect is simple, delicious, full of flavour and dazzling. My family and I we sat down to a culinary adventure that was riveting and all too exciting. With my Peranakan parentage, I quickly discovered how ingenious the creator of the restaurant truly is. The flavours were recognisable but what have been served in front of us were all new and invigoratingly delightful. For starters, we had the Kebaya Banh Xeo and Otak Otak – turmeric curried fish custard, usually steamed in banana leaves, was encased in homemade puff pastry and served as a starter instead of a shared dish with rice.As for the mains, we had Prawn Geng, a wonderful dish of fresh jumbo prawns cooked in creamy coconut curry flavoured with fresh turmeric and lemongrass; Thai Soft Shell Crab Salad with spicy chilli lime dressing, mint, mango, green apples and pomelo; and Organic Roast Pork Tender – succulent sous vide 3-layer pork belly served with a hoisin balsamic reduction dipping sauce.To accompany the mains, we had sautéed market fresh selection of greens and Sambal Goreng – french beans and baby corn, lemongrass, shallots and belachan coconut cream, with cashewnuts.It was an interesting meal; certainly quite different from the tradition Nyonya cuisine, yet the core of the dishes were distinctly recognisable Peranakan flavours. However, I think it is in the desserts that was surprisingly delightful. Kebaya's made inventive creations bringing long-established favourites with evergreen recipes kept perpetual through generations, into the realm of the present.Nyonya Tang Yuen, glutinous rice balls coloured blue with bunga telang (blue pea flower) were filled not with crushed peanuts and sugar but grated coconut cooked in brown palm syrup (recognisable in the classic green ‘onde onde’). The bite-size tang yean sat in warm coconut cream with slivers of young coconut flesh awaiting our indulgence. A brilliant merriment of coconut in three different forms – cream, grated and slivers. My wife’s favourite dessert was the Crème Brulee. Crisp burned sugar topping enhanced the fabulously deep, rich flavour and smooth creaminess of the pandan egg custard. She also enjoyed the Gula Melaka Mousse sprinkled with caramel macadamia nuts very much. Coconut Panna Cotta topped with passion fruit and candied pistachios was sinfully delicious too. Indeed, a truly satisfying end to great meal.Service was impeccable and the sublime beauty of the Kebaya dining room completes a memorable dining experience, especially on the special occasion of celebrating my wife's birthday.Show less

Author: Richie WPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: just "wow"
Review: no wonder this restaurant is number 1! you go in and it's just "WOW" ... from the piano music to the food recommendations of Prakash and everyone's sincere service. it's just that perfect place for a special occasion. really loved the three-layer organic pork - three different textures in one bite, it's amazing!Show less

Author: 69ingBishop
Title: Very pleasant
Review: Turned up on spec and they managed to squeeze me in (reserving is normally a must here).  Very pleasant setting, excellent food (though huge portions, so make sure you're hungry!)  Very reasonable price for what you get.  Oh, and rather good pianist!  Highly recommended.

Author: Ben WPerth, Australia
Title: Splendid experience
Review: Housed inside the stunningly decorated seven terraces, Kebaya offers a unique and refreshingly balanced menu of items that assaulted my taste buds and preconceptions of classic south east Asian dishes. With a four course meal split into entre (protein), main (carnivore), greens, desert. It encourage sharing as every dish was carefully crafted to compliment... Couldn't get enough... The drinks and especially wine list was surprisingly for Malaysian standards quite extensive and impressive. The atmosphere and service alone was worth half the cost. Perfect for a special occasion. Culinary highlight of the trip for me!Show less

Author: EvieGDL
Title: Amazing Dining Experience
Review: Came here for my birthday dinner in Penang, every course was delicious (especially the soft shell crab salad). Beautiful building and atmosphere and very well priced (under $35 US) for four courses. Perfect place for a romantic evening out.

Author: GoodtimenotlongtimeMelbourne, Australia
Title: Great special dinner for 2
Review: Exceptional food. First class service. Felt like King and Queen when we were there. Had dinner while staying at the hotel for my 41st birthday and the staff all made us feel fantastic. We shared 8 courses and were really thrilled with the diversity of flavour from this quaint restored room. Penang isn't a hub city for travel but we will go out of our way to return to savour the flavour from this magic kitchen. Wait staff were excellent - all wished me happy birthday without being obvious or fake. These people have obviously been hand picked for their jobs because they really love what they do and they do it with the best attitude and grace one could possibly hope for. 10 stars, two double thumbs up and a heart felt wink of appreciation for this little gem.Show less

Author: PiliPala_83London, United Kingdom
Title: Great setting and food
Review: We visited this restaurant in August based on Trip Advisor reviews. We weren't disappointed. We arrived early and had a drink at the bar. Menus were provided at the bar allowing us to place our order before being seated.All courses had great flavour. We really enjoyed it. This was one of the best meals we had in Malaysia.The restaurant is a great venue, full of character.Definitely recommended. It is a set three courses, but there is plenty of choice for each course.Staff were great.Show less

Author: Kallang
Title: Original tasty food
Review:
It serves peranakan food with a westen twist.
There is a lot of bad fusion food, but this was done very well.
Food was original and tasty.
Sevice was quick.
The dining room is beautiful

Author: TCK KKuala Lumpur
Title: Sensationally refreshing
Review: Kebaya is a bewitching inter play of the old and new. Challenging one's senses and preconceptions. What you see is old, what you taste is refreshingly new. Housed in a row of 1900s Strait Settlement shophouses, the exquisitely restored Seven Terraces is charmingly chic. The antiques and collectibles of old in Kebaya bring back the ambiance of refined nonya living of gone by days. The menu itself sounds familiar enough among the numerous nonya restaurants of today. However the taste is delightfully avant-garde. Kebaya's Loh Ark, duck confit infused with the flavours of plum and orange, is a good example of a classic nonya dish thoroughtly rethough, recooked and refined. The lamb Hong Bak, organic roast pork, Gula Melaka mousse and Tong Yuen are other memorable re-interpretations by Kebaya. Congratulations.Show less

Author: Laura H
Title: Delicious food and plenty of it!
Review: We visited this restaurant on 27 August. I went with 2 work colleagues whilst on a business trip to Malaysia. It is a set menu of sorts - 100 ringgits per person and that gets you a starter, main with side and a dessert each so it's quite good value for the quality of food served. We shared everything so we got to taste more of the menu. It was all gorgeous, especially the red snapper in pastry starter with a Malaysian curry sauce. The main courses were huge and we were all totally stuffed at the end. There was a pianist playing which was nice although his choice of sad Disney songs was a little melancholy! The restaurant us attached to a gorgeous looking hotel which we wished we had stayed in rather than our own! Would definitely go back and stay there.Show less

Author: 112358-12Perth, Australia
Title: Nice place, friendly staff, dinner a bit hit and miss.
Review: Perhaps the great reviews gave me too high expectations, but this is good, even in parts very good, but it is no stand-out as a restaurant. The tempura vegetables were a disaster: thick batter encasing enoki mushrooms -- perhasp the worst thing one could think of for this style of cooking -- were more batter than anything resembling food. The confit duck was, strangely, duck breast. I guess there is no rule agianst it, but say "confit" and one thinks the melting tenderness of a long cooked leg and thigh, not a semi-rare sliced duck breat. Dessert on the other hand was lovely, and the starter -- betel leaves one stuffed with the usual mix of nuts, dried fish, fish eggs and so on -- was pleasant if nothing beyond the ordinary. A nice meal: mostly, yes.Show less

Author: koshpatPenang, Malaysia
Title: Favor some Local/Nyonya Food but classy?
Review: This is the place where you do not have to compromise either food or atmosphere. Both equally outstanding. Parking space is slightly a problem, arriving by 7pm should solve your problem. Be sure to make reservation as they do not take walk in customers. Dinner for 2 will cost about RM300 without wine, but it's worth the price.Show less

Author: 635PeterD
Title: A gem
Review: Great restaurant with friendly service and great food. It is in a heritage hotel and the atmosphere and furniture help make this a great dining experience. Strongly recommend!

Author: kai_khemCandy Land
Title: lost in emotion que sera sera
Review: hate to rate poor but cant give enough gains for the flavor and expectations. going with the #1 pick here and close to our room we had to check them out. the pictures look great and the reviews genuine. the night before we did Gurney Drive and have to give the street food a better vote. the gf is an interior designer and architect and just loved the place. its quite nostalgic and was told nothing in the lobby is under 80 years old for this quaint hotel. props to all staff and piano player it was still a fun night.  the fault fell on the meals. appetizers surely passing and have to be the best part of our meal. we did the pork buns and the Thai Miang Kham with salmon roe. another starter looked interesting but the menu is set so one app one main one veg and one dessert. the price wasn't much a factor, the service and presentation with ambiance covers that. for mains we got the chicken kapitan and the lamb. lamb was tender perfect but taste was infused or just overdone in flavor, it tasted as if we were eating flowers. same with the chicken. the veggie dishes again were okay but nothing exciting. I would highly recommend doing the tempura or fried dish. we didn't try it but it should throw a different variety on flavors as we got two similar in flavor sauteed dishes.  desserts should pull them ahead cause they are better then my rating, though I'm sticking with poor since their #1 status is what dragged us here. okay all in all nice place and lovely evening. if your reading this and contemplating don't get both the chicken and lamb main. there's several more options. would we come again? haha on someone else's dime but again they are not offensive expensive, you should enjoy ur evening here.Show less

Author: Frella24Cheltenham, United Kingdom
Title: Classy setting and meal
Review: Lovely setting, excellent service and the food selection was expertly cooked, with each dish having piquant/individual flavours. We had the duck in plum sauce which was exquisite and the sea-bass. Would go again. Pricey compared to many places in Georgetown but worth it for the setting, service and quality.Show less

Author: Cook ZSydney
Title: Great service and atmosphere
Review: We came in with a full stomach from China House (trying to overstuff ourselves with Penang delicious food). We were greeted by a beautiful old lady (the manager or owner?) in her colorful Kebaya (it made me want to own one!). It's a charming restaurant with really helpful and friendly staffs. They offer a four courses set dinner at rm100++pp (entree, main, greens and dessert). We absolutely loved the lamb dish, it was so succulent and tender, great with the rice. The other main we picked, the duck confit, was disappointingly dry and average. It tasted like they just poured the sauce (which was actually very refreshing and good) over the reheated two days old fried duck. The tempura veggie was unexpectedly light in flavor, which was a good break from all the strong flavored dishes. As for the dessrt, we really liked the panna cotta with passion fruit.Show less

Author: ZebulonUkuk
Title: Great food
Review: Georgetown is a foodie paradise and this restaurant is up there in the must do category of local attractions. Delicious food, cool building, great service- all good! A meal for two cost about $100 so not cheap (considering that the hawkers sell similar quality for $10) but still worth going!Show less

Author: JoseLuisG160Benicasim, Spain
Title: Great atmosphere and service
Review: We were staying in 7 terraces and we had to try Kebaya. Our fellow travellers left me no choice based on raving reviews.This is definitely a must in Penang.My 5 * score is based on the combination of atmosphere and food.7 Terraces is indeed a charming hotel and if you are not staying in it having dinner at Kebaya gives you the chance to both have an ellaborate meal and enjoy the atmosphere of the place.Foodwise It is a fusion Malay/ western. Some dishes were really fantastic. We had only 1 so so dish. Please note that some of the fusion approach may not offer you the strong flavours of 100% local cuisine. This is more on the subtle, sophisticated side. Service was fantastic.Show less

Author: manyamsSingapore, Singapore
Title: Loved this place
Review: We went to this place for my boyfriend's birthday and really enjoyed it! We spent around 350 ringgit for the two of us, and it was a really nice meal and great value for money. We had 4 courses and 2 drinks each. The staff was great, and friendly, and the food super delicious and in really generous quantities. At the last minute I informed the staff that it was my boyfriend's birthday and if they could do something then that would be great. Well they put a candle in my boyfriend's dessert and the pianist played happy birthday. It was really lovely, and kind of them! Will recommend tourists to try this place for any occasion where you just want to have a great time!Show less

Author: namealusDallas
Title: Amazing meal and service
Review: Best meal in Georgetown. Relatively expensive for Penang standard, but still relatively cheap for European or American standard. 4-dish set dinner is 100RM/pax. Large portions that will fill you up and more. Service is impeccable. The waitress brought a pillow for my jetlagged daughter to sleep on without prompting. All the servers are knowledgeable about the food.Show less

Author: chikka2002Hong Kong
Title: Excellent and exquisite
Review: Kebaya is a "must do" for any visitors to Penang. From the moment we stepped through the door, my seven guests and I were well looked after by Prakesh, Kebaya's excellent and attentive F&B manager who seated us at the bar and guided us through the set dinner choices and making practical suggestions about food portions. Kebaya's decor is exquisite, a wonderful combination of beauty and warmth, creating a very inviting ambience, a testament to the discerning taste of owners Chris Ong and his partner Karl Steinberg. Dinner was excellent, each dish distinctively different, so that our taste buds experienced a new sensation each time. Five of my seven guests were first time visitors to Penang and they were absolutely bowled over by the discovery of such a gem.Show less

Author: gohomemumbaiCanberra
Title: A delicious birthday celebration dinner
Review: We chose Kebaya to celebrate my birthday in Penang and it was the perfect choice. What an amazing place to begin with, so well renovated and in keeping with the flavour of Penang and its history.The food was wonderful, the cocktails perfect. It really was too much food, but it was so delicious that we waddled out after the meal and had to walk it off for about half an hour.We had the snapper in pastry and the crab meat on sugar cane skewers. This was followed by the prawn curry and lamb shank with tempura vegetables and a mixed vege. Sorry I cannot remember the exact names but it was all amazing. Apparently the jury is out on the lamb shank, some like and some are not so sure we were told, but I must admit both my husband and I LOVED THE LAMB SHANK. Desert was a mind blowing palm sugar mouse and a rice ball (with palm sugar insert) in coconut milk. WOW!! Relative to Australia, it wasn't expensive, but it was really very special. A special thanks to the staff, everyone who were amazing, especially our waiter. Thanks for a great birthday dinner Kebaya.Show less

Author: ALee2912Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei Darussalam
Title: Wonderful food and excellent atmosphere
Review: Me and my girlfriend had dinner here on our last night in Penang and I have to say its one of the best restaurant we have been to. The atmosphere brings you back to my nostalgic days of my yesterday years with the pianist playing classic Chinese oldies songs which I enjoyed very much. It's not everyday you get to enjoy good meal, good drinks with good ambiance. Love all the plates and furnitures and layout.
