The food we had was a four course meal based on traditional nyonya but with their own modern twist. The food portion is more than enough to feed 4 pax! We also loved the dessert. Overall spend a bit more to soak in the wonderful dining experience here.Show less

Author: ZephyrCanberraCanberra
Title: Fantastic food in a beautiful setting
Review: While staying at Seven Terraces we ate twice at this restaurant. The menu is degustation style, which normally I don't like but in this case it was a great way to experience different tastes. The food is imaginatively based on Nonya food and there is a good range of choices. Everything is beautifully presented on blue china and the service is friendly and helpful. The surrounds are part of the whole experience, with elegantly displayed antiques and a piano player in the bar. Recommended for a special place to eat.Show less

Author: Mark-J-StapletonBunbury, Western Australia
Title: Fabulous food, fabulous location, fabulous service
Review: Thank goodness for Trip Advisor! The reviews of Kebaya convinced us to walk the character-laden streets of George Town to find this absolute gem. From the understated and warmly helpful manager to what must rate as one of the most exquisite colonial restaurant interiors anywhere, this restaurant was from the outset something special. The company was as always a delight and still I haven't mentioned the food! Faultless in all respects - full of taste explosions provided by just the right amount of spices and very generous in terms of portions - and how many times have you been to a restaurant and been told that you will not need as many dishes as you were considering ordering! Every dish, both savoury and sweet, was a triumph, as evidenced by the cleanest of plates at the completion of what has to be one of the best meals any of us has ever tasted. I would at the same time like to apologise for Malcolm licking the plate after his passion fruit panacotta - you just cannot take some Australians to wonderful eating places without them disgracing themselves! In summary, WOW! We will be back. This was fine dining at its best.Show less

Author: GuntscheSingapore, Singapore
Title: Go to the best!
Review: Each town has somebody that is creating something special. This restaurant (and hotel) is the designed and excellent place for Georgetown.The staff is extremely friendly and having a drink at the Bababar gives you the feeling of being at a special place.I recommend to follow recommendation of the staff. I had a lamp and my wife the curry. Both where excellent. Starters are coming in tapas-form and are very tasty.Show less

Author: May SSydney, Australia
Title: Nice but expected more...
Review: After the rave reviews on TA about Seven Terraces and its restaurant, Kebaya, I just had to find out for myself what the fuss is all about. I rocked up with my partner on a Monday evening without a reservation and luckily for us there was a table available. It's a set menu requiring diners to choose a dish from 4 sections. The portion sizes are generous so no complaints on that score. The quality of food is good but I expected more based on the feedback received. First of all, the food offered is not authentic Nyonya fare. It should be more accurately described as Asian fusion as it combines Chinese, Malaysian, Vietnamese and even Japanese styles of cooking and flavours. Whilst I enjoyed the stir fried morning glory and prawns cooked on sugar cane sticks, my tempura vegetables lacked flavour and the slow cooked lamb shank was overly spiced for my personal taste.The positives are good customer service and the inviting ambience of the setting created by the tasteful choice of beautiful antique Peranakan style furniture and furnishings. The highlight for me was having our coffee in the bar area whilst listening to the pianist's renditions of some timeless tunes.Show less

Author: Sophie BAdelaide, Australia
Title: Best meal I had in Malaysia
Review: Aside from the fact that this place was absolutely stunning to look at (and you should go for a wander while you're there) the food was incredible! Set menu, but you can order extra dishes and the staff are very flexible. The price you pay is a little more than the average meal in Malaysia, but the quality and flavour of the food it that which would cost three times as much in a western country. The food was flawless, great quality meats and seafood. The lamb shank practically fell apart on the plate, and the prawn curry was amazing. The staff very attentive and even brought out a complementary local dessert for us to try. Also, make sure you try the gallforte cocktail - like no other. Do not leave Penang without visiting this great restaurant.Show less

Author: CaroRob72
Title: A gastronomic delight
Review: Had the pleasure of a couple of great meals here in the past week- I now need to seriously diet! Including celebrating my husbands birthday here a couple of night ago. Started with some great house cocktails at the bar poured by the very affable Aruna. Then on to a four course sharing menu. Highlights were the snapper pastry parcel starters, soft shell crab salad,chicken kapitan and OMG the deserts. We've been eating great local food all week and consider ourselves foodies but by far the best for food,ambience and service these guys win hands down. Prakash runs a tight ship and gosh it tells. Service was wonderful, helpful and friendly but not fussy. Well done guys a superb experience all round. Thanks for those small touches like helping find a great bottle of wine it meant a lot. Show less

Author: 24PercyMelbourne, Australia
Title: Excellent maitre d'
Review: We visited this restaurant almost by accident, and were delighted with the experience. It was really hot, and we'd had an hour's bus ride to George Town, standing up, then a few hours walking round. Just before 6.00 pm we walked by Seven Terraces and remembered being told about the restaurant. They didn't open until 7.00 pm, but we were invited to sit in the cool bar until then. We really didn't look like guests at an upmarket restaurant, and appreciated the way we were made to feel at home by the maitre d'.The waiter helped us choose dishes to share, with the pick of them being the chicken kapitan. With drinks in the bar and at the table, our total bill was 380.50 MYR, or ~$A136, a fair price for the quality.Show less

Author: RosiePerth123Dundee, United Kingdom
Title: Hidden Gem
Review: Tried this restaurant after reading other reviews and we were not dissappointed....what a fabulous renovated building, creating a lovely relaxed ambience. We were shown to a seated area for drinks first...however the female maitre D forgot to follow through after showing us to our seats and we had to ask someone to take drinks order and supply menus, however we were extremely well attended to be a charming waiter who was very knowledgeable about the food and explained every dish and we enjoyed every dish we had. The menu was a set price of 100 myr for 4 courses so expensive by Malaysian standards but not by European and worth every penny..Show less

Author: 636foodiePenang Island, Malaysia
Title: a must visit for a special evening out
Review: This place is magical.7 terrace house have been converted into restuarant and boutique hotel.Ambiance is peaceful.Car park outside the boutique hotel if you enter from Agus RoadFood is fusion, sort of a set menur, but waiters will guide you as to how much one needs. last order by 10pm so advised to go early for dinner and relaxHightly recommendedShow less

Author: Danoutje
Title: Absolutely delicious
Review: so good, we had dinner there the 2 nights we spent in Georgetown! delicious food, full of flavors and the advice and care of a very attentive staff. Highly recommended.

Author: Karen MBlantyre, United Kingdom
Title: Thank you TripAdvisor
Review: We were backpacking from Thailand to Singapore and one of our stops was Panang. Food throughout the trip had been kind of below average and a bit repetitive, so when we arrive in Penang i checked out TripAdvisor and this was the No 1 Restaurant so we headed here. It was Friday night and just by chance we arrived at 7pm as the restaurant opened and we were lucky enough to get a table as it filled up very quickly.The whole layout of the restaurant was lovely and very fancy, we all started to question if we had brought enough money with us - lol.We were sat our table by a very helpful and friendly waiter and given the menu, and surpassingly it only had a few choices for each meal (starter, main, sides and dessert) most places we had previously visited the menus always had pages and pages of dishes to choose from which sometimes can be quite off putting.There was 6 of us dinning, and we were all very pleased with the menu made our choices and ordered drinks - we opted for a lovely chilled bottle of prosseco which was delicious.The food was amazing, from the starters to the desserts we all enjoyed every last mouthful, with not one complaint or criticism.The biggest surprise was when the bill came, we all had three courses each with a side of vegetables and drinks and it worked it at approx £20 each - easily the best value meal we have ever had.Definitely worth finding this place if you are in Penang!Show less

Author: Maow2012Hong Kong, China
Title: Such a nice meal
Review: I had dinner in Kebaya with my husband, made a wonderful setting for a special meal although the price was really reasonable.We had the set dinner (not sure if this is all they do), it was so tasty and lovingly presented. The chicken curry (in a satay type sauce) was particually good and the passion fruit pana cotta was just divine and a perfect finish to a wonderful meal. Show less

Author: Jamessta
Title: Yummy Malay delights
Review: Brilliant food OtakOtak! fabulous location, wonderful service. We were fortunate to catch a sublime pianist who really contributed to the atmosphere. Don't miss the Lor Ark-a duck confit with caramelised plum and orange in a cinnamon + star anise jus

Author: Valerie G
Title: Wonderful food and service
Review: Beautiful place, with impeccable service. Staff was very attentive to our needs, and allergies. Food was amazing, but it was the service that blew me away.

Author: voyager52Newport Beach, California
Title: great food and great atmosphere
Review: We had a wonderful meal at Kebaya. I had duck and my husband had the lamb as mains. Both were wonderful. The dining room and bar are furnished with classic chinese and colonial furniture. The owners collection of porcelain is beautifully displayed and at very least worth the price of a drink at the bar to see. We had drinks there several times. They made a good cocktail and poured a decent glass of wine.Show less

Author: LetsDoCurry
Title: Kebaya
Review: Highlight of our Penang dining. This is class both in fitout and food. It's a don't miss on your dining out list in Georgetown. Cool bar, spacious dining area, great floor staff. 9/10

Author: JaggardsNorwich, United Kingdom
Title: A delicious dining experience
Review: Having eaten in food courts and night markets on penang, we decided to try something different for our last evening on the island. After a look on the TA mobile app, I came across the good reviews for seven terraces and we decided to try our luck. The hotel looked to be beautifully and gracefully appointed and the restaurant elegant, with pianist on grand piano and a very welcoming and professional maitre di. The chef came out and proudly talked us through the menu while we sipped our pre-dinner G&Ts, and we had trouble choosing as the whole menu sounded exquisite. In the end we were kindly offered a selection of the various starters so we could share and not miss anything. For mains and then desserts, all four of us had different dishes. Not one of us could fault any of our dishes. The food was cooked to perfection and so well presented. The bill was, as you'd expect, not cheap for penang, but still far far cheaper than we'd ever get for this quality in the UK. A lovely evening.Show less

Author: occasional_typoSydney, Australia
Title: The highlight of our stay in Penang
Review: We ate at Kebaya the day after the election and the experience was the highlight of our short stay in Penang.Although we are big fans of Malaysian food and are returnees to Penang after 25/30 years respectively, we found the heat in Chulia St and the chaotic eateries a bit daunting so it was an absolute joy to sit in beautiful, calm surroundings and sample some fabulous dishes at an extremely reasonable price. The standout for us was the pork mantou and the softshell crab.The staff were knowledgable, discreet and attentive. Their attention to detail was second to none.We were still smacking our lips as we rolled out onto the street that night.Thank you Kebaya.Show less

Author: SaudiArabia1002Saudi Arabia
Title: 5 Star dining
Review: The food was gourmet quality, every dish was outstanding, infact each one got better. The set menu was well thoughtout and complimented each other. Wine list was balanced and well priced. We stayed at the 7 Terraces accomodation and the restaurant does room service what a bonus. The dining room was elegant and the crockery was beautiful, a lovely experienceShow less

Author: WandRMelbourne
Title: Not to be missed
Review: In a city with some many great food options, when you want a stylish, delcious and totally enjoyable experience, eat at Kebaya. We ate there a couple of times to try more menu items becuase they were all so good. Wine list was carefully edited, food was beautifully prepared and presented - and you'd be mad not to have the divine palm sugar mousse dessert. Loved it.Show less

Author: Citygal12456Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: best restaurant in penang!
Review: Kebaya is definitely the best restaurant in Penang. I can not agree more that it is the number 1 restaurant in Tripadvisor. While Penang boasts of its hawker food, it is refreshing to have a restaurant that is decent and unpretentious. I particularly like how they marry the eastern and western cuisines - they do it perfectly. Nyonya food is something very heavy for me. The last time I had nyonya food was eons ago - the food was fantastic but I just couldn't eat it after that as I felt it was too rich and heavy. After taking the food in Kebaya, I think I can have it often.Show less

Author: LionelWhiteSingapore
Title: Style or Substance?
Review: M & I have not been to Penang since 1989/1990 and was looking forward to a short break there recently. We stayed at the E&O and were pleasantly surprised by what the island has to offer: laid back vibe, beautiful architecture and the promise of good food.After a quick surf on Tripadvisor, i made a reservation for two for dinner at Kebaya, the coconut creme de la creme of culinary Penang, on a Sat night. First impression: housed in the beautifully restored Seven Terraces hotel, the decor/interiors of the restaurant ticked all the right boxes; I love all the hints of Peranakan culture.But my fleeting love affair with Kebaya ended the moment the menu was presented. Disclaimer: It's a not a HUGE menu but it has a reasonable range. But what surprised me was the inclusion of things like prawn meat wrapped in sugar-cane, which, frankly, was a Vietnamese concoction, and lamb cooked, sous-vide, in its own juices - which M ordered – which was frankly, another geographically-displaced dish that had no business in peranakan food culture.The food wasn't un-tasty. Au contraire, it was nice but it wasn't what i had expected... may be it's me, not Kebaya. I know it's meant to be fusion but the problem with fusion cooking is that the line between traditional fare and modern interpretation is extremely fine. Done right, it could be exquisite, done wrong, it's (con)fusion. (PS. the dishes that night were liberally spiced with coconut milk which made them a tad too sweet for my taste.) With Kebaya, my verdict is that it veered off into the latter territory, which is a shame, as Peranakan food is so rich in its pedigree and is one of my fave in the world.So why the praise? My only guess is that: 1) Most of the reviewers have never had proper Peranakan cusine; 2) it probably is the best modern cuisine in Penang. I certainly hope that the good reviews on Kebaya is not a case of "The Emperor's New Clothes" syndrome where nobody dares speak the truth or dissent. I will give Kebaya another chance when i visit Penang again. And i hope there is the option of ordering a la carte instead of the set meal for RM$100, which is not expensive at all, but would be nice to have.Show less

Author: SF_Kin
Title: Great value and quality
Review: Kebaya captured all the essential flavors of the traditional nyonya cooking, but still made it interesting with some modern touches. Check it out, and for the set price (RM100 for four courses) it is great value.

Author: SingaporeTraveller21Singapore, Singapore
Title: Just wish we had stayed at the hotel- the food is fantastic!
Review: We chanced upon this hotel during a wonderful long weekend in Penang. Perfectly located in the heart of Georgetown the boutique Seven Terraces hotel was the host to our best meal in Penang, and if you have been before you will know that the whole place is a gourmet adventure. The 4 course set meal was an overwhelming display of delicious Nonya food. With the amazing choice of food on offer it was hard to choose, but the friendly restaurant team helped us to select a melt in the mouth 72 hour cooked beef rib (the daily special), prawn laksa, mixed greens and 2 amazing starters- I think there was a pulled pork filled steam bread and something equally delicious. For pudding we had a passionfruit cheese cake and pandan crème Brule- which I wanted to go back again the next day just to eat again. The decor of the restaurant is old school colonial with old wooden chairs and marble topped tables. The only thing to watch out for is the pesky mosquitoes, wear some repellent. The restaurant, the staff and most of the all the food at the Kebaya restaurant were just fantastic- we will definitely be back and confidently recommending this restaurant to all our visiting friends. Set meal was well worth it at RM 100++ (16% tax)- just make sure you have a light lunch to prepare you for this indulgence fest! Make sure you ring ahead and book as the restaurant is only open from 7-10pm, we were lucky to get a table.Show less

Author: gbtl
Title: nice food
Review: Each set costs RM 100++ (16% tax), and its a four course meal, with appetizers, greens, main course and dessert. The ambience inside is great and the interior decor is well furbished.

Author: guitarman666Richmond-upon-Thames, United Kingdom
Title: Deserved number 1
Review: Kebaya is the restaurant of the newly restored hotel, Seven Terraces on Stewart Lane in Georgetown. It proposes fusion Nonya Peranakan food and it is probably the best restaurant in a city which is potentially the food capital of South East Asia. The newly restored premises are remarkably pleasant with a colonial touch but not overdone and the food is excellent. I strongly recommend the Thai style soft crab. Absolutely wonderful.It is certainly more expensive than most places in Penang, apart from the overpriced hotels, but the whole experience and service is worth it.Show less

Author: timsvr
Title: One  of the best 3 restaurants so far in Asia on my 5 month trip .
Review:
Excellent fusion food from chef Zak ...and stunning cocktails !
Great fusion food served in atmospheric surroundings . Im dificult to please ..been in the restaurant business for many years ,,,but this was great

Author: SmagyarErdobenye, Hungary
Title: Good food in a stunning setting
Review: I went to Kebaya for dinner on New Year's Eve. The ambience of this restaurant was fantastic -- a beautiful setting with traditional old world style. The service was excellent. Even though I was dining alone, I was given a good table (which is sadly often not the case in restaurants when you are dining solo) with a perfect view of the piano; and had very attentive and helpful, but unobtrusive wait staff. The manager also stopped by several times to advise me on the menu and to check that I was enjoying my meal. The food was really good -- well presented and tasty. My only comment would be that it would be useful to also be able to order less -- the set menus were quite substantial and more than 1 person alone could eat.When I return to Georgetown, I will certainly return here and would also recommend it to others.Show less

Author: LSManleySydney, Australia
Title: A MUST in Georgetown
Review: This was EXCELLENT. Fantastic ambience in the Seven Terraces Hotel with excellent staff to match. Went there with friends and were advised o order only 3 set meals for the four of us, as servings were large - even then we did not manage to eat it all and it was delicious, every one of the 12 dishes we had was exceptional. Great restaurant, great ambience, great staff, good wine list - do yourself a favour and go. (it is a bit more expensive than other Georgetown restaurants but you will not be disappointed)Show less

Author: Venetia18Switzerland
Title: Great food, great place, great people
Review: To me this place is practically flawless. It feels refined and elegant but simple at the same time. I loved the fact that the tables are not too close to each other, that it was very quiet even when completely full, that the waiters are very kind and ready to help and that it no problem at all to share your meal if you feel you don't want to eat too much. What counts most, though, is the quality of the food, tasty and well presented. One can feel that the two young chefs are passionate and want to do something traditional but with a modern twist.Show less

Author: lullabelle71Doha, Qatar
Title: Dinner for two
Review: We had our hotel book for us and we managed to get in the same night. I have read all the great reviews on here so thought it might be difficult to get a table but it wasn't. The place itself is very nice, clean and tastefully decorated. We were met by the owner who was very nice and helpful. The service was very good and all the staff were polite and well trained. One even showed me around the "guests only" area which was also lovely.The food was good but I have had better from the street stalls!! It was well presented and good quality but the fish was very over cooked. We also had the beef ribs which were delicious. I would recommend this place as a little oasis of calm in busy Georgetown. I cannot comment on the rooms as we did not stay but I imagine they are very nice!Show less

Author: annmarie1122New York City, New York
Title: Wonderful experience in Georgetowb
Review: The atmosphere alone is worth a visit, in a stunning old hotel. The food and service is top quality and delicious and transports you back to another time.... The streets surrounding the hotel are beautiful and make for some treasured snap shots. The osak osak is a must.Show less

Author: yanatnes
Title: We will be back again.
Review: The best food ever had in Penang. Unique restaurant decorate with chinese style. I go to visit my boyfriend there. Then me and my boyfriend want to have a beautiful dinner before i leave. We were looking for good restaurant. Finally we decide to book Kebaya coz so many people talking about it. We wandered how nice it is. We did not regret to go there the food was delicious and reasonable price. I will go there again for sure.Show less

Author: dbajillBangkok, Thailand
Title: I loved this place
Review: As usual we went to trip advisor to find out the best restaurant in Penang and as usual.. Trip advisor came up trumps. We booked into Kebaya for the Saturday night and I am glad we booked early as we would not have got a table. The restaurant is really beautiful, very authentic and plenty of room between tables. Its cool and sort of trendy.. but with an old oriental feel.. difficult to describe but well worth a visit. To start with we hit the cocktails and everyone was a winner, in the end I can’t remember my choice as I am writing this a couple of weeks later but both my husband and I loved what they poured us!Now for the food... The Capitan’s Chicken was fabulous and my Pork was the best I have ever eaten. We got chatting to the couple next door and they had the slow cooked beef, we were lucky to have a taste of it and it was soft, tasty and with a great depth of flavour. It seems that it does not matter what you choose everything is a winner. The staff are very attentive without being over powering. The wine was excellent and not too expensive; we managed to get through a couple of bottles because we did not want to leave the place. All in all I can say it was probably the best restaurant we have been to this year, I could not recommend it more.Show less

Author: Cynthia RParis, France
Title: Museum quality surroundings outdone by exceptional cuisine
Review: Kudos to native son Christopher Ong and his partner Karl Steinberg for a modern Perankan menu of delectable dishes, including the otak otak sea bass in light and flaky pastry, and a luscious prawn curry. Freshly made fruit juices are highly recommended as well, though the restaurant offers a notable wine menu as well. As exceptional as the food, is the sublime high ceiling dining room, lovingly filled with Ong's museum quality collection of Chinese ceramics. We dined here every night of our recent stay at Seven Terraces, the chic heritage hotel that is home to Kebaya. Both are tops for Penang.Show less

Author: PinsonniereMaisontiers, France
Title: A culinary haven in Georgetown
Review: As with the last few reviews we have nothing but praise for Kebaya and the Seven Terraces Hotel.We only managed to eat here on our last night in Penang, but was so glad that we did. The greeting by all the staff made us feel very welcome, and their advice regarding choices and portion sizes, was extremely helpful. We had one degustation menu and supplemented with an extra entree and an extra vegetable dish (the tempura vegertables are a must!), and this was more than enough. The service throughout the evening, both in the bar and in the restaurant was impeccable.If you are in Penang do go out of your way to visit this restaurant. It is well worth it! Some people have commented on the price, saying that it is expensive. Maybe by Malaysian standards, perhaps, but when you can have a superb meal with four glasses of good wine for about £60 for two, that can't be bad!!If you are not staying at the hotel, do ask to have a look around. It is simple stunning what has been achieved from seven derelict buildings.Show less

Author: WarwickHall101Sydney, Australia
Title: Add this to you trip - this is a standout
Review: We enjoyed this so much the first time we revisited on our last night in the city.Food, very high standard. The creme brûlée is worth a visit in itself but everything we had both times was cooked to perfection and very tasty.The service was first rate. Friendly and accommodating.The atmosphere was lovely and the piano player gives a real sense of occasion.The wine list could use a bit more depth but acquiring wine at a reasonable cost reliably can be as issue it it is hard to hold that against them.Value - it is expensive, relatively speaking so do not attend if you are expecting chicken rice prices. When you compare the outstanding quality and price against Sydney prices the value is very good indeed.If there is an equivalent restaurant in Penang we did not find it. This is a stand out.Show less

Author: johnobreMelbourne
Title: This has to be on your list if you are in Penang
Review: From the moment you walk into Kebaya you are struck by sheer serenity and class. The restaurant is to the right upon walking in and the bar to the left. This is a very special experience. A pianist set up in the bar plays all evening and adds to the wonderful ambience of this beautifully renovated old Chinese mansion. The waiting staff are warm, helpful and keep it real. They suggest rather than direct and are also great founts of knowledge for other things to do in Penang. I had the chicken kapitan, my partner the duck as mains. My partner had a chicken sort of pie/samosa for entree that was to die for. The dessert - two turquioise balls stuffed with from memory almond meal and something else - was unbelievable. We spoke to the chef at the end of the night to thank him and tell him how amazing it all was. He, like everyone else at Kebaya, was such a warm genuine human being. The only downside for me was that we didn't stay in the hotel here because it looks amazing. A truly memorable place that was so extraordinarily cheap as well.Show less

Author: jazzncaz
Title: Simply stunning
Review: The restaurant exceeded all of our expectations! The room is amazing, full of antique furniture. We ordered the four course meal with addiTional appetiser and main but in all honesty could have managed without the second main. We ordered red snapper in a pastry parcel with a wonderful sauce and a Vietnamese style prawn roll, fill of lovely fresh herbs and a chilli sauce. As a special favour we were served a crab curry for the main course. This was truly delicious. We also had 72 hour cooked rib of beef in a chilli and garlic sauce, again this was wonderful. The tempura vegetables were the best I have ever eaten, light crispy and delicious. The deserts were also fabulous, a light mouse and a pana cotta, neither were too sweet. the wine was also good. We will be going back again before we leave Penang!Show less

Author: PinkAddictKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Classy place, though not as perfect as I thought
Review: Doorman didn't speak English, we asked where we could park he obviously didn't understand and responded in accordingly.Upon entering, no one welcomed us and we stood awkwardly waiting to get the waiter's attention while they were busy serving.Thankfully the kind waiter suggested that the menu set might be too big so we might want to consider sharing instead of ordering a set for each person.For a clasy place, they had only one (and I mean only one) baby chair. Unbelievable! We had to wait for someone else to finish before we could borrow it.Food was okay. Hits for me were appetizers and dessert. Totally didn't like the lamb (we found it too sweet to our liking) and the duck was okay and a much better choice.Beautiful place and nice ambience. For sure will impres you and your guests if you go.Good experience with improvements needed. Not sure if want to go back though.Show less

Author: CharlieT615
Title: Extraordinary cuisine and ambience
Review: If you love incredible food this restaurant is a must. Ken, the Chef, is outstanding. He truly knows food. Waiting staff are attentive and courteous. That is all i want to say. Experience it yourself!!

Author: viajuliaParis, France
Title: Seven....stars
Review: This was definately the culinary highlight of our Malaysian journey - a wonderful re-discovery of Nyonya cuisine. In fact, at Kebaya one could say that it's been re-invented: all those traditional herbs ,spices and essential ingredients are still there but have been expertly tweaked and tuned and the result is sensational. I'll remember in particular the duck with star-anis and the light and witty starters. The service was as good as the feast we found on our beautiful flower- patterned plates and, just as important, we could hear ourselves talk. A perfect evening !Show less

Author: wagetKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: the classiest place in georgetown
Review: Kebaya is in a totally different plane compared to all the food and beverage outlets in Penang. Finally, there is a place you can actually sit and savour the food. This is not a place for hurried dinners - it is best to make reservations and the first thing you do is to order a glass of wine while taking pleasure in admiring the elegance of the bar and the tasteful interiors. They also have a piano player on weekends and on holidays. The fusion of flavours in their food is refreshing - it is something you have to relish. I went there a few times and the smiles of the staff are genuine, they even remember my drink. The best part is, it is non-smoking!Show less

Author: Sammy W
Title: Fantastic!!!
Review:
First time of "Nyonya Food". I would say, it was a fantastic night in Georgetown (Penang).
The food is superb from starter, main course to dessert. (My fav is "Crab curry")...the decor, the ambience, services staff is nice.

A must visit when in Penang!!!!

Author: IngunnandEspen
Title: High expectations - disappointed
Review: We wanted to try due to good reviews onTA. Average food, main course(the recomended duck) was burned and destroyed. No reason to go back. For the price of 100 RM pr person it was a disaster.

Author: FoodEnthusedKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Outstanding meal!
Review: We had read a lot about Kebaya as well as The Seven Terraces where it is located, and decided to have my birthday dinner there - and what a wonderful meal it was!As past reviews have mentioned, their set meal at RM100++ per person consists of an appetizer, main, vege dish and dessert. As there were five of us, their affable staff recommended we take four sets where we can choose a range of dishes from their menu. Good call as the dishes were huge, more than enough to share between five hungry people!We had their Pie Tee and Pork Mantao to start. Our mains were the Lamb, Chicken Kapitan, Prawn Curry and Duck; plus the Sambal Vege and Tempura Vege. Desserts we had the Pandan Creme Brûlée, Gula Melaka Mousse, Tongyuen and Tab Tim Krob. Each and every dish were delectable and memorable in its own way. And what a novel concept, cooking our respected Nyonya food with French techniques! The interior was beautiful, ambience warm and cozy with a live pianist in the neighboring Baba bar. The restaurant is smart enough for a special occasion, while casual enough for locals to go in their Bermudas for a good meal out. Parking is by the narrow road it's located, and not easy to find! We will definitely go out of the way to have a meal in Kebaya again.Show less

Author: Enrico FNew York
Title: it is not just about food
Review: The food was good at Kebaya. No doubt. But a 5 star rating cannot just be about the food. The ambiance still needs work. The bar is an underdeveloped opportunity. The white marble tops of the dining room make you want to wear long sleeves. They are cold - the whole place needs a "warming up" sort of thing. I am sure over time the Kebaya team will succeed to make their place a 5 star venue. For the time being I would like to give them 3 stars. Anyway - if one visits a place with expectations that are too high you are most likely not to enjoy your evening.Show less

Author: KennardFamilyPerth, Australia
Title: Finally some real Penang food ... with a twist
Review: Our hotel, the E&O recommended Kabaya at the Seven Terraces Hotel and it was the best dining experience of our entire stay. Superb food, warm attentive service and a stunning setting.The 'degustation' set menu (100RMB) is really 4 courses which comprises an appetiser, main course, vegetable side order and dessert - all quite generous serves. However, as explained, the dishes are designed for sharing and with around six choices for each course plenty to tempt, allowing you to sample much of the menu. The chef is obviously very experienced and passionate about food, successfully combining traditional Nonya cuisine with European influences and the result is simply amazing. We loved the ambiance and decor with the magnificent Georgian bar, relaxing armchairs & rich drapes, all the while being entertained by a very accomplished pianist on the grand piano. When we showed interest in the hotel our host, one of the owners was kind enough to take us on a tour which impressed us immensely. Since opening only in November 2012 they are striving for excellence in all areas and eager for any feedback. Nice touch. Loved the friendliness, loved the relaxed atmosphere, and will definitely be staying stay here next time.Show less

Author: Alf O
Title: Truly outstanding - probably our best meal Malaysia
Review:
We had a really lovely meal at the Kebaya. It was probably our best meal in Malaysia.

It's also a fabulous room and excellent service. 

This one is not to be missed if you are in Georgetown, Penang

Author: Chippering
Title: Don't miss this one!
Review: Beautiful decor, excellent service and superb Nonya food. Meal for two: 300+ MR, but worth every cent.

Author: Rodger BVictoria, Canada
Title: Excellent
Review: Kebaya has a set menu (for about 100 RM), but when we arrived we weren't really hungry enough to warrant a set menu with 4 courses. No problem. We told the manager that we'd just like to have a drink and perhaps a few things off the menu and he made it all happen for us.While we waited for our table we lounged in the bar area listening to the very talented piano player, which creates a delightful ambiance throughout the entire restaurant.Once we were seated, we were treated to excellent cuisine. They really know their stuff. We had no idea what Nonya cuisine even was before we walked in (it's a combo of Malay and Chinese food), but we'll try and find it at home. The portions are very large, and by design, for sharing. I am glad we ordered only two dishes, because we barely got through them, though if we had room we would have happily ordered more.This was a lovely evening for us and we will definitely return when back in Penang.Show less

Author: JadePenangPenang
Title: A taste of elegance
Review: After a lifetime of eating in restaurants with zero ambience while perched on plastic stools and being served food on plastic plates with bent cutlery, dining at Kebaya feels surreal compared to the rest of my foodie experience in Penang.Kebaya serves nyonya food in grand ambience complete with a pianist playing on a grand piano. Along one side of the dining area is a row of glass cabinets with exquisite blue and white porcelain and stunning chinoiserie which add to the splendour of the room.Dinner is offered in sets of RM100/- per person for 4 courses with an option to order dishes a la carte. We went for the set and left it to the manager, Prakash, to pick and choose a variety of dishes for us.The nyonya cuisine at Kebaya seems familiar but different at the same time. It is as if grandma has just gone back to the kitchen after taking time off to attend a cooking course at Cordon Bleu. Traditional dishes like chicken curry kapitan is infused with a smoky barbecued flavour, crab curry is served with just crab meat (very luxe, no need to tangle with claws and shells), braised duck is served with fresh plums to attenuate the richness of the dish.I intend to go back and eat my way through the whole menu.Show less

Author: lin3_13George Town, Malaysia
Title: two thumbs up from a 93 year old Nonya cook
Review: Took my Mom, daughter and son-in-law to dinner at the Seven Terraces last week.Mom, who is 93 and a good Nonya cook in her own right, really enjoyed the modern twist to the traditional nonya dishes she is used to. When asked how she liked the dishes - it was both thumbs up, and that is really saying a lot. My daughter and son-in-law, who live in the US and are always on the look out for Michelin star places when they travel, were also very impressed. The favourite dishes were the otak (fish cake in a puff pastry) and the crab curry. That was my third time, and the dining experience was still special - surrounded by gorgeous traditional nonya style furniture, dining on nonya crockery and listening to live piano music. Only one suggestion - I wonder whether it might not be a better idea to have individually priced food items rather than a set price (RM100 for three courses) - would make choosing a lot easier. Definitely a place I will bring any visitor to Penang.Show less

Author: DJCBKK
Title: fantastic food in a fantastic setting
Review: Penang has wonderful food everyplace you go — However when you find you need to relax and enjoy a more elegant experience AND great food this is the place to be. Cant wait to go back!

Author: PeterFiftyLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic evening
Review: We stumbled across the Facebook page of Kebaya when on holiday in Penang and the prompt response in emailing their menu was a positive sign.The restaurant is located within the recently (Nov 2012) opened 7 Terraces hotel; as the name suggests 7 former heritage terraces houses painstakingly renovated to provide boutique accommodation in the heart of colonial Georgetown.The menu consists of a choice of around six starters, mains, side dishes and puddings which are delicious, great for sharing and good value for money too at 100 RM ++ Kebaya has a relaxing bar area with a grand piano, with a talented pianist providing excellent background music throughout the evening..the bar was busy when we arrived so had our coffee at the end of the meal there.We have already recommended the restaurant to eight others who thanked us for finding it after an equally enjoyable experience.Good luck Kebaya with you first full year and we will return and continue to recommend.Show less

Author: Hock-ChyeWashington DC, District of Columbia
Title: Nyonya cuisine with a modern twist
Review: Had dinner with a small group of friends on New Year's Eve at Kebaya restaurant. I like how Baba Bar is at the other end of the room, allowing guests to have pre-dinner drinks before moving a short distance across to the dining area. Very civilized. I was very curious when I heard the restaurant serves modern nyonya cuisine. As it turned out, modern nyonya cuisine is traditional nyonya food that has been given a modern twist - satay pork ribs cooked sous vide until it falls off the bone, hong bak (meat cooked in cumin and ketumbar) is done with lamb instead of pork, and otak-otak is encased in puff pastry instead of banana leaf. The rosé wine offered went well with the food but I would've preferred a more extensive wine list with a wider selection of rosé wines. In all, a memorable dining experience. I plan to dine there again soon.Show less

Author: IanCerfontyneSydney, Australia
Title: Great spot to eat!
Review: We spotted this place on a trishaw ride and felt it looked attractive. On going back in the evening we were warmly greeted and loved the setting with a cool temperature, great decor and traditional feel despite obvious renovation. The menu is a set price of RM100 for 3 courses with 6 or so choices at each course. The food is excellent, creative, interesting and well presented. There is real talent in the kitchen and is was a highly enjoyable evening. The pianist added to the overall enjoyment and I would recommend this highly to anyone. RM100 for 3 courses of this quality of food is excellent value and service delivered by Prakaash (hopefully spelt correctly) was top class and helpful. Our only suggestion would be a slightly longer wine list and champagne or sparkling wine by the glass. Other than those suggestions, faultless!Show less

Author: FoodFun775George Town, Malaysia
Title: All Hype and for Tourists only
Review: I had lunch at Kota recently and it was an experience that would never be repeated. First of all, you have to go through Fort Cornwallis where the entry charge is RM10 per person for locals, foreigners pay more. The charges can be off set against the food bill. First of all, only 1 table was occupied by a family of foreigners. Service was prompt as the restaurant was almost empty but it was without a smile and when asked for more information regrading the food, the server was not sure. The menu was also very limited. We knew it was fusion food so it will be somewhat different but the food was more of a confusion. The Cendol, which came blended in a bottle tasted kilometres away from its name sake, and the coconut milk/santan used came from either a can or packet, with a few hard pieces of red beans and it was thick and gritty. We couldn't finish it even though it cost RM16. It had an unpleasant taste with a strong hint of rancidity.The Hokkien Mee, RM 25, was actually Italian pasta with a stingy serving of gravy that was not enough to mix the "noodles" in. It had a couple of prawns which was fresh but that was its only saving grace. It tasted faintly like hokkien mee, just only a hint of it. The laksa was an interesting dish with a small bowl of normal laksa sauce (but with no ingredients) served at the side and a few pieces of cucumber, lettuce leaves, onion slices, a tiny amount of prawn paste and 2 small rolls of what looked like sticky rice "noodles," more like rolled pancakes on a bigger plate. I wouldn't eat that again. The Poh Piah Acar Awak, RM 15, was overwhelmingly sour and spicy and you can stand to eat only a couple of rolls. No water was served but you can buy some from their exorbitantly priced mineral water. The total bill came to RM89.10 but was deducted RM20 (the entry price). The ambience was sterile and it was like eating in a canteen. Prices must match quality, fusion must be clever and creative but sadly these two factors are not present at all. Not recommended for locals, it's food for tourists.Show less

Author: Andri_mfa
Title: Great Creme Brulee !!!
Review: Located inside the Fort Cornwallis, Kota offers a unique opportunity to learn a part of Penang’s history, then follow up with their east meet west culinary. You must try their creme brulee which come as a 3-pieces creme brulee; original, gula melaka-based, and pandan-based. And a glass of Sunrise to quench your thirst...Show less

Author: ekeat79George Town, Malaysia
Title: A hidden gem for local fine dining....
Review: Came here for lunch in February and had their 4-course meal consisting of an appetiser, soup (i.e. tom yam), main course (nasi dagang) and dessert. The restaurant is located inside the Fort Cornwallis grounds and is accessible via its main entrance (beside the light house). You will need to pay the entrance fee to the Fort itself, but this fee is claimable at the restaurant. Probably the biggest drawback is the lack of parking spaces, but other than that it's a nice and quiet place to enjoy a fine-dining experience for local cuisine.Show less

Author: tehd2020
Title: Birthday meal
Review: Second time visit here.. Thanks Miko, Ronald and Vince sever with nice food and good service, food is delicious

Author: maggiecool
Title: Nice Food Nice Service
Review: Great dining experience at Kota Dine & Coffee. Lovely and friendly service crew(Ronald). Taste of food is good. Highly recommend for couple.

Author: sarabisgaard2101Copenhagen, Denmark
Title: A hidden gem in Penang
Review: This place blew our minds - in a very positive sense. The food is incredibly delicate and tasty and served with an aesthetic touch like it was the finest gourmet - all at or below average prices for this type of restaurant. We payed 150 RM for appetizers, two main courses and two deserts + cocktails! The place is small and isolated which makes you feel that you have left the city. The staff is very polite and friendly, with personal recommendations and a very good understanding of the food they serve. We were served by Vince and Ronald, which was a pleasure! Highly recommend it and we intend to come back! Show less

Author: CCHSingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: What a Thirst Quencher!
Review: I popped into this cafe after a round of the tourist attraction. Its cool interior was a stark contrast to the heat outside. Since I was there just for a drink, I browsed through the menu, only focusing on the beverages. I did notice a lot of thought was put in the way the dishes were created and presented, looking at the description of each dish and its accompanying photo. The theme was fusion, and if not for the fact I was not up to eating then, I would have ventured to try a few dishes. My beverage was an ice-blended Cendol drink. It was full of flavour, and I felt I was literally eating the dessert Penang is famous for. The coconut milk brought out the best in the beverage and I loved it. What a thirst quencher!The service was prompt and the wait staff, warm and friendly. Well done!Show less

Author: juhar1234Tampere, Finland
Title: Not worth visiting
Review: Me and my wife had our last dinner in Penang, saw the good reviews here and decided to go. Sadly we were disappointed. The starters were good and a little spicy, the fish -stake a little odd though. Our main courses were small and bland, the chili crab buns had absolutely no chili (or any flavour whatsoever) and inside was one lettuce, one deep fried shrimp and some mayonnaise, on the side a few curly fries. Also we felt like we weren't welcomed as there were 3 tables with big families and the waiters took pictures of them etc and none bothered to even tell us about the menu. As we finally asked for our check the waiter looked closely next to me as I counted my money. No one thanked or said goodbyes as we left. We felt treated as unwanted customers but with no reason we could think of. Not worth your money, there are many excellent restaurants in Georgetown to go to instead.Show less

Author: lyxe_ljotravelSingapore, Singapore
Title: Must Try Hokkien & Creme Brulee
Review: A restaurant located inside a UNESCO site. You will have to pay for an entrance fee to enter the site before getting to the restaurant. Worry not. The entrance fee will be offset when your bill at the restaurant is above a certain amount. We ordered Chilli Crab Mantou, Hokkien and Creme Brulee. The Hokkien is one to die for. It reminded us of the lobster soup we had in Iceland. It's rich and flavourful. For dessert, we had creme brulee. We were surprised that it came in 3 small bowls - pandan, glutinous rice and gula melaka. We preferred the pandan and gula melaka. Show less

Author: Aldona FSzamotuly
Title: Lunch - excellent dining experience
Review: Malaysian tradition meets western modern attitude to food. Delicious experience in a very pleasant setting. Staff, especially Vince are helpful and polite.Show less

Author: 176janea
Title: Nice spot for dinner
Review: My partner and I went here for dinner and it was really nice. The staff were also helpful and really nice and made some good recommendations. I would recommend if you feel like eating some local food but don’t feel like street food. FYI it’s halal so there is no booze :)Show less

Author: delaz11Malaysia
Title: Adequate
Review: Menu choices are very limited.I didn’t really fancy the food of asian fusion,nothing on the menu catches the eye and the tongue. Staff are friendly though. They only accept cash.Show less

Author: dukekevHong Kong, China
Title: Creative and tasty fusion food
Review: The restaurant is located inside Fort Cornwallis. For foreigners, it costs RM20 entrance fee per person, but you can only claim back RM10 for spending in the restaurant. The food is a fusion of Malaysian food in Western style, which is quite creative. We ordered two main dishes - Chili Crab Mantou (RM25.00) and Nyonya (RM25.00). Chili Crab Mantou is a fried steamed bun with crab meat and pomelo. It is served with soft shell crab and fries. Nyonya consists of colorful coconut rice, rendang and otak-otak, which tastes very good. For dessert, we ordered Creme Brulee (RM19.00) with 3 flavors - palm sugar, pandan and black glutinous rice.Show less

Author: skyhightravellers
Title: Great menu
Review: Interesting and varied menu. Food very well presented and tasted delicious. Staff were friendly and helpful. Overall an enjoyable experience.

Author: hmstravellagi
Title: JalanJalanCariMakan@Penang
Review: Very good ambience, tasty fusion food! Love the creme brulee, dessert you should not skip!! Very good hospitality, will come again, for sure!!

Author: pekuliina
Title: Fantastic good and service
Review: We really enjoyed all the food here, after a mediocre hotel dinners the nights before. Very reasonable prices as well and great service from our waiter, Rusty, who was really attentive, nice and considerate to our 4yo son. Would come again and probably will. Show less

Author: chanlim89
Title: Great Place, Food &Service
Review: This place has a good ambient. The food are great! The dessert creme brulee is a most try! The service provided by the waiter Vince is excellent as well!Show less

Review: Live the honey chicken appetiser and creme brûlée dessert! Attentive and great service from our server Vince Show less

Title: Thank you
Review: Highly recommended. Thumbs up to Resty who had given us a great service. Will definitey visit again.

Title: Farewell
Review: The customer service are good. The food is impressive. Ambient is nice. The staff named Resty gave us great recommendation n frendly

Author: safooraha
Title: Amazing food and excellent service staff very helpful
Review: Resty was very informative and helped us to choose what to order which really helped as we did not know what to orderWe ordered the sharing platter which I would recommend and as you can try quite a lot Note: if you want to come to this restaurant you have to buy tickets to fort cornwallis which cost 20 MYR however you will get ten MYR redeemed off your billResty also explained all the flavours to us with whatever we ordered and even offered to take picture of hsWill deffo be coming back here againShow less

Title: Experience
Review: The food is good and the waiter,  Resty is very polite  and patient.  This is my third time here and I was never once dissapointed!  Recommended!

Author: Selina668
Title: Makan experience
Review: Great experience with lots of grrat recommendations from the smiling staff. Willing to take feedback with a golden smile. Great to be here

Author: Edlow75Pulau Perhentian Kecil, Malaysia
Title: Delightful and Charming.
Review: Hosted a lunch there last week for my grand aunt who love history and historical charms. The combination of history and perfect dining experience is phenomenal at Kota. The marrying blend of recipes, that presents Penang peranakan and malay heritage in a tantalising taste. Every bite is an explosion of flavours.This is of course coupled with the awesome service from the team at Kota. Their attention to detail and recommendations were very much appreciated. The person that took our reservation and greeted us upon our arrival, really represented true Malaysian hospitality, that's no other then Mr Resty.In summary - it was a delightful and gorgeous culinary experience coupled with our charming host Resty and team. Show less

Author: Joanne5356
Title: Good environment,  food and service
Review: Good ambience, excellent staff service especially Resty and love the desert creme brulee and sunrise drink

Author: Sasitaranvasu
Title: Good food & good service
Review: Good fusion food especially Creme Brule and main dishes. Everyone is extra friendly especially Resty,our waiter.

Author: Howard KFoshan, China
Title: Nice Local cuisine, pitty to many items where sold out @18.00 hrs
Review: nice diner , all very tasty courses, its Halal so no beers, we enjoyed several dishes and all perfect, staff very helpful and friendly,decoration and atmosphere very nice.Show less

Author: nisnomads
Title: Good Innovation!
Review: We tried the creme brulee, they put their own touch in it and somehow it tastes perfect! it’s a must to take a rest in this restaurant after a walk inside the fort cornwallis (+you’ll get a discount if you’re a visitor!)

Author: Michaelcklim
Title: Nice local cuisine and a must try!
Review: The service provided by Mr. Vince is warm and the cuisine is nicely prepared with originally and creative appearance.

Author: DebbieStothard
Title: Nice take on local cuisine. But book or miss out
Review: We were a family group of 8 who are all foodies. We enjoyed the twists and fusion interpretations of local cuisine but missed out on the nasi lemak cornetto and a bunch of other  dishes that ran out before we got there. However, the sambal belacan was justifiably true to tradition. Dessert was amazing.Resty our waiter was patient and attentive. Location was amazing. 2 caveats: 1. Parking in the immediate vicinity in not allowed and parking in this general area is bad, esp on weekends so consider your options 2. This is a halal restaurant so the drink list extends to juice, mocktails, soft drinks and water.Show less

Author: JaneDoe201907
Title: Chillax cafe
Review: Good food and great restaurant for hanging out with friends. The herbal chicken is a must have! The service also fast and informative— Resty has been helpful in recommending food and also in preparing vegan option for me

Author: Leeyaaaa
Title: Nice ambience
Review: Resty (the waiter) was so nice and polite. He explained me all the vegetarian and vegan-friendly option. The restaurant so clean and nice 👍🏼 worth the visit !

Author: Sin032
Title: Nice restaurant
Review: Good vibe. Relaxing. I like it. The waiter and waitress serve us well n the food is nice. Worth the visit.

Author: SalzagalbackpackerMelbourne, Australia
Title: Amazing Asian fusion food
Review: The quality of the food and service at Kota were amazing. The menu is deliverse and includes a few vegetarian options. Each meal is quite unique and presentation is beautiful. The waiter went out of his way to recommend special dishes. He encouraged us to try the nasi lemak cake and trio of crepe brûlée and the flavours were fabulous. It is not expensive and a bargain for what you eat. The atmosphere is really lovely. You do have to pay myr 20 to get into the fort to enter the restaurant. But receive myr 10 pp off the food bill. As. An aside the fort really is nothing at all to rave about but it’s a charming setting for a fabulous restaurant.Show less

Author: RamblinRed67Sydney, Australia
Title: Nasi lemak dessert - are they serious?
Review: At 20MYR entry and really only a predictable small numbers of sights, this fort is best left to those with a hot blooded enthusiasm for anything fortlike. However, the Kota restaurant inside is terrific with kinda pricey but very tasty offerings. The Nasi Lemak dessert sure sounded weird but was actually spectacular. You have to buy fort entry to go to the restaurant but they then take half the entry off the bill. Waiter Resty served with a smile and helpful recommendations.Show less

Author: Mrgcrntt

Review:

Service was also very great!!!

Author: OoiY47
Title: Lunch
Review: Nice view with mouth watering foods! It’s a nice place to visit with friends and family. Good service from Hassan! Will come back next time!

Author: MengMeng13
Title: Best place to hangout
Review: Found this place by chance. Went with friends and have a blast here. Thank you for waiting on us for the staff Emy, Hasan, Vince and Resty. The good is yummy with great ambiance. A good place for hanging out with friends and having a blast.Show less

Author: Adani SPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Great ambience, exceptional service and even better food
Review: Came here with my friends for lunch and we were pleasantly surprised. Ordered the kota chilli crab and I loved it! The portion looks small at first glance but it turns out to be very filling. Tasted my friends' food and they were good too.Shoutout to our server, Hasan, for his great service and making us feel welcomed! Would definitely come here again! :)Show less

Author: chewyixuan
Title: Food & Service
Review: The food & service are very nice and I like the environment here. Wish to come again for fine dine here.

Author: serenemoon85
Title: Nice ambience and courteous staff
Review: Been here a couple of times, enjoyed their food. The staff, Resty, has been very courteous and friendly. Will definitely be back again!

Author: Naimsuhaimi
Title: All nice & superb
Review: Good food with good service from Resty. Good environment to enjoy your food with family..Surely will come again n again.. highly recommended.. 10 stars from me!!

Author: Yrah32019
Title: Nice place, good environment
Review: Had the chance to tried this cosy restaurant, beside fort Cornwallis compound. The food was absolutely awesome, very tasty and refreshing fresh juice. Thanks to Resty for the wonderful service.

Author: Glen C
Title: Modern perankan flavors
Review: An interesting take on traditional Perankan spices, cooking with modern interpretation, a true blue nonya would appreciate the complexity of flavors in a western presenation,, StarterMango krabu - great flavorsChicken rumpah yummy Pie tee grandmother's would approve Nasi lemak cornetto a good twistMainsTandoori chicken, the ghee rice super, chicken a tad dryChilli crab, great flavors and presentation in a mantou bunHokkien, more Bisquit please it's divine,,, Barramundi W nonya sauce tasty, brown rice super,,, Dessert Creme brulee - double serving pse,,, Nasi lemak cake - was a bit apprehensive about the peanuts n anchovies but it balance the sweet flavors of the cake,,, The dessert was definitely the diva,,,, Service great, knowledgeable Worth a second visit,,,,, Show less

Author: Jackie CSingapore, Singapore
Title: I just got rempahed!
Review: Tip: order the set menu each and share everything if this is your first trip here as the menu is exhaustive and everything reads so deliciously, you wouldn’t be able to make up your mind. However as every dish is executed so perfectly, you can’t be faulted for being greedy and not sharing and just coming back here again and again.Show less

Author: Sinbadthessailor
Title: Mr
Review: Great ambiance friendly helpful staff. Our MD Resty was helpful knowlegeable and friendly. The food was superb. Unique dishes perfectly prepared and presented with well balanced spicing.We enjoyed a guided tour of every dish presented by Resty. This restaurant is thouroughly reccommended for all vistotors and residents in Pinang.Show less

Author: tmhptmhp
Title: Excellent service and food!
Review:
Seeing food in another perspective! Inspirational! 
The Staff (especially Mr Hassan) were friendly and helpful in sharing with us the interesting menu. Will definitely revisit on my next trip to Penang!:)

However, when I went to pay my bill which was 35MYR, the employee informed me that they only discount 10MYR for tourist. I felt a bit misled since the ticket agent gave me different information. Author: adeline_potterCanberra, Australia
Title: Excellent birthday dinner
Review: We visited as a family group of eight (5 adults and 3 children) on Sunday evening for my sister’s birthday dinner and we had a very pleasant experience! We only booked that afternoon and we were pleased that they could fit us in. Upon arrival, Richard (one of the staff) very kindly agreed to my mum’s request to place a candle on one of the desserts that we ordered as a surprise for my sister’s birthday. Richard also advised that with more notice the kitchen can also do special writing on desserts, such as happy birthday, etc..We were also very happy with the food, which was delicious and fresh. However, note that the barramundi dish is only one piece of fish, not the whole fish. The style is a mix of nyonya with Western presentation, and it was also well-priced. A main course varies from RM25-28. We decided to share dishes which allowed for a variety of food. There is also dishes for children and vegetarian options. The kitchen was very accommodating for our kids and made a non-spicy version of the Kapitan chicken burger. The highlight was the dessert, which was a trio of mini Creme Brulee, with local flavours, such as pandan and Gula Melaka. The other desserts also looked interesting (e.g nasi lemak cake and tiramisu with pandan) which we will try next time! FYI - as the restaurant is in Fort Cornwallis, customers will have to buy an entry ticket (which is RM10 for Malaysians upon presentation of MyKad, and RM20 for foreigners) but this is redeemable at the Kota restaurant. However I would advise potential customers to call the restaurant to find out exactly the terms of redemption as it was unclear to me, but we managed to redeem the cost of the adult tickets (child tickets (RM5) are not redeemable). Show less

Author: FatOldDudeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Peranakan Fusion Food
Review: We visited Kota Dine & Coffee on Boxing Day for lunch and we were pleasantly surprised at what the chef could pull off. The restaurant is in Fort Cornwallis which means you need to pay the RM20 entrance fee per person. However, if your bill is over RM60, the restaurant will deduct RM10 for each person. The Christmas set menu was still in effect and you only get to choose your mains. We asked for a substitution for the turmeric mussels and the chef kindly swapped them with prawns. We then found the gravy too salty and asked for bread to balance it. No problem, the chef again obliged. For the trio appetizer, we loved the otak pai tee. The cannonball chicken rice was delicious. The only item not to my taste was the kari (curry) chicken where my old taste buds found too spicy hot. I had anticipated that and had ready on hand a glass of Penang chendol to snuff out any fires on my tongue. Dessert was a dome of Japanese sweet potato, yam and mango. We found that literally hard to crack and would prefer to have it thaw a bit more before serving. Service was excellent and I let the staff know. Do check out Kota and you may also want to tour the fort to walk off your meal. Show less

Author: Victor KPenang, Malaysia
Title: Looks better than it tastes
Review: Went there recently with my mum and sister. Kota is located inside the historic Fort Cornwallis. To get to the restaurant, we need to pay an entry fee! It costs $20 ringgits for non-Malaysian and $10 ringgits for Malaysian. The fees can be deducted from the restaurant bill if you spend more than $20 ringgits on the food and beverage.On entering the restaurant, there were 2 other tables - one with a young couple and another with a group of family of six. The restaurant looks quite sparse and tired. There is a statue facing the front door dedicated to Captain Francis Light, a British India explorer and founder of Penang island. A gimmick to lure in the tourists. There were several staff fluttering around with no one taking charge. It feels clinical and very bright with mostly glass walls and grey unpolished concrete floor. The chairs looked mismatched and one of the chair cushion we sat was stained. The menu looks nothing special for such an establishment. The waiter who served us couldn't speak proper English and local Hokkien. He could only converse in Mandarin. I asked for water and he told me that I could only order the bottled water! Some of the listed drinks were not available. I insisted to him that he had to bring warm/hot water for my elderly mother, which he eventually agreed. An unpleasant start to the meal.We ordered a kerabu salad to share and a main dish each - the nyonya blue rice with curry chicken, a herbal mushroom soup with grilled marinated chicken and rice, and a traditional nasi lemak with fried chicken. The kerabu salad was first to arrive. It was not freshly made. It was chilled and left in the fridge for too long making the salad too sloppy with too much lime/lemon juice. This should have been strained from the excess liquid. It was unpalatable and too sour and sweet to eat. However, the 3 main dishes were much better than the kerabu salad. The best dish among the three was the blue nyonya rice with curry. It was extremely tasty and delicious. I couldn't fault this dish. Every single element on this dish was well executed and definitely worth going there just to try it. The herbal mushroom soup was mildly strong and tasted like the local "bak kut teh". The mushroom was the enoki mushroom with a few slices of chinese bean curd skin which was undercooked, tough and chewy. The marinated grilled chicken fair better. It was smoky, tender, moist and very tasty. Nasi lemak was average and a let down for a Malaysian dish. The fried chicken was over cooked, tough and dry. The coconut rice was a bit starchy and not aromatic with sufficient coconut santan. The worst on the nasi lemak plate was the egg - it should not have been plated. I was so disappointed. It was over fried and burnt on the underside. The yolk was overcooked and dry - not oozed with a runny yolk. I told the staff about this and to let the chef know. Unfortunately I don't believe my comment was relayed back to the chef. Overall experience at Kota is just average. Lack of ambiance and inexperienced staff. Food inconsistent - hit and miss. Expensive for a total bill of $106 ringgits. I wouldn't be rushing back to this place anytime soon.Show less

Author: MeiLeong
Title: Local fine dining food
Review: A good and unique experience on local fine dining. Portion of the food were small... nice environment. Pricey but worth the try. Food taste good! Love the dessert!

Author: 411emilytBromley, United Kingdom
Title: A wonderful surprise!
Review: We came to the cafe only because we were visiting a Fort Cornwallis and the lady at the ticket office said we can get a rebate in the cafe so we figured we'd stop for a drink. We ended up having drinks and dessert - we got the creme brûlée - and it was amazing! The creme brûlée comes in a trio of flavours - pandas, black glutinous rice and gula melaka and it was really top notch! Just wished I'd tried more items there now!Well worth the trip there!Show less

Author: Bridget OCheltenham England
Title: The sort of food that makes you squeak in delight!
Review: If you pay to go into the fort, you get 10 MR off your 20+MR spend. This is the only reason that we entered this restaurant. So glad that we did. Had the most amazing and delicious meal. The 3 creme brulees will remain a benchmark for every crème brûlée in the future. But unlikely to encounter such bliss again.Show less

Author: meaningremissionSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Progressive cuisine
Review: A restaurant located in the Fort Cornwallis. This restaurant themed themselves as progressive cuisine whereby they try to present local delights in a different way. At times it is very confusing, in a positive way. Nice presentation however taste is rather bland, comparing to their original version. There is a entrance fee charged for entry to the Fort Cornwallis but the fee will be reimbursed if you dine in the restaurant.Show less

Author: Koh W
Title: Refreshing and relaxing
Review: The setting is very relaxing after a walk in the park. Drinks here are about Rm16. But I got a voucher that gives me a discount of RM 10 for every Rm20 spent. So I paid 21rm for 41 rm worth. Overall good experience.

Author: SoonShirlynn
Title: Special memory in KOTA
Review: Previously, a lot of friends keep talking about KOTA, how special is it and how good their food taste. Well, this is my turn in KOTA. Order their recommend nyonya, hokkien, satay. Lastly, 3 differents creme burlee make my day !

Author: DylanW781
Title: Amazing experience
Review: An amazing place in Penang. The Fort Cornwallis is a star fort that the British East India Company built in the late 18th century on the northeastern coast of Penang Island, Malaysia. Fort Cornwallis is the largest standing fort in Malaysia. Besides that, the highlight was the restaurant - Kota, when Francis meets rempah. The cuisine is mixture of traditional and futuristic. Combination of both uplift the food to different level. It bring great memory to me and my family. I strongly encourage everyone should visit this restaurant.Show less

Author: NatAli494Penang
Title: Great ambiance, average food
Review: The restaurant is located inside Fort Cornwallis, one of the oldest standing fort in Malaysia. They serve Asian fusion food, some very interesting and "instagram friendly" dishes. If you are visiting, I recommend you to visit the Fort and perhaps have some coffee / tea at the restaurant. The mains /set dishes are a little overpriced for the average quality. Service is quite poor, the waiters are obviously not trained well to serve food in a restaurant like this. Show less

Author: LNZJKulim, Malaysia
Title: Kota : Colorful & Tantalizing for the eyes
Review: Family dinner here on a Sunday evening while waiting for the Timeless Penang show to start at 8.30pm. Blessed air conditioning was a reprieve from the 6pm humidity outside. The waiters were accommodating but new and could not elaborate on the menu. It is not a normal menu so we had to check trip advisor for pictures of what we were ordering. We ordered Laksa (a bowl of laksa soup with separate noodles wrapped for your convenience), Nyonya ( blue rice, not glutinous, with some rendang and some Otak Otak) and the Masaala ( ghee rice with tandoori chicken). Also ordered prawn chowder, cendol and honeydew juice. Forget the cendol. You get better outside. The Nyonya was good and so was the laksa although Wifey didn't like it (she being the laksa connoisseur) and I would give the tandoori chicken a miss (smells too much like sweaty armpits). The prawn chowder tastes like tom yam and was ok. Portions are smaller than average so do not expect to be filled. Pricing was average. A good place to wait and also to bring friends to try but definitely not to frequent to fill the tummy.Show less

Author: Kuroneko300Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Fusion at its best
Review: A lovely cafe situated right in the middle of Fort Cornwallis serving unique local food with a big twist. Standouts are their take on Hokkien Mee - stunning burst of prawn flavors in a very Western styled dish; and their take on Satay, which was very innovative and absolutely delicious. Their interpretation of Laksa serves as a great introduction to the famous dish - rich, flavorful and visually beautiful. Overall good service and calming ambiance. Good place to relax and hangout. They also have a VIP room so great place for private dining. The cafe itself is not very big so if you're coming in a large group, good idea to book first. Looking forward to going back again. Show less

Author: KhaiPg
Title: Nice little hide out
Review: Small cafe inside Fort Cornwallis. Limited choices of food, mainly nyonya cuisine. Food is average and come in small portion. A little bit pricey but acceptable for the ambience. Nice place to relax with jazzy background music.

Author: koshpatPenang, Malaysia
Title: One time visit
Review: This restaurant is located inside the historical landmark of Penang, Fort Cornwallis.Good for a one time visit. Food is okay but oily and very small portion. Ratio is like a big bowl of rice and 1 piece of chicken and 1 teaspoon of vegetables (referring to "Nyonya" on the menu). If you intend to only serve 1 piece of chicken (like a "fine local dining"..), please just give us 2 tablespoon of rice instead. What am I gonna do with the remaining rice after the first two mouthful of rice and chicken/vege? Overpriced. Staff can't wait to take away your food, even if you have not finished. Noisy patrons during lunch. Quiets down after 2.30pm if you want to have a peaceful lunch.Park your vehicle at the Fort Cornwallis car park opposite the police station.Entrance fee to the fort is RM10 for locals and RM20 for foreigners. The entrance fee will be deducted from your bill if you dine above RM30.Look for Fort Cornwallis on Waze to reach this place. Happy dining.Show less

Author: YummySumPuchong, Malaysia
Title: Creative Pleasing to the eyes
Review: At Kota (meaning "Fort" in Malay language) you can find some famous local delicacies being given a twist of art.You may find Hokkien mee, Satay, Nasi Beriani, Asam Laksa,etc here, but be warned that these definitely look vast different from their originals.Hokkien Mee (prawn mee) is something one would not missed during a Penang trip. The version in Kota came in the form of Angel hair pasta fully absorb and coated in prawn bisque. The pasta was overly cooked, but I guess that is how it absorbs the prawn gravy. Oh, I really miss the soup hawker version! Next, the Satay was served and to my astonishment, it really didn't look like the conventional satay, and I certainty didn't expect Satay to be served that way. What an experience!Asam laska was given lots of twists and turns. It came in the form of noodles & the usual condiments wrapped as rolls. These rolls are eaten by first dipping into the asam laksa soup!! Don't forget to try the Nutmeg drink too!Show less

Author: jerryjamesgriffithCanada
Title: Excellent choice for tasty and exciting food!
Review: We came apon this restaurant by accident really. After visiting Fort Cornwallis, we were looking for a cool place to eat. What a wonderful find! Not only was the place cool but the food exceptional! We had the Chicken Curry and Spaghetti with shrimp and caviar. The curry takes 20 minutes but well worth the wait. Both tasted extraordinary!Show less

Author: Jason O
Title: Super duper small portion
Review: The food serve is darm small portion...don't qualify to call it main course... service also react very slow...totally not worth for the price!!

Author: collie72
Title: Crazy good
Review: The food n presentation is sensational. Out there crazy good. Yum. Yum yum. Never seen anything like it. Can't wait to visit again. Brilliant what else can I say? Book n go there.

Author: pugdoggy5Liverpool, United Kingdom
Title: Lunch stop
Review: We visited the fort and stopped here for a drink. We decided to order an appetiser platter as well. The menu says that flavoured San Pellagrino is available (fruit flavours soda water) but our server made clear that they would put a slice of lemon in if we wanted which isn't the same thing. The service was polite. Menu was appealing. Our platter was very nice, though I would recommend that they look at the portion sizes 3 pieces of chicken but 1 lollipop, perhaps they could offer one person or sharing platter. The only negative was that the chicken although well flavoured tasted like it had been reheated in the microwave. There are cheaper options in the city and nearby but this was a very pleasant experience. You get a credit for your entrance fee. Show less

Author: snakes116Frankfurt, Germany
Title: Pretentious, looks better than it tastes
Review: I would recommend as a date restaurant or for a special occasion if neither of you like food but love presentation. We happened to be close by waiting for our ferry and came across Kota. It was lunch and the place was empty. There were another pair of diners at the same time as us.It was unclear from both waiters what was and wasnt available. They did not understand vegetarian which was not a good sign.The menu could be improved with proper explanation of ingredients, instead of Malay/ English hybrid list. I ordered the chowder as the Hokein was unavailable (the only two none meat diahes on the menu) and I was surprised at the portiin size. It was miniscule!They will bring the food out as it is cooked. I had finished my lunch, whilst my husband was still waiting for his. Could be an issue (especially if the restaurant was busier)My husband had a meat dish, but he ended up with a lot of rice and a piece or 2 of meat. He ordered a main course, and was let down.We were disappointed with lunch. It looked the part but failed to deliver. I would describe the place as pretentious. Show less

Author: AhLiang9Sungai Lembing, Malaysia
Title: Romantic place
Review: Having my dinner there . Good environment . Food was nice, the price was slightly high but acceptable for me .However , there are some part that I personally wish can be improve . Pain water is not free . As a local , I won't pay rm3-4 for just a 350ml water . Most of the restaurant or even coffee shop serve free water .
