It tastes fresh from the abundance of mint leaves, sourish too like the asam laksa counterparts despite the addition of coconut milk.Something I'm looking forward to eat again on next visit.Show less

Author: kristiinasuvi
Title: Tasty lunch
Review: I visited during quiet lunch time. Service was friendly, restaurant has nice traditional decoration, bit of "home" feeling, not too fancy. I took rice with some veggies & tofu. It tasted great. Really nice set up & quality of food.

Author: Stanly K
Title: very rich flavour but not spicy
Review: Food is excellent.. rich with taste and diffrent types of herbs.. good for people who cant handle spicy food.. I like the second floor decoration and design. nice experience & worth the visit..

Author: sb_travel_bugNewcastle upon Tyne
Title: Amazing lunch time find.
Review: What a lovely place for food. The house is beautifully maintained and decorated. We ate in the back courtyard and felt like we had a private dining room. Service was professional, food was just delicious. Finished with tea and cake which was a real treat. Totally recommend. Show less

Author: matthewl254
Title: Simple food taken on an off night
Review: One of a few diners in the cafe. Food simple but particularly concocted in local tradition. Some tasty things but not special. Staff busy closing premises early on a slow night.

Author: sherenengadeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great experience
Review: Didn't set out to specially find this place to eat, but stumbled upon it after a visit to the nearby Camera Museum. Service was great! Its one of the few halal places around the heart of Georgetown. Tried the nasi lemuni and laksa. It was delicious! Portion servings are generous too. Just be careful if you need to go to the restroom as you have climb up and down rather steep steps.Show less

Author: ontjemoreJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Delicious Food
Review: The foods are very delicious. Roti Surai for starter then briyani rice with lamb for the main course. Arabian sorbet for the drink complete the dinning experience. Herbs and spices blend so well. With great taste and big portion you can get happy tummy within reasonable price.Show less

Author: Ismile E
Title: Good Indian & Malaysia restaurant
Review: Comfortable eating and listening to music. Meals are prepared from Indian Peranakan food. Suitable for tourists who want to try Malaysian food. But not the best place for local people to eat here because there is a better place

Author: susannn0612
Title: Good indian restaurant
Review: Tried the Nasi Lengit with sambal fish. The rice itself doesn't have a rich taste, but the fish is very good. The waitress are very nice and they willingly explain the food to you.

Author: andrewmY8759PF
Title: Great Service and great surroundings
Review: The food was well presented but sadly too westernised and lacked local flavours . So this  resturant battle. Its a shame as staff were wonderful.  Lets hope they get message in time.

Author: Divemaster S
Title: Authentic Malaysian cuisines, admist an ambience of past splendour.
Review:
Authentic Malay and peranakan dishes, mouthwatering and good.
Enjoy the ambience of jawi house with pieces of history in every corner of this interesting cafe.

Author: PassionatehawkerMelbourne, Australia
Title: Lovely Oasis in Armenian Street
Review: This was a lovely place for lunch - food was fresh and tasty and the service was very nice. The decor was tasteful and peaceful. Armenian Street is a very busy tourist street and this lovely place is at the quieter end of the street and is very much appreciated after a hot morning walking around. Cur Cur Udang highly recommended.Show less

Author: Judith APittsburgh, Pennsylvania
Title: Unique and delicious
Review: We first walked into Jawi House by chance, arriving in Penang very hungry after a long day of travel. What a pleasant surprise to find such a lovely restaurant happy to serve us at 3 in the afternoon. After a delicious meal of their special Peranakan food, we were astonished to find an authentic New York style cheesecake also on offer.Show less

Author: soubhagyajenaPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Malaysian But Expensive
Review: If you are looking for authentic Malaysian cuisine this is the right place. A varieties of menu serving different kinds of rice including "blue rice" .Those who don't know, the color of the rice comes from one Butterfly Pea Flower. Apart from this it serves varieties of dessert and cakes.  The other thing u ll notice is the interior. It makes u feel an old historical house with full of paintings and furniture. U can visit upstairs to see the art gallery.So overall a nice place to dine with ur family. Staffs are well behaved and service is good. Taste is average but i personally felt its a bit expensive.Show less

Author: justinhewettHo Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Title: Delightful
Review: Jawi House Cafe - Jawi; meaning "Locally born Southeast Asian Muslim" was delightful and rather inexpensive. I came for lunch and had the salmon baguette and it was delicious. This restaurant is immaculately clean and the detailing inside is very interesting. I suggest putting this towards the top of your places to eat list while in town.Show less

Author: AiNSTAiN83Kota Bharu, Malaysia
Title: Slow Service
Review: After spending some time under the scorching sun trying to find all the street arts we went into Jawi House to have a drink and snack. The ambiance was quite cosy and we loved the simple and old time decor of the cafe. The drinks were good but their food was quite bland. Maybe it is because we have Asian palettes. The staffs, whom I believe were foreigners based on their accents, seemed bored and uninterested. I think they could have done much better if they step up their service.Show less

Author: SalouWLondon, United Kingdom
Title: A taste of something different.
Review: I really enjoyed eating here - there were so many things I wanted to try! To my understanding, the food served here has its roots in the Muslim peranakan community, and the food on the menu represents a fusion of these flavours. I absolutely loved my rose chicken curry - the rose flavouring wasn't over powering but added a delicious twist to a popular dish. We thoroughly enjoyed our deserts and drinks too. As a couple of reviewers have mentioned, the staircase is slightly challenging to reach the toilet and you have to remove your shoes to go up - not ideal if you are wearing trainers in a room full of diners! However, don't let this stop you enjoying a fantastic meal!Show less

Author: 564janekHong Kong, China
Title: Not what I expected
Review: Based on reviews of Jawi, decided to try it out on my last evening in Penang. Service staff were very pleasant and the ambience was delightful. However, the food was mediocre and was rather bland. Also, the toilet is located up a steep flight of wooden stairs. You have to remove your shoes before proceeding to protect the wooden flooring. I didn't go as I felt uncomfortable about walking barefeet on the floor of a public toilet. Don't think I'll be visiting Jawi on my next visit.Show less

Author: Dina A
Title: Good place
Review: I came here with my boyfriend and had a good time here. I liked that food but I did not think it was spectacular. We had a lamb biryani and some other appetizers. I definitely had much better biryanis in other parts of Asia and did not really feel the fusion or burst of different flavors that I was expecting. Having said that, the lamb was exquisite and extremely tender. We also had the description entailing " tomato, mint and yoghurt sauce" but our sauce was lentil-like curry sauce and that was a bit confusing. It was a very good meal but it was not a very memorable one. Friendly staff, clean place and great location.Show less

Author: Lingyun
Title: Superb home cooking
Review: Fresh and tasty food. Clean and relaxing environment. Sometimes they are just so hard to find when u travel, but not when you are at Jawi! We ordered curcur udang (deep fried prawns and bean sprouts coated in batter, served with tough, cucumber and stay sauce) every ingredient on the plate is sooooo fresh!! For main, we had Jawi bamieh, herbal rice with chicken curry. The lamb with tomato soup is light with flavour. Curry is not spicy at all. While restaurant is clean and well decorated. 2nd floor is a small gallery with 10-20 paintings. Love it! Show less

Author: AzOthmanBern, Switzerland
Title: "Revisited"
Review: Was here with family for a pre mother's day dinner. When we booked the table over the phone they bring to our attention that there is a large birthday group at the same time. It didn't stop us to taste their excellent food.We had mango Kerabu, Cucur udang, Laksa, Lamb beryani, salmon Quiche, tomato rice and for desserts, Lemon tart and Sago Gula Melaka,Everything was very delicious and well executed. The staff very attentive and friendly.Will return with other guests here!Show less

Author: alton21Alton, United Kingdom
Title: Lovely food
Review: Are here on the recommendation of my hotel. Food was lovely - had the mango salad to start and then the chicken biryani. Generous portions so was very full! Was dining on my own so nice there were magazines and wifi. Wasn't busy and could have done with some music or candles to improve the atmosphere. Overall would recommend. Show less

Author: Suzanne DWellington, New Zealand
Title: Beautifully executed food
Review: Every dish we ate here was excellent, as was the care shown to the customers - one of us is on a strict gluten free diet and the lovely woman at the front desk rang the head chef at home to double-check what was safe for me to eat. Table service is a bit low-key, as is the Malaysian style.We skipped lunch so we could work our way through all three courses before waddling home: I really enjoyed the Malayan salad, full of fresh local produce and flavours. The beef rendang was also delicious, full of spices and texture and very tender meat - the herbal lemuni rice with it, the house specialty, was interesting but quite subtle in flavour; if I went back I would try one of the more robust rice options. The sago gula melaka was also a great combination of flavours and textures but unfortunately I was too full to finish it. My partner also really enjoyed the bamieh lamb, another signature main dish, served in a very tasty sauce.The price is moderate by Penang tourist standards - and unbelievably good value for money compared to most Western countries.Show less

Author: c1ksha
Title: Cafehopping
Review: Warm welcome by the waiters, nice coffee but review for red valvet is a bit disappointing. Im expecting the conventional  red valvet cake with cream cheese topping. Taste bitter abit. Sorry if it should that way ( well, im not a baker) . Overall, nice!

Author: PaulD1812Alsager, United Kingdom
Title: Not the easiest place to find, but worth the effort
Review: Marketed as "a different kind of place, Penang's first Peranakan Muslim Heritage Cafe Gallery" this place serves great local food. I'm glad I got a lift here as it looked confusing how to get here, but it was definitely worth the trip. The food tasted fantastic. Service was OK and meals turned up very slow, eg for a group of around 10 of us some had finished our starters before other had even been served... and this happened for the main course as well. I guess for small groups this place would be great but struggles with medium to large groups.Show less

Author: deki_mandela
Title: Excellent food with nice service
Review: We had some really nice Biryani and chicken sandwich with hummus. However, even it was Sat evening we we're the only guests and no music was playing so not really a place with atmosphere. Maybe we just came at the wrong moment

Author: BlueCupboardSingapore
Title: Good Peranakan food
Review: Lovely food in this restaurant and really nice waiting staff. Only comment would be that lacked a little atmosphere as lights were very bright and music was very Low so the place was very quiet. If these two things were fixed it would be an excellent restaurant Show less

Author: StanilausC
Title: Nice food
Review: Very nice food to eat. Every food with very special taste and it's delicious. Nice services,kind and polite. And they have nice gallery

Author: beccq2014Singapore, Singapore
Title: Beautiful food and service and vegetarian options!
Review: This lovely decorated place serves Indonesian fusion food. I got babaganoush with bread and a vegetarian cheese sandwich. Hubby got a lamb dish. The babaganoush and lamb in particular was exceptional. I also had a really interesting nutmeg and lime drink. Highly recommended for something different.Other vegetarian choices were hummus and indonesian rice dishes with vegetables. I feel a bit disappointed for having not tried the indonesian food since it was an indo restaurant but really just felt like a sandwich that day!Service was very good also. Show less

Author: 186nikhila
Title: Good heritage food
Review: I found the place through trip advisor as the rate was 4.5 with good reviews. I with my girlfriend came to Penang for holiday. We stopped at the place for dinner after a full day of walking in the national park. The delicious rice ,lamb cooked in perfect blend of spices and coconut pineapple tart just made the perfect ending for the day. The amicable and quick service by the staff definitely deserves the highest rating. A must try for heritage food and don't forget to sign the guest book.Show less

Author: frydayuk
Title: Unique flavours and relaxing atmosphere
Review: We stopped by here for lunch and felt instantly relaxed when we entered the cafe. The staff were very smiley and attentive. The juices were unique in their local flavours and we enjoyed their curries. The value was excellent for the amazing flavours!

Author: Gareth_RichardsGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Excellent food with en eye for detail
Review: Jawi House is a very welcome addition to George Town's culinary offerings. Originally conceived by the anthropologist Wazir Jahan, and helmed by her award-winner son and chef, Nurilkarim Razha, the menu offers an innovative range of food drawing on the Jawi Peranakan heritage (combining Malay, Indian and Middle Eastern influences). The emphasis here is on fresh ingredients -- including the delicate use of herbs and spices. The house speciality, Jawi herbal lemuni rice, is excellent; there are vegetarian options; and an excellent range of desserts and (non-alcoholic) drinks. Add to that the beautifully restored decor and friendly service, Jawi House has a winning formula. Not to be missed.Show less

Author: Tim M
Title: Cool break from hot tourism
Review: After a morning of looking round the sights, the Jawi House cafe is a wonderful, cool refuge.  Best lime sodas in Malaysia. Delicious food. Stylish design. Friendly team.

Author: Mika C
Title: Great Muslim food and service level
Review: Pleasant to find good Muslim food in an area filled with cafes. Mainly has different kinds of rice to choose from. Flavorful and delicious. Service staff were professional and friendly. Photos don't really do the food justice, it is really good.

Author: panzoecha
Title: Nice food with cozy atmosphere
Review: This is a good place to escape from the hot weather outside. I and my friend decided to try the perianakan food. We chose 2-3 menu for lunch i.e. signature dish - Nasi Lemuni, another curry plate. The Nasi Lenumi (15 RM) is nice with colorful rice with small fish and herb paste. Another menu is Chicken curry (seem like indian style) that I cannot remember the name, this one might be too strong for some people (including me). For overall ambiance and service is great I think if you wanna know Peranakan food this place i worth to try ;)well, there is also the art gallery room on the second floor you can walk around (that time it was not crowd of people)Show less

Author: nellielimKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Food not up to expectations
Review: Had looked forward to dining at the restaurant after learning it has a Certificate of Excellence Award from Tripadvisor. The location is on Armenian Street, 2 doors away from Yap Kongsi/Clan House. The decor here is Peranakan Malay. The restaurant is clean and tastefully furnished. We each ordered a different rice and meat dish and shared our food. We also ordered Armenian salad and cucur udang as starters. The cucur udang was really nice. We ordered briyani rice, herbal lemuni rice, tomato rice and pandan rice. The rice cooked in various styles were light and well cooked. The 2 styles of chicken, a vegetarian and the fish dishes were average but their curries/gravy were all rather bland. We also had 4 desserts to share. The pineapple and coconut tart was too sweet and with no fresh pineapple scent, semolina and creme caramel as well as the sago pudding were good. The chef and service staff were all very friendly but we were served by a new staff who got some of our orders wrong. Pricing is on the high side. Food not up to expectations. All in an average rating.Show less

Author: Caitlin BCanberra, Australia
Title: What a treat!
Review: We had been sightseeing in the heat and humidity for sometime. I guess we were unconsciously looking for Jawi House Cafe and Gallery because it was exactly what we wanted. We had the restaurant pretty much to ourselves and the food did not leave us wanting. My first green vegetables on our trip were a welcome sight. We had delicious drinks and great food in a lovely atmosphere for such a reasonable price. And all in the middle of historic George Town. Show less

Author: 965jainecHaast, New Zealand
Title: Average
Review: After reading such good reviews we were really looking forward to dinner at this restaurant. I don't know whether it was because we had been spoilt with the food eaten over the previous days but we found the taste lacking, quite bland. On a good note the staff were very welcoming and friendlyShow less

Author: MikeWells90Brighton and Hove, United Kingdom
Title: Attractive restaurant with pleasant low key ambiance.
Review: Attractive restaurant with pleasant low key ambiance.Service friendly and efficient. Food well prepared andpresented. Sample prices Penang nutmeg juice 10,hummus 15, briyani lamb 30, popadom 5 and pineappleand coconut tart 14. Not budget backpacker travelerprices. Restaurant popular with families with childrenShow less

Author: Alex CAntibes, France
Title: Best restaurant of Malaysia!
Review: We came here following tripadvisor's ranking and comments about this restaurant. We had a wonderful diner! Everything was delicious from the starter to the dessert! And the atmosphere was great - quiet and relaxing. We didn't speak that much since we were focusing on the delicious food :D Will definitely come back and recommend it to my friends!Show less

Author: RoyF31Newark-on-Trent, United Kingdom
Title: Over Rated
Review: We went to this cafe in Armenian St. having read some good reports on this site but were not as impressed as some of the reviewers. The house is interesting being one of the buildings in the historical part of the City.We made the mistake of having two starters which we shared the roti surai and the cucar udang and they were huge as big as the main meal and filled us up. For the mains I had briyani lamb which was a big disappointment as the lamb was still on the bone covered by rice. The menu gave the impression it would have been cubes of lamb not great chunks of rib and bone, my wife had lemuni randang which was good.The staff are very pleasant and the service was fine but we left with the feeling that the place is over rated.Show less

Author: untakenname
Title: Unusual food
Review: Nice little restaurant with some unusual dishes, situated in an old house. Don't be fooled by the Bengali bread - it's toast.  Nice but not what I was expecting. The lemon tart was great.

Author: Singapore1704Singapore, Singapore
Title: Glorious Soul Food in Quaint Setting
Review: My wife and I were on a vacation in Penang and tried Jawi House upon the recommendation of our hotel. We tried going there on Tues, but it was closed. We were headed back to Singapore on Wed, but made it a point to have lunch there. We were not disappointed. Located in historic Georgetown, and at the very artsy and funky Armenian Street area (where you can also catch the famous street art of Penang), the restaurant has a lovely gallery. We had Nasi Dagang with curry fish and Herbal Lemuni Rice (rice with ground lemuni leaves and specked with blue telang flowers) with beef rending. Both were very good. We also had chance to speak with the friendly co-owner, Dato' Dr Wazir, who had studied at the University of Singapore and had shared memories of Singapore. Show less

Author: angeloi2901
Title: The Best
Review:
The Best place I've eaten in Malaysia.
Simply delightful!
Nice and friendly atmosphere, excellent cuisine.
All homemade with genuine ingredients!!!

Author: Ashandben
Title: Just yum
Review: Perfect place for lunch, very quaint and the staff are lovely! I would really recommend if you are after traditional food!

Author: wintermelonKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very nice Peranakan Food in George Town, Penang
Review: We had a very nice dining experience here.We tried a vegetarian dishes with tomato rice, a herb roasted creamy chicken with herbal rice, a beef rendang with herbal rice and a jawi biryani rice with prawns. They all are tasty and good value. The food were mildly spiced, very suitable for European.The staff were friendly and efficient.It is not a big place, but it is presentable and clean and it has a comfortable home feel.I would recommend this restaurant for people who want to try out good Malaysian Peranakan food while in George Town, Penang.Show less

Author: 648IanC
Title: Best food we had in Penang
Review: This was the best meal we had during our stay in George Town. Fantastic food in nice surroundings with great service - and very competitively priced! We really enjoyed our meals.

Author: nikchua
Title: Great comfort food for a very good price
Review: Went here for lunch with my family on a Sunday afternoon. No issues with crowds and we got a table immediately. Staff were all very helpful and attentive. They do mostly Malay food with some specialties. I would highly recommend the prawn fritters for appetizers as that was the highlight of my meal there. We also tried the briyani with prawns that was very fresh and well cooked and portions are very generous. In the end, our meal for 5 with drinks came up to barely $50 sgd. Not the cheapest for Penang standards but very reasonable priced for the portions and quality of food served in a comfortable air conditioned environment. Show less

Author: greendocVictoria, Canada
Title: Great traditional Peranakan food, but very modern
Review: I came across this by chance, only to discover later it is one of the favourite restaurants of my friend, a local resident in George Town most of his long life. I can see why. A modern take on traditional Peranakan food. Unfortunately I could only eat there twice, delicious both times. Show less

Author: mafletcherSydney, Australia
Title: Small but interesting menu.
Review: Had dinner here on our first night, it is a modern interpretation of Peranakan food.The co-owner is a minor celebrity in Malaysia having won a food related tv contest, I can see why with the food. He also spends time on the floor talking with the patrons and discussing the food which is nice. The food had a nice balance of flavors and good portion sizes - we wanted to go back but there are just too many choices in George Town :-)Will try again next though.One minor downside (for us Euro heritage types) - you have to take your shows off to go upstairs to the toilet.Show less

Author: ryana310
Title: Sensational
Review: Wow, da food was delicious, magnificent, vunderba! Best meal of our entire Malaysia trip... Staff was very kind and the food came out fresh

Author: freedomfridayAdelaide, Australia
Title: Food for thought
Review: I was intrigued by the fact this was not listed in my guidebook. A lovely setting and a diverse menu allowing for late lunch. I ordered a local specialty and my taste buds were rewarded with my late lunch choice. Just off the main part of the popular street with a 'touch of class'' in it's approach to the customer. As a solo traveller, I felt most comfortable with my meal and my book and away from the noise of the tourist places.Show less

Author: Iman S
Title: Nice
Review: Food and place are good...the staffs are warmed welcomed....Besides ,after taking a meal..we can look around the street art..and many more

Author: Khayriyyah M
Title: great authentic home-cooked style local food
Review: great staff, loved the decor, yummy food and drinks and the gallery upstairs makes the cafe very special. we had nasi lemuni, jawi basmieh and briyani, and had tiramisu and bubur chacha and all were good quality and value for money.

Author: henyw2016
Title: Nice place to dine in a perfect location
Review: Visited this place after reading all the recommendation. So i walked here on a sunny afternoon hoping to taste their famous nasi Lemuni ( the blue color rice). Unfortunately when i got there the dish was sold out for the day, so i had nasi biryani with chicken rendang instead, with ice mint tea. The dish came in a good portion, very fulfilling and taste good. Had short chat with the chef ( bumped into him few months after in KLIA ...)The cafe is housed in an old beautiful shophouse in beautiful Armenian street, close to beautiful murals. Will come again to try their Lemuni riceShow less

Author: 2232KenJiSan Jose, California
Title: A welcoming restaurant
Review: When we entered Jawi House we were welcomed with smiles , a warm and friendly greeting by the waitress. We had a dinner and a lunch at Jawi House. Both meals were exceptional except for a rather tough piece of chicken in my dinner entree. My partners chicken dish however was savory. At lunch I had a delicious brisket sandwich and a very good Armenian salad.Show less

Author: Shopgirl8850
Title: Nice little restaurant
Review: Staff very friendly, food very nice though I personally find not spicy enough but taste good. I would come back again and this time request for more spicy taste. Situated in a very nice area on Armenian St, interesting area to walk about!

Author: Wardysworld2Kathmandu, Nepal
Title: Heritage elegance
Review: Lovely airy cool space with art and reading material on show...attentive and friendly waiting staff and wonderful food...the Jawi laksa healthy and tasty; the smoked salmon baguette, the traders rice with beef rendang all good and eaten up quick smart...the desserts were impressive also with creme caramel, yogurt cheese cake and others...this is a special place to be enjoyed with special peopleShow less

Author: harrytravellers
Title: Quiet with Good Service
Review: We enjoyed our outing to Jawi, although it was very quiet and lacked atmosphere, possibly just a quiet Sunday night. The food was tasty and nicely served, but nothing special. Our waiter was exceptionally pleasant and accommodating.

Author: rozy18
Title: Small and cosy
Review: Nice place in between old buildings. The food is nice, a bit too much for us. Lemuni, lentil n briyani rice are among their specialities.

Author: WahidahWBKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Quaint place to unwind
Review: It's hot outside and all the walk through the heritage trails would left us hungry and long for a cold drink to quench the thirst. And this place did just that for us. The food were nice and fairly priced (considering the prime location). It was nicely decorated (with a gallery upstairs) with the old-day charms. The chef and staff were friendly. Will definitely come back!Show less

Author: chrishE4589JY
Title: Great food, worth a visit
Review: Lovely little restaurant, friendly a staff and delicious food. Would highly recommend as one of the many fantastic restaurants in penang.

Author: iskhandar
Title: First timer
Review: I read about this place in the tripadvisor...and dine there at about 11.30am. The service was good, we ordered nasi lemuni and chicken briyani. Both food was average. Portion a bit small for the price.

Author: annelien1960
Title: Beautiful place, good food, nice people
Review: Good honest food, beautiful place, nice gallery, and lovely people. I loved the rendang, and the redvelvet dessert.

Author: RoverTreksThailand
Title: Excellent! Try it!
Review: Highly recommended.This place gets high ratings on trip advisor. These reviews are spot on.The restaurant is on Armenian Street, George Town, Penang Island 10200, Malaysia. Per the menu, JAWI is a term used by Arabs to mean "Muslims of SouthEast Asia", in particular, Malays who used the JAWI Arabised script. The menu is replete with descriptions of the food ingredients and preparation — well done.The food is tasty — quite good for what it is. But we wouldn't want to eat it every day. If we lived in Penang, we might visit this place once a month. That's because it's a niche offering and too narrow for our palates.Show less

Author: amritjsaPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A Must Try Prawn Biryani!!!!
Review: You must order the prawn biryani if you are eating at this restaurant. It was so tasty!!! It come with 4 large grill prawns, eggs, small salad at the side and good amount of basmati rice. Usually after eating biryani, you will feel very heavy inside the stomach cause biryani is always consider a heavy dish. However, when I tried the prawn biryani here, it was so light in the inside. You feel full but not like you have over eaten. Amazing blend of herbs and spices used by the chef's family pass down through generations.Hospitality and service was simply pleasant & welcoming!!! I will surely return for another around of prawn biryani.Show less

Author: Sitamshu
Title: Cosy little place, liked the tofu dish
Review:
Friendly host gave us a glimpse of the history of the place.
They had souvenirs as well if one is interested.

Author: Andrew K
Title: Breakfast
Review: First of all: property was closed till 11:00 (they says from 10:00). Waiting of breakfast was about 40 minutes. After all: it wasn't tasty.

Author: yellowtulip18
Title: Malay heritage
Review: I am so proud of this cafe, i love this place the restoration work is wonderful. The fact that they serve halal food is overwhelming. I tried their nasi lemuni, a dish my mother use to prepare when i was little. Although the taste is not the same but the smell of lemuni leaves really bring back nostalgic memories. The nutmeg drink is good, they serve with honey & a slice of lime, so refreshing. The owner & her son, chef Nurilkarim was also there (i only know later that the man i met was the chef)Believe it or not i come again the next morning to try their lemon tart. Very zesty...zingg!! The portion is big (for me) i actually has been eyeing the lemon tart since my first visit but too full to have them.The lady helper also is very friendly Do visit the gallery at 1st floor, i admire the architecture.Show less

Author: Samuel S
Title: Great food with quaint surrounding.
Review: The lamb lambieh was exceptional. They have a great range of fruit juices too. I loved the restaurant interior.

Author: Dabai
Title: Must try Lemuni rice
Review: This is the only restaurant to sample the unique lemuni rice beside Malay street vendors, and their rice is very fragrant and tasty, I can eat it without curry, although it comes with curry chicken. Nice embience, quiet and relax.

Author: RupulLondon UK
Title: glorious food & atmosphere
Review: Had a family reunion meal here. The food was outstanding and the service impeccable. We met the Chef and Manager Nurilkarim who was passionate about what he cooked and what he had learnt from his mother. It was home cooking par excellence. To be recommended as not to be missed.Show less

Author: landseairmudWorld
Title: Fuss Free & Straightforward
Review: Service is not too intrusive, very serene ambience and good to have conversations. Menu quite extensive and had a good variety of options. Taste of food was basic(as the title suggests straightforward) flavour was not complicated. Had the beef brisket sandwich, tender beef but not as flavorful. Nasi Lemuni, well nothing to shout about, it is what it is. The laksa however was special and had a unique taste. Show less

Author: ivons946Kulai, Malaysia
Title: Food is special.
Review: The parking is hopeless there, go by cab or rent a scooter! That day, I ordered a beef briyani (couldn't quite remember the name), the beef is very tender and nice. My wife order a prawn briyani, turn out is not very special but still slightly above par level. My daughter order a "Sarapai"(again not quite remember the name), with Kaya is quite special, i like that taste but didn't eat much because I restricted to consume Kaya. Lastly the dessert cake is quite nice! I guess everyone will like to try their cakes! Final tips is that the table hiding behind has very nice atmosphere, i found out that after I finish my food and on the way to wash my hand. Show less

Author: tony12cuKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: A restaurant model that everyone else should follow
Review: What I mean by the title? Instead of being fancy, such as fine dine, good solid restaurant business should simply offer great value to customers in terms of food, quality, ambience, service etc. In return, the customers will recognize the value and return to the restaurant again and again.There is little wonder why this restaurant keeps climbing the charts on Tripadvisor year after year. It has great ambience (old time Penang), great lighting, decor and ambience, friendly and knowledgeable staff, excellent food and unbeatable pricing for what a customer is getting. Just hope that everything stays the same.Although tucked in a small alley that is a little challenging to find even to the locals, but it is definitely worth the "treasure seeking" journey to get to it.Please note, this is a small restaurant with limited seatings, do call and book in advance (they still take bookings at the time of this article)Show less

Author: RahmatAs
Title: Love it
Review:
Felt strange that Penang closed early on a Saturday night. But luckily found this gem. 
Great hospitality. Good food. Non pretentious. Had the Briyani, the Hummus as starter but the Bubor Chacha was the killer dessert. Just right amount of sweetness.
Money well spent.

Author: Nicola C
Title: Amazing food
Review: Amazing food, came last year and the prawn biriyani left such an impression I had to come back again this year to try the Lemuni rice which did not disappoint. Really nice restaurant and staff are lovely.

Author: ECKLKualaLumpurKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Less is More Part 144 - Unique Peranakan Malay
Review: (Dato' Dr.) Wazir Jehan Begum (the owner) may appear to be a no nonsense matriarch but she's totally animated, passionate and charming when she starts relating stories of her family, how they arrived in Malaya seven generations ago and the 'strong and influential' women she admires including her own mother. She constantly refers to the original Penang Malays as 'Orang Tanjung', their special cuisine, how the ethnic communities lived then in the true spirit of "muhibbah" (goodwill) and laments that much of old colonial Georgetown now belong to foreigners. I could spend the whole afternoon listening to her tales and insights but she had to leave for Kuala Lumpur and we had to get on with our lunch before it got totally cold.Peranakan usually refers to the fusion of Malay Chinese cooking traditions. I am made to understand that it apparently includes the lesser known blending of Malay and Indian sub-Continent (Pakistan & North Indian) culinary styles as well. The difference is fairly distinct. The former (i.e. Nyonya) uses lighter aromatic herbs while the latter relies on stronger dried fragrant spices.We ordered all four different set dishes (three rice; Lemuni, Lentil, Briyani - one roti; Balmieh). Each came with a different curry - chicken, beef, prawn and lamb. They are all elegantly plated, well prepared and very delicious. The quality of the rice is superior. The spicy sambal is also unique. Dessert options were rather Anglo-inclined with cakes on the front line. Try the Red Velvet Gallete, a lighter version of the creamier sweeter classic. The creme caramel is good too.An altogether delightful lunch experience in very decorous surroundings. Prices are very reasonable and service impeccable. Would definitely come back for more good food and even better stories.Show less

Author: PhilbjojoBrisbane, Australia
Title: Wow! A great little find and worth a visit.
Review: A great little restaurant that offers very interesting alternate menu items of the Peranakan kind - Malay/Muslim therefor no alcohol but very much worth the visit! I had the lamb which is one of the signatures and it was lovely! Laksa was also excellent! Interesting historical visit also as amongst the restaurant is a small gallery! Show less

Author: WineloverMelbourneMelbourne, Australia
Title: Great food and good value
Review: I probably would have given Jawi House a 5 rating if they served wine. I also understand why they don't being a Muslim restaurant. The food here is delicious and very reasonably priced. We went 3 times and the quality and the service were all equally good experiences. We had the Lemuni rice, the Balmieh and the Jawi Laksa. I wasn't so keen on the Laksa, but that may come down to personal taste. The rice of the day is a great choice for only 16 rm, depending on the day you have a choice of beef redang or chicken, I had the beef and it was excellent.The dessert's were excellent, the Red Velvet and the Lemon Tart were great. Had the Red Velvet twice.Also try the Arabian Sherbet, you won't be disappointed.I highly recommend this restaurant.Show less

Author: Marian SPenang
Title: My Lovely Regular Lunch Stop for Years
Review: This is my favorite lunch or early dinner refuge in Georgetown.It's right in the center of where you will be wandering around. In fact, that's how we first discovered Jawi House.The food is delicious and freshly made. Juices are fresh and wonderful with sirop on the side (for once, thankfully). Service is gracious and attentive, which is most rare in Penang. Evidently, the staff are well trained and enjoy their work.I love the atmosphere and am made to feel right at home by everyone. A very welcoming place, lovely, with good food. Don't hesitate to try it out!Show less

Author: LWixwellington, nz
Title: ok
Review: decided to splash out on a more fancy restaurant on our last night in town. comparable to the street food of the area we were a bit disappointed. the food was ok, the service was ok, we were the only ones in the restaurant so there was zero ambience. when you consider the food outside is so cheap and so good this was not worth it unfortunately. we had a prawns dish, a lamb dish, a mandarin soda and a coke. we also got a seasonal fruit platter, watermelon apples and oranges. malaysia doesn't even grow apples and oranges, most are imported so to see these on a fruit platter was disappointing, especially for a place supposedly about the "local" food. Just ok. probably wouldn't return next time in penang.Show less

Author: JulieJohnIzzyMelbourne, Australia
Title: Lovely Food - Welcoming Staff - Charming Cafe
Review: We called in at Jawi House for a cool drink and snack one afternoon. The food was simple but delicious and the staff most welcoming. So we returned a couple of nights later for dinner and were welcomed like old friends. Again we enjoyed the local dishes and desserts and highly recommend Jawi House for a genuine Peranakan experience.Show less

Author: 635dirks
Title: You must eat here
Review: We went twice. Typical malaysian main courses complemented by european desserts. Small choice but excellent we ate the briyani,lamb curry, fish and veg curry. All excellent. Nice setting and very nice service. Prices are very reasonable. You will not be disappointed.

Author: EmC_caFrankfurt, Germany
Title: Good Peranakan Food & Nice Environment
Review: We decided to dine at this cafe based on TripAdvisor review.Food: We ordered JAWI Bamieh (boneless lamb, stewed in tomatoes and Peranakan herbs, served with okras and crusty Benggali bread) & Laksa (rice noodles in fragrant fish gravy with coconut cream, herbs and greens). We enjoyed the Jawi Bamieh. The lamb was cooked perfectly. The Laksa tasted differently from the other ones that we tried in Georgetown. The taste was not bad, but we preferred the regular version of Laksa. For dessert, we had Sago Pudding (sago, similar to tapioca, with coconut cream and palm sugar), and it was really yummy.Cafe & Gallery: It's nice and clean, and artistically decorated.Services: The waitress was really friendly, and she helped us to order a taxi.Show less

Author: Ford006KL
Title: Good food, clean and classic looking place
Review: Went there last week, 35 of us in total. Some could not appreciate the taste and some loved it. Friendly service but food took some time to be delivered. I think they cooked it individually. Authentic Jawi peranakan dishes...acquired taste. Place was clean and beautiful. Overall everyone enjoyed the experience at Jawi.Show less

Author: sarah y
Title: delicious Malay food
Review: A good place for authentic Malay food in a pleasant setting.  Clean and attractive with friendly service and a good choice of dishes.

Author: Jenni WPerth, Australia
Title: Delicious had to go back several times!
Review: Fantastic! Jawi / Peranakan cuisine, a style of cooking and flavour combinations we had not experienced before. The Lemuni Rice is also one of the best and most pleasant surprises, not at all what I expected, not to mention the Bamieh which was just wonderful, a unique flavour and aromatic dish. The staff are lovely and knowledgable and nice ambience as well. Such a shame we couldn't fit in dessert but it was a very good excuse to go back three times in the ten days we were in Penang.Show less

Author: RocketMelbourneMelbourne
Title: Great lunchtime venue
Review: Seven of us had lunch at Jawi and we weren't disappointed.The standout was the Briyani which luckily was my choice but what the others had was also received well.A nice location in the heritage area of Armenian Street and would recommend this restaurant to all.Show less

Author: aandlkchKuching, Malaysia
Title: Excellent restaurant in Georgetown
Review: We went to this restaurant 3 times in 7 days and it was excellent every time. We tried many of the dishes, and the food was so tasty, the presentation was very good, and the service was very good too. This was the best Penang restaurant for us, and the place where we had the best and most enjoyable food. The food was authentic, subtly spiced and well-balanced.We were made very welcome and the staff looked after us very well. Jawi House will definitely be on our list next time we go to Penang.Show less

Author: ShaunandSam2014
Title: Lunchtime Visit
Review: Lovely service and excellent food. We sampled the signature dishes for main course and both were excellent. Great selection of deserts and non-alcoholic drinks. Will visit again.

Author: SchosanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Fine dining at mid-range prices
Review: If you really want some fine dining at mid-range prices go to JAWI House Café Gallery.Owner and Chief cook Nurilkarim Rasha really takes proud of his job and is always ready to explain you all about the different dishes and their meaning. He can also tell you all about the Muslim history of Penang which is also very interesting. Our family of five came for dinner twice so we were able to try everything and we loved it all. The deserts are also very special.Show less

Author: BradJill THong Kong, China
Title: Jawi House Cafe & Gallery - We liked everything we tried here!
Review: We recently visited Penang for 5 days and Jawi House Cafe & Gallery was our favourite restaurant tried. This is a nice little place found on Lebuh Armenian not far from the intersection with Lebuh Cannon. The interior of the restaurant is nicely decorated and air-conditioned, with several sections of attractive seating area. The ambience is very nice. During our lunch, staff service was courteous and helpful in explaining the menu items to us. We tried the Balmieh (RM18) which was a lamb stewed in Peranakan herbs, served with okra and bread. The lamb was tender and took on the flavour of the herbs and stew very well. Overall, a nice dish that was easily enjoyed (rating 4 of 5)The other main sampled was the Jawi Briyani served with chicken (RM17) that was delicious. Prepared with fragrant rice, lovely curry chicken and salad, this was an excellent briyani that was as beautiful in preparation as it was delicious in taste (4.75 of 5). This dish was a real winner, one of our very favourite foods sampled during this trip to Penang. They did a great job with this briyani dish. For dessert we tried the coconut tart with pineapple (RM12) that was very nice, as were the Nutmeg juice and the Arabian Sherbet drinks we had with our meal. Overall, everything we tried was very good at Jawi House & Cafe, making this an easy restaurant to recommend to fellow travellers seeking a nice venue for a quality meal in George Town. We will specifically target returning to this restaurant during future trips to Penang.Show less

Author: jeff1955malaysiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Peranakan cooking
Review: it is located in the heritage site near kapitan keling mosque. The ambiance is really good and cool. Well laid out with wooden tables and marble tops. paintings on the wall gives a good atmosphere. the food is more peranakan style cooking and very different from the normal chinese baba cooking. The briyani is muticoloured rice with chicken curry. Prices are mid range but you are paying for the ambiance. Nice place to have you food in a cool setting.Show less

Author: Andrea L
Title: Don't miss it!
Review: We are regulars for lunch and dinner at Jawi and just love it. Everything we have tried has been excellent and they can even make one of the best flat white coffees we've found in Georgetown.

Author: Khaled B
Title: Excellent
Review: Really Excellent food, located in the heart of Georgetown offers variant dishes a must try is the baba ganuj! Very good service a must try when visiting the art street!!

Author: kaytee89
Title: Nice place to eat in Georgetown
Review: Jawi was a lovely restaurant, the staff were very friendly and it was also very clean and air conditioned. The food was definitely above average, I ordered the Lentil rice beef rendang and it was great. Worth going to and reasonably priced as well for a proper restaurant.the service was also fairly quick too.Show less

Author: GiorgioBen
Title: Great food and kind service
Review: My wife and I came here for a late dinner on a Monday night and the staff was kind enough to keep the place and the kitchen open just for us. The food was impeccable and the experience overall superb.

Author: Nurhuda N
Title: th most memorable red velvet gallete
Review:
nice and cozy restaurant to enjoy local delicacies, appreciate paintings by local artists, with authentic jawi peranakan ambience to boost your mood for the food.
the local food are served as in 5 star restaurants. above all, red velvet gallete is the best for me.

Author: porkkkchopSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent service!
Review: The service here was excellent, despite the restaurant being very packed at lunch. As there was a big group who arrive ahead of us... the briyani was sold out and we were unable to try it. The service staff was very apologetic about it and we were able to change the prawn briyani to lemuni rice:). These were some nicely flavoured prawns! The lamb stew with toast was superb, and some of us like the laksa (fish coconut curry and thick white noodles) as well! Suggest calling to reserve in advance, especially if you are coming in a big group. This will help the chef prepare sufficient ingredients! Show less

Author: Johan S
Title: Tasty Briyani
Review: The place to go for a tasty briyani meal (lots to choose from, whether you like chicken, mutton, prawn or beef).  Restaurant is small and quaint, located in the heritage area of the city.  Friendly staff.  Has a museum above on the upper floor.

Author: CurrumbinGold Coast Australia
Title: A very special spot in Georgetown
Review: We felt privileged to experience this unique Peranakan restaurant run by a loving family who have so very carefully restored Jawi House. We loved every aspect....menu, food, ambience, architecture & staff. A must try when in Georgetown.Show less

Author: madone1181Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Nice ambience but mediocre foods
Review: I feel for this nice little cafe where its trying so hard to impress every visitor here and also trying so hard to highlighted the culture and understanding of malay in the Penang island especially the women.I just came here for the food.But to my disapointment, the food here tasted very mild and not what i expected. The set rices and even the dessert just not up to standard. Maybe yes, this is not a dessert specialty store, but even its main attraction that is the NAsi Lemuni, tasted very mediocre instead.For tourists, maybe it can be nice and mild, but to locals...i have to say not a good job.One more thing is, the service is very very slowwwwww....i have to remind them 3 times that I'm still waiting for my meal to be serve!!The ambience and the surrounding of this place is quite nice and serene and they have a mini museum upstairs, which i think is very cool.But apart from that, nothing much is good in this joint.Show less

Author: Cliff6108Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Memorable dining experience
Review: My friend and I were warmly welcomed by the proprietor herself. We both ordered Lemuni Rice which was accompanied by a sweet and tangy sambal which whetted our appetite. The flavor was well balanced and needless to say, we both immensely enjoy our lunch and chatting with Datuk Dr. Wazir Jehan who described the meal that we had ordered. A memorable dining experience it Indeed was. Coffee was good too.Show less

Author: PompeyPenangPrincessPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: As good as expected
Review: Have been wanting to go for a while and finally got the chance today. First thing that impressed was the ambience, then the fact that the pot of ginger tea came without being sweetened-a rarity in Malaysia, and therefore very refreshing, literally and metaphorically! Have the prawn biryani which was delicious served with a rich, tasty daal and cucumber salad. the prawns had a very tasty sambal on them and while more expensive-RM 27 than I would usually be willing to pay, it was worth it, with 4 large prawns. Every mouthful was absolutely delicious. You do have to wait for your food-as it was mid afternoon I was the only one there and it still took a good 20 mins, but that's because the dishes are clearly freshly prepared. It's a pain for me to get to town, but it was so good I will be returning with friends very shortly. Definitely a must try, and that's from someone who has spent years here!Show less

Author: Regina_Lum
Title: Excellent food! Cozy place!
Review: The cafe has a cozy sense of home which goes extremely well with the delicious-almost-feels-like-home-cooked food that they served.

Author: Adilla R
Title: Love It
Review:
We dine lunch and dinner at Jawi House. love it very much especially Nasi Kacang. Staff and Owner very friendly. 
We will come back when we in Penang again.

Author: PaperStoneScissors
Title: Little gem
Review: This is a nice little cafe in a street that is becoming increasingly commercialised.  So nice to find somewhere cool to sit and relax with a drink and snack without feeling pressurised into buying more than we wanted to eat, or hurried to leave.

Author: 182victorialWalkerville, Australia
Title: Art house cafe
Review: This is a lovely art gallery come cafe serving local specialties which we had dinner in. It is on the gorgeous Lebuh Armenian which is delightful to walk down of an evening. The waitress was lovely and friendly and the food descriptions on the placemats are helpful. It is a Muslim establishment, so no alcohol is served. Definitely try the Sherbet drink and the nutmeg drink, they are delicious.Show less

Author: Tappin8r
Title: Lovely food, lovely setting, friendly service!
Review:
We shared some delicious hummus, divine laksa, and a life-changing Bamieh. Oh and the "sherbet" drink was interesting too!  

Don't miss this place. It's air conditioned!  ;)

Author: 622alastairgLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Delicious food in restored shop house
Review: The staff were very friendly and welcoming at this Muslim restaurant. It has a varied and innovative menu taking its influences from many cultures from within Asia. The chicken biryani with a generous and tender serving of chicken was excellent. The yogurt cheesecake may sound ordinary but was not; it made an excellent finale to my Lemani rice dish.Our nutmeg sodas were freshly made and provided a refreshing compliment to the meal. At around US$ 20 in total for the two of us this was excellent value for the quality food and drink and atmosphere.Show less

Author: Thalesapp
Title: Great surprise
Review: I've been with my family. We have a baby and a toddler. They prepared a special food out of the menu for my son. Our choice was also great! Very good value for money.

Author: LA3112
Title: Lovely food
Review: Very impressed with the food here. Had the lamb biriyani. Was very good. Next day came back for lunch. Sandwiches were very nice. Friendly staff also. Nice decor.

Author: TonyMcS
Title: Underwhelmed
Review: Attracted by the reviews, we came away disappointed.  The food was average and, in the context of Georgetown, a bit overpriced.  Not bad, just not very goos=d.

Author: Luis S
Title: Good food and ambiance
Review: Good service, food, ambiance, and drinks, nicely presented. The portions are sufficient, but you may want an appetizer if you are very hungry. Did not try the desserts but they looked great! Also one of the few places that accept credit cards, so kudos!

Author: PrernaS269
Title: Uniqueness
Review: The food tasted great and different but in my opinion the price didn't agree with the portion. It should have been lower.

Author: bert88Reading, United Kingdom
Title: Great food
Review: This place is now on my favourites list as we have visited this place 3 times in a week! On one evening, we came in for the desserts only.The food is very flavoursome and the desserts are simply exquisite. Ambiance is very calm and relaxing.The service is great and everyone is very helpful and cheerful.Highly recommendedShow less

Author: U5571MLjenniferlPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: a good try
Review: finally made the visit to the cafe after reading the reviews.. i had the 'jawi bamieh'(boneless lamb stewed in tomatoes n peranakan herbs,served with okras n crusty benggali bread-like d bread but the dish was a bit salty for my liking even though the lamb was nice :() while my fren had d herbal lemuni rice...both of us needed something sweet so we ordered the jawi cream caramel n red velvet galletes with cream cheese. It was okay. like the ambience with the music, feels like being at home..and service was good :) may come back to try other food as well :)Show less

Author: Giogina R
Title: Tasty
Review: Another good choice of peranakan food to complement that of Kebaya. As recommended the Lemuni rice is excellent so is the lamb. Very relaxing ambience and good service too.

Author: JinnyChew
Title: Average Briyani
Review: I'm no expert of Jawi delicacies, but my taste bud never fails.l can practically introduce 5 briyani houses in the 5km radius from jawi house which serves the best briyani in town.The staff was not attentive and lacking knowledge.We had visited many heritage houses in georgetown, jawi house is no close by any standard. Show less

Author: Susan RLondon, United Kingdom
Title: delicious food & friendly staff
Review: one of the staff at our hotel suggested this restaurant and I'm glad we followed her advice. We went for an evening meal and really enjoyed the food which was a mix of Indian and Arabic. The atmosphere was relaxed and the staff friendly. Although we were only in Georgetown 3 days we went back to Jawi house for lunch the next day.Show less

Author: Olakhoma
Title: Tasty
Review: Had our dinner at an elegant ambience was so amazing. Food was tasty and delicious. Staffs were friendly and welcoming. We will be back

Author: travelchick202Washington DC, District of Columbia
Title: Incredible restaurant
Review: My husband and I came here for dinner on our last night in Penang and were very impressed. The service was impeccable - I believe one of the owners greeted and waited on us. He was very friendly and gave us the best service we had in Penang. The restaurant itself is gorgeous and full of history and vibrancy. My favorite part was the stained glass windows and the place mats, which had press releases on it. The food was very delicious. We ordered netbread as an appetizer and were very pleased. Our entrees were also very good. The prices are very reasonable - we would have gladly paid more for such a fun experience. It was raining when we were leaving, and the owner called a cab for us, then walked us out with his umbrella. You seriously cannot get better food and service!Show less

Author: Ferro27Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: (Almost) Tastes like home
Review: Jawi House serves 'Jawi Peranakan" cuisine which is basically cuisine from the people of Indian/Punjabi/Arab/Persian/Turkish and Malay descent. I was a little hesitant to try this restaurant at first because I come from a Jawi Peranakan family and the menu contained a lot of things my own parents cook for dinner parties. I was pleasantly surprised however as everything we ordered was delicious. Not quite like my parents' but close. Would definitely recommend it.Show less

Author: Wani87Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Classic in a good way
Review: We accidentally found this nice café gallery as we strolling around the area. They serve well seasoned Peranakan food (something you cannot find easily in Penang). We tried a few main dishes and exchange it among us. The ambience is just great with open gallery on the second floor. Would recommend this place if you want something different from the nasi kandar, Indian foods and coffee shops.Show less

Author: lmeinkingBuffalo, New York
Title: Love this food
Review: I have been to this restaurant at least four times now and I am always very happy with the food. I like the taste, the way the food is arranged, the house itself, that means, the ambience is a bit of George Town itself so it is really worth trying out. Even though I am a vegetarian and even if there are not many options for me, the ones I do have are great. I would love to see the cook create and offer more vegetarian options. Show less

Author: mohzan hSeremban, Malaysia
Title: Good Malay food in Penang Island
Review: Penang is famous of its Mamak (Indian food ) n other delicacies. There is not many traditional Malay crusine restaurants .Accidently found this place while walking around the famous "Armenian Street area " - National Heritage area under UNESCO. Unfortunately I did not try any of the dishes, as i just had lunch,but the menu 'looks' good ( agree with the other reviewers ) Price is ofcourse slightly on the higher side with each dish averages rm15.00 ( usd5) n coffee n other drinks around rm10.00 (usd3) What is great is the ambiance / set up of the place , the owner ( a former university proffessor) wishes to keep alive the Jawi Peranakan tradition ( i don't quite understand this) but there are write ups n articles in the restaurants to 'explain' all these. Nice art gallery n photos , very clean place n you must go to the 1 st floor which the owner arrange some nice furnitures to make it look like a living room and very clean toilet too. Cook is the owner's son , a yound friendly guy. I had coffee and the lemon flavour custard was excellent, just could't resist the creamy look.Show less

Author: mansoors246
Title: Good ambience.
Review: Tried this place a week ago, food didn`t impress me much. However, the ambience and the owner`s  attention deserves recommendation. All in all, a one time visit only.

Author: JACKHONEY
Title: Interesting place
Review: Limited menu but ALL the food great and especially as home prepared no fast food.... good customer service and good photo ops.

Author: ScarlettParkinsonLiverpool, United Kingdom
Title: Worth a visit.....
Review: A short walk from our hotel on a quiet street in George Town. A simple menu but plentiful portions. A few tips, the Chicken served in the Bryiani is on the bone, just in case this doesn't agree with you. This restaurant doesn't serve alcohol but has a very good range of soft drinks, fermented lemonade and coffees etc. The food itself (apart from the chicken on the bone) was lovely. THE most flavoursome rice dishes we had outside of India and the vegetable accompaniments, again were beautifully cooked and they don't lack in presentation either. I would recommend this restaurant and would certainly go back. Show less

Author: Dutchie_in_SingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great restaurant in the hart of Georgetown. Must go!
Review: The friendly Mango Tree Hideaway in Georgetown, our guest house during a weekend in Penang, recommended us to have dinner one evening at the Jawi House Cafe & Gallery, just off Armenian Street. What a lovely meal we had at this cosy and relaxed restaurant! Host Karim recommended us a few of the house specials which we were happy to order. Laksa Lemak, Nasi Lemuni and Chicken Curry, all very fresh and tasty.Karim was a wonderful host and his staff was friendly and unobtrusive. When back in Penang will definitely pay Jawi House a visit again. Highly recommended!Show less

Author: NazmicxSingapore, Singapore
Title: Prawn Briyani Baby!!!
Review: Karim was a fantastic host and the food was sublime, I am extremely particular when it comes to food (I am from Penang) and I left this place knowing I would return. Their briyani is different - not oily at all and the taste was a unique blend of shah ruhk khan meets bruce lee. Its amazing what they have done in just over a year, keep it up Karim!!Show less

Author: Ellison00Zurich, Switzerland
Title: Excellent Food in a very friendly atmosphere!
Review: We went for dinner to Jawi House and were completely delighted. The food was very tasty, we tried the hummus and Jawis speciality with lamb. We also tried the penang drink, which I can recommend. The owner of the restaurant was very friendly and explained the origin of the food, it was extremely interesting. Prices are quite fair and the place is just lovely with a gallery on top!Show less

Author: KatFromAussie
Title: Excellent food
Review: We had lunch at Jawi House Cafe today and really enjoyed our meals. The food was so delicious, the portions were good and the prices were quite cheap considering the high quality of the food. Can't wait to eat there again.

Author: cerka2019Hastings, New Zealand
Title: Flavourful food
Review: Decided to forgo the cheap hawker food and try this place. Had a beef rendang while my girlfriend tried the lamb rendang. They were both delicious but the lamb was more so. Lots of different spices used which made the food aromatic and delightful to eat. I also tried the beef brisket sandwich which was melt in my mouth goodness. The lemon tart was yum. Really delicious food.Show less

Author: Hera DJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Excellent Nonya Food
Review: Tucked amid a lovely neighborhood on Armenian Street, Jawi House offers the refined version of nonya food. The ingredients are still rich but the combination is subtle. Desserts are light and not overly sweet. Service and ambience are great. The only downside is, the sambal (chili paste) is not spicy at all.Show less

Author: DaudRayPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Excellent local Penang food in an upscale environment
Review: Some of the best Penang sauces I've ever tasted are found here. This place is smart, well decorated in period style in an old colonial house right in the middle of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Georgetown, Penang. The food may cost a bit more than elsewhere, but the quality & atmosphere are worth it because it's all top notch. Talk with the cook about special deserts they have that day. Also, talk with the proprietor who is a super interesting scholar, author & cultural expert. In the few minutes you're waiting for your food, look at the books she's written & that are available for purchase. A really cool place to take your wife or girlfriend & friends for special date & delightful experience.Show less

Author: PaoloferranteMombasa, Kenya
Title: I really love this place
Review: I had an outstanding lunch in this heritage café. I really recommend to anyone who visits Penang. The cuisine is a fusion of middle eastern, malay and Chinese traditions with a modern twist. The best ingredients are chosen and are cooked to perfection. The biryani and the homemade sembal are the best I have had so far. Last but not least, the ambience is really full of charm thanks to the interior design, the furniture and the decoration. An absolute must go in George Town.Show less

Author: Christeene818Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Excellent Nonya food in the amazing Armenian Street....
Review: We stumbled upon this restaurant whilst exploring Armenian Street which is my all time favourite street in Georgetown. The menu has some great options including interesting salads - we had the Special salad which came with generous slices of pear - very refreshing - followed by babagannouj which was a lot different from the Lebanese version we are use to but also was very good - was served with two large pieces of toast. They also have hummus which is a favourite. They do a great Salmon sandwich and save some room for cake. We had a baked cheesecake which tasted like a mix of lemon tart, meringue pie and cheesecake - ate every crumb. They do a good cappuccino which is full of flavour. Overall a lovely restaurant in a very interesting location. Staff are very friendly and helpful. They also have art on display in the dining area as well as upstairs. Highly recommend checking out Armenian Street and drop into Jawi House for a break from the heat and enjoy their hospitality.Show less

Author: myflashngo_ken
Title: Comfort environment with great food
Review: I like the "homely" environment, feel cozy and warm. Friendly staff with great smile. Serve delicious Peranakan Jawi Cuisine, definitely will visit again.

Author: StefvgiTurnhout, Belgium
Title: Great atmosphere and tasty food!
Review: We visited this restaurant for brunch. The welcoming by the personnel was really friendly and made us feel at home immediately. The decoration of the interior makes you wonder if you are eating in a cosy museum rather than in a real restaurant.I had the sandwich with salmon, with crunchy French bread, a little bit of olive oil and some fresh vegetables. Very tasty for a reasonable price!Show less

Author: Frequenttraveller076Japan
Title: Beatitful setting, delicious meal
Review: I visited Jawi House for what turned out to be an exceptionally convivial lunch with friends in its welcoming atmosphere. The décor is eclectically elegant, and also relaxing, the food generous, subtle and varied. The hybrid nature of the establishment part high-end restaurant, part gallery and part patisserie somehow exudes singular charm. Its proprietress and manager, a world-renowned scholar, launched this business in order to promote Georgetown's culture writ large. She has succeeded magnificently. Highly recommended as a cultural + culinary experience. Value for money excellent.Show less

Author: Kat FPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A Must-visit in Penang
Review: I have been living in Penang for 2.5 years as an expat, and can safely say that this is now at the top of my list of lunchtime cafes in George Town. Nuril, the chef, said that he has been cooking traditional Malay food since he was a child, and based on the quality of food he serves at his restaurant, I have no doubt this is true. He is very active in the restaurant, and will gladly explain what is in each dish, as well as give recommendations. So far, I or my friends have tried the rendang, the biryani rice, the rose chicken, the lemuni rice, the vegetarian rice and even the beef brisket sandwich, and I have yet to taste anything that was not absolutely outstanding. Food here has such depth of flavor -- he uses his spices to perfection. On top of this, prices are right, with a good-sized entree costing RM 12-RM 16, and snacks costing no more than RM10. The atmosphere perfectly matches the food -- the cafe is light, airy, very tastefully decorated in the Malay style, and not to mention spotless. Guests are treated as family. They also sell a range of heritage books, including a recipe book that includes recipes for the food found on the menu -- very helpful for those trying to bring a taste of Malaysia back home with them. I usually like to leave a helpful comment to the restaurant owners, but frankly I cannot find anything to suggest. They do it right here. I highly encourage all those visiting or or living in Penang to try this place out.Show less

Author: Bohenia CMelbourne, Australia
Title: A must !
Review: My husband and I loved the food and people at this restaurant very very much that we went there three times.The food is absolutely beautiful! Its so homey and warm. The son of the owner is very welcoming and friendly. The staff were fantastic. I strongly recommend anyone visiting Penang to try out this wonderful restaurant.The porridge is unforgettable. We will definitely go back when we next visit Penang!Thank you for making our meals in Penang memorable!!!!!!!!Show less

Author: WillyWah
Title: Nice food
Review: I like the waitress, polite and friendly. Everything was fine, the food taste good too. I love the herbal lemuni rice and prawn briyani.

Author: najieb
Title: best food ever had
Review:
good food, good environment and friendly staff.....what more can you ask for.

it is a must to try to everyone visiting penang

Author: Radek SEdmonton, Canada
Title: OK
Review: Good atmosphere & setting. Did not enjoy the food that much since the meat was a bit undercooked for us (chicken still had some blood), waiter said that that is how the dish is made; OK.Show less

Author: WishgiverStockholm, Sweden
Title: We have been blessed!
Review: My wife and I stumbled upon this restaurant by accident. But we are so happy that we had our lunch there. We tried their Herbal Lemuni (a chicken curry dish) and their Jawi Balmieh dish (lamb) and we were both taken away how good & well balanced the food were.( Don't forget to try out their multi coloured rice.) We will go back before we leave to try out the rest of the menu as this was one of the best Nyonya meals we ever had. The prices are also good (10-20 RM for main course) we would recommend this restaurant to anyone asking for good Nyonya food.Show less

Author: Sunmonkey01Adelaide, Australia
Title: Jawi House; outstanding food and experience!
Review: Quite by accident we happened upon this serene and authentic Malay eatery. Despite entering near closure, Nurilkarim (owner and chef) accommodated us with engaging charm and hospitality.The menu was authentic Jawi Peranakan; offering dishes gleamed from Malay family traditions and served in both style and setting akin to a home-style eating. Let there be no miss-apprehension concerning the freshness and quality of the food and experiential nature of the food....all are astonishingly good! We had the signature dish (Bamieh lamb stew with bread and orca), black glutinous rice porridge, sago pudding and Arabian sherbet, nutmeg juice, frothy tea drinks. A most fortuitous experience and highly recommended.Show less

Author: JessR0b
Title: Great lunch in a beautifully restored house
Review: Excellent food- we had lemuni rice and a brisket sandwich. The owner blends middle eastern and peranakan flavours quite well in their dishes. The house itself was beautiful- everything is well designed and the house comes complete with an indoor courtyard and light well.

Author: MurniIsha
Title: A must try!
Review: Awesome meals! we had our lunch here, briyani rice with beef rendang, superb taste and really authentic. The Lemuni Rice is also one of the best. Meals comes with big portion. Friendly customer service and nice ambience as well.

Author: radsgfSingapore, Singapore
Title: One of the Best meals in Penang
Review: We dropped in on a whim passing by this little gem of a restaurant on Armenian Lane. We were glad that we did. We had the roti jala, which was soft and good. Then the bamieh which was absolutely the best dish of our meal - the delicate spices and the delicious lamb, served with thick toasted bread had us talking about it afterwards. We also ordered the lehmuni rice which was incredible. We had never tasted lehmuni rice and were pleasantly surprised. The coconut flavour wasn't overpowering and was well- balanced with the spices, served wth crispy anchovies and egg and chicken curry, it was satisfying.For dessert we had the pineapple and custard tart which was slightly sweet and the bubur cha cha which is slightly different from the Malaysian style, but also good. The staff were very friendly, and I highly recommend to anyone who wants something a little different from the usual Penang fare.Show less

Author: JamesLai28Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Best ever lemuni rice!
Review: We heard about this place from a friend and decided to check it out. Never heard about Jawi Peranakan food before, and it was a very pleasant surprise. The food was unusual, and yet what you would expect from Penang – comforting, fusiony (if that’s a word), unique. And excellent! It was also one of the prettiest cafés I’ve seen. The proprietor was also there. She is actually an anthropologist - a life fellow in Cambridge University - and we got a very interesting (and free) crash course on the history of Penang. We left the place satisfied, and glad we chose to holiday in Penang. It really made our trip.p.s. try the lemuni rice, the balmeah, the gallette (although a little too sweet for my taste), and the fentimans soda’sShow less

Author: Sharnaz90Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: "Georgetown Patrimonial Cafe"
Review: We had their speciality lemuni rice and beef brisket sandwich, and both were excellent. The nutmeg juice and Arabian sherbet was very refreshing. We also visited the gallery upstairs, full of interesting paintings and artifact. The chef was funny and helpful, and explained the menu to us very well. Will definitely come back.Show less

Author: DeepakG1471
Title: Must visit in Penang
Review: Recommended by a fellow tourist, I decided to pop by this cafe. I must say I was greeted warmly by the staff and given a brief summary on the availabile menu. There is even an art gallery at this place, where I eventually buying 2 pieces. Will definitely be back!Show less

Author: RunnerJaimeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Quaint Place in the Heart of Georgetown
Review: I came upon this restaurant by accident while walking around Georgetown. It looked interesting so I decided to check it out during lunch the next day. The food options are quite nice and price is very reasonable.It offers a unique take on the Penang culinary experience. It was great to know that there's more to Penang than char kuey teow, assam laksa and the usual fare of satay and oyster cake. I tried the Jawi Balmieh which was a divine lamb stew that was light and filling at the same time. The beef brisket sandwich was yummy too. For dessert I had to try their red velvet galletes. It was indeed worth every calorie and I must say I even liked it better than the famous Georgetown cupcake's red velvets. Certainly a place to visit for foodies visiting Penang.Show less

Author: John SSydney
Title: Lovely lunch
Review: We came across this cafe quite by accident. The facade attracted us and once we saw the menu we decided to have lunch there. The food options were all appealing, moderately priced and the general atmosphere was relaxed and friendly. Lunch was terrific and we will return.Show less

Author: DollyBirdScotlandScotland
Title: A Treasure Trove of Goodies
Review: In the blazing heat we stumbled in here thinking well the little art galleries do drinks. It had sooooo much to offer and it was such a shame it was our last few hours in Penang! i wanted to go through the whole menu but we could only manage a few of the smaller snacks which were divine. A real feast for the senses.Show less

Author: Rema N
Title: Local cuisine with a difference
Review: Penang is famed for its cuisine , Jawi just raised the stakes. The menu appears similar but flavours of the dishes are subtle and exquisite. Certainly a place to visit for those who ' live to eat'.

Author: Fazrein_Meah1303Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Good Food! Great Ambience
Review: Been to this place a couple of times and the food is simply excellent. The passionate young chef really puts great effort in every dish. The numerous authentic rice dishes available are simply mouth watering but dont forget to leave space for the homemade desserts. The ambience of this place is very homely with a lot of natural lightingNice place to take a date after a long walk along the Penang Heritage area ;)Show less

Author: zaiemmPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Great Ambiance, Better Food
Review: I have visited the Jawi House Cafe and Gallery twice since its opening. On the first occasion i fell in love with the friendly chef and the cafe owner. Their welcoming demeanor and warmth truly moved me. Couple this with some heartwarming home cooked food from yesteryear, i truly found the experience worth reliving. I ordered the Balmieh Lamb Stew, served with crusted beggali roti. It tasted just like how my grand-aunt (who passed away in 2011) used to make.I coupled this with some fentimans Rose Lemonade.From here, i went on schedule a date at the restaurant in September 2013. This time, per the chef's recommendation, pre-ordered a chateaubriand steak. Turns out, the chef in attendance, has won various awards at a local and international level. I requested it be served medium-rare and it was cooked to perfection. The steak tasted exquisite. The best part? For a steak, salad and dessert, it barely costed me RM50!! A downright steal.The chef even took the time to carve the chateaubriand table-side. This made the experience truly different, better and most importantly special.My girlfriend was thrilled by the experience.We capped the outing with the home made yogurt cheesecake which did not disappoint.Thank you and a BIG BIG thumbs upShow less

Author: sweetaftonSingapore, Singapore
Title: A very modest menu
Review: One eats inside a gallery of artisan handcrafts on 'antique' tables and chairs, surrounded by antique benches and coffee tables. Upstairs is an art gallery. This place is located inside a historic part of town within the UNESCO Heritage City of George Town. Armenian Street itself is full of history. The café gallery opened in June 2013, very recently.
