Review: A great place that serves good Italian food and drinks.  Food is prepared with passion, the chef would also improvise to create out do the menu drinks and dishes.  We had our best meals and dessert in Georgetown here at Il Bacaro.

Author: Al SHenley-on-Thames, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent Italian eatery
Review: Everyone at Il Bacaro will make your meal an enjoyable experience.The waiters are all intimately knowledgeable of all the menu items, including daily specials.The lamb shank (tenderised in Coca-Cola and cooked in a red wine sauce) fell off the bone, just like it should.The desserts are also to die for.Show less

Author: Rufli KLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Can highly recommend, great experience
Review: We made a reservation by email and promptly got a friendly confirmation. Upon entering the lobby, which also serves as lobby for the boutique hotel Campbell House - we were warmly welcomed by the owner couple. The restaurant is cozy and has a warm feeling. Great buzz with many patrons already dining when we entered. The owners are working and supervising that all is going well and assisting the well trained staff. Prices are low for the quality food and they feature reasonably priced wines - a promotion for white or red at 85 ringgit. From the E&O Hotel where we stayed it takes a 5 minutes taxi ride for Ringgit 12. We had the ruccola salad, the spicy prawns with garlic and chili followed by a white pizza with gorgonzola. All delicious. Go for a nice evening out.Show less

Author: sam_meilingSingapore, Singapore
Title: To Venice with love...
Review: As guests of Campbell House, we were privileged to experience the 'private dining' version of Il Bacaro on the hotel's breezy but ambient rooftop terrace. We started with the chichetti of 6 tapas sized starters - an arancini rice ball, deep fried squid with lemon, clams in white wine (my fave) and garlic, salmon balls, deep fried chicken and grilled vegetables. Since there were four of us we also ordered the special Gnocchi bolognese (close your eyes and breathe in - you're practically in Venice) and a buffalo mozzarella pizza - both dishes are a must order if they are on the menu.For mains, we had sage chicken, the super yummy beef involtini, seafood spaghetti and baked salmon in pastry - all fabulous and delicious! And of course to finish no one can resist any dessert that involves hot flowing chocolate or the equally irresistible affogato.Luckily for us it was less than 10 steps to bed - a perfect evening with family made possible by attentive staff (who were manning a full house restaurant), hospitable owners and fantastic Italian food and wine. Don't miss this restaurant if you crave a night off Penang's incomparable local cuisine! We can't wait to come back. Show less

Author: JoanneChowPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: An Italian Gem in Penang
Review: Il Bacaro was on one of the local news ads recently and when I read it, I told myself that I'm gonna visit this place and we did last night! We had a reservation and the moment we stepped in, there were 2 bottles of wine on the reserved table waiting for us! We took the Red and it was the right choice! We had the Chef selection of 6 dishes as starters. It was just delish! We loved those Italian Tapas so much! My hubby had lamb shank and trust me, it's a killer and it's cooked to its perfection! And I took Roberto's advice and went for gnocchi and it didn't disappoint me! One of the best gnocchi I have tasted! While we thought we didn't have any more space for desert, Roberto came and told us about Mount Etna, and we decided to have a share! How could we not have desert to complete a superb meal? And yes, it's worth the wait of 30 min for a desert to be cooked from scratch, it tasted heavenly! Apart from the great food, Roberto and his wife are 2 lovely, friendly people who made great recommendation to our food selections! With the cozy ambiance and excellent service, Il Bacaro just made us feel like home! We will certainly go back to this gem again! Show less

Author: cmleicesterPhnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: Wonderful Italian surprise in Georgetown
Review: Struggling to find a local Malay restaurant on a Sunday afternoon and battling the heat, we randomly ducked into Il Bacaro for a light lunch and were pleasantly surprised. Great service, a good basic menu supplemented by an interesting specials board, a light lunch was clearly not an option. Beef Involtini was luscious and the naughty cheesy garlic bread a real treat. I would probably recommend for an indulgent dinner rather than trying to 'be good' at lunch!Show less

Author: dorbetts
Title: Best Italian in town hands down
Review: After a change in chef or supervisor, this is by far the best Italian in town. A lot of attention is put to the end result. The chocolate mt Etna dessert is good..albeit involving a 30 wait as it's made to order.

Author: KevinC183
Title: Kevin
Review: Used Trip Advisor for suggestions and opted to eat here. Very pleasing experience. Food was great and the service was equal to that. Will definitely go back again.

Author: Tom v
Title: Amazing food
Review: Great Italian food from Venice. Ordered 6 dishes chosen by the chef, all of them had a great taste! The dessert was stunning as well. Staff where very attended!

Author: hendrikwal
Title: Pizza bottom a bit soggy and undercooked
Review: Apart from that the 9 atarter plate was great. Pizza taste was ok but i prefer a bit more crispy bottom. Chocolat samosas a real treat!, its not t best in town but close second for italian food!

Author: Stephen VCuenca, Ecuador
Title: Surprising Great Italian in Malaysia
Review: When in another country, one doesn’t usually look for food that is not synonymous with the region. When in Chinatown, one doesn’t usually look for Italian food. But, when an excellent restaurant comes across our path, we will do our best to experience their culinary delights. This is what happened to my husband and me. Il Bacaro was right in front of us when we checked in to the Campbell House. Besides, how can one go wrong with Italian in Penang when one of the co-owners (Roberto) is from a small town between Roma and Venezia?Located in a renovated historic building, the décor in the restaurant makes for a relaxed atmosphere. It is understated elegance that combined with great food makes for a romantic evening. This was perfect as we had spent a good part of the day getting to George Town. We started out with a couple of the restaurant’s mixed drinks. My husband took a chance on a drink that was tropical and he highly approved of his Lychee Martini (RM23 / $8). I went for their Moscow Mule (RM24 / $8) that was made to perfection. Since we were rather hungry, we had an order of Cheesy Garlic Bread (RM10 / $3) brought out. It was perfect, especially since it had fresh garlic. At that point, we knew our dinner was going to be wonderful and fresh (Think of farm-to-fork).Roberto came by our table, and we struck up a rather lengthy conversation. We talked about Italia and the wonderful dishes that come from that part of the world. His advice was taken when he recommended a wine from Friuli-Venezia Giulia in Italy that he says was up-and-coming. He was spot on as the Luisa Refosco (RM95 / $32) was a perfect accompaniment to our dinner.As you can see, everything on the menu is very affordable. My husband had their special, Lamb Egg Tomato Filled on Mash (RM36 / $12). Where else are you going to get quality lamb for such a cheap price? I opted for another special that night: Penne Ala Norma Ricotta (RM28 / $9). Our meals were just heavenly and very Italian. As a previous TripAdvisor reviewer exclaimed about Il Bacaro, “There is Italian food, and there is Italian food...and then there is REAL Italian food!”Though we had eaten quite a bit, Roberto convinced us to split a dish of their Tiramisu. I am a huge fan and connoisseur of Tiramisu, and what we ate is some of the best I have ever had. This includes what I have eaten in Roma.Our entire bill was RM243 / $81 for some great Italian food, wonderful ambience, and attentive service. We love Il Bacaro so much that on another night after having dinner, we split an order of their Deep Fried Mozzarella in Breadcrumbs (RM14 / $5). It was crunchy, hot and fresh. The appetizer was washed down with some Tiger Beer. By the time our stay was over, the waiters at Il Bacaro knew what beer we wanted before we could sit down. And, our beers always came with a smile. That is how good the service is. Needless to say, the next time we are in George Town, Il Bacaro will be one of our first places for dinner. And of course, we will have Tiger Beer!Show less

Author: koshpatPenang, Malaysia
Title: Hidden Italian Jewel
Review: We have so many places to dine, we sometimes missed places where we frequently pass by. Like some Italian food? Try il Bacaro in Campbell Street, Chinatown. If you can't make up your mind of what to order, is best to check the Special Menu or grab any pizza. Mostly delicious! Just one thing, fork and knife not so clean but maybe I was unlucky.. Price, about RM200 for 4 but it's value for money.Show less

Author: blackbirdjellyKo Phi Phi Don, Thailand
Title: Breakfast Delight
Review: I happened upon this restaurant while wandering through chinatown, as it was 11.15am it was a bit early for lunch but luckily they were still serving breakfast and what a treat it was! I ordered Eggs Florentine, which i have had a number of times while travelling in Asia with very mixed results, but Il Bacaro really got it right, perfectly poached eggs, lemony sauce and lots and lots of spinach -just perfect. The tea was good too and the freshly squeezed orange juice was delicious and beautifully presented. Service was friendly and attentive from the moment i walked in and the room itself is stylishly decorated. As for price, I would say it offers excellent value, I will have to return again to sample the full menu!Show less

Author: Enrico FNew York City, New York
Title: Venetian Food
Review: Il Bacaro, the restaurant in Campbell House was long on my list to visit and now eventually I made it possible. I am glad. And also have a happy full belly. Satisfied. It is funny how Venice comes to mind when you enter the premise. The walls look water stained like you could really be in an old Venetian building. The place has style. A very ... I don't know ... it is modern, but also old. Anyway - I really did enjoy the food there. It is real. Italian food is not just pizza and Bolognese. They eat real food in Italy, too. Herbs, spices, fish and meat, you know. And then a nice espresso from a professional waiter. Shortly I saw the cook peeking out of the kitchen. An old man with a chefs jacket that has the Italian colors on the collar. Maybe he is the real ItaIian cook in Penang. Must be the only one. I really enjoyed everything there. The atmosphere. And then I stepped out the door and realised that I just had spend 1 hour in Italy ... funny that.Show less

Author: 141BlueskyHong Kong, China
Title: Good food and Value for Money
Review: Visited il Bacaro in August, the food was very good with some regional dishes you do not normally find in Asia, also the flavors were of a real Italian restaurant ....not too catered for the local market all at a perfectly reasonable price.My wife and I had the pizza, by far the closest to a real Italian one, I had in Asia.The boneless Lamb was very very good, tasty and tender....and the Cicchetti to start, was just like in Venice... the service was good, friendly and efficient.On my next Visa run, I will visit again!!Show less

Author: NazdemMurrumbeena, Australia
Title: Nice atmosphere but dinner really not worth the calories
Review: We came here with my husband in August 2013. My husband had a pizza and I had a pasta carbonara . Pasta was cooked well but was dry the sauce was very poor and not tasty at all. I literally can cook better myself. My husband pizza was ok except flooded with cheese not even buffalo mozzarella. Wine was good. Interiors and service was good . Show less

Author: RoberticusMunich
Title: Venetian Experience
Review: On our June visit to Georgetown in Penang, we visited this extremely quaint restaurant with our friends. The atmosphere was friendly, the restaurant spotlessly clean and, being in Chinatown sitting at a pavement table, there was plenty of watching the "world go by". After your meal, try the "Grappa" (it helps with indigestion). As to be expected in an authentic venetian restaurant, the food wasn't the cheapest in the area, but very good value for money. We will return in January,Show less

Author: hunnybunxSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lil Italy in the heart of Georgetown
Review: Lovely Lovely italian fare in the heart of Georgetown. Cosy homey atmosphere with enthusiastic and helpful waitstaff, the food is gorgeous and authentic. The restaurant is located within Campbell house -- a lovely heritage hotel which we hope to visit again in the near future. I;d come back to Il Bacaro again -- even if just for coffee while people watching :)Show less

Author: maxyboy888Greater Sydney, Australia
Title: il bacaro july 2013
Review: We have been to this restaurant twice, first time we stumbled upon it whilst shopping in Chinatown , Georgetown late June and we had what was put to us as a snack, wow what an understatement it was huge and so nice and the second time we were so impressed with the first we invited friends to join us.Both times we had great meals and our friends were so impressed they intend on staying at the hotel when next in Penang as we will do also.The meals and service were first class on both occasions, as was the wine selection.We met the owners of the place and we found them to be very genuine and decent people.Cannot wait to return in January.MaxyboyShow less

Author: Janet LPenang, Pulau Pinang, Malaysia
Title: IL BACARO RESTAURANT-ITALY FOOD
Review: The IL BACARO Restaurant is a very nice & good place to have lunch & dinner over there even have beer or wine gathering with friends also a very good & comfortable place. Environments very clean, airy and the staffs are very friendly. I and my family like to go there to have dinner because the food are very special and the taste are very delicious and original Italy style and use original Italy ingredient all prepare & cook by Chef Mario. New Zealand Lamp Cutlet with Puree Potato, Short Rib Beef with Roast Potatoes, Pasta Salmon & Cream Sauce, Pizza Turkey Ham & Mushroom these all are our family favourite also don't forget the dessert Paciugo & Tiramisu. Price are reasonable. We will always go back to the IL BACARO Restaurant and of course will introduce to our friends too!!Show less

Author: ScotsmaninmalaysiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great food and service
Review: Part of the excellent Campbell House Hotel. Good Italian menu and fine specials board. Extensive wine and cocktail list. Service of the type that you don't get in Malaysia very often, which is a credit to the owners, who are hands on themselves. And a best of Cafe Del Mar CD playing to boot. Wish it was in KL.Show less

Author: Jaisya
Title: Cosy & Authentic Italian
Review: Had a great sampling of food here, would like to try more but we had limited time. The coffee, latte and cappuccino were great. The food just like the tasty ones we had in Venice, very authentic and delicious..

Author: tenukKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Disappointing
Review: I went to Il Bacaro for a hope of real authentic flavorful Italian dish, but ends up disappointed and i cant even finish my main course. It's bland, not enough flavor and a total rip off.The Minestrone i had is also pretty basic and i'm sure i can do better at home.The only positive part i could say is it's a nice place, good service and they packed my unfinished main course (some lamb risotto) well.So i said goodbye to that place and swear i will never return again.As for the lamb risotto, we brought it at home, re-cook it with added spice and herbs..and it became so so good. See better cook at home than go to this place.Show less

Author: locomotoreNasushiobara, Japan
Title: real italian food, at last
Review: if you want to dine in a cozy and sophisticated atmosphere, this is a good place to be.If you also want to have good italian food this is definitely the place to be.Try the fish - any style - and don't forget the tiramisu.Good wine list.Show less

Author: ChunYeowPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: A Great Italian Restaurant in Campbell Street
Review: I have stayed in nearby area for almost 20 years before moving to PJ. Could not believe there will be one high end Italian restaurant just near to the wet market. Went to the restaurant with my wife, brother-in-laws and 17 months old baby. Tried out the pasta and pizza at about 3.30 p.m. The restaurant AC was not opened and it's quite hot during that time. Pasta and pizza were great and staff was helpful. Think of revisit it again. By the way, my little daughter gives a big thumb up to the Pizza!Show less

Author: Charissa PMalaysia
Title: Not up to my expectation
Review: I came to know this place through a very well known online website. However, reading the reviews written by the author and having to experience such a horrible service, was a disaster. We made reservations prior, upon arrival, they couldn't find our RSVP. Secondly, Service Manager speak arrogantly and doesn't know his food list & wine list well. Thirdly, unable to recommend what's their specialty. Food was just okay. Nothing great. There was one table ahead of us, and it took us 1 hour later for the food to be served. I won't look forward to this place again. Is totally different from what I read from the reviews.Show less

Author: BillreeseLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Il Bacaro is a good Italian restaurant
Review: I visited Il Bacaro with my wife and five year old daughter and was very impressed by the hospitality of the Venetian owner. My daughter is not a fan of spicy food so the offer of a very authentic Italian margherita pizza brought a real smile to her face.Has a very extensive Italian wine list for any European craving some real old world wine. A perfect restaurant for families.Show less

Author: john pPhnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: A genuine and very popular Italian family run taverna for a relaxed but elegant atmosphere and great food. .
Review: This Italian family run restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere, understated elegance and great food. It is very popular with discerning local families, expatriates, as well as foreign guests and busy every night of the week, so you may want to book; as an Italian taverna in style it is typically child friendly, though romantic couples shoud find a cosy corner as well. Prices are middle range and family affordable.An instant clue to the quality of the cuisine is the brevity of the menu with four or five choices on each menu segement, starters, pasta, pizza, main course, and dessert; nonetheless the choices are varied and ample, from refined elegance to Italian staples. Especially noteworthy is the soft shell crab on polenta, delicious bruscetta, perfectly cooked breaded scallops, as well as classic and exotic pasta selections and the delicate moist local fish with puree. The menu is gently rotated so there is always something new for the local fanbase.Located within the stylish Campbell House Hotel, recently converted from a Chinese shophouse in the heart of old China town, this restaurant has already become a landmark in Penang's cuisine scene.Show less

Author: Richard R
Title: Food for thought
Review: We had lunch there the other day and it was very good. A well rounded menu that delivers. Friendly and efficient staff. Only let down was the limited wine list but then it is Malaysia.

Author: KelvinPgGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Value-for-money semi-fine dining!
Review: my friend recommended me this restaurant which is located at the corner of the cross road between Cintra Street and Campbell Street. it is at the ground floor of Campbell House boutique hotel. upon entering, an elegant model-alike lady greeted you. there was no two-seated table. the ambient was cosy. the menu was a single sheet double-sided. menu is simple, typical venetian food. i ordered the Vongole Al Pepe (clams sauted with garlic) as teh starter and main course comprised Stuffed Chicken with Mozzarella, Tomatoes, Basil, on Soft Polenta. Zablaglione was the choice of dessert ordered. I love the clam soup. it has easily more than 30 pieces of clams. the breast meat of the chicken was not dry. I spent all-in-all rm75 for everything including a cup of black coffee (americano).by 1230pm. there were already 7 - 8 tables filled up. price was reasonable for the service and food one gets. the restaurant together with the hotel were 3 months old.Show less

Author: gumtree10London, United Kingdom
Title: Very Nice
Review: I have been back to Il Bacaro, and again I was very impressed, Penang is starved of GOOD places to eat food that is not Asian; Il Bacaro is filling the gap, my pasta was good and innovative, representing Italian food of Today rather than Italian food of 20 years ago.The pizza was very good and my Italian friends loved it.I will be back againShow less

Author: gumtree10London, United Kingdom
Title: Great place
Review: I have been back to Il Bacaro, and again I was very impressed, Penang is starved of GOOD places to eat food that is not Asian; Il Bacaro is filling the gap, my pasta was good and innovative, representing Italian food of Today rather than Italian food of 20 years ago.The pizza was very good and my Italian friends loved it.I will be back againShow less

Author: KhalilMariamMalaysia
Title: Exquisite Italian Dining
Review: At IL Bacaro, you'll have your money's worth. The food is excellent. It’s where one can enjoy authentic Italian dishes served in a warm and friendly atmosphere. And the desert is to die for. If you are ever in Penang, make sure you drop by IL Bacaro Restaurant in Campbell Street, you won't regret it...Show less

Author: PaperStoneScissorsPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Not very authentic
Review: Sadly we were disappointed by this restaurant. It seemed to catering more for the local clientele (no Pork!) which meant there were non of the glorious Italian salamis and hams that you would expect.. There was only one chicken dish (a leg) and the lamb osso bucco wasn't what we expected either as there was no bone insight, just a pile of stew. In other ways the menu was sometimes misleading (items described as "with" which came without) and the service was not as good as it could have been.Show less

Author: MikeMalaysiaMalaysia
Title: The best Italian in town.
Review: We enjoyed a VERY nice lunch ...we are not very familiar with Italian food so were glad to have Roberto (the owner) guide us through the menu and help with our choices. We started with the Mixed Salad with Grilled Vegetables which was excellent, and then shared the Pan Seared Catch of the Day and a Margherita Pizza. Both very nicely done and tasty....one of the best Pizzas we have had in a long time!!! The decor is very nice, and the place is not overly pretencious, with relaxed but very attentive service.The owners Roberto and Nardya have been in the hospitality industry for a long time in Europe, and their chef is seriously passionate about Italian food....and all of thos shows!!!This is a seriously good restaurant ,and in the short time it has been opened has already built up a strong following among locals. The restaurant is part of the Campbell House Hotel, a restored heritage building, and this will also soon become a very well know hotel of distinction in Penang.Fabulous food and ambience, a must do in Penang.Show less

Author: PaperStoneScissors
Title: Not very Italian
Review: We visited this restaurant and wouldn't call it particularly Italian.  It was as if the restaurant has given up on being Italian and has gone for the local clientele instead.  Ever heard of Duck Pizza with Bechamel sauce before?

Author: John RPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A Welcome Change
Review: Having just visited IL Bacaro last night for the first time with clients and colleagues i would like to say that we will most definately return for more of the same. Fantastic hosts that look after you as family, knowlegable, approachable and friendly staff and great food at the same time. A compact and relaxing restaurant with an open plan kitchen. ( Its great to see the chefs at work ) serving traditional dishes in a traditional way, rustic, charming and full flavoured be it starter, main course or dessert, what you see is what you get. If only more restaurants looked at food in the same way we would all be happy diners more often.Show less

Author: Ross739Penang
Title: Much welcome addition to Penang dining scene
Review: I visited this restaurant with some friends and we were all very impressed with the quality of the food and service. On the night we were there (a Wednesday), it was full with tables filling almost as soon as they emptied. It was recommended by a colleague, and I'd certainly go back Having lived in Penang for over a year, such a restaurant experience was a great surprise. A really nice touch was the time taken by the owners Nadia and her husband (an Italian guy, don't remember his name) to check on their customers.Show less

Author: amvg2015Renesse, The Netherlands
Title: Great location, good food but small portions
Review: Located in a very nice old building with great atmosphere; not a big place and only 10 tables, but quite busy at the time I was there. Staff was very friendly and attentive, menu was limited, and good wine selection. Had a 3 course dinner; started with salmon and tomato salsa (very nice but small portion), fish with vegetables (no idea what fish it was and it was a very small portion) with roasted potatoes (some were overroasted which I left and no remark when they took my plate) and tiramisu (very nice, but was on my table within 30 seconds after ordering it). The food quality of what I tried is without doubt very good, but after 3 courses still feeling hungry is not a good sign; maybe I should have taken pizza (saw them in normal sizes passing by) or pasta to avoid this. The bill came up to 145RM including 2 glasses of good wine and that would be fine if portions are bigger. Overall it was far too cold for me and think you really need long sleeves. As this is new place (and was recommended by a friend) I will give it another try within the next 6 months as I think that many things were on the positive side.Show less

Author: Marc WSingapore
Title: So much hype over nothing.
Review: Coffee, espresso, was a totally watered down americano and they had the cheek to tell me THAT was how they served espresso, utter rubbish! Coffee grounds could be found at the bottom of the cup! For that sort of price, Starbucks does a far better job! Looks can be deceiving. Show less

Author: gumtree10London, United Kingdom
Title: Well Done!!
Review: Had dinner at "Il Bacaro" recently, the atmosphere was wonderful, a very nice place, well in keep with the Heritage building is located in; warm and friendly, it seemed to be in a European city instead of Penang.Smart but not pretentious, a place where ANYBODY will feel comfortable dining in.The food was very good and fresh, very new addition to the Penang restaurant scene.I cannot recommend this place enough!!!!!!Show less

Author: edward1380London, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent Italian cuisine, friendly service and contemporary feel
Review: We visited Il Bacaro numerous times during our stay in Penang, and each time the food and service is consistently excellent. As frequent visitors to Penang we have tried many of the local and international-style food vendors and can say without reservation that Il Bacaro serves the best Italian food in Penang, and quite possibly in Malaysia!The menu is small, mirroring the high quality, attention to detail and the fresh ingredients used to prepare the dishes (not a 20 page menu where each dish is frozen and cooked in a microwave!) Although small, the menu is varied enough to cater for most tastes: vegetarian, seafood and meats, pastas and pizza are all available. The menu changes quite frequently and food is very reasonably priced (main courses started at around 20 RM).For us, a very nice feature was the home-baked pizza's made fresh on order; the home made breads and the excellent wine selection.The surroundings are very pleasant and tastefully decorated to a high standard - staff are very knowledgeable and happy to assist. In short - Il Bacaro is a very welcome, although unexpected, addition to Penang's food scene (Penang is known as the "food paradise" of Malaysia). One could even be forgiven for thinking that there were in Italy, once seated in the restaurant, as to find an Italian restaurant of such high quality in Malaysia is most unusual. Il Bacaro would not be out of place in London, Paris or Venice!Show less

Author: TheBitterTruthGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: BRAVO !
Review: There is Italian food, and there is Italian food ... and then there is REAL Italian food !!! It made my heart sing and put a giant smile on my face. No more "American-Italian-Localised" nonsense like Aglio e Olio with seafood (what???), cardboard pizzas with pineapple (?), soft spaghettis with a sugary tomato sauce ... NO! Not here! It sure takes guts to do what is done here. Just try the duck canneloni (yes - not only the french use ducks for food) and you know what I am talking about. Proper Italian cooking. North Italian in this case. Most people have never experienced it. You should. I hope the team at Il Bacaro will stay with this fabulous food concept and don't make changes towards the "Italian style" food everybody knows here. That would be tragic. A lost opportunity to experience real Italian food. Il Bacaro is setting the Gold Standard for Italian food in Georgetown. I hope some restaurants will look at their own menus now and "put it up a notch". Good luck Il Bacaro. I am a fan. Keep it up. I will be a regular at your table.Show less

Author: Kheng YMelbourne, Australia
Title: Variety the spice of Sri Weld
Review: Sri Weld food court is one of my favourite. The eating place is big and airy and not a heat trap for lunchtime diners.The variety of cuisine is enough to satisfy any taste buds. Penang hawker favourites are all there - from char koay teow, chinese pasembor, hainan chicken, mee rebus, beef noodle soup, wanton mee, balachan and other varieties of fried rice, curry mee, hookien prawn mee, koay teow soup, and the dependable lady at the entrance selling three varieties of nasi lemak.There is a large choice of drinks and fruit juices.This is a cash only transaction. There is a car park right next to the food court.The place is only opened for lunch.Show less

Author: Jan Willem tNijmegen, The Netherlands
Title: Before travelling back once again a splendid breakfast here.
Review: The day before we are travelling back to our home in the Netherlands, we took our breakfast at Sri Weld Food Court. When we are in Georgetown this is our favorite food court for breakfast and lunch. This day we choose the fried Char Kuey Teow and the Hokian Mee soupe, both ful of flavour, very tasty. Also the ambiance is here very pleasant, the hawkers as well as the customers very friendly. In one year we will be back in Malaysia and for sure back to Sri Weld Food Court!Show less

Author: Jan Willem tNijmegen, The Netherlands
Title: The place for a delicious breakfast or lunch
Review: This is our favourite Food Court in Malaysia, famous and delicious Nassi Lemak, for me the one with Ikanbilis and egg but many other kinds available! This morning I went for the Hokian mee, a delicious kind of noodle soupe with little shrimps, chicken, beansprouds, etc. Todays lunch I will go for the Char Fried Kwey Teow, one of the most known Penang dishes. The drinks such as Kopi or Tea Tarik etc. are delicious too. The people here, guests as well as staff are very friendly and cheerfully, a pleasure to be here.Show less

Author: poyosann
Title: Very busy hawker in the morning,
Review: Very busy hawker in the morning, famous banana leaf nasi lemak must order the braised chicken feet from wanton noodle shop! A lot of choices and the humble bakery in the food court is good for their butter cake

Author: Tour167331
Title: once a week
Review: Just had one of the best claypot rice. Only Rm6 with lots of rice and meats. Good value. Overall good variety of penang street food. A must visit when in Penang.

Author: Dashers2014
Title: Splendid
Review: Very clean. Extremely quick and polite service. Only had a drink. Was delicious and satisfying. Extremely cheap.

Author: 858tehsh
Title: Nasi Lemak
Review: If u are in Penang, go to this food court to try nasi lemak, first store when u enter food court. It’s sooo good.... It’s spicy for those who can’t take spicy food. If u r foreign tourists, must try this authentic local food :)

Author: TH06MAY
Title: Brunch
Review: Dined here for brunch on a Thursday - had 3 dishes: fried pork wanton (5), chicken and shrimp hokkien noodles and char kuey teow. All were tasty. They were around 23 RM so very reasonable.

Author: yuenwahKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Plenty of variety
Review: After reading the many reviews of this food court, decided to try out during our recent visit to Penang. Arrived around lunch time on a weekday. Waited a few minutes for a parking space. Place is packed, notice with more locals than tourists. Plenty of variety to choose, would say reasonable in taste only for the food that we ordered. But price is cheap.Show less

Author: Rachel MLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Great food court
Review: After visiting the Penang Peranakan Musuem I came for a weekday lunch. I had the Nasi Lemak from the front which I thought was pretty decent and cheap as well (a little less than 2 MYR for a small portion). I had some excellent chicken rice from a stand inside though, really tasty and only 4 MYR. Show less

Author: Mycroft678
Title: Good food in a spacious place
Review: We got there just before the lunch crowd so finding a table for the 5 of us was pretty all right. The highlight is the nasi lemak which dad and lil sis bought a packet each. It was simple and delicious but the chilli might be a little too intense for some.Lil bro and I got the chicken rice and asked for a combination platter which was chicken, roast pork and char siew. The rice was nothing great and felt like normal steamed rice that was a little salty, but the meats were pretty good. The chicken was not overcooked, and the roast pork was fresh and the skin was crispy.Mum got a herbal soup dish that was next to the chicken rice stall, I did not try it but mum said it was simple and tasty. There was also a fried kway teow / horfun stall that served excellent food. We ordered a plate to share after our mains and were were not disappointed!Some stalls may not have English signage but they have pictures of their popular food, so just point and do charades if all else fails! =DShow less

Author: FLBBPCMM
Title: Good and affordable
Review: This place has more local than tourists. Price is much lower and good quality of food. Keow teow tng soup is so delicious mix with sambal. Lots of ingredients too. My 1st choice here. Curry mee not that fantastic but it comes with cockles that plus point for anyone like cockles. But I prefer the one at joo hooi cafe the curry mee taste is more memorable. Loh mee and CKT not bad. But a bit salty for CKT. Nasi lemak taste is really those old day nasi lemak and the coconut rice very fragrance. Show less

Author: rowlongLongreach, Australia
Title: Delicious Nasi Lemak
Review: We stayed at the Royale Chulan and this eatery is just outside the hotel. How lucky we were! The food here is so yummy. The Nasi Lemak was fantastic and so was the Laksa. I'd go as far as saying it is the best Laksa I had in Penang. Lots of locals eat here and it's busy every day so you know it's good.Show less

Author: DonipkuPekanbaru, Indonesia
Title: Best Nasi Lemak in Penang
Review: If you got chance to visit this food court the nasi lemak is the best food they have. The nasi lemak is not packed earlier but packed invidually as the queue is waiting. So the nasi is still hot. They have three choices. Fried sarden fish, fried salt fish and small shrimp. Beside the nasi lemak there is a stall selling fried donut. Should try this one too because it tastes so goodShow less

Author: PhoonKHSingapore, Singapore
Title: Clean and cheap food court in Georgetown
Review: Our family had our lunch at this food court. Diners comprise of mostly local office crowd and the price is very affordable. Here’s our verdict on the dishes we tried:1. Claypot rice: 6/102. Pancake: 8.5/10 (generous with peanut)3. Nasi lemak: 9/10 (spicy)4. Mee goreng ayam: 7.5/105. Taiwanese braised pork rice: 9/106. Taiwanese chicken chop rice: 8.5/107. Curry noodles: 6/108. Char kway teow: 7.5/109. Roasted pork rice: 7/1010. Roasted chicken rice: 6.5/1011. Fried banana balls: 5/10You only need to order the food from the stall and indicate your table number. The food will be served and you only pay when served. Show less

Author: bennyvectra
Title: Extremely yummy Nasi Lemak
Review:
Extremely yummy Nasi Lemak

Small packets that cost about MYR 1.80 each. But the sambal was fantastic.
Bought 1 of each type - Ikan, Udang, Sotong, Bilis.
Unfortunately ayam was not available.

Author: Abiseshana
Title: Nasi Lemak was amazing! CKT was okay.
Review: The nasi lemak is bite sized and absolutely yummy. The sotong sambal and Ikan sambal was really delicious. The char kuey teow was okay it was missing the oomph

Author: LiewSLLutry, Switzerland
Title: Good food at very good prices
Review: We were at the Penang Information Centre where the friendly lady manning the counter, Ms Rosaline Chan, gave us much useful information. One of which was that the food court just a few steps away was a good stop for food. We followed her advice and were so Glad we did. We had the Hokkien mee (it was so good I had 2 bowls), wantan Mee and kuey Teow T'ng. They were all good. We wanted to try out the beef noodles but the queue was too Long. There was a good crowd of office workers and also tourists at lunch time. The place does get crowded but that is to be expected as the food is good and the prices too.Show less

Author: sandgrownun18
Title: Cheap as chips
Review: Great selection of food from different stalls, we ate there 4 times and were satisfied every time, average price for a meal is MYR 7 (£1.40).

Author: SzeYongSRawang, Malaysia
Title: Nice Local Food!
Review: The food court which most visited for my business trip.Which the food court have the nice local coffee and various choices food that you can choose!The food court easy to drop by which beside provide a car park for customer who drive to park & enjoy the food!Also that the food court having Malaysia local famous food - nasi lemak which costs min RM1.80 (might change depending on time when you visited)Show less

Author: Clarence YSingapore, Singapore
Title: Cheap, local food ...
Review: Penang is famous for its food, and this place has a good collection of many of them. While the stores here might not be the best versions there are, the ones offered here are not bad at all. I like that I get a huge variety of food to choose from, the place is clean, and the prices are cheap. I tried - and thoroughly enjoyed: nasi lemak, beef noodles (kway teao), and the char kway teao here. And the drinks store serves lovely versions of local beverages.Show less

Author: MschilliPerth, Australia
Title: White curry mee
Review: You choose a table and then order at the stalls. Remember to look at you table number as you will need to tell the stall holder this. Your food is then cooked and they will bring it to your table and you pay. I had the white curry mee and asked for it with out the blood cubes. A large bowl was 5rm. It came with two sorts of noodles yellow and white and a spoon full of sambal for you to mix in.Show less

Author: jokl78
Title: Cheap eat
Review: Went there around 1.30pm on weekdays. Place is packed with people working nearby. Plenty of variety to choose from and price is cheap. Parking is easy.

Author: Jeremy Loh J
Title: Very good wan tan mee
Review: Wan tan mee tastes so good that you can find nowhere else that tastes like this. Try the spicy wan tan mee its real good.

Author: nanakokna
Title: Clean and comfortable food court!
Review: Ali nasi lemak is located here. The nasi lemak is superb, worth the queue. The food court itself offers plenty of choices from chinese, japanese, local penang street food and cool delicious drinks. They have parking area beside it.

Author: yxink
Title: Nasi Lemak
Review: I think most of the people visit here for the famous Nasi Lemak. There are few variety of nasi lemak suck as prawn, fried fish, chicken, anchovies & egg. I personally prefer fried fish and extra curry gravy.

Author: simonkI295EZ
Title: The Best NASI LEMAK at Beach Street
Review:
The BEST Nasi Lemak near Beach Street, George Town.
Simply get into Sri Weld Food Center, and you will surely find this stall.

Author: Michael_Teoh
Title: Yummy Nasi Lemak
Review: For me go to this food court I just go buy the Nasi Lemak. The nasi lemak here are very yummy and for spicy lover should have a try..sure you will like it.

Author: Joyman LPerth, Australia
Title: Only went for the nasi lemak
Review: Located in Georgetown, we only came for the nasi lemak. The shop stand is in front of the food court and although there was a line, the service was quite efficient and we were served in no time. The menu options (different nasi lemak variations of either with fish, squid, egg, combination, etc) and prices were on display on a banner and a board in front of the shop stand facing the road. There were plenty of seating inside under the big roof for a quick dine in or take away was also possible. The nasi lemak was delicious with the right amount of heat in the sambal and ratio to the coconut rice. Accompanied by crunchy anchovies and peanuts and a refreshing cucumber, it was good enough without the extra protein (fish, egg, squid). The extras does make it better! Definitely make a side visit to try if in Georgetown (within walking distance 10min from Pinang Peranakan Mansion)Show less

Author: Happygirl004
Title: Not recommend wan tan mee
Review: Wan tan mee hawker bad service, cleanliness is poor, wan tan mee not any special. Not recommend to try this at sri weld food court. Nasi lemak taste good and cheap. Should try this out.

Author: cprsjo
Title: Famous nasi lemak here
Review: If you're exploring Georgetown and walking towards the Fort by the seafront, make a stop at Sri Weld foodcourt and get a poate of yummy nasi lemak!

Author: 0401wsze
Title: Nasi lemak
Review: The nasi lemak here is very spicy which is suitable for people that love and able to take a high level of spiciness. Due to i could not take high level of spiciness, I requested less spicy which is perfect for me.

Author: kinmuntam
Title: Good for lunch
Review: Had very spicy nasi lemak which ticked all the boxes, fragrant and rich rice with spicy anchovy sambal gravy. Wife had pan mee which she deemed good but son's chicken chop rice was barely adequate.

Author: norlailis
Title: Nasi Lemak Hunting
Review: The best in town!  Highly recommended. If you like spicy, just request to add "sambal". It's for free!  For me...I can go up to 3 packs at once 🤗🤗🤗

Author: Martinyaw
Title: very good nasi lemak
Review: The nasi lemak were very fragrant and tasty. I would recommend the ikan bilis. However, the drawback is the price which is at RM1.80. If you dont mind paying 1.80 for a pack then this is a good ansi lemak spot for you.

Author: situwen
Title: Love the variety!
Review: We had Nasi Lemak, white curry mee, chow kua dao and tuk tuk mee. All pretty average... that said the bar for the best food is set very high. If I had this food court near my home I'd be there all of the time!

Author: kaseysf
Title: Hawker food court in Beach Street
Review: The hawker food court is located at just next to Alliance Bank and Ambank in Beach Street. My favourite stall is Pak Ali Nasi Lemak. Fresh and delicious anchovies in sambal gravy.

Author: RobertKoh936
Title: Great hawker center
Review: This hawker center have a lot of chooses of food such as  local food, Thai food, Taiwan food, Japanese food and western food. The food must try are mee sotong , Nasi lemak and three layer tea. The price are reasonable.

Author: MikeChu89Ipoh, Malaysia
Title: Good cheap food at strategic location
Review: This place is reachable by foot if you are coming from Fort Cornwalis or the ferry terminal. The food here is priced within the range of RM2 - RM5 and you will find a lot of local delicacies here.The people of the food court kept the place real clean as well which is always a plus point.Show less

Author: Kin_mun_dot_net
Title: Mee sotong
Review:
Another delicious cuisin, if u like sliced squids. Another must try malaysian food and make sure you grab one before sold out on daily basic.

-kinmun.net

Author: MsSoloTraveller
Title: Streetfood under cover.
Review: Super close to Royale Bintang hotel and a great variety of street food at super cheap prices compared to european or western eateries. Closes early so not really suited for dinner.

Author: jeff1955malaysiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: variety of food under one roof
Review: it is located close to fort conwallis. You will a variety of food to choose from. Chinese, indian and malay. the nasi lemak here is quite good and at times you need to wait for your turn. You just order your food and you have the tables in the centre with the food stalls lined up on both side. price is reasonable but the place is a bit stuffy.Show less

Author: Alan_Bligh
Title: Foodie heaven
Review: It's a food court will all kinds to choose from. The aroma of the Nasi Lemak will grab your attention the moment to arrive. Chinese food together with Indian and Malay will make go crazy trying to choose.

Author: GuliWherePenang, Pulau Pinang, Malaysia
Title: Beef noodles are ok
Review: Other than the super famous cheap but very spicy nasi lemak, the beef noodles are ok.Be careful if you park your car in the lot next door. When you step off the elevated floor and onto the tarmac, especially when there is a drain opening, I have personally seen a snake there...a pit viper to be exact, just waiting to strike . Let's just say you walk without looking, you WILL be bitten !Show less

Author: marianneongllGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Lots of choices
Review: Early morning you can get the tasty and famous nasi lemak. For lunch you will be spoilt for choice. Always ask if the waiting period is long just in case you are in a hurry. Avoid going during lunch hour (1-2pm) as it is very crowded and can hardly find a place to sit. If you like spicy food then you can try the "Mee Sotong".Show less

Author: PenariTopeng
Title: Wonderful stuff
Review: Lots of great stalls with a wide variety of foods. It is only open day times, however, & some stalls close by 2pm, so best to get there early.

Author: CKT379
Title: Nasi lemak Nasi lemak and Nasi lemak
Review: That is all that you get really. The best is that it is freshly made and Ina's production also. There is some standard Penang hawker dishes at the back but still Nasi lemak, Nasi lemak and Nasi lemak is the most popular here.

Author: maiden_v
Title: Sedap!
Review: The nasi lemak sold here I must say is mouth-wateringly good! But some may say they're too spicy, my s.o included. I love the spicyness. They open for breakfast and lunch. Lots of variety from other stalls as well.

Author: MieSon
Title: Best Nasi Lemak in town
Review:
This food court has the best nasi lemak in town. Wide varieties of nasi lemak, not only selling the typical egg and ikan bilis, but also others like chicken, cuttlefish, salted fish and fish.

Other than that, the Beef Noodle/Rice is fairly delicious too.

Author: PaperStoneScissorsPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Always busy
Review: This place is always busy. Food is good but I particularly like the stalls at the front selling bags of crispy chicken skin. Just love them. Now I know where all the skin goes when I buy chicken in the wet market and they take the skin off!Show less

Author: CeaserBoyBangkok, Thailand
Title: Nasi Lemak Banana Leaf
Review: Go for thier nasi lemak which is wrapped in a banana leaf and newspaper. Cheap and good at RM 1.50 per packet but be warned, its pretty spicy. The stall is located right at the entrance can get very busy during lunch.There are a few stalls inside this food court selling various local delights. One stall worth mentioning here is a stall at the end of the food court selling Beef Koay Teow Soup. Closed in the evening.Show less

Author: saronicZurich, Switzerland
Title: tasting Nyonya Penang specialities
Review: The Jetty Fooud Court, not far from the Chew Jetty and the Armenian Street, is a convenient and easy place to sample some local food. During my stay in George Town I went there twice for dinner and once for lunch. There are several stalls, all advertising their speciality. One can find ^Traditional Steam Rice and Noodles', 'Penang Tatsujin Ramen', 'Nasi Lemak/Boat Noodles', 'Hokkien Mee', 'Fried Oyster', 'Wantan Mee', 'Sizzling Claypot Noodles', 'Lor Bak/Chee Cheong Fun', 'Taiwan Ramen', 'Hainan Chicken Rice', 'Texas BBQ', 'Dumpling/Pau', 'Bak Kut Teh', also Japanese, Vietnamese, Western Style Cuisine.My interest was mainly in Nyonya Cuisine, which I first got to know in Melaka and which some consider one of the best cuisines in the world. It is also called 'Peranakan Cuisine' after the early Chinese settlers in the British controlled towns of Singapore, Melaka and Penang's George Town. They were usually men, who then married Malay women, thus the cuisine is a mixture of Chinese and Malay cooking. Especially the Chinese found here tropical ingredients, which they didn't know back home, but which they happily integrated into their way of preparing food.Thus I tried a 'Grouper with Nyonya Sauce', which I found rather bland though, almost no salt and hardly any spices. When I asked the friendly young woman in charge, what there was special in the 'Nyonya Sauce', she said: 'Not spicy, but with a lot of vegetables'. The next time I went for a 'Penang Special Nasi Lemak', which consisted of a heap of plain rice, surrounded by a chicken leg in a thick crust, roasted peanuts, tiny fried fish, a boiled egg, two slices of peeled cucumber and a spicy tomato sauce. It is best eaten, after having stirred all together.For lunch once I had a 'Penang Laksa', a spicy noodle soup of the Peranakan Cuisine, with the Penang variety also being called 'Asam Laksa', after the tamarind used in it, while the Laksa's further south are based on coconut milk (lemak). Usually one orders here at the stalls with the dish then being brought to the table, where one sits. Often a man from an extra stall passes by to ask for drinks. Regarding beer the most popular is 'Carlsberg', which has advertisements all over, and the cheaper 'Skol' from Brasil, which also belongs to the Carlsberg group, but is produced in Malaysia.Show less

Author: chrisjavassal
Title: A good place for street food in Penang
Review: Went and had meals several times and I like it. Food is good and cheap including Thai and Vietnamese as well Arabic ones. Drinks are at decent prices. Car park a bit challenging during rush hours. Definitely recommend it

Author: breky_nuno
Title: Great food and great price
Review:
Variety, price and quality. Expect it to be hot, as the food is also very hot!
You can choose from many dishes from differente cuisines around Asia.
tried it two times. And loved it in both of them.

Author: redpolka14Perth, Australia
Title: Value and Relaxation
Review: After a long walk in the hot sun, it was such a pleasure to relax at the Jetty Food Court and enjoy some delicious, great value food. We had Won Ton Mee, which was one of the food highlights of our trip. Dark, sweet/savoury gravy on perfectly cooked noodles with little crunches of pork crackling for texture and flavour. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. The centre is also perfectly placed to enjoy the cool breezes from the shoreline before heading inland to discover the many heritage sites of historic Georgetown.Show less

Author: leea115Sheffield, United Kingdom
Title: Delicious
Review: After a long walk around George Town feeling hungry and in need of a sit down before we had to get back on our ship we called into this large covered food court. We had 2 different chicken rice meals at 11 Malaysian ringgit each which is about £2.10, very cheap and delicious, we also had 2 large bottles of tiger beer a 19 Malaysian ringgit each about £3.60. It was Great to eat how the locals do in this authentic Malaysian friendly food hall with a vast choice of dishes. Show less

Author: Q6699London, United Kingdom
Title: Great selection of cheap food
Review: Great selection of cheap food.Really quick service for the amount of people.Very popular so not the cleanest of places as some tables are not cleaned that thoroughly quickly enough.Ordering beer is centralised at one outlet so can be haphazard depending on the availability of staff.Food very good and price dependent on type of food ordered.Live entertainment a bit hit and miss depending on your nationalityShow less

Author: TonyB_au
Title: Great place, lots to choose from
Review:
I went at lunchtime and it wasn't too packed. Lots of stalls to choose from, too many perhaps.

Service was quick and the food excellent.

I can recommend the Clay Pot chicken rice.

Author: MichaelE_DKKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Surprisingly good
Review: Visiting Penang with overseas family, and wanted to try street food. We were early, so the more popular hawker center at Gurney Drive was still closed. Instead we ended up at The Jetty Food Court, and were very impressed by the cleanliness. This can be a challenge at times at Malaysian hawker centers. The selection of food was very varied and the 5 different shops we tried were all good.Show less

Author: DnarayAberdeen, United Kingdom
Title: Great Selection
Review: We went twice in 5 days as there was so much choice. From Malay to chinese to vitnamese to BBQ. We found it clean, quick and efficient.Some stalls were more welcoming than others - shout out to BBQ staff and things took different times depending how busy places were.You can go to the bar to order/select your drinks if you prefer,Show less

Author: Graham PUnited Kingdom
Title: Delicious food market
Review: A wide range of cuisines to choose from in a good location near Chew jetty. Has TVs which were showing live sport when we were there. You pick a table, order from whichever stall you fancy and pay when they bring it over. We had Thai, Malay and Chinese - was yummy and very reasonable. The drinks are done centrally and they come to your table to take your order and you pay when they bring the drink. There is a 50 sens charge for the table per person if you don’t order a drink even if you eat. Show less

Author: Obrienl67Grovedale, Australia
Title: Go for the dumplings near Chew Jetty
Review: Best range of dumplings around. So delicious but be early as they sell out by lunchtime. While you are down that way, after 2pm, keep walking towards the bridge turn off until you reach a bustling stall selling banana fritters (the best ever) You will notice the nameless stall by the group of people. They sell a variety of fried sweet treats at local prices. Worth the walk. It is Jetty side. Show less

Author: Curtis B
Title: Great fun
Review: Something for everyone and at great prices.  I haven't been, but I hear it's quite lively at night, will have to give it a try.

Author: Saishidan
Title: Probably the best hawker market
Review: Probably the best hawker market in Penang. Clean with good variety of food. The prices are as good as anywhere.

Author: Virginia231975
Title: OK food, nothing special but Ok, a lot of choices (perfect that for)
Review: I discovered the place in 2019 and I only went one time because I don’t like the traffic jam to go there and besides with such a heat and no shadow on the road. Besides I went on a week end when there was the market.I recommend the roasted duck which is very good but in a small portion however. The passion fruit jucie is also good with a good portion but the claypot chicken rice had a kind of fishy aftertaste. It was average.There seems to be a lot of Thai options but to eat Thai fod, better be in Thailand. I didn’t try, also a few Western optionsIt is a busy place but not overcrowded which much space with plastic chairs and tables. It is quite noisy (with a bit loud background Chinese music), authentic but why going there to eat (see above) Mostly Chinese people go there. Shady but not necessarily cool as it’s under a big canopy and it remains relatively exposed.Cleanliness semed to be okThe food choices were so good, so many options. The food quantity was in summary ok.The service was quick and friendly service, however a bit pushy while you need the time to check all the different dishes they can offer. You order at the stall of your choice and sit down, then the stall workers come to find you once the food is ready and you pay then. Be ready to wave them over if they can’t spot you! The food of some customers took a while to get prepared;The value for money was ok, a bit cheaper than Red garden in a same kind of atmosphere but to go to red garden there is less traffic. I prefere to go that way. Would I go back? Maybe because the place has nothing wrongShow less

Author: Nikki BRotterdam, The Netherlands
Title: Lots of food!
Review: We went here twice during our stay in Georgetown as our hotel was really closeby. They have so many different types of foodstalls and everyone we tried was great. I can especially recommend the stall with falafel. The dish is created with so much love and was really good!Show less

Author: Sophie RLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Best food court! (Also known as Jetty foodcourt)
Review: This has to be one of the best food courts around. Having visited the amazing Sri Weld food court earlier in the day for lunch I found this baby. We visited for dinner and what a dinner it was! So many options to choose from you can have practically any dish on the island. Highly recommend a visit! Must order drink or pay 50cent which is fine. The drinks person kindly kept attending to pour my beer out into my glass which was just so kind. Also they start doing live music around 9pm which is great. A must for any visit to Penang!Show less

Author: SusanC4948Melbourne, Australia
Title: We came back three times - brunch, lunch and dinner
Review: This food court (now called the Jetty Food Court) is just across the road from Chew Jetty which is why we visited the first time. The delicious range of dim sum from a stall at the front is why we came back twice more. My daughter, in particular, loved it. Opening hours for the stall are morning or evening with a break in the afternoon so we missed the dim sum on the second visit (though we were happy with offerings from other stalls), necessitating yet a third visit at night.This was the first food hall / hawker centre we tried in George Town. The table area is cooled by ceiling fans and, while busy, we didn’t have any trouble getting a table though once we needed to share with others. Aside from the dim sum we had satay sticks, fish cakes and nasi goreng. There is a .50RM charge if you don’t order drinks.Show less

Author: dan2963eveGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Go for the Wan Tan Mee
Review: This food court serves most types of hawker food. The one that stands out for me is the dried Wan Tan Mee (Black Soya Sauce Egg Noodle). In one of the late Anthony Bourdain's episodes of Penang, he sampled this particular stall's noodle. There are limited parking lots at the back of this food court.Show less

Author: Michael1052Armidale, Australia
Title: Great place for a beer and good cheap food
Review: Firstly, I'm from Australia, so what I write here is probably only of interest to Western traveller tastes. There are some things I should explain before I describe the various stalls I liked best.Malaysian food is almost completely devoid of vegetables. They really don't know how to eat healthily: just walk around the tables, and you'll soon see that everyone eats meat, fish with rice or noodles, and the small rare drop of what could be a green or red vegetable (you can't be sure). You soon get sick of food without vegetables. So there are a few stalls that include a good amount of vegetables, but those are only very limited in range.Oil: much of the food in the court is oily, and keep in mind that this is ultra cheap food, so don't expect anything other than the cheapest palm oil. This means, restrict your deep-fried meals, and fried noodles or rice (except for the Thai stall).Fish: the sea around Penang is notoriously polluted, so be aware that seafood has a lot of heavy metal pollution. Doesn't mean as a visitor you can't enjoy some fish and prawns, but just keep in mind what your eating.Tofu: as far as I could tell, there was only one stall selling tofu meals (probably are more if you know what to look for), and that stall is called Yong Tau Foo. This food is supposed to be specially prepared tofu, which it isn't, but it is very nice nonetheless. It is a noodle soup with some greens (surprise!) and different kinds of tofu. Quite tasty if you are into noodle soup.In general Chinese food is bland - they use garlic and soy, but that's about it. It's all about variety of food rather than taste (unlike Indian). That means noodle soups can be boring - just cheap noodles in hot water, which the locals seem to enjoy. You can get a flavoursome laksa, but the one on offer at the food court is not very good.Stalls:Taiwan Ramen. I didn't try his ramen, as most fried noodles I saw on tables turned me off that kind of meal, and anyway, the Japanese stall didn't sell a raman dish, and they're the only ones I trust to do that properly. His fried sweet potato with plum is very good, as is his fried mushrooms.Itinerary Gallery. They make very nice boiled dumplings and their fried chicken with five spice is delicious - not too oily.Poh Piah: in stall by similar name - very good. A large spring roll.Sizzling Claypot Noodle. Their sizzling plates are quite pleasant, and the woman serving is equally pleasant.Chinese steamed dumplings etc at the front. Only open in mornings and lunch (except Friday nights). Quite good selection, if you don't mind solid chunks of meat.Vietnamese Spring Rolls (forget the stall name, but easy to see). These are quite good. They are cold and mainly salad vegetable as far as I could tell. Light and crispy. So that's one option for vegetables.Thai stall (last at the back). This is the place to get good food. I can recommend them - the Thais know how to prepare quality food, with vegetables.Japanese stall. Tried a few of their dishes, and they were good.Note: you have to buy drinks. Not to, can cause a hefty fine (not that anyone would bother fining you). Always ask for 'little ice' (anywhere in Penang) otherwise you get a glass full of ice. Tiger beer is a nice addition (a better quality prepared beer without additives).In all, hawker food is more fun that a culinary delight. In fact most of it in Penang is quite poor quality. As I recall it was much better decades ago. But you can still find some good cooks among them if you are willing to pay attention and have the patience to make many mistakes.Most important, the atmosphere in CF Hawker centre is great. Friendly and relaxed - watch a bit of curious TV while eating and sharing with friends. Best to order a number of dishes and share - that way you also share the good choices and avoid surprise disappointments.Show less

Author: JonofromcasCastleford, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent and cheap food
Review: Happened on this after walking to see Clan Jetties which were surprisingly disappointing and as the tide was out, the air around the jetties smelt of effluent and we wouldn’t have wanted to stay and eat in any places there. Perhaps that’s why we were disappointed. However, the food in this court was spot on. Cheap, cooked fresh and tasty. We tipped one stall 5 ringgits and she looked as if we’d made her day. You pay for the drinks separately as in other hawker centres, but for the price you pay, this place would be hard to beat. Show less

Author: Cheryl RMerthyr Tydfil, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic Street Food
Review: The Jetty Food Court is across the street from Chew Jetty and I can't recommend it enough to you to go and eat here. The different food hawkers are along the sides of the building with the tables and chsirs in the middle. We settled on a Thai meal and it was about £4 GBP for the two of us and excellent quality. Drinks are from a separate vendor on the site. Show less

Author: fat_miaoKota Bharu, Malaysia
Title: Its now called The Jetty Food Court
Review: Stop by here after the Clan jetty visit as they have better choice of meals, from dim sum till texas bbq. Taken some dimsum, especially love those Portuguese Egg tarts and Deep Fried Yam Balls, also were nice were the Thai Sausages and Pork Skewers aka Mu Ping ~ not pricey and nice. They do have a rule that all patrons must order drinks else they must charge table charge, but if you buy meals from the stalls, 5 favorite drinks will be offered at RM 1 each. Egg Noodles wanton cost RM 5, and you get to order a drinks at RM 1 ... why not, its cheaper then a Starbucks.Show less

Author: lucianal619Mount Pleasant, Australia
Title: Good Food At A Great Price
Review: We came across this food court while walking along Armenian Street to Clan Jetty. Its actually directly across from the jetties. I was apprehensive at first about eating at any food court but we found this place to be very clean so we tried the kway teow which was delicious. Better than any I've ever had back home. So good that we went back a couple of days later. Prices are very cheap, kway teow was only $2.00 aud.Show less

Author: CanmoreFunkyDudeCanmore, Canada
Title: Clean and well organized. Not Too Pricy.
Review: This modern, clean hawker centre is located on Armenian Street at the Weld quay. You can find just about every food style you might be looking for, including a dim sum cafeteria, western style BBQ, Halal, dessert choices, and of course plenty of stalls serving Penang and Hainanese cuisine. There is a central stage, so there is probably live entertainment nightly, although I went early enough to be excused from that! You choose a table, find some way to hold it (order drinks and leave them there while you visit the food stalls works pretty well), order your meals at any stall you want, they will bring it to your table when its ready. I ordered from the Hai Tian Seafood stall, located centrally on the Armenian side. They had an attractive display of fresh seafood on ice, just point, and tell them how you want it cooked. They also have a large illustrated menu to help out. I chose the Baby Octopus, Gung Bao style with steamed rice - stirfried with loads of dry chilies, onions, a few greens and garlic, quite spicy, and a little on the sweet side. It was really good, I didn’t need to visit any of the other stalls once I had finished it. MYR 16, including tax and tip. Show less

Author: TheGluteDarwin, Australia
Title: Loved this place.
Review: I normally avoid places like this because I’m concerned about food safety. Made a decision on my latest cruise to get over it and eat at local places like this. Penang was our first port and we ended up here after walking the streets all day and had just finished walking around Chew Jetty. I ended up eating from three different places because the food is cheap. Around $3 AUD a meal and every dish was fantastic. I had Char Siew & Rice, Crispy Pork Chop and Rice and Char Siew Bao.Show less

Author: friskycelery
Title: Good Food Court
Review:
There are a lot of good choices here at a very reasonable price, you can take your pick.I had the roast pork with rice, and it was outstanding.

This is right across the street from the Chew Jetty, and it can get crowded at lunch.

Author: Javaneselady90Lucerne, Switzerland
Title: Anything you want
Review: The location of this food court is near to the street with mural. Here you can almost find any kind of food that you should try when you visit Penang. From Dimsum, Thai food to Char Kuew Teow with very affordable prices. Different kind of beverages are also offered. Show less

Author: larisat444Moscow, Russia
Title: Quick average food, free fan space
Review: Quick food, free space, fan zone, so you can relax a bit from the heat outside. We ordered rice with duck, which was too fat and salty, it could be of higher price but better quality Squid spicy was good But overall I would not say that the food here is delicious, just average Show less

Author: momo402London, United Kingdom
Title: Authentic experience of hawker stall food
Review: Delicious pad Thai, som tam (papaya salad), and chickenThai green curry. You order at the stall of your choosing and sit down, then the stall workers come find you once the food is ready and you pay then. Be ready to wave them over if they can’t spot you! Our food took a while to get prepared; it all felt freshly made. Be warned that there is a “drink tax” to pay if you sit down, to the drinks stall people, payable in cash immediately. Shady but not necessarily cool as it’s under a big canopy/awning and remains relatively exposed.Show less

Author: raymondw-72
Title: Good food, lots of choice
Review: Different food stands with central seatings. Good quality. During lunch fewer choices than for dinner.

Author: johnmL3393EPGeelong, Australia
Title: an essential way to explore local cuiisne!
Review: CF was our first experience of hawker food, and it was an easy and amazing way to explore Malaysian food culture in Penang. This is where the locals eat and the food is rich in variety and flavour. It is so fresh - cooked in front of you and delivered to you plastic chair and table in an incredibly efficient way. And did I mention CHEAP!!!Show less

Author: ApocalypseYana
Title: Beers, snacks and karaoke!
Review: I enjoyed the atmosphere at CF because it was lively and open late. I spent a few nights and afternoons having snacks and drinking beers here. I really liked the deep fried enoki mushrooms and tofu nuggets!

Author: CraftBeerDeanDoncaster, United Kingdom
Title: Good place to eat. Plenty of food choice
Review: Good place to eat. Plenty of food choice. When you sit down someone will come up to you and offer to sell you a drink. I chose a large Guiness foreign extrat stout which was 20 Rm. You can then wander around and see what food takes your fancy. There are plenty of pictures and clear prices. I paid 6 Rm for sizzling chicken with rice and an egg. The tables have no number so either describe wehere you are sitting or sit close to the stall you want to eat from. They have ceiling fans. No wifi. Red Garden is a better food court as th e beer is a bit cheaper and they have ice bucketsShow less

Author: John H
Title: a wonderful place to eat.
Review: again i have been to the cf hawker centre quite a few time, there are so many stall to choose from you can have a wonderful time there. the food is good and not to expensive and you can mix them if you like. i am lucky i have friends who take me there when ever i visit penang. so go and have a look for your self.Show less

Author: 419chrisqLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Great place to eat
Review: This is a great food market /hawker centre. The food we had (from a variety of stalls was fantastic. The only thing worth mentioning is how it works. First you decide where you will sit then you order the food at the stall and tell the cook which table you are sitting at -they will then bring the food to your table - you pay when the food arrives with cash. The average price per dish was about 5MR. At the drink counter you order, pay and collect at the same time. 100% worth a visit. Show less

Author: wendy sKuah, Malaysia
Title: Great food and entertainment
Review: We went to this hawker centre twice during our week in penang. The food was great with a good variety. We enjoyed thai som tam (green paw paw salad), frog with chili and ginger, crispy frog, satays, sotong (squid), chicken rice, popiah, fresh juices among other things. My particular favourites were: *satays - best satay sauce we had during or entire trip with a lovely bite to it*som tam - fresh, zesty and spicy* frog with chili - succulent and delicate, the sauce was to die forThere was nightly music entertainment which was fun. Very popular with locals who were friendly and loved to chat and laugh with us. This was great fun. On our second night or group even received a gift from one of the drinks sellers which was very special. All around a great experience. Show less

Author: JoostG3Amsterdam, The Netherlands
Title: Great value for money
Review: Ate here few times during our stay in Penang. Food - excellent, freshly prepared food. We tried as many dishes as we could (hot pots, curries, dumplings, sateh etc.) Service - good, you order, point at your table and pay as soon as it is delivered. For some reason one of the stalls left for the day before fulfilling our order; be clear in what you wantPrice - great, mains are anything between 5 - 15 MYR. Fresh juices are available for 2.80 MYRGreat way to sample many dishes from the amazing kitchen of this island, and cheap ti boot. Show less

Author: ellyrieTokyo, Japan
Title: Great food and atmosphere
Review: Visited here in the late afternoon which was convenient since most of these places only open up at night. The market seems to be one entity with lots of different stalls operating where you can grab bits and bobs from. I recommend just choosing 2-3 dishes from different places and eating at once. Food - Excellent. As a first time traveller to Malaysia I just chose dishes at random and was not dissappointed! I recommend the fried chicken though, it was amazing. Annoyingly, there is a lack of tissues or napkins in the food court and you have to work hard to find some. A lot of the food is finger food so this was frustrating at times.Service - Excellent. The servers often bring the food to your table and are very polite and friendly.Price - On average dishes cost about 5 ringgit which is really cheap. Be sure to take advantage and try lots of things!Although I hadn't visited anywhere else in Penang, I had an excellent experience here and I highly recommend it. The only reason why it got 4 out of 5 stars is because the lack of napkins meant the meal was messier then it needed to be. Also if you are foreign then people will push in front of you at the stalls and the servers won't stop them or acknowledge you were there first.Show less

Author: gloryredstar
Title: Food for Tourist
Review: I personally found the food served here to be of inferior quality compared to other hawker centres in Penang.

Author: Cat333M
Title: Amazing food! I had the Thai!
Review:
Food was amazing, the whole Hawker was really clean and well maintained. I had the Thai green curry, rice and egg from the Thai stool at the back! It was delicious and only 7ringgett. 

Would highly recommend. So much to choose from!

Author: meecht
Title: Awesome wan tan mee
Review: Tried the dry wan tan mee for breakfast. The noodles are soft and springy, the fried wan tan are crunchy and delicious.

Author: Lauren RHamilton, United Kingdom
Title: Great Hawker Center
Review: Was a lively and fun Hawker center to eat and drink in. Lots of stalls with many different dishes from all over to try. There are also people going around serving drinks, we got a bucket of beer which was good value for money. They have bands playing music and was a great place to sit at night and soak in the atmosphere.Show less

Author: mousevandemole
Title: Great food with entertainment
Review: We found this place by chance and LOVED it! The food was cheap and good, the beer cold and the singers were super entertaining!

Author: terimeganDubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: Dinner experience
Review: My friends and I found this place amazing! It's truly what we were looking for on our holiday. Good street food and friendly food venders. There is also alcohol available if you wish. There is such a variety of food and it is quite cheap. You can spend a few hours there trying all the yummy food! There is also a few musicians that play/sing for a nice entertainment factor. Show less

Author: sebhoffTrier, Germany
Title: Typical hawker centre with great choice of different kinds of food
Review: Recently had early dinner here before the place got too packed - and we left very happy. There is plenty to choose from - some reasonably cheap (4.80RM for a medium-sized WonTon soup) and also some more pricey options. Plus your usual selection of fresh juices and beers. There is much less fresh fish than at Red Garden Food Paradise & Night Market, though.On the whole, this is a decent option - nothing to write home about, but perfectly fine hawker food.Show less

Author: AnnabelD999London, United Kingdom
Title: Char Koey Teow and so much more...
Review: We stumbled across this Hawker Centre when we were ambling around Armenian Street and I am so glad we did. We had heard that Char Koey Teow was not to be missed and found a stall here amongst all the others where he was making it fresh for each person. But there was so. I h food to be tasted here you could just take your pick...The Char Koey Teow was delicious and although I wish we had ordered it with prawns - we gobbled it down. 5 Ringgit! Bargain. Whilst we were there we noticed that it was recommended by the Food Ranger on YouTube and there was a film he had made whilst he was eating here!Show less

Author: andrewee88
Title: Suitable for all ages
Review: Surprised with the event of young band singing from 青蛙王子. Great sing and Great job. Food was okay...

Author: Jozzee
Title: Great food
Review: We visited the CF Hawker centre twice while in George Town. Great cheap local food. Best hawker centre we found in George Town. Open for lunch and dinner.

Author: koolcatPenang
Title: Average food court
Review: Problem is parking and narrow street. This area is picking up as alot more fusion food can be found here. At CF, majorities are local food that can be found anywhere in penang.

Author: WS28Penang_Malaysiq
Title: Good food but Pricey!
Review: This is a good place for local hawker fare but the prices are wayyyy tooo steep ! Probably because it is very near to Armenian Street where there are lots of tourists .Drinks costs a bomb too !

Author: RichardLWH
Title: Many choices, many tastes and reasonable prices
Review: We dined in this place twice as it was near to our hotel and other attractions. There were many choices and the prices were reasonable. The food was above average and the main attraction was that it is near quite a few tourist attractions (Chew Jetty and murals).Show less

Author: Fangqi_ASingapore, Singapore
Title: Tasty Kway Teow Thng
Review: Went for lunch and was surprised the Kway Teow Thng I tried was quite delicious. There is a variety of local delicacies and the environment appears clean and well maintained. We are encouraged to return to try other dishes the next time we are there again.Show less

Author: 801xinyuez
Title: Yummy and cheap food! Must try-curry mee!
