I enjoyed them with a dollop of sambal belacan. The grouper was another visually stunning dish. The fish flesh was deboned, battered and fried till golden. The photo would illustrate better that what I can describe. The arrangement with shitake mushrooms and sio pai chye was indeed a work of art. Long Life Noodles with prawns and quail eggs had strong wok hei (breathe of the work) aroma. To conclude the scrumptious meal, poached pears with snow fungus and nam pak hup was served chill. A perfect ending to such a delightful feast. Dining under the stars next to the pool made the evening even more special with excellent service to boot. A big thank you to Mr Poh Seow for taking such good care of us. You're a star.Show less

Author: ACDC29Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Terrible Chicken Chop
Review: The design, decor and ambiance of the place was very nice. The feel was nostalgic, bringing to mind colonial style hainanese cafes of yesteryear.Unfortunately the chicken chop came with a horrible clear starchy sauce! My dining companion's mee mamak looked alright and the fish and chips was so-so but for a place popular for the Hainanese Chicken Chop this was a let down in the biggest proportions!Show less

Author: Ezhamk
Title: try all
Review:
the signature dish is the Hainanese chicken rice...a must try dish.

for the Muslims ...don't worry...this is a halal cafe but they do serve liqueur.

Author: Callum M
Title: Rude to put it simply
Review: Went to Yeng Keng because of the good reviews but didn't get an opportunity to eat their food. Rocked up and we were told it was too busy inside to sit despite more then half the room being empty and with very few reserved tables. They made a table for us outside with another family also being set up. 5 minutes later they conveniently let the family in and left us outside with no communication of the situation. Just really rude and felt extremely unwelcome, I never like to negatively attack people or a place but they were pretty shocking. So we get up and walked out and went to far better places! Show less

Author: EvaP1270
Title: Sit down 9 course dinner
Review: My BFF had her birthday there and the dinner was excellent from the spring roll, yam duck, Shepard pie, bomb Alaska (dessert), inchee kabin...every dish was just delicious.

Author: safwanlim
Title: Yum! Yummy! Mouthwatering dishes tserved from kitchen... must try...indian fried mee..spring rollls....
Review: Along the streets of chulia street in penang ...pay a visit to savour dishes or  book a room one could not forget ...a walking distances to  cultural... heritage...places

Author: JaturungkabartSingapore
Title: Good comfort food!
Review: Stayed at the hotel itself. The buffet breakfast is above average at best. However, the a la carte menu is much better, especially for the local food. We had tea at the cafe ordering the giant spring rolls, hainanese pork chop and fried mee mamak. They were delicious. The table next to us had the bombe alaska which is a sight to see always.Show less

Author: melissamun
Title: Best Hainanese Food
Review: Tried special menu of the day "hokkien mee" , the soup is rich and sweet. The big prawn hokkien mee cost us RM20 but the portion can be served for 2-3pax.

Author: tango122008
Title: Yummy food
Review: Delicious food, whole family over-ate, got a 10% discount due to us being guest at the hotel. Inchi kabin a must for order, as well as the braised duck with yam!!!!

Author: nzbear
Title: Average kind of palce
Review: Doesn't seem quite to know what kind of café it is. An eclectic mix on offer. Decent food and service, but more authentic food available in the area.

Author: jessstefanPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: "Could have been better"
Review: Love the quaint little Peranakan themed hotel - pretty and cozy..yes, also love the airconditioning in the restaurant on a hot hot humid day..Food- the portions were generous and quite delicious..the iced lychee and mint was not my favourite , the local coffee was not too bad. We had the chicken pie and fried rice - the pie was quite delicious and the rice was yummy. I am hainanese so I know what good hainanese food should taste like..i think..:)however, the services need to be improved - we were the only couple eating there and there were 3 foreign waiters in the restaurant - first they should just serve water without being asked, secondly the waiter should have announced the month special when taking our order and thirdly its quite hilarious to see the waiter drinking the leftover of my order of lychee and mint at the counter ..when serving water and food they should use a tray to avoid fingers and thumbs straying into the food..prices were a bit on the steep side.Show less

Author: Nicole L
Title: Delicious Hainanese Chicken Chop
Review: Their Hainanese Chicken Chop was delicious. The chicken was soft and succulent and the fried batter was crispy. The Iced Lychee and Lime drink was yummy. The decor was old style Hainanese cafe. The waiter was friendly. Air-cond was very cold. Overall I enjoyed my meal at this restaurant.Show less

Author: 2RightyPerth, Australia
Title: Great food and service
Review: Very welcome air con on a 32 degree day. Beers cold so good start. Chicken chop with Hannanese sauce excellent, chicken moist and not dried out like else where. Horfun probably better than anywhere in Penang, plenty of sauce. Sizzling steak set of the fire alarm, so obviously very good, and served just as I ordered it. Visited this place three times over the 2 weeks and never disappointed. Very clean too.Show less

Author: Isabelle LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Fabulous beef hor fun (and setting)
Review: I've had char kway teow for 4.50 MR on Chulia Street, but sometimes it's nice to pamper yourself a bit. I've had the best beef hor fun in my life at Yeng Keng Cafe, which was recommended by a local friend. Cannot compare to street food. Of course, with a fresh orange juice, it costs me 31 MR, but given the setting (posh 30's look), I'd happily return. Excellent service, too.Show less

Author: MStJB
Title: They delivered
Review: Just popped in for a quick dinner. A noodle dish and a club sandwich washed down with an apple and orange juice drink. All good, reasonable service and price. End.

Author: 495marcusk
Title: Good Chinese Food
Review: Good Chinese food for family and business. Good service and good Chinese Spring roll and fried flat noodle.

Author: llsee
Title: Food and service were excellent
Review: Penang is a food city. With an abundance of excellent hawker stalls, and plenty of great restaurants, we only ate at this our hotel restaurant one evening, because it was raining hard. We were pleasantly surprised by the food. Very good, and service was excellent.

Author: David T
Title: Cool Retreat
Review: We enjoyed lunch here a couple of times and can recommend the Mee Mamak. The dining room is interesting and a cool refuge during a hot day. Hotel guests and those from the Nam Keng hotel (same owner) get a discount.

Author: rainerp698
Title: Great place for Hakka food
Review: They do a mean Inche Kabin. It was a short walk from Campbell House. The restaurant is quite intimate and the menu has a medium range of dishes.

Author: TravelCatY
Title: Yummy
Review: good service and good food. must try their hainanese chicken chop. chicken rice (for min 5pax) and chicken pie also very delicious but need to book 1day in advance.

Author: Beejay1948South Ayrshire, United Kingdom
Title: Great place to eat in the rain.
Review: Ate at cafe on two nights and enjoyed both meals. Good food and friendly service. We had intended going out on our first night but the heavens opened and rain was bouncing of the courtyard so we used the cafe. The quality of street food in Penang is stunning so that we used the hotel cafe again is testemont to its appeal.Show less

Author: ThomasDahlDusseldorf, Germany
Title: Nicht aircondioned, Good ok
Review: The style and space is great as is the air-conditioning. The food is basically ok but not brilliant. I would say above average. The staff is not massively attentive. Main course arrived before starter.. That sort of thing. Coffee is not great. Taste a little like instant coffee. Still a nice place to hang out for a while. I will be back. Show less

Author: ylfunSingapore, Singapore
Title: To-die-for Chicken Pie!
Review: The Chicken Macaroni Pie is to die for! The chicken stew was very flavourful and paired with the bread-like topping was a match made-in-heaven! The service was quite fast and attentive, and one of the waiters was very friendly and even gave us recommendations of what to order. I highly recommend going Yeng Keng Cafe for the lovely ambience and the uber delicious Chicken Macaroni Pie! The rest of the food is OK, but cannot be compared to the chicken pie.Show less

Author: CaCarolin
Title: Good food
Review: We're staying at this hotel and didn't feel like walking out on our first night. Glad we went in. Food was good!

Author: Baronclog
Title: Always very good
Review: I have eaten here a lot while staying at the  Yeng Keng hotel, every time I go they never disappoint. Hainanese tastes are so well catered for and the flavours are bright and authentic.

Author: Tammy7767
Title: Yummy Hainnaese fare
Review: We had the chicken pie which needs to be preordered. Do try the hanianese  food like the chicken chop, Assam gulai fish and spring rolls.

Author: Martin DLondon
Title: Yeng Keng Cafe Bar
Review: Four of us went for dinner. The food was best forgotten but wasn't forgettable enough. Hainan spring rolls ok. Inchi Kabin and Curry Kapitan truly lousy, rock hard lumps of deep fried chicken. Neither were recognisable as Inchi Kabin or Curry Kapitan. The noodles were tasteless and watery. The service was as good as could be done by untrained people without the appropriate skills in the restaurant and kitchen. Food and drinks arrived in a haphazard way so that 4 people had to share one dish while waiting for the next. I have never waited so long for white rice which arrived last of all after we reminded them a few times and the food it was meant to accompany had gone cold.Show less

Author: jeff1955malaysiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: hotel cum cafe
Review: it is located along chulia st and has an arch for its entrance. In the afternoon the outside can be a hot and humid. they have umbralla but it wont help. they have nice fried spring rolls. not too oily. they have both local and western food. service is kind of slow. Staff not attentive.Show less

Author: prudencelohKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Retro Cafe
Review: A respite from the sun whenever you are outdoors in the old part of Penang.Decorated like a 1930s cafe restaurant, the food is authentic.Love the fact that Executive Chef Tan comes out from table to table at times to ask about our opinions about the food we order.That's cooking with passion!Show less

Author: Ivyteh84
Title: Poor Service! Overrated hainanese food
Review: We ordered Hainanese chicken chop based on good review from blog. It was disappointing! Poor service, food was not good! Not worth to try with such price...

Author: ratabreakSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pleasant cafe
Review: Quaint Hainanese cafe, a good escape from the afternoon heat! Tried the Char Hor Fun, Hainan Mee, Hainanese style, Spaghetti Aglio-olio, Homemade Cream of Mushroom Soup and Banana Split. Service was a little slow considering that only another table was occupied. All the food was nicely done except for the soup which was a little watery and too garlicky. Friendly staff, pleasant and quiet cafe to dine-in.Show less

Author: TattH
Title: Hainan food
Review: When you go in to this shop. You will found out that the waiter mostly are foreigner and it is not hainanese shop. Try out the chicken which is good and it kill my doubt. Lastly you must try the spring roll.

Author: IsselerhofSingapore, Singapore
Title: A quick bite on the go
Review: Me and a friend went for a quick bite on the go to this place:Truly average atmosphere and foodService rather slow but friendlyI had the club sandwich and my friend the chicken salad, both truly averageI would think there are many better options in the area, so I cannot really recommend to actively seek out this placeIt deserves an average recommendation.Show less

Author: Angeline CAustralia
Title: Disappointing Hainanese food
Review: Good ambience reflecting traditional Hainanese settings. However, the dishes we ordered were disappointing. Inche Kabin chicken was over fried & tough, kerabu mango too sour, sweet & sour fish had more onions & capsicums than fish, stir fried vegetables were average. Prices were above average.Table service was inattentive - only 4 of us were served water whilst 2 others had to repeated request before they were served to wards the end of the meal.Show less

Author: mlien
Title: Great food and great atmosphere
Review: My heading says it all. It's cosy, quaint and has great food and great service. They have wifi in the restaurant. You might want to boom as people were being turned away as it was full.

Author: Pin C
Title: Worth the price and walk
Review: A little mre expensive than the other stalls, and a little out of the way, but worth the trek. Good stuff.

Author: SumanaBananaChiang Mai, Thailand
Title: Chic & Lovely Experience
Review: You must call to reserve the chicken pie around 4 hours before.They prepare everything for us more than a pie. We got the good seat with very nice service and our chicken pie arrived in 5 min after.I don'l like the chicken skin in chicken pie but you should try this experience.it's amazingShow less

Author: Chris Y
Title: Good cafe and ambience
Review: Good food. Limited range but they ARE good at what they do. The 'Ar-Or' soup was really good. The Hainanese chicken chop was good too! Overall, went back there three times in two days when we wanted air con dining along Chulia Street.

Author: huanyinchanMalaysia
Title: Simply terrific
Review: Yeng Keng Cafe is no doubt one of my favorite restaurant whenever I am looking for authentic hainanese cuisine in Georgetown. The restaurant is relatively small in size with very limited seating capacity, thus I would highly recommend reserving for your table as well as some of the famous pre-order item like chicken rice (24 hours in advance) and pie (3 hours in advance). I particularly love their Hainanese style chicken chop and Hor Fun paired with a glass of passion fruit juice. There is one small car park at the back of Yeng Keng Hotel- complimentary for the café guest. This is always a great option not only for a authentic Hainanese lunch but also a great place for a cup of coffee in late afternoon.Show less

Author: PaperStoneScissorsPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Lovely setting
Review: Ate here recently and enjoyed the decor. We ordered 3 small portions between us and were so glad we had, Small they were not - just so glad we didn't order the larger ones! We tried the Mango salad, Kapitan Chicken and Ginger Beef and all were extremely flavourful. Service was good and attentive but not over the top. Highly recommend this place. We were there on a weekday and were surprised that when we left at 8:30 there was only one free table. May be an idea to book if you want to guarantee eating there.Show less

Author: sinny7
Title: Great atmosphere, food and service
Review: This restaurant has a great surrounding and nice decor. The food was excellent and so was the service. Can't fault this place. We look forward to going back soon.

Author: Yang2011Penang, Malaysia
Title: Gigantic Chicken Pie
Review: There were 20 of us sharing among the well famous chicken pie and hainanese chicken rice. Both dishes were slurping good! Despite the size of the chicken pie, it was moisture on the inside and crispy on the outside. The chicken rice, I love the ginger aroma from the rice that I could just eat it by itself.We also order 'jiu hoo char'; though a bit saltish, it surely went well with the lettuce. Oh, lastly, we order The Alaska bomb. Another gigantic dish, a warm dessert filled with mix fruit cocktails and covered with egg white. Gotta eat it warm to enjoy the 'kick'!Show less

Author: 106mtmt
Title: Good food and nice ambience
Review: Had dinner there and ordered salad, fish and chip, and sandwiches. The salad and fish and chip were good and tasty, and they were generous with the vegetables and sides. The little one enjoyed the sandwiches and you can have a choice of two fillings, to the little one's delight. Service crew was very helpful and pleasant. Overall a nice dining experience.Show less

Author: leoki77Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Poor services
Review: I went with my colleque for dinner, we are enjoying the food while dissappointed the staff was fighting and arguing in front of customers ,,, it's a bad manner services. We are planning once a having birthday party for my daughter,, then i don't thing so,it's a not a right place to celebrate the party and i don't thing so we will coming to this place anymore,,and i won't recomended to go the place anymore,,its a very shamefull for me.Show less

Author: Hobbitsbaggins
Title: Good place to treat the elders
Review: We love the menu which specialised in Chinese Nanyang Cuisine, especially the Hainan and Baba & Nyonya cuisine. The food, the furniture, and the atmosphere will surely bring a lot of good memories and strike great conversation as we enjoy the food.

Author: Christopher NPenang, Pulau Pinang, Malaysia
Title: Delicious and simple with feel-like-home ambient
Review: This is one of the need-to visit cafe in Penang. The food is simple and delicious. If you're bored with the usual Penang delicacies, please come to this cafe to try out the original Hainanese food.The cafe is well decorated and is situated in a heritage house.Those who plan for a visit to Penang, please stop by here.My visit to this cafe will not be the last.Show less

Author: PaklincLMexico City, Mexico
Title: Authentic Malaysian Style Breakfast
Review: My wife and I had breakfast at this cozy little cafe one morning. We stayed at the Yeng Keng Hotel as well. Both the service in the hotel and cafe were unbelievably amazing. The food in the cafe was delicious. I grew up in Malaysia as a kid and the breakfast food was exactly the same as I use to have as a child. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to everyone who wants try real, authentic, and typical Malaysian food.Show less

Author: john1604Sydney, Australia
Title: this cafe will make your trip
Review: a real special cafe and what service.the high quality of the food is something to talk about.the flavours stay with you.the spring roll has come to a very high level.the service is excellent staff are very polite and know their menu.the bombe laska is out of this world.you must book to get a table you can also bring your own wine a small corkage fee is charged,.well woth the effort to go there.loved it.Show less

Author: Paul113
Title: Strange order
Review: Decent selection of Malaysian/Chinese food in air conditioned comfort. We ordered spring rolls as a group starter and they came at the end of the meal...which caused some amusement. Cost was about £40 for 3 adults including drinks

Author: gun47
Title: Heritage dining , Hainan style
Review: They have good beef char hor fun, go there regularly for it. Their chun piah is also best in town. You may also like the Hainan style chicken chop and pie. I will also like to try their chicken rice one day, but will need advance order.Show less

Author: Vance_FionaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great Hainanese Lunch
Review: Reservation for Yeng Keng’s specialty (The Macaroni or the Chicken Pie – Serves 4 to 6 person each) would be required as we understand that the restaurant need at least 4 hours of preparation time. So what’s the differences between the Macaroni Pie and the Chicken pie? The differences lies in the crust, if you prefer a flakier crust, order the Chicken Pie as it’s topped with puff pastry instead of soft egg pastry. Beneath the brown crispy pastry was smooth and creamy mixture of chicken, vegetable and other ingredients that was absolutely delicious. When our Hainanese Chicken Pie was presented to our table, the customers (from the other table) wanted to order the same but they returned disappointed since they didn’t make any prior reservation. So do call and make a reservation before your visit. The Bomb Alaska was as much a treat for the eyes as it was for the sweet tooth. Best served for at least 4 persons, any number less than that you would find yourself having problem finishing it. The exterior is covered by beaten egg whites which was spectacular when the dessert was flambeed using rum. Underneath the egg whites were Neapolitan ice-cream, fruits and sponge cake. Absolutely superb and you should really try this rare dessert when visiting Penang! Check out the YouTube video on The Bomb Alaska @ http://youtu.be/XRTCijONmTkFor more details, check out http://hamhamfarm.com/travel/main.html#Malaysia_PenangShow less

Author: AnfieldReds
Title: Great Food, Great Ambience
Review: The food here is authentic and will serve a wide variety of tastes. You can't go wrong with the local or western delights. Their specialty is Hainanese cuisine.

Author: MinkyMSydney
Title: Air con, big serves, nice food
Review: Good place for lunch as it has white tablecloths and booth style lounge seating in a pleasant, high ceilinged air-conditioned room. Entrance is through the hotel garden next door. Had lunch twice- the onion soup is very good, as is the garden salad. The potato salad and fried Hainanese chicken are good, the lamb shank OK, a little bland - served with spaghetti, oddly enough. The wine and beer are drinkable and not too expensive. However, the breakfast is quite average - we had the light breakfast of scrambled eggs, toast, 2 small cocktail sausage things, turkey ham, tea (ok), coffee (not great) - the eggs were good but the whole thing not that awesome. Yum Cha dumpling from a little local style joint is a better breakfast bet. The Hainan cuisine other people were eating looked and smelled very good (we were just not in the mood for that) - I'd try that next time for lunch (I think runs from 12 noon to 3pm)Show less

Author: nikki32892
Title: good eats
Review: belacan chicken and italian spaghetti very yummy... got food for kids infront of Hompton hotel.... we love it..

Author: Tony B
Title: Excellent local food court
Review: Great for economical local food with cheap beer. There is a wide range of Malaysian, Arabic and Western food. The clay pot dishes were particularly good as was the braised duck with rice.

Author: Kelvin K
Title: Excellent value
Review: Great place with about 20 food stalls covering western and asian, not much fish or desserts but great prices. Majority under cover. Bus stop for 101 bus very close. Opens from 5 to 12 midnight

Author: snowy1_66Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Penang Street food
Review: If you are travelling down to Penang, obviously there many places to visit. Aside to the attractions, Penang is also known for its food especially their street food. There are some places that I would like to recommend for you to explore. First stop at Bridge street prawn noodle shop where you will find a good prawn noodle. Next to the shop, there is a parking area, so finding a parking is not an issue. The business is so good that the stall is closed by noon. So, be early to try out their food. 2nd stop is at Jalan Trang where a row of hawkers stall sells their food. You can try their char keow Teow and other food too. Next stop is the Viva local food court at Tanjong Bungah. There are many stalls there and the food here is really tasty. You will find varieties of street food here. Totally recommend this place foe you try if you are visiting Tanjong Bungah. Show less

Author: Mankin7913
Title: Nice and inexpensive!!!
Review: This is a very nice food court and it is located just opposite to the Sentral hotel where we stayed for 2 days.Open at 5pm and there are many varieties of Penang street food available here and I think that the prices are cheaper than if you have them at the Gurney drive hawker centre. Show less

Author: Shainacanadian
Title: Taiba Shawerma was absolutely delicious
Review: We stayed at the Jazz Suites and took a 13 minute walk to Viva Local Food Haven. We found such a gem. Taiba Shawerma was incredible and the three staff were so friendly. We enjoyed shawarma wraps that was paired with a fresh coleslaw, and the flavourful rice with a side of the garlic sauce. I loved every bite. The chicken was fresh off the rotisserie and was so warm, seasoned with a comforting cinnamon spice and perfectly juicy. Looking forward to going back for another round of gooood food here.Show less

Author: fookmainPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Not worth the visit
Review: Went there with friends who visited me from Melbourne. Going there was a mistake (as a local). Food was mediocre ( hokkien mee was bad, fried chicken was average) and worst of all the drinks ( ambra with sour plum) WAS OVERPRICED. I will not go back again. Show less

Author: Jan Willem tNijmegen, The Netherlands
Title: This is probably the best foodcourt of Georgetown
Review: Many special local delicious dishes are served here. We choose the frog rice and the claypot chicken rice, both delicious prepared, top! As dessert we ordered the thin pancakes with peanut crumbs and banana, delicious again! Also the kopi and ice tea were very good. A real pleasure to dinner here, the service is cheerfull, honest and efficient. A pleasure to be here.Show less

Author: RiekoPoppyNijmegen, The Netherlands
Title: Nice place for Penang Local Food, lots of choices and good service
Review: I am a Malaysian Chinese (from Kedah State) married with a Dutch husband. Back to Malaysia to visit my family and we came to Penang for a few days short holidays. My husband and I both enjoy the Penang local food very much and we often visit the hawker center or local coffee shop (kopi tiam) to have our breakfast, lunch and dinner.This time we stayed in Mecure Penang Beach for 4 nights and we read on Tripadvidor that this hawker center is good, since it is just walking distance from the hotel, we decided to visit for our 4 dinners (4 nights stay). Oh yes, this place only open in the late afternoon to late evening (5pm-11:30pm).The Char Koay Teow (Fried Rice Noodles), the Clay Pot Chicken & Chinese Sausage Rice, the Duck Rice & Porridge, the Keoy Teow Fishball Soup (Rice Noodle Fish Balls Soup), the apom (Indian Pancake), the Bang Chang Koey (Chinese Pancake), the fish noodle soup all all highly recommended.If we visit Penang again, will definitely visit this place again.Show less

Author: RossR908
Title: Great range of foods.
Review: Just across from Holmpton Hotel is this gem of a foodcourt. A collection of vendors selling a wide array of foods to suit all tastes. Good range of beers and other beverages. Well worth a visit for the food and atmosphere.

Author: SriJoe74
Title: Plenty Of Choices
Review: The place will spoil you with plenty of good local hawker food choices. Most of the food stalls has very tasty dishes. While you are there, don't forget to try the mouthwatering char koay teow...

Author: PKKCLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Nice local food centre that has lots of choice
Review: A nice hawker centre located near a couple of hotels. The selection of food ranges from local specialities to some western fare. All the famous local food is here though some are better than others. Ordered a range of food. The assam laksa is OK, the law bak adequate and the fried oyster omelette nice. The best was the apom or pancake. Crispy outside with a nice soft centre. Very Moorish.Show less

Author: KJLKLKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good local hawker food
Review: When there for dinner as it was near my hotel I was staying which was the Mercure Hotel Penang Beach. It was only a five minute walk. In general the place was not as crowded as Gurney Drive. At least there is a much better place of getting a table. In addition, the hawkers will take your order and ask for your table no. After preparing and cooking the food, they will deliver the food to your table. You get almost all types of Penang local hawker food there. It’s not as large as Gurney Drive you get lots of repetitive stores. Quality of food varies but in general of good standard. Would come back here again if you do not want to fight with others at Gurney Drive for a table. Show less

Author: Mark DPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: A Very Good "Hawker Centre" with lots of "Favourites"!
Review: There are many such "Hawker food centres" in Tanjung Tokong and nearby Tanjung Bunga--- but the "supper offerings" are super! Most of the Chinese favourite dishes [like char Kway Teow, "Frog" Porridge, clay pot chicken, "Hor Fun" etc.] as well as Malay dishes [like Assam Laksa] are "on offer". The food is freshly prepared, the vendors specialise in one or two dishes and all dishes are quite inexpensive. What is perhaps best is that you can watch the food being prepared, what it looks and smells like before making a choice! It is definitely worthy of a visit.I hope that this Review has been helpful.Show less

Author: M5764IUcolins
Title: Best Local
Review: Have been to 3 other ‘food courts’ In Penang and this by far is the most authentic! Great array, many choices, cheap, flavourful and adequate quantity. Best is the Stingray, Assam Laksa and Char Kaoy Teow.

Author: PremalathaSKuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan, Malaysia
Title: asam laksa is the best
Review: we chanced upon this restaurant 6 yrs ago during our visit. and the taste of the asam laksa i had here was the best. so during our recent visit, we drove looking for this place. and i found the asam laksa which i was craving .its so delicious and fragrant. asam laksa will have the pungent fish smell that will put most people off, but this was so tasty and fragrant and i wish i had more of itShow less

Author: amyrosylilyAsia
Title: Nice variety of food at good price
Review: Went there for dinner and ordered a full table of food - six dishes for two. Find a table, make your order at the individual stalls, give them your table number, then the food will be delivered to your table hot and nice. Recommend ordering small portion of each, so that your could try more variety in one go!Show less

Author: inverness-uk
Title: Excellent food!
Review:
I just love this place! 
No wonder they are always busy. 
Perfect food, cooked to order and delivered to your table. Lots of stalls to choose from, each making a different thing..
Well worth a visit.

Author: TPT_TravellerVancouver, B.C.
Title: Large food court; good selection
Review: I ate here several times over the two weeks I stayed at the hotel next door. There are a lot of stalls but not a lot of vegetarian options here. However, with help from a local I was able to negotiate with the vendors, and was able to try different things each time.My main complaint with this place is that they push certain brands of beer. I asked for a Tiger beer and was told they didn't carry it. The beer ladies even have a card showing certain brands of beer they carry. The lady wanted me to order a Carlsberg, so I did. Then I saw that the people at the next table had a bucket of Tiger beer. On the next visit I insisted on Tiger beer and the woman was very disappointed.I ate at a number of food courts during my stay on the island. This one was one of the larger ones and was consistently busy with locals. Prices were average, as was the food.Show less

Author: Calle K
Title: Good dinner and cheap
Review:
We went here as a walk from Four Pints by Sheraton for dinner.
Friendly people and friendly prices with good service.
Beer was readily available.
We especially liked the Char Kuey Teow and Prawn omelette

Author: MellisaD18
Title: Best pizza and burger
Review: Tried the homemade burger and pizza.Value for money and generous toppings.Hawaiian pizza and beef burger is a must try

Author: traderdadStuttgart, Germany
Title: All the local classics and then some
Review: We have been to many different food courts and hawker centers both in Penang and KL and found Viva delivers some of the best variety and quality of them all. We especially loved the Char Hor Fun stall, the Apom Telur and the grilled fish (they will also do eggplant the same way they do the fish - excellent!). It is not the cheapest hawker place to eat and the choices for Vegetarians are indeed rather limited, but overall we would highly recommend it! One thing to note however is that there is no Indian stall here, so no roti Naan or Tandoori chicken. They do have a stall serving Taiwanese food which is not too common in this type of place.Show less

Author: amflhu88Saskatoon, Canada
Title: A great food court to try many different dishes!
Review: This hawker court is wonderful to take a group of people with divergent tastes - there are a couple of dozen stalls to order from, so most people will find something to eat from traditional laksa, to meat on rice, to satay, to many soups, and shawarma. I think there might even be a western food place in the back. A note for tourists: when you arrive, claim a table and note the number. Someone will come take your drink order. Once your drinks have arrived and you’ve paid for them, then you go order from a hawker. Tell them your table number and they will deliver your food to the table when it’s ready. Show less

Author: sugania20Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Great stop for local food
Review: We had just driven to Penang from KL and were not in the mood to drive far for good meal, so we decided to google and found this place. It was really near to where we stayed (Tanjung Tokong) and you can get a lot of variety here. If you are a vegetarian, dont expect to have much though, but everyone else can have a good meal at really good price.Show less

Author: cincaujonathanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Many foods
Review: Great place to eat if you're in tanjong area doesnt go into City area jam. Lots of choices, lobak, oyster omelette is nice, sambal chicken, satays, burgers, Western and Japanese food as well. Bak ku Teh and claypot also available. Overall great place to dine in family group and friends. Show less

Author: BoredAuntie
Title: Dinner
Review: Ok place if u are near by nothing to wow about. Clean enough for Malaysia standard. Apom telur is tasty, I op for the egg version.

Author: JulesP205Ballajura, Australia
Title: What a gem
Review: Just 2 minutes walk from our hotel or a short bus ride on the 101 things sxplace us buzzing from around 6pm. Great selection of foods no t being terribly adventurous we settled on the grilled fish, it was so good that we ate there again. Beer is available at half the hotel price. Don't not miss this for good cheap tuckerShow less

Author: Sheena B
Title: Small, Clean and Oh So Much Good Food
Review: A great place to drop by and fill up your stomach if you're in the area. Go for the char kuey tiaw. You won't regret it.

Author: EZaborski
Title: Claypot Chicken rice!
Review: The CCR is always a must for me when I comer to Penang!! It doesn't disappoint here at viva. Also, the satay and char koay teow are very good as well! Highly recommended hawker joint :)

Author: Bomoh
Title: Newer hawker centre
Review: Newer is usually better in Penang and this is the case here. Very good hor fun and char koay teow as well as competitively priced beer. My son loves the apom manis.

Author: 6784_dog
Title: It's definitely just local and fun
Review: Dropped by via driving from batu ferringhi to Georgetown and it has pretty much everything. All local food with lots of locals at locals pricing. Everything in English as well and prices are marked and non negotiable. Just point if required and tell them your table number. You pay when the food is delivered to your table. Have fun! The prices are cheap so our kids tried pretty much everything but poor dad had to mop up the leftovers (which were just as yummy) Show less

Author: kkazzpro
Title: Great hawker food
Review: Delicious local hawker food with more of a Chinese/Malay influence. Loved the BBQ Pork Cheung fun, chicken feet, and steamed spring rolls. Also has a Japanese stall serving the freshest sushi and sashimi. Satays are wonderful.

Author: shunwoiKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Variety of hawker foods
Review: This foods court is walking distance from Hotel Sentral Seaview, for those who would like to try Penang foods, you can order Char Koey Tiaw with duck eggs and spicy, price is RM7. Foods and beverage here very expensive, above average, feed for tourist price. However 90% is local. Show less

Author: Nr277
Title: Best satay in Penang
Review: Good foodcourt overall, but its best offering is the satay. Definitely visit if you want to know how satay should taste like. The apom (coconut pancakes/crepes) are also very good, though the stall does not run week-round, so check beforehand.

Author: barchart184
Title: Typical local Food Court
Review: Good selection of dishes from the region, so dining out as a group there is something for everyone. Good food in the hustle and bustle of local life

Author: cannyp4
Title: Tasty local food
Review: Our hotel was just behind the Viva food centre. During the 3nights stay we have our dinner there on the first and the third night. Our favorite was the bak ku teh. Must try!

Author: sisko2u
Title: Good food
Review: has variety of choices and food are good especially the chee cheong fun, pan mee and there are many more to suit personal choice.

Author: DhayapariPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Best Apam in Penang Island
Review: Mr. Subra and his better half Mrs. Lakshmi make the best egg Indian pancake (Apam Telur) in Penang island! Located in Tanjung Bungah, this humble pancake stall serves soft centered pancakes surrounded by crunchy crust at a reasonable price! Absolutely loving it! Highly recommended. Penang Famous Heritage Apam Telur! Show less

Author: PaulInManilaMidland, Australia
Title: Very Good and Tasty Hawker Food
Review: Viva Food Haven was just across from our Hotel, we loved the Indian Curry, and the Banana Leaf Char Kuey Teow. Ate there most nights that we stayed in Penang, most of the other food where was also quite good, did try the Clay Pot Chicken and was disappointed, may have been just a bad night. But do try the Banana leaf and the curries on the left after the side entrance.Show less

Author: reg_butler
Title: This is a very good place to find a quick and tasty hawker food meal
Review:
I love the Banana Leaf Char Kuey Teow. Always very tasty
Also the Chicken or Duck Rice is good.
The Oyster Omelette is not so good.
Plenty of other choices available, mostly Chinese but some Western food.

Author: hamp2016Singapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner in Aug 2016
Review: The variety of local Penang dishes are available here. Char Koay Teow, Poh Piah, Bak Kuet Teh, Char Ho Fun and satay are some of the popular dishes I like. Average price and acceptable environment similar to food court. Nyonya kueh also available for desert. Visited several times in the last 7 days.Give it a try to enjoy variety of foods in one sitting. Show less

Author: WS28Penang_Malaysiq
Title: Good range of hawker fare!
Review: Come here if you are looking for a wide range of hawker food ! They serve cool beer as well. Taste is comparable to all the good ones out there in Penang, A one-stop Penang local food !

Author: 211selinan
Title: Offers a variety of hawker fare
Review: Often crowded with tourists and locals alike,  this local food Centre houses many stalls that offer both local,  western abs Japanese cuisines.  While you  get to enjoy many types of local fare here,  the parking can be challenging. .

Author: 886arianes
Title: Ok
Review: We were late there at 10pm, some food sold out. Friendly waitress for drinks. Food nothing special, but OK, typical hawker style. Nice atmosphere, even one Malay stall between the Chinese and Indian ones.

Author: DutchTraveler99Zutphen, The Netherlands
Title: Great place
Review: Typical system: large court with tables and chairs where each table has a number. You can order at each food stall, give the number of your table and after a few minutes someone is bringing the food to your table. Only then you pay for your order. The only exception are the drinks. A waiter will serve you at your table. Wide range of choices including western food which appeals to some of our kids. Good value for money! Very relaxed atmosphere.Show less

Author: tgiblinGreen Valley, Arizona
Title: Great outdoor food court
Review: This is where locals eat so you know it's cheap and tasty. I usually go to Long Island cafe in batu farenge get, but was staying close to viva so gave it a try. Decent food! Lots of choices and even cheaper than long beach. Try the char hor funShow less

Author: Chris_ElsonMorpeth, United Kingdom
Title: You have to try this place!
Review: We were staying in the Four Points Sheraton just down the road and the food and drink were ridiculously expensive there. I had seen reviews of Viva on here when planning the trip so we decided to give it a go... And we didn't regret it! In fact we came back here on every night of our stay in Penang!We tried food from most of the stands and it was all really good. The highlights (although we loved it all) were probably the Char Koay Teow, the Prawn Katsu Curry, the Apom pancake things and the fresh grilled fish (although this was a little more expensive). The atmosphere is fantastic, it was busy every night and you order as many dishes as you like from a selection of stands and then you pay when the food is brought to your table. It was the start of Euro 16 whilst we were there and I got to watch a couple of the matches in there as they have a couple of big screens, which was an unexpected bonus!We found that we could both eat till we were stuffed and have a couple of drinks for about half the price of 1 main meal at the hotel.Would highly recommend that everyone gives this a go. It's quite an experience, it's really cheap and the food is delicious. It is possibly a little bit unhygienic in places, as a lot of street food will be, but we loved every second. Give it a try!!Oh, and it's not open through the day, only for dinner at night.Show less

Author: Clam77
Title: Local food
Review: Large food court with a variety of local foods all cooked fresh. It's cheap and easy, order then they deliver to your table and take payment.

Author: wintermelonKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good wanton noodles, char koay teow and Bak Kut Teh
Review: We came here three times while staying at Sentral Seaview Hotel for two nights. We tried the wanton noodles, char koay teow, duck rice, clay pot chicken rice, Beef Lasagne and Bak Kut Teh (Herbal soup with pork.) All are good especially the wanton noodles, char koey teow and Bak Kut Teh.One thing I don't like is that some of the stalls owners were smoking while handling the food.Only available from late afternoon till midnight.Show less

Author: diner18Melbourne, Australia
Title: Not recommended
Review: Conveniently located for Quayside condominiums, this food court looks clean and well presented with a good mix of food stalls but the quality of the fare was most unimpressive. The Apom stall was probably the pick of the bunch but the rest was pretty average. In a food haven like Penang, this is a waste of time when one could go further down the road to the Gurney Plaza hawker centre for much better food.Show less

Author: Lau DIpoh, Malaysia
Title: Variety but not really on the yum list.
Review: Its location right in front of the Sentral Seaview Hotel is a plus point.All the must eat local fare like char kway teow, laksa , kway teow thng etc. etc are there but taste wise , to me, only average. But since I was there with a big group it helps that there was a great of food to cater to everyone's tastebuds!Show less

Author: syingee
Title: Lots of food variety!
Review: A few must try stalls, Malay satay, char koay teow, Indian apom, Siamese laksa, Chicken claypot rice, Yong tau foo!

Author: balijazzJimbaran, Indonesia
Title: A Great Hawkers Food Court Just 10 Minutes Walk From The Four Points Sheraton..
Review: We really enjoyed eating eating in this food centre. We basically chose it on the first night of our stay because it was close to the Four Points Sheraton our hotel and we was lazy to go into town. We ended eating here every night of our stay because we enjoyed the food so much. There is a really good choice from many stalls, Thai, Chinese, Indian, Western and more and it is mainly used by locals and is busy every night. The food was good quality and the prices of both food and drinks was reasonable. Beer is also readily available as the locals like to drink here too. We tried many choices over the 3 nights all mentioned above except the western stalls at the back popular with locals and particularly enjoyed the stall cooking frog dishes in many styles a highlight for us. This place is well worth a visit if you are in the area and great to soak up the local atmosphere.Show less

Author: drewboycSingapore, Singapore
Title: Penang food haven
Review: This is a hidden gem which to be honest, I was so reluctant in sharing on TA. I'm just so afraid that after sharing, more and more tourists will visit viva, pushing the prices up and the quality down! Yes.. I'm selfish! So what??! Hahaha!!!For the betterment of man-kind.. I will share my treasures with the rest of the world. This is one food court you have to try when u visit Penang!! The lor bak (choose the one with century and salted egg!) it's so special u will only find this concoction here!! The char kuey tiow with duck egg is the best I've eaten in Penang!! Better then all the highly raved places that u find online.. The Kang Kong cuttlefish is awesome. The 'hae kor' with the fresh vege and cuttlefish makes this an awesome dish.. But it maybe an acquired taste.. Bak kut teh is very good.. Soup is the herbal kind, with lots of different ingredients.. The pork ribs was pretty hard though.. And didn't quite enjoy it.. Kui pie tee was ok.. Though I've tasted better.. And the prawn noodle (hae mee) was not that good.. There were quite a few other shops that I wish I tried but I just couldn't stomach anymore food!! I'm sure there were many other food stalls which I've yet to explore! Will definitely be back for my authentic Penang spread when I next return to Penang!!Show less

Author: 572phila
Title: Good selection of food to cater for all tastes
Review: Usual selection of food available. Right at the very back is a burger stall and a pie stall if you want a change from local food. The burgers are very good.

Author: ArfaMindCalella, Spain
Title: Great food court. Great fun.
Review: Fantastic food court out just out of George Town. Grab and table and note the number then see what you fancy. The stall will bring over your order when ready. Floating waiters will fetch you drinks. I had to try the clay bowl frogs, done four different ways. Really taste. The place can get pretty busy but this does mean the turnover is great and therefore all the food is really fresh. The wet fish stall has some of the freshest fish I have seen here. I could have eaten it raw but they delicately fry it in a delicious coating of spices. The chap on the Char Koay Teow stall has been cooking this one dish in the same pan for 30 years and it is quite wonderful. Also try the Apom Manis, a light stuffed pancake.Prices are ridiculously low. Tuck inShow less

Author: TousTnTPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Busy Foodcourt with wide selection of food
Review: This is my nearest foodcourt & luckily for me one of my favourites. It is always busy with a good atmosphere. There is a wide selection of predominantly local foods but some international as well including Italian & burgers (no beef though). I find all the stall holders friendly, helpful & sympathetic towards non-locals & explain their food & offer variations if you prefer. The service is great with a large selection of drinks including beers & washrooms & toilets. Judging by the popularity with the locals the food is good & I certainly enjoy all that I have eaten with a special mention for the Char Kway Teow, claypot chicken & both the steamed & grilled fish stalls. The prices are very reasonable.Show less

Author: HLCheeGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Taste of Penang all in one place
Review: Been there many times and felt I should write this. This is a large hawker centre/food court, some may call it. Food ranges from Char Koay Teow to Seafood and Burgers. My fav is Char Koay Teow and Chee Cheong Fun (HK style). There are so many others take will make your trip there worthwhile.Show less

Author: Rani_1110
Title: Good food spread and taste good.
Review: This place is much better than Gurney drive. Good spread of local delicacies cooked by locals. Easy to find parking too

Author: 309jackiepPerth, Australia
Title: Good for chee cheong fun
Review: We came here to dine only because we were staying at the Four Points and didn't want to drive anywhere. There certainly is variety but don't think they're the best you can get in Penang. It's a convenient place to have a bite only if you're staying at the Four Points, I reckon.Show less

Author: SandyZebrasTanjung Bungah, Malaysia
Title: We ate there every night for a week!
Review: Staying at the Hotel Sentral Seaview meant that Viva was a 30 second walk. We tried different places there over the course of the week but each night started off with the excellent satays. 5 beef and 5 Lamb satays came to RM 8-50. Fantastic value.Tandoori Chicken with a Naan bread was also a great choice. All up RM12-00. TRy getting that sort of value in Australia! The gentleman who ran the Indian place also cooked us a Chicken Korma and a Lamb Tikka Masala dish that weren't on the menu. Delicious. If you get a chance go and ask him if he'll do these for youOther places we tried were the Prawn Omelette stand and the Char Kway Teow stand.On one night I ordered the large serve of Claypot Chicken Rice. Big mistake. The serving was HUGE. Way too much for one person.As is the case with the food courts, the drinks people were always ready to get you another Tiger Beer or Skol beer. And with a couple of TV's there I was able to watch the opening match of the EPL season with a few young Dutch guys who were also staying at the same hotel.Sure we could have gone to other places close by to eat, but we enjoyed Viva that much that we simply decided to eat there each night. Even when we stayed for a week at Batu Ferringhi, we jumped on the 101 bus and went there for a last meal before we left to go homeShow less

Author: danboz1

Author: Virginia231975
Title: Claypot chicken curry rice
Review: I do recommend in this little nice cafe the claypot chicken curry with rice (exquisite, very refined, with bit of anis and sugar taste, an old grand mother recipe, only there the chicken curry has such a taste, it is unique, you can get it also with shark and stingray), lemon with rose syrup is oki, you can add sugar. It costs like 21 rm drik included. I also tried the spaghetti carbonara. It was good.They organise cooking lessons I didn’t try and they used to organise guided tours of the city in a car (5 hours)The atmosphere is artistic and trendy. It is a simple place where the music takes you back in time.The many mixed races manager plays his own kind of music. The decoration on the walls is cute and well done, relaxing, located a bit away from Chulia street. If you don’t like the music, they make it less loud.You eat inside or at two small tables outside on high chairs but I prefere eating inside where it is less hotcFew people walk in that street. You are away from the noisy and boisterous crowd on Love lane and Chulia.The place seems to be very clean. There are not many dishes to choose but what they cook is good and special.The elegant and charming young German wife takes cooking courses to improove the menu. They didn’t have mushroom and parmesan cheese for the pasta one time so they charged me less. Food quantity is oki to very good. I was more than full with the curry/rice, and just oki full with the pasta carbonaraThe manager and his wife come to speak to you easily to know you, they check if you like the food and ask if something has to be improoved. You do feel they do like their place and job. You feel welcome. However it maybe takes some time to get the food because they cook it fresh. You have to be patient and after it is very good. It is the inconvenience there but they tell you beforeA good value for money (more expensive than stalls but worth). I’m looking forward to go back. I went there like 5 times.Show less

Author: S P
Title: Three experiences in one!
Review: We stumbled across the Brick Cafe one afternoon in Georgetown when we were looking for some Malaysian food. We noticed a sign outside advertising cooking classes and went inside to eat.We had lunch at the Brick Cafe on two occasions; the first time we ate fish and chicken curries, the second time laksa and with banana pancakes to follow afterwards. As we think about the food now to write this review, our mouths have started watering!! The food was delicious, Lisa the owner is extremely friendly and there is a great atmosphere in the cafe. The second time we visited, my boyfriend got his food before I got mine as the cafe was full, and there are only three people working there, but Lisa explained this before we sat down to eat and it was no problem for us; we shared both portions so the wait time didn’t matter, and it wasn’t long in any case. If you are looking for traditional Malaysian food, this is definitely the place to go. We had claypot fish curry on a couple of occasions and this was definitely the nicest we had, and the unusual fish choices were great (shark, catfish or flatfish). Banana pancakes were also delicious, with the bananas mashed and baked into the batter! I don’t like spicy food much, but Lisa asked before she brought the portions and I didn’t find mine too spicy; everywhere we ate in Malaysia we found that ‘not spicy’ still meant ‘a bit spicy’, so it wasn’t a suprise to us to find it a little bit hot! We also participated in a cooking class with Lisa, where we made the claypot fish curry. This was a very good price compared to other cooking classes in Malaysia and Lisa took care to explain how we could find the ingredients or adapt the recipe for cooking at home in Germany/England afterwards. She gave us the recipe to take home when we were finished and we got to eat our creations (this was the third time we ate the The Brick Cafe!) when we were finished. We really enjoyed the class.We also took a tour around Penang with Lisa’s husband Remy, who works as a guide. This was also very reasonably priced (50Rm per person for a six hour tour). Remy took us to places we hadn’t yet been (it was our last day in Georgetown after a week there), based on where we wanted to go. We went to a beautiful, deserted beach, the temple of the ‘laying down buddha’ (I think it was called), a waterfall, the Tropical Spice Museum (we paid the entrance for this on top) and a Durian stall where Remy said that they sell the best Durian in the area. Throughout the day, he bought us so many Malaysian sweets and snacks (included in price) that we hadn’t found anywhere else in Georgetown. He had a lot of knowledge about local legends too. We would thoroughly recommend the Brick Cafe to other visitors to Georgetown, as we got so much out of our visit there and it really made our time in Penang. Thank you Lisa and Remy! For some reason, Tripadvisor won’t let me rate the service, food and value for money, but we would give 5/5 for all.Show less

Author: MaureenO608
Title: Someone recommended this
Review: Someone recommended this place, I had a few hours to kill in the island, look on tripadvisor and the opening hours and it was stated 10am on a Saturday morning. 7 of us arrived at 1037am after a long walk with 4 children, we were told they open at 11am. I asked if we could sit down and wait for 30 mins inside since tripadvisor lead us there with the faulty opening time and the children were tired from walking.
